Question/Consideration:
Question 2
Data on finished drugs under subparagraph 2(c) of Article 7 of the same regulation,
B. 1) Related regulations: Article 7 (Requirements for review data) 2 © and Article 34 of the same regulations
2) Feedback: Regarding 3.2.P.5.6 Justification of specification, it is not reasonable to omit the Sterility test at the time of release on the submitted evidence as a requirement that should be satisfied even in the manufacture of general sterilized injections.
3) Request for supplement: Regarding 3.2.P.5. Control of drug products, it is required for reasonable evidence for the change of the sterility test method during quality control of drug products.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 2 ( CTD section):
The sterilization cycle for Radium-223 chloride solution for injection was designed using the overkill design approach. Xofigo is released before the sterility test is concluded on the basis of a review and verification of the executed batch record and defined critical in-process acceptance criteria for the terminal sterilization and overall sterility assurance parameters, which may be described as semi-parametric release. This is in accordance with established procedures for radiopharmaceuticals where the time required to conclude results for sterility testing constitute a significant proportion of the half-life of the radionuclide and thus the shelf-life of the product.
The historic sterility testing data from the two manufacturing sites, Agilera and Cardinal Health, show no sterility failure among the total of 1400 commercial batched that have been manufactured between 2013 and 2022. Due to the nature of monographed sterility test method and Xofigo's short shelf life of 28 days, the test result is available after the drug product has been distributed and is available for patient treatment. The historic review of all data for bioburden testing performed at Agilera and Cardinal Health show no growth (< 1 CFU/mL), apart from one batch (result of 3 CFU/mL) for Agilera and 6 batches (results of 1 CFU/mL) for CAH. The consistency of sterility testing and low bioburden has been shown in the latest product quality review, of which relevant sections are provided again.
The Korean Regulation on Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) for Medicinal Products (No.2021-87, Nov 4,2021)” describes Parametric Release in annex 14. Korea is also a member of PIC/S and the PIC/S GMP guide annex 17 also states that products sterilized in their final container by moist or dry heat is applicable for parametric release, as written below:

3.4 At present Parametric release can only be approved for products terminally sterilized in their final container.
3.5 Sterilization methods according to European Pharmacopoeia requirements using steam, dry heat and ionising radiation may be considered for parametric release.
(Source : GUIDE TO GOOD MANUFACTURING PRACTICE FOR MEDICINAL PRODUCTS ANNEXES 17, PARAMETRIC RELEASE)

In conclusion, parametric release strengthens patient safety by confirming sterility before patient administration and is in line with Korean regulations and PIC/S GMP guidelines and the production of Xofigo injection meets all the formal prerequisites for parametric release that include:
• Successful validation of the sterilization process that ensure a sterility assurance level (SAL) of at least 10-6 as the main prerequisite.
• Pre-sterilization bioburden monitoring program that ensures that the microbiological status of the product before sterilization meets the established microbiological control level used for validation of the sterilization process.
• Definition of critical parameters and key parameters based on operational sterility assurance risk assessment of the production process.
• Container closure system that ensures the integrity of the containers under all relevant circumstances in the manufacturing and sterilization process.
• Product release procedure that describes in detail the release steps and the documentation required for a parametric release

Question/Consideration:
Question 5
Please provide detailed justification of delta-5-norandrostenedione synthesis changes.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 5 (CTD section):
Steroidal APIs like Dienogest are usually synthesized starting from a natural occurring 
steroidal precursor which provides the four-ring skeleton and predefined chiral centers of the 
API. One of these sources is diosgenin which derives from dioscorea species. The plants are 
cultivated in China, but Bayer AG is aware of a tendency that this may no longer be the case 
in the future. Consequently, phytosterols are qualified as a second source of steroidal 
precursors in order to guarantee market supply.
keywords: synthesis; Starting material; Manufacturing Process Development; manufacturing description; Proof of Product Equivalence after Change of Production

Question/Consideration:
Question 6
Please provide justification of starting material for phytosterols, structural formulas of 
phytosterol.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 6 (CTD section):
Phytosterols are the naturally occurring steroidal source which derive from a variety of plants. 
They have the following structure in common:

phytosterol skeleton 
R= sidechains of different lengths 
 
The designation phytosterols comprises mixtures of compounds like beta-sitosterol, 
brassicasterol, campesterol, campestanol stigmasterol, sitostanol, etc. Being natural products 
from various plants (e.g. soybean oil, rape seed oil, corn oil, sunflower oil) they have not one 
single structure and not one defined composition. For an overview please refer to the assessment 
in literature “Phytosterols, Phytostanols and their esters”, R.Cantrill, Y. Kawamura attached 
Please be informed that both routes via diosgenin (current) or phytosterols (proposed) are 
classical sources for, so called, partial synthesis of steroidal APIs and being used for decades 
already. The quality of delta5-norandrostenedione from either source is equivalent as explained 
in response to question 4.
Source:  Publication. R. Cantrill, Y. Kawamura, Phytosterols, Phytostanols and their
esters (CTA) 2008 – page 1 – 13.
keywords: Starting material; synthesis; Elucidation of Structure and other Characteristics; Support documents; Comparative Batch Analysis

Question/Consideration:
Question 1
Process validation data directly relevant to the proposed change: The data should confirm that 
the control strategy is adequate for the process design and the quality of  the product.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1:

The manufacturing process of recombinant interferon beta-1b (rIFN beta-1b) as a drug 
substance for Interferon beta-1b lyophilized powder (Betaferon) at Boehringer Ingelheim RCV 
GmbH & Co KG is well-established for over 30 years and adequately monitored by in-process and 
release testing.
In order to assure adequate process performance and product quality, continuous process 
verification (CPV) is performed once every quarter to assess the quality of the output material as 
well as  system performance in a continuous manner.
The test to analyze the content of rIFN beta-1b by ELISA after fermentation was originally 
implemented for monitoring purposes only. Consequently, the results of the ELISA test are not used 
for any process decision and do not prevent the proceeding from the fermentation step to the primary 
recovery step of the inclusion bodies. In addition, the test results from the ELISA assay are not 
included in the CPV documentation. Considering the above, all available data of  rIFN beta-1b 
content measured by ELISA was thoroughly analyzed and it was confirmed that no deviation from 
the registered limit (NLT 0.3 mg/mL) was identified over the past 80 manufactured batches. Please 
refer to Error! Reference source not found. below.
Moreover, in the subsequent manufacturing step (primary recovery of the inclusion bodies (IBs), 
the content of rIFN beta-1b is measured with the RP-HPLC and strictly controlled with an action 
limit of NLT 11 mg/g. Over the last four years, historical CPV data for the most recent 50 IB batches 
demonstrates that rIFN beta-1b content measured via RP-HPLC analysis was well within the 
control limits (12.55 – 23.09 mg/g) and above the low alarm limit (11.00 mg/g). Please refer to 
Figure 1 and Figure 33 below.

As the ELISA test shows higher variability in comparison to RP-HPLC analysis (intermediate 
precision for ELISA is 20 %  versus 3.0 % for RP HPLC) and both tests can be considered 
redundant, it is intended to monitor rIFN beta-1b content on the level of recovered IBs measured 
with the more precise RP HPLC analysis in future.
Notably, the deletion of this test is currently in the process of being registered globally. Until all 
approvals are obtained globally, this test is continued to be performed and thus no CPV data with 
the deleted ELISA test is currently available at this stage.
Bayer confirms that once all approvals are obtained for this variation globally, the ELISA test after 
fermentation is omitted from the drug substance manufacturing process and CPV data will be 
collected quarterly to continuously monitor the quality and process performance over time. 
Moreover, Bayer confirms that except for the deletion of the monitoring ELISA parameter at the 
end of fermentation, no further changes to the manufacturing process were introduced and no impact 
on CPV data is thus expected, also considering that the ELISA test was not part of the CPV 
documentation before.
Please also refer to the Declaration submitted within this response for further details.

please provide the comparability evidence that the Lift-Off Volume (LOV) IPC parameter
could be replaced by Transition Analysis (TA) strategy and to support the consistency of

Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 3 ( CTD section S.2.4):

Along with lift-off volume (LOV) monitoring, transition analysis (TA) data were used to 
analyze the aflibercept lots processed between 25Jan2013 and 31Dec2020 (1,151 lots). 
Regeneron routinely evaluates TA data with respect to unit operation-specific historically 
accepted limits for non-gaussian height equivalent of a theoretical plate (NGHETP) and 
skewness. Historical TA data were assessed for excursions from these historically accepted 
limits. LOV and TA excursions were further categorized according to Table 1 to directly 
compare efficacy and robustness of TA and LOV. A representative example from every 
excursion category is detailed below.

Overview of the investigation data analyzed by both the LOV and TA methods:
Of the 1,151 lot investigations analyzed, there were 213 LOV and 20 TA excursions 
identified. 133 of these LOV investigations identified a root cause corresponding to Normal 
Process Variability/IPC Monitoring whereas only 15 TA excursions were found in this same 
timeframe. Therefore, the rate of false positives within this category was observed to be 
88.7% lower for the TA monitoring approach than for LOV.

Figure 1 below shows the comparative number of excursions corresponding to each root cause 
category for the TA and LOV methods of monitoring column performance. TA is proven to 
have comparable robustness for detecting instances of column deterioration. Out of the 1,151 
lots analyzed, a total of 213 LOV excursions were identified. Of these, three investigations 
were found to be attributed to unacceptable chromatography Column Performance. TA 
excursions were also identified for the three lots requiring an LOV investigation; in addition, 
TA identified two additional instances of column deterioration for aflibercept which did not 
correspond to an observed LOV excursion (refer to Table 1 ). No instances of 
chromatography column deterioration were identified from 25Jan2013 to 31Dec2020 that 
were not identified by TA. In addition, significantly fewer false positive excursions have been 
historically identified using TA.

Figure 1: 
Root Cause Categorization for TA and LOV Excursions
Examples

1) Example of Column Performance Root Cause Categorization 
In accordance with internal procedures, manufacturing chromatography data is reviewed to 
monitor chromatography bed performance. Any anomalies identified during the review 
process are assessed for associated risk and appropriate mitigation action items are identified 
and implemented.
During performance of chromatogram review for aflibercept Protein A lot 8115100052, 
NGHETP and skewness values were found to be outside of accepted limits.  Evidence of 
column deterioration was also identified for the UV absorbance trace. In accordance with 
procedure, the issue was investigated, and a decision was taken to repack the chromatography 
column prior to processing the subsequent lot to ensure appropriate column performance.  The 
column was subsequently repacked. This TA excursion was categorized as “Column 
Performance.”

The column deterioration was also detected by LOV monitoring. A quality event was initiated 
in response to Rule 1(3s) violations, being defined as one data point that falls outside the 
±3SD control limit, which was identified for the LOV IPC parameter for aflibercept Protein A 
lot 8115100052. Within the quality system, it was determined that this LOV excursion 
corresponded to column performance and a column repack had already occurred as a result of
the chromatogram review CFT meeting.

Product quality data (VI pool CHO HCP and step yield) were also reviewed for lot 
8115100052 and are summarized in Table 2.  This data suggests that the column deterioration 
was identified and mitigated prior to any impact on product quality data. The sensitivity of 
TA to identify instances of column deterioration and the rapid response strategy of the 
chromatography review program allow detection and mitigation of chromatography column 
deterioration prior to observed impact to IPC product quality data.

The Transition Analysis and LOV methods of monitoring column performance were both able

2) Example of Normal Process Variability/IPC Monitoring Root Cause Categorization

For aflibercept Protein Affinity lot 8115100059, Rule 1(3s) violations were identified for the 
average LOV parameter and a quality event was initiated as a result. Within the quality event, 
it was identified that LOV values had exhibited a downward trend throughout the lifetime of 
the column pack.  Historical aflibercept Protein A LOV data spanning from March 2015 to 
September 2019 was aggregated and a statistically significant relationship was identified 
between average LOV and Protein A resin cycle number. Therefore, the root cause of this

Question/Consideration:
Question 2
The FDS manufacturing process development is with HC1, HC2, and further optimized to 
HC2 optimized, please provide the full report of the comparability studies, including 
comparative characterization data, comparative batch analysis, and comparative stability 
studies.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 2 (3.2S.2.6):
Additional information related to comparability of HC1, HC2 and further optimized HC2 
optimized manufacturing processes are provided in CTD Section S.2.6.11 and is summarized 
below.
Analytical comparability of aflibercept high-dose HC1 and HC2 FDS was assessed with 
release, long-term storage, accelerated stability, and stress stability testing. This evaluation 
determined that HC2 FDS is comparable to HC1 FDS with no impact to potency, biochemical 
attributes, physicochemical attributes, or stability of the protein.
Production-scale aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL FDS lots manufactured by the HC2 
process were evaluated for comparability to HC1 FDS lots.
The release results were evaluated against release specification acceptance criteria as well as 
historical results from HC1 lots. The long-term storage results were evaluated against stability 
specification acceptance criteria and the accelerated and stress stability results were compared 
to data from an HC1 FDS comparator lot (8305500001).
Comparability of aflibercept high-dose FDS manufactured by the HC1 and HC2 processes is 
supported by the following product quality assessments.
• 
The HC2 FDS lots met the release specification acceptance criteria. The HC2 FDS 
results for potency, purity, and physicochemical attributes were well aligned with 
historical HC1 FDS results. Differences in fragmentation and charge variants were 
likely attributable to process variability in the DSI source lots.
• 
HC1 and HC2 FDS showed little to no degradation under the long-term storage 
condition and HC2 FDS met the stability specification acceptance criteria through 36 
months.
• 
Common mechanisms and rates of fragmentation, aggregation, and charge variant 
formation were observed for HC1 and HC2 FDS under the accelerated and stress 
stability conditions. Additionally, potency by bioassay was largely unchanged for 
material from both processes under both conditions.
Overall, aflibercept high-dose HC1 and HC2 FDS are comparable and this assessment 
supports the use of the HC2 manufacturing process for production of aflibercept high-dose 
DS and FDS. Based on comparative batch analysis and comparative stability analysis, HC1 
and HC2 were found to be comparable and thus no extended characterization was deemed 
necessary. In addition, both HC1 and HC2 material was used in the clinical studies.
Analytical comparability of aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL HC2 and optimized HC2 was 
assessed with in-process, release, and stress stability data. Release results from optimized 
HC2 process are compared to release specifications and comparability limits.
The three production-scale optimized process lot results all meet the current and proposed 
release specification acceptance criteria. Additionally, all results fall within the comparability
limits. This evaluation demonstrates the product quality of the optimized process lots are 
highly similar to historical lots at release.
Extended characterization testing was performed to assess molecular weight, glycan identity 
and heterogeneity, molar mass, and size heterogeneity of the test articles and comparators.
Additionally, a side-by-side stress stability study at 37 °C was performed with the three 
optimized process lots and three representative historical lots to compare the degradation 
trends. Additional timepoints for long term stability studies have been provided with the 
response to Question 5.
The information including comparative characterization data, comparative batch analysis, and 
comparative stability studies is provided in CTD section S.2.6.11.

Question/Consideration:
Question 1.1.3
The comment of request No. 11813 dated June 23, 2023, clause 1.3.12.2 “In criterion No. 4, add the factor “аst/аcontrol” to the calculation formula, taking into account the actual weighted portions of the standard sample taken to prepare two replicates of the standard solution R2” was not addressed by the applicant.
Applicant's response “The Company considers it inadvisable to include the multiplication factor “аst/аcontrol” into the calculation formula of criteria No. 4, because direct comparison of the two separate portions of the standard sample used to prepare the standard solutions R2 has the advantage of checking the system suitability and also cross-checking the preparation of the standard solution” cannot be accepted by the Expert Institution.
The approach proposed in the current version of the section is methodologically incorrect, since the method of preparing standard and control standard solutions involves taking a sample of, for example “approximately 10 mg”, which in Pharmacopoeia terms means an acceptable sample of 9 to 11 mg (or a deviation of up to 20% of one sample from the second).
Thus, with a constant detector response, the discrepancy in peak areas caused only by differences in reference standard portions will exceed the established criterion, but will not characterize the suitability of the system or the correctness of preparation of the standard solution.
Accordingly, take into account the actual portions of the reference standard taken for the preparation of the standard and control standard solutions in the calculation formula of criteria No. 4.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1.1.3
Bayer apologizes for the confusion caused.
Bayer has adapted the documents accordingly so that it is clear that the exact weight must be noted and used for further calculation and evaluation. The reason why Bayer used formulation "approximately" in the documents is as follows: The "approximately" statement attempts to maintain a certain degree of freedom at the weighing step but at the same time to specify the concentration range of the solution to be prepared.
With the exact weights recorded, it is possible to carry out the corresponding comparisons accordingly.

Source:
P.5.2.01_022971798_06 - Test Procedure - Larotrectinib solution 2 % 50 mL for oral use (updated)
Normative Document (updated)

Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 2
Choice of Excipients

Hydroxypropylbetadex
In order to ensure the solubility of larotrectinib sulfate in the aqueous oral solution in the targeted pH range it was necessary to add a solubilizing agent. Hydroxypropylbetadex, complies to Ph. Eur. and USP/NF, was used here analogous to the initial ORA-SWEET®-based Larotrectinib solution 2 % for oral use for the clinical/primary stability batches.
When administered orally, cyclodextrins are considered to be generally non-toxic, as insignificant amounts are absorbed due to their bulky nature. When taken at large doses, cyclodextrins may cause soft stools and diarrhea 1. However, taking into account the proposed indications for the product, the benefit of including this concentration of hydroxypropylbetadex to maintain the physico-chemical properties of the formulation is considered to outweigh the risk of potential adverse effects associated with this excipient, i.e. soft stools or diarrhea.
Hydroxypropylbetadex with slight differences in molar substitution grades and in the amount of unbound betadex are used in the clinical formulation and in the commercial manufacture. The Maximum Daily Exposure of Hydroxypropylbetadex in approved drug products, as retrieved from the FDA Inactive Ingredients Database, currently amounts to 8000 mg [1]. This is more than 4-times the daily exposure to Hydroxypropylbetadex (1746 mg) when Larotrectinib 2 % solution is ingested at the max. recommended daily dose in pediatric use of 100 mg BID (200 mg/day).

Flavor Strawberry
For taste masking in pediatric preparations, especially for masking a bitter taste, flavors with a fruity aroma are accepted and preferred by children. Therefore, the taste masking agent flavor strawberry is used in combination with a sweetener to enhance the palatability of the solution. This is in line with the EMA Guideline on Formulations of choice for the pediatric population [2] where specifically strawberry flavor is recommended to mask bitter sensation arising from a medicinal product administered by the oral route.

Sucralose
One of the most important components for masking the bitter properties of a preparation is the use of a sweetener. The use of sugar (sucrose) has been dispensed with. In order to achieve sufficient sweetness of the solution, a sugar substitute (sucralose) was used here. Therefore, sucralose is used in combination with flavor strawberry for taste masking. When using sucralose, no sugar (sucrose) needs to be added for ensuring acceptable palatability of the oral solution.
Sucralose has been approved for use in pharmaceutical preparations by the Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives (JECFA) in 1990 and by the Scientific Committee on Food (SCF) of the European Commission in 2000 (now European Food Safety Authority (EFSA)). In 2016 EFSA noted that the use of sucralose in foods for special purposes in children aged from 1 to 3 years would not be of safety concern. Sucralose has been extensively studied and more than 110 safety studies were reviewed by FDA in approving the use of sucralose as a general purpose sweetener for food (21 CFR 172.831).
For Sucralose a WHO-established acceptable daily intake (ADI) of 0-15 mg/kg exists [3] (WHO-defined ADIs cover children older than 16 weeks of age) [4]. The recommended dose of Vitrakvi in pediatric patients is based on body surface area (100 mg/m² BID), however, the daily dose is limited to, at maximum, 100 mg BID Vitrakvi (200 mg/day). This dose would lead to a maximum daily ingestion of 150 mg Sucralose by a child at the maximum pediatric recommended dose, i.e. a child with a total body surface area of ≥1 m². A child with approx. 1 m² body surface area (ca. 6-12 y; cp. EFSA 2022 [5]) would probably not have a body weight less than 10 kg, thus the max. daily ingested amount of Sucralose of 150 mg is covered with the WHO ADI.

Sodium Citrate
Sodium citrate is generally used and accepted as an acid regulator in pharmaceutical preparations. It was used in the development of the larotrectinib solution for adjusting the pH value to the desired value.

Citric Acid
Citric acid is commonly used excipient in oral solutions and accepted for pH-adjustment purposes.
Citric acid is used during the manufacturing process to adjust the pH of Larotrectinib solution 2 % 50 mL for oral use into specification only in case the pH is out of the specified pH-range.

Sodium Benzoate
Sodium benzoate is used in Larotrectinib solution 2 % 50 mL for oral use as a preservative. The results of various microbiological studies (AET's) have shown effectiveness for sodium benzoate and potassium sorbate. Based on the prior knowledge it was decided to use the sodium benzoate for formulation development.
Sodium Benzoate is known as a generally safe food additive, e.g. in the US (21CFR184.1733) and in the EU (Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008). Additionally, the WHO established an ADI of 0-5 mg/kg for Sodium Benzoate [6] (WHO-defined ADIs cover children of more than 16 weeks of age) [4]. The recommended dose of Vitrakvi in pediatric patients is based on body surface area (100 mg/m² BID), however, the daily dose is limited to, at maximum, 100 mg BID Vitrakvi (200 mg/day). This maximum dose would lead to a maximum daily ingestion of 20 mg Sodium Benzoate by a child at the maximum pediatric recommended dose, i.e. a child with a total body surface area of ≥1 m². A child with approx. 1 m² body surface area (ca. 6-12 y; EFSA 20225) would probably not have a body weight less than 10 kg, thus the max. daily ingested amount of Sodium Benzoate of 20 mg is covered with the WHO ADI.

Purified Water
Purified water is used as solvent for the aqueous solution. Purified water was selected as it is a standard solvent commonly employed in oral solution dosage forms. Clinical trial batches and the primary stability batches were manufactured using water for injections. The technical batches were manufactured with purified water. Since the standard for the production of oral solutions is purified water, it was decided to use this water quality for the commercial-scale manufacturing of Larotrectinib solution 2 % 50 mL for oral use.

The immunochemical properties of aflibercept, including effector function activity and FcγR binding, are dependent on the primary structure and post-translational modifications of the molecule which are established during production in the bioreactor and downstream purification. Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL and Aflibercept solution 40 mg/mL share the same manufacturing process up through drug substance intermediate (DSI), thus, in vitro characterization of these attributes referenced from Aflibercept solution 40 mg/mL are applicable for Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL as well. The extended characterization of Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL (Formulated Drug Substance (FDS) reported in CTD section S.3.1.01, was consistent with historical data for DSI and Aflibercept solution 40 mg/mL demonstrating no significant differences in biochemical and structural attributes (including glycan profile) which could theoretically impact immunochemical properties. The immunochemical similarity of Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL is further supported by release potency testing which utilizes the same reference standard as Aflibercept solution 40 mg/mL demonstrating similarity from a target binding and activity perspective.

For information, the CTD section S.3.1.01 from the original Aflibercept solution 40 mg/mL registration is enclosed.

Question/Consideration: Question 3
Answer/Response:
Virus removal studies for aflibercept were performed in qualified small-scale models which are representative of the PA9 Raheen manufacturing site. The study reports are included in CTD Section A.2.03.
At-scale manufacturing site-specific virus removal verification studies are not performed, as it would require introduction of viruses into a GMP-approved facility.
Small-scale studies were performed, and they were determined to be fully representative of both the Rensselaer and Raheen manufacturing processes. During the DSI technology transfer from PA5 Rensselaer to PA9 Raheen, a gap assessment was performed and the identified gaps were assessed and mitigation strategies were employed. The assessment concluded that the non-identical hardware and manufacturing equipment at PA9 Raheen and in PA5 Rensselaer were functionally equivalent, see CTD section S.2.6.01. The only two gaps with potential impact to viral clearance were the control mechanism of the virus filter inlet pressure, and the bed height variability due to different chromatography column packing, that may lead to differences in linear velocity and column protein load. There was no change to the production process itself or process parameters, which are the same at both sites.
The equipment difference of the virus filter inlet pressure control mechanism was mitigated through control optimizations and both systems maintain robust operation below the defined pressure maximum. Furthermore, the parameter is classified as a CPP (Critical Process Parameter) and is closely controlled and monitored through review of the data historian as part of the Master Batch Record in PA9 Raheen and within the in-process monitoring program.
The impact of bed height variability on column protein load was mitigated by changing the manufacturing documentation to use the actual bed height for column loading calculations. The potential minor linear velocity variability was further assessed by Regeneron based on platform data and published literature, and concluded to not have any significant impact on viral clearance. The amount of buffers going through the columns is not impacted by the bed height variability as these buffer amounts are controlled by the equipment and calculated per actual column volume (CV).
The changes implemented to mitigate both gaps had no impact on the validity of the small scale models. Therefore the viral clearance data in CTD section A.2.03 is valid for both the Rensselaer PA5 and Raheen PA9 DSI manufacturing sites.

In addition, historical DSI data sets used for poolability analyses are included in the submitted S.4.5.01.

SE-UPLC
After careful evaluation of all currently available results, Bayer agrees to set the SE-UPLC specification of FDS at ≥ 98.0% for main peak and ≤ 2.0% for aggregate. The SE-UPLC acceptance criteria in the associated standard operating procedures for reference standard material will also be updated to ≥ 98.0% for main peak and ≤ 2.0% for aggregate once the corresponding SE-UPLC updates have been made effective in the associated product specifications.
Additional justification of specification for CE-SDS and SE-UPLC is included in response to Question 5A.

Endotoxin
The Endotoxin content acceptance criterion of ≤ 0.2 EU/mL is set based on regulatory safety criteria for intraocular fluids, process capability, and is in alignment with the clinical specification. The regulatory safety criteria for intraocular fluids is based on USP <771> Ophthalmic Product-Quality Tests, which states that the Endotoxin limit is not more than 2.0 EU/dose/eye for injected drug products. The endotoxin acceptance criteria of ≤ 0.2 EU/mL was selected based on guidance presented in U.S. Food & Drug Administration (FDA) document Endotoxin Testing Recommendations for Single-Use Intraocular Ophthalmic Devices. The recommendations within this guidance document state that the endotoxin limit for release testing is ≤ 0.2 EU/mL.
All manufactured batches of FDS exhibit bacterial Endotoxin levels of < 0.05 EU/mL. Taking the maximum Endotoxin level detected (<0.05 EU/mL, and assuming a value of 0.05 EU/mL), the maximum EU/dose/eye would be 0.0035 EU/dose/eye (with dose of 8mg/70 µL of aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL). Taking the maximum allowable Endotoxin level based on the specification (0.2 EU/mL), the EU/dose/eye would be 0.014, well below the 2.0 EU/dose/eye stated by USP <771>.

A2.

Host Cell DNA (HCD)
CHO DNA levels are measured on the DSI specification and are held to the acceptance criteria of ≤ 2.0 pg CHO DNA/mg Aflibercept. This specification was set based on historical DSI release data. Process validation and batch analysis data shows that there is no additional clearance of CHO DNA from the SEC step during the FDS purification process. The acceptable limit of residual DNA set by the FDA and other global regulatory agencies is 10 ng per medicinal dose.
Clearance at the DSI level was demonstrated, but a worse-case calculation demonstrated that the maximum amount that could theoretically be present in the FDS, assuming no additional clearance and no additional sources of residual DNA, is 35.28 pg of CHO DNA per dose. This value is well below the 10 ng per medicinal dose limit. Therefore, CHO DNA removal is well below the acceptable limits in the FDS manufacturing process and routine testing is not required.
An overview of CHO DNA content for Aflibercept drug substance and intermediate batches is available in CTD section S.2.4.06.

Protein A
Protein A is a potential leachable from the Protein-A Sepharose resin used during the affinity chromatography step of aflibercept purification. Leaching of the protein A ligand is expected to be low and subsequent purification steps are expected to clear Protein A. To assess this, protein A was tested in 194 DSI lots and all of the results are below the LOQ of the method as described in S.2.4.06.
rProtein A results of DSI manufactured lots are available in CTD section S.2.4.06.
Although clearance of Protein A ligand is established, if Protein A is present in FDS, the final concentration can be calculated using the worst-case LOQ observed in the historical lots assessed (3 ppm or 0.003 μg Protein A per mg aflibercept). Assuming no additional clearance during the FDS purification steps, the maximum amount of Protein A that could theoretically be delivered would be 0.053 μg Protein A per dose. An ADE for Protein A of 0.4 μg per day was recommended by a certified toxicologist in a Toxicological Risk Assessment prepared for Regeneron. Since the Protein-A Sepharose resin is not used after the DSI affinity chromatography step, there is no additional risk of Protein A leachate that can be introduced to the product and routine testing is not required.

Sialic acid content testing is included on the DSI specification. An analysis was performed across different formulations and product stages (DSI, final concentrated pool (FCP), FDS, DP) to show that sialic acid content does not change during processing from DSI to FDS to DP. The results of the study are reported in CTD section S.4.5.01. and confirm that the practical difference between the different formulations is quantifiably zero, and testing at the FDS stage is considered superfluous.

Oligosaccharide Profile
Oligosaccharide profile testing is included on the DSI specification. An analysis was performed across different formulations and product stages (DSI, FCP, FDS, DP) to show that the oligosaccharide profile does not change during processing from DSI to FDS to DP. The results of the study are provided in CTD section S.4.5.01 and confirm that the practical difference between the different formulations is quantifiably zero, and testing at the FDS stage is considered superfluous.

B.
A Low Endotoxin Recovery (LER) study evaluated the effects of storage at a refrigerated temperature and at room temperature on recovery of Endotoxin in Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL formulated drug substance (FDS) test samples. Table 2 provides the test data for the spiked samples held at room temperature (22.5 °C ± 2.5 °C) for 7 days (168 hours). Table 3 provides the test data for the spiked samples held at refrigerated temperature (2 – 8 °C) for 14 days (336 hours).
The values for each time point (Tx) were calculated to determine the recovery of Endotoxin when compared to the equivalent timepoint of the spiked limulus amebocyte lysate (LAL) reagent water (LRW) control to determine change of endotoxin recovery over time at room and refrigerated temperatures. Acceptance criteria was defined as sample recovery being within 50-200% of the recovery calculation to be considered passing and low Endotoxin recovery was defined as two consecutive time points in which Endotoxin recovery is less than 50%.
The results show no impact to endotoxin recovery for the study durations for both room temperature and refrigerated temperature storage.

Question/Consideration: Question 5
Answer/Response:
A.
Further justification for Endotoxin, reduced and non-reduced CE-SDS, and SE-UPLC acceptance criteria are provided below along with representative CE-SDS electropherograms and SE-UPLC chromatograms with peak IDs labeled.

Endotoxin
The acceptance criterion of < 0.4 EU/mL for Endotoxin was set to ensure consistency between Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL in vial for intravitreous injection and the approved product Aflibercept solution 40 mg/mL in vial for intravitreous injection.
Thereby, the justification for the acceptance criteria for both drug products is based on the Endotoxin limit of < 0.2 E.U./kg for parenteral intrathecal products, which is provided in Ph. Eur. Monograph 5.1.10 and USP <85>. The justification of specification was only adapted in accordance with the dose volume of 70 µL/eye for Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL in contrast to 50 µL/eye for Aflibercept solution 40 mg/mL.
The calculation has been performed as follows:
The proposed endotoxin limit of < 0.4 EU/mL for the drug product combined with the injection volume of 70 µL leads to 0.028 EU per injection as worst case. Considering a conservative patient’s body mass of 45 kg leads to 0.028 EU/45 kg = 0.000622 EU/kg body mass.
The compendial limit of < 0.2 EU/kg is therefore around 320 times higher than the worst case scenario described above. (0.2 EU/kg / 0.000622 EU/kg = 321.43). The limit of < 0.4 EU/mL is therefore considered justified for Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL.
For Aflibercept 40 mg/mL the limit is about 450 times lower than the maximum value for parenteral intrathecal products considering a 50 µL injection volume and also a conservative body mass of 45 kg.
In conclusion, the limit of < 0.4 EU/mL results for both products in a very high safety margin compared to the allowable maximum Endotoxin content for parenteral intrathecal products as defined in compendial monographs.

Reduced CE-SDS
The reduced CE-SDS purity and LMW release and end-of-shelf-life (EOSL) acceptance criteria for DSI and FDS are aligned (≥ 92.5% and ≤ 7.5%, respectively). This is supported by the poolability analysis provided in CTD section S.4.5.01 as well a lack of change observed for DSI and FDS under the frozen long-term storage conditions. The DP release acceptance criteria for purity and LMW are also aligned with DSI and FDS (≥ 92.5% and ≤ 7.5%, respectively), because the DP manufacturing process is not expected to impact LMW species.
Based on further evaluation of DP long-term storage stability data, Bayer agrees to tighten the reduced CE-SDS Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL DP EOSL specification:
• for purity from ≥ 91.0 to ≥ 91.5%, and
• for total LMW from ≤ 9.0 to ≤ 8.5%.
The tightened DP EOSL criteria are supported by the maximum observed decrease in purity and concomitant increase in LMW (by 1%) under the long-term storage condition (5 °C) through the 24-month shelf-life. Therefore, the tightened DP EOSL criteria for purity and LMW are 1% wider than the DP release criteria. It needs to be noted that this estimated decrease in purity and concomitant increase in LMW is based on a limited data set where only n=3 stability studies reached 24 months so far as shown in Figure 1. A notably higher number of stability studies over the next years is required to derive a more robust estimate of the change across the shelf-life and to carefully evaluate whether a further tightening of the EOSL criteria can be applied. Furthermore, it needs to be considered that the manufacturing variability can, in principle, generate batch release results of up to 92.5% purity and 7.5% LMW in the future. A respective safety margin across the shelf-life is therefore required and any further tightening of the EOSL criteria, e.g. to use the release specification acceptance criteria also as EOSL criteria is therefore not considered to be supported by data at this point in time.
Importantly, the LMW levels observed at DP EOSL do not correlate with a decrease in potency as potency remains largely unchanged through 24 months of long-term storage (Figure 1). Additionally, when reduced CE-SDS purity and LMW levels exceed the DP EOSL criteria under the stress stability condition at 1.0 month (37 °C, Figure 2), potency by bioassay results are not expected to fall outside the EOSL criterion (60 – 140%) until 2.8 months (extrapolated based on slope). Therefore, although fragmentation occurs in the vascular endothelial growth factor receptor (VEGFR)-1 domain, which may impact target binding, the reduced CE-SDS purity and LMW acceptance criteria control the level of LMW such that potency is maintained within the bioassay acceptance criteria.
Release as well as shelf life acceptance criteria are reflected in the LAF in addition.
The results described above were generated with the validated reduced CE-SDS test method, which is used for release and stability testing per the specification. The LMW results provided as part of extended characterization were generated with a reduced tryptic peptide mapping method; therefore, the LMW levels from the two methods cannot be directly compared.
A representative reduced CE-SDS electropherogram (with labeled peaks) for Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL DP at release is provided in Figure 3.

Non-Reduced CE-SDS
The non-reduced CE-SDS purity release and EOSL acceptance criteria for FDS are aligned (≥ 97.5%). This is supported by the poolability analysis provided in CTD section S.4.5.01 as well as the lack of change observed for DSI and FDS under the frozen long-term storage conditions. The DP release acceptance criterion for purity is aligned with the DSI and FDS, because the DP manufacturing process is not expected to impact LMW species. The DP EOSL criteria for purity (≥ 96.5%) accounts for the maximum observed change (0.51%) under the DP long-term storage condition (5 °C) through the 24-months shelf-life (Figure 4).
Release as well as shelf life acceptance criteria are reflected in the LAF in addition.
Importantly, the purity levels observed at DP EOSL do not correlate with a decrease in potency as potency remains largely unchanged through 24 months of long-term storage (Figure 4). Additionally, when non-reduced CE-SDS purity levels exceed the DP EOSL criterion under the stress stability condition at 2.5 months (37 °C, Figure 5), potency by bioassay results are not expected to fall outside the EOSL criterion (60 – 140%) until 2.8 months (extrapolated based on slope). This analysis supports that the non-reduced CE-SDS purity acceptance criterion controls the aflibercept purity level such that potency is maintained within the bioassay acceptance criteria.
A representative non-reduced CE-SDS electropherogram (with labeled peaks) for aflibercept 8 mg DP at release is provided in Figure 6.

SE-UPLC
The FDS release and EOSL criteria for SE-UPLC main peak and aggregate are set at ≥ 98% and ≤ 2%, respectively, and are supported by historical FDS manufacturing process capability and calculation of 95%/99% tolerance intervals as described in CTD section S.4.5.01, as well as the lack of change observed for FDS under the frozen long-term storage condition. The DP release acceptance criteria for main peak and aggregate are set at ≥ 97% and ≤ 3%, respectively, due to a 0.77% increase in aggregate during the DP manufacturing process. The DP EOSL acceptance criteria for main peak and aggregate are set at ≥ 94% and ≤ 5%, respectively, to account for the maximum observed change (1.4%) observed during DP long-term storage (5 °C) through the 24 months shelf-life (Figure 7). Main peak has a greater change on stability compared to aggregate due to the detection of LMW species emerging at later time points. This, coupled with the lack of historical data, led to the 3% increase in the DP EOSL acceptance criteria for main peak.
Based on further evaluation of FDS and DP long-term storage data, Bayer agrees to tighten the SE-UPLC aflibercept 8 mg FDS and DP release and EOSL specification (Table 4).

Bayer would like to clarify that Container Closure Integrity Testing (CCIT) on the PPQ lots was performed using the dye ingress method, and all results passed (results are documented in CTD section P.3.5.01 as “no dye detected”. The dye ingress method used is based on USP <1207.2> Integrity Leak Testing Technologies. With the dye ingress method, aflibercept DP vials are placed into a vacuum vessel and are completely covered with a blue dye (0.1% methylene blue) under vacuum (-18 to -22 in Hg) for 30 minutes and then at atmospheric pressure for an additional 30 minutes. In addition to a positive and a negative control, a system suitability control was prepared by inserting a 20 µm microcapillary tube through the vial stopper and resultant vials were subjected to dye ingress testing. After cleaning the vials to remove residual dye, samples were analyzed for the presence of dye by measuring the absorbance at 660 nm. The sensitivity of the dye ingress method to be able to capture container closure failures using breached vials is 20 microns.
In addition, CCIT was performed during the crimp pressure testing as part of the supportive validation studies using the mass extraction method. Section 4.6 of CTD section P.3.5.01 has been updated accordingly to reflect this clarification. The mass extraction method is performed based on USP <1207.2> Integrity Leak Testing Technologies. Test articles are subjected to a high vacuum, causing ejection of molecular mass from any breaches in the test article. Flow values above the pre-determined threshold value are considered failures. A result below the pre-determined threshold is considered to have no leak detected. During assay validation studies, the sensitivity of the mass extraction method to be able to capture container closure failures was determined to be 5 µm using breached vials.
As per the procedure, a representative sample (similar in size to the test article designed to represent a sample free of defects), is used as a negative control. A Calibrated Leak Orifice (Calibrated leak device (5 µm) installed inside the mass extraction instrument) is turned on to mimic a 5 µm defect and used as a positive control. During the study, 30 vials were analyzed at each crimp pressure (2.0 Bar, 3.0 Bar and, 4.0 Bar) and CCIT was performed to ensure adequate seals between the vial and the stopper. Crimp pressure is considered suitable if container closure integrity testing of all 30 vials is integral (no leaks detected). All results passed, and the detailed results of this study are provided CTD section P.3.5.01.

Question/Consideration: The Sponsor indicates that results from the FDS PPQ CHO HCP retain testing demonstrated additional reduction of CHO HCP over the SEC and ultrafiltration/ diafiltration (UF/DF) unit operations, however, the LOQs for the CHO HCP assays differ between the DSI and FDS samples, making direct comparison of the results difficult. Please explain why the LOQs differ and demonstrate that the assays used between the two sample types are comparable.
Answer/Response:
The limit of quantification (LOQ) for CHO HCP is calculated each time the method is performed using the optimum sample testing concentration (mg/mL) as determined during method development/validation, and a spike recovery correction factor generated each assay run based on standard curve (ng/mL) (where 100% spike recovery corresponds to 1, 99% corresponds to .99 etc.) as follows:
LOQ = 1 ÷ (spike recovery correction factor × sample testing concentration)
where 1 is the lowest point on the standard curve
Aflibercept intermediate and aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL formulated drug substance (FDS) have different total protein content (mg/mL) and formulations as denoted in Table 1. To mitigate any matrix interference caused by the formulation there are different optimal testing concentrations for each presentation. During assay validation activities, the optimum sample testing concentration for aflibercept DSI was determined to be 0.25 mg/mL. When the testing was initiated for aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL FDS Process Performance Qualification (PPQ) testing, the optimum sample testing concentration for FDS samples was determined to be 4 mg/mL. As a result of the different total protein contents and optimum sample testing concentration for aflibercept DSI and aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL FDS, each presentation has a different LOQ.

All results were generated using the same test method and were within the specification acceptance criterion of ≤ 20 ppm. While the results presented for aflibercept DSI in CTD Section 3.2.S.3.2 are below the DSI LoQ of < 4 ppm at the time of testing, data presented in CTD Section S.2.4.06 demonstrate that DSI (P3) batches have had recoverable CHO HCP levels of 3-17.5 ppm, below the specification ≤ 20 ppm. Comparing these to the 0.6 -1.0 ppm seen during PPQ of the aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL FDS (LoQ < 0.2 ppm) demonstrates the capacity for reduction over the process. Additionally, there are no introduction points of CHO protein between aflibercept DSI release and aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL FDS release. The aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL FDS process also includes a SEC column designed to clear further impurities through exclusion by having set collection absorbance start and stop points.

Question/Consideration:
In relation to the container closure system:
Regarding the container closure integrity study, please provide a summary including the following information:
• The number of samples tested
• A summary of the dye ingress method
• Confirmation that positive control samples (i.e. vials that have been intentionally compromised) were immersed with the test vials to verify the test conditions were suitable, or that the dye ingress method has been suitably validated including positive controls.
Answer/Response:
The Sponsor would like to clarify that Container Closure Integrity Testing (CCIT) on the PPQ lots was performed using the dye ingress method (results are documented in CTD section P.3.5.01). After the PPQ lots were tested, the CCIT was revised and changed to a non-destructive mass extraction method. This method was used to complete the CCIT during the supportive validation studies. Both the dye ingress and the mass extraction methods are able to capture container closure failures with acceptable sensitivity.
CTD section P.3.5.01 has been updated to reflect this clarification.
Description of Dye Ingress Method Used for Process Performance Qualification Testing
The dye ingress method used is based on USP <1207.0> Integrity Leak Testing Technologies. With the dye ingress method, 30 samples per sample set of aflibercept DP vials are placed into a vacuum vessel and are completely covered with a blue dye (0.1% methylene blue) under vacuum (-18 to -22 in Hg) for 30 minutes and then at atmospheric pressure for an additional 30 minutes. In addition to a positive and a negative control, a system suitability control was prepared by inserting a 20 µm microcapillary tube through the vial stopper and resultant vials were subjected to dye ingress testing. After cleaning the vials to remove residual dye, samples were analyzed for the presence of dye by measuring the absorbance at 660 nm.
Description and Results for the CCI testing using Mass Extraction Method during  Supportive Validation Studies
The container closure integrity test is a mass extraction method performed in accordance with USP <1207> Package Integrity Leak Test Technologies. Acceptable performance of the mass extraction method is ensured by the following assay validity criterion: The standard must give a passing result with the orifice turned off and a failing result with the orifice turned on. Container closure integrity results are reported as “no leak detected”.
As per the procedure, a representative sample (similar in size to the test article designed to represent a sample free of defects), is used as a negative control at each crimp cap pressure. A Calibrated Leak Orifice (Calibrated leak device [5 µm] installed inside the mass extraction instrument) is turned on to mimic a 5 µm defect and used as a positive control for each crimp cap pressure.
During the crimping study, 30 vials were analyzed at each crimp pressure (2.0 Bar, 3.0 Bar and, 4.0 Bar). Crimp pressure is considered suitable if container closure integrity testing shows that all 30 vials are integral (no leaks detected). All results passed and the detailed results of this study are provided CTD section P.3.5.01.

Answer/Response:
There are several required actions as a result of a failed media fill. They include, but are not limited to the following:
• A deviation will be opened to assess all batches filled during the media fill.
• Investigation will determine most probable root cause and implement appropriate correct measures.
• Any product batches manufactured since the prior passing media will be included in the investigation.
• The microorganism will be identified to the species level.
• A sufficient number of successful, consecutive repeat media fills will be conducted in order to demonstrate that the process has been returned to a state of control. All failures will require a minimum of three consecutive media fills, excepting growth promotion failures which only require 1.
The sponsor confirms that requalification of filling lines following media failure is compliant with ISO13408-1/Amd 1:2013. This standard requires repeating initial qualification when an aseptic process simulation yields contaminated units. Catalent's policy also requires such repeat qualification.

This means that excursions from the approved storage conditions are not permitted. Should such a temperature excursion occur, the TGA should be informed before the batch is released as detailed in the guideline Temperature excursions of biological medicines under Deviations from approved storage conditions.
Answer/Response:
At the time of initial submission data from a cycling study was not available. Meanwhile, a cycling study was initiated.
Cycling studies to investigate 3 aflibercept drug product (aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL in vial) lots 8345600001, 8345600002, and 8345600003 are currently ongoing. Data are recorded at pre-cycling conditions (zero time results) and then exposed to the cycling conditions. A single cycle consists of 24 hours at -20 °C followed by 24 hours at 25 °C 60% RH. Samples were exposed to three rounds of cycling, followed by a fourth round of cycling for 24 hours at -20 °C followed by 8 hours at 30 °C. All tested parameters are within specification after this cycling and as well as after additional storage for 24 hours (results tabulated as “0+1 days storage at 25°C”) and 48 hours (results tabulated as “0+2 days storage at 25°C”) at 25 °C. The post-cycling samples are currently stored at 2-8 °C and will be tested again after 24 months. The available data is summarized in CTD section P.8.3.04.
On the basis of available data the Sponsor can evaluate temperature excursions from the approved storage condition according to internal standards and upfront information of TGA prior to release is not considered necessary. The Sponsor commits to inform the TGA in case of adverse results after the 24 months testing point.

the test product across the physiologic pH 1.2-6.8 (without surfactant) and in the QC release 
medium (if different) under 3.2.P.2. Note that the batch submitted for executed BMR should 
be used for comparative dissolution profile. However, if this is not feasible then submit the 
COA and the batch manufacturing record of the batch used to demonstrate the comparative 
dissolution profile.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 4:
Comparative Dissolution Testing between clinical batches used in phase 3, and commercial 
drug product batches has been performed in quality control dissolution media (HCl pH 2), as 
well as in ICH M9 guided dissolution media without addition of surfactant: HCl pH 1.2 / 
NaCl, acetate buffer pH 4.5 and phosphate buffer pH 6.8 (P.2.2.10#022950143, see below for 
results summary excerpt from document).
Results show that under all tested conditions phase 3 clinical batches and commercial drug 
product batches are comparable. Commercial drug product batches used were BXA8559 (2.5 
mg), BXA82XU (5 mg), and BXA85A3 (10 mg).
These batches are representative for the batches mentioned (BXA855B, 2.5 mg); BXA82XT, 
5 mg; BXA82SB, 10 mg), since they have the exact same composition, have been 
manufactured using the exact same process parameters, and the manufacturing was 
documented in the exact same batch master record.

For more details please see P.2.2.10_022950143_01. For easy reference please find some 
figures with comparative dissolution profiles further below. Respective data tables can be 
found in the P.2.2.10 mentioned before.
Figure 1-1 shows comparison between Phase III batch (batch KM601KU) and commercial 
drug substance (batch BXA85A3) at HCl pH 1.2/NaCl.
Figure 1-2 shows comparison between Phase III batch (batch KM601KU) and commercial 
drug substance (batch BXA85A3) at HCl pH 2.
Figure 1-3 shows comparison between Phase III batch (batch KM601KU) and commercial 
drug substance (batch BXA85A3) at acetate buffer pH 4.5.
Figure 1-4 shows comparison between Phase III batch (batch KM601KU) and commercial 
drug substance (batch BXA85A3) at phosphate buffer pH 6.8.
The clinical batch KM601KU will be presented in R.3.3.02_022278660_01, whereas 
commercial batch BXA85A3 (10 mg) can be found in executed batch record 
R.3.3.01_022219724_01. For a clear understanding of the details shown in the before 
mentioned R.3.3.01 please use additionally batch record master R.3.1.02_021743174_01 (10 
mg) provided as English translation.

Question/Consideration:
Question 1
For API levonorgestrel micronized, provide an explanation of how API microbiological purity 
is controlled (control for microbiological purity is required due to the Ph. EAEU requirements 
(2.3.1.2. Requirements to the microbiological purity of drug products, drug substances and 
excipients used for their production), State Pharmacopoeia of the Russian Federation (Ph. Rus 
XIV), GPM 1.2.4.0002.18 “Microbiological purity” and general monographs on 
microbiological purity of leading foreign pharmacopoeias) or provide a justification 
confirming that there is no need to control the pharmaceutical substance for the 
"Microbiological purity" parameter in accordance with the Decision of the Board of the 
Eurasian Economic Commission No. 151 "On approval of the guidelines for the preparation 
of a regulatory document on the quality of a medicinal product" dated 07 September 2018.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1 (3.2.S.4.1):
According to ICH Q6A decision tree #6 a microbial test is not required since levonorgestrel is 
not capable of supporting microbial growth or viability. Therefore, microbiological tests are 
not included in the drug substance specification of levonorgestrel.
The manufacturing process of levonorgestrel is monitored for potential microbiological 
contamination on a regular basis and is considered for release. Batch results are provided in 
the attached S.4.4.11-01 which demonstrate that no microbial contamination is observed, and 
which support the claim that levonorgestrel is not capable of supporting microbial growth or 
viability.
Source:  S.4.4.11-01 Additional Batch-Related Information / Levonorgestrel micronized
drug substance (#021111075; new)

Question/Consideration:
Question 2
Process validation report of three batches (Levonorgestrel 20microgram/24hr Intra Uterine 
Delivery System)
The PV data is found of 2011. Please clarify- 
l. Weather any change is equipment in last 11 years and leading to re-validation, please clarify 
and justify? 
2. Any PAC (mfg. process / batch size increase or decrees / packing etc.) in the said RC  
3. Re-validation SOP is to be provided.  
4. The assembly of the IUSes is Mechanically done: or manually done?  
5. Is there any change in sterilization site at Belgium wrt technical process, equipment's.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 2 (3.2.P.3.5):
1. A new version of TRD P.3.5.01 (please see P.3.5.01-02) is provided with updated 
validation data. Separate steps of the manufacturing process of Mirena (preparation of core 
elastomer mixture, extrusion step, post-curing step and the subsequent assembly and 
packaging steps) are usually validated separately, when a new equipment will be taken into 
production use. For example, if a new assembly machine is acquired, only the assembly step 
is validated to verify the acceptable result, comparable with the previous equipment, of this 
process step. Of course, the quality of the finished product is also evaluated in this context. 
All the new equipment taken into use during the recent years are operating in the authorized 
ranges of process parameters and are producing similar product compared with the product 
produced using the preceding machine. These changes have not resulted into changes in the 
quality characteristics of Mirena IUS. Therefore, the start of using the new equipment, and the 
process validations performed with them, have been covered by the company’s Quality 
Assurance system without the need to submit regulatory variations.
2. No PACs have been provided to any Health Authority concerning the manufacturing 
process or batch size or package of Mirena IUS.
3. The processes used for the manufacture of medicinal products must be validated. 
Validation of manufacturing processes is carried out in accordance with internal SOPs.
All changes to the manufacturing procedures must be checked with regard to their 
revalidation requirement. The goal of effective change management is to identify and evaluate 
the revalidation needs of the processes. Manufacturing processes as such are not subject to 
periodic revalidations, except for the sterilization process, which is revalidated annually.
The manufacturing process validation status monitoring is a continuous process. The 
validation status of manufacturing processes is performed by Ongoing Process Verification 
(OPV), by continuous monitoring of trends and process performance of critical quality 
attributes and in-process control results. The validity of the process and possible suggestions 
for improvements are documented in the annual evaluation. Need for revalidation  can also be 
identified in the handling of deviations and CAPA operations.
Sterilization process of Mirena is revalidated annually.
4. The assembly process is currently performed mechanically only.
5. Two alternative ethylene oxide sterilization line sizes at Sterigenics Belgium for the 
sterilization of the product have been available (16 and 32 pallet lines) with cycle #44 for a 
long time already. There is no changes to that.
Source:  P.3.5.01-02 Process Validation and/or Evaluation / Levonorgestrel
intrauterine delivery system 52 mg with inserter (Mirena) (#005811029; 
changed)

Question/Consideration:
Question 4
Identification: Please add the preparation of sample solutions without reference substances to the registration specification (JX specification).
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 4:
HPTLC is used for identification of the used APIs in Progynova 1mg (estradiol valerate). The identification is done by comparing the peak spots on the HPTLC plate. Different compounds move up the plate by different speeds, based on the different attraction between the substances, the mobile phase and the stationary phase. Therefore, different compounds can be separated and this separation is used for identification. In the present case, the standard method of comigration is used. On the TLC plate is applied (a) the reference substance, whose identity we know and (b) the substance/tablet to be examined mixed with a defined content of reference substance. Solutions of (a) and (b) are applied and developed on a common TLC plate. A comparison of the retention behavior of the observed peaks is made. We expect a congruent behavior of all observed peaks, since they should be the same substances. So we expect a peak for (a) and the same for (b). In (b), the manually added reference standard should behave congruently with the substance contained in the tablet, if it is the same substance. The method of comigration is used to be able to exclude any differences or external influences on the development of the TLC plate. This has the advantage that the substance under investigation is tested against both an external (a) and internal standard (b).

According to the release (P.5.1.01#020135106) and shelf life specification (P.5.1.02#020135107) the identity testing of estradiol valerate (EV) in “Estradiol valerate sugar-coated tablet 1.0 mg (PROGYNOVA)”, using HPLC, is carried out with the help of the validated coelution method for HPLC to show “peak homogeneity for the drug substance”.

The identity testing of estradiol valerate (HPLC3) using the coelution method is described in detail in the test procedure (P.5.2.01#020135571).

Three solutions S, R2 and SR are to be prepared. The sample solution S contains a sample with the to be identified substance. The reference solution R2 contains the proposed drug substance EV. The sample solution SR is a 1:1 mixture of the sample solution S and the reference solution R2. During the identity test the sample solution S is only prepared to produce the sample solution SR.

The validated HPLC coluetion method is a state-of-the-art method for the identity testing of drug substances in drug products. Herein a sample solution SR is injected into the chromatographic system which contains the substance to be identified and a reference solution of the proposed drug substance (in this case Estradiol valerate).

If the to be identified substance is not the same as the drug substance in the reference solution (in this case estradiol valerate) two peaks would be visible in the chromatogram of the SR solution (= mixture of sample solution and reference solution). If only one peak is visible in the chromatogram of the mixture and the peak is matching in terms of peak shape to the peak of the purposed drug substance in the chromatogram of the pure reference solution R2, peak homogeneity is given and the identity is confirmed.

The advantage of the coelution method over other methods, e.g. retention time comparison, is the insensitivity of the method to the influence of the matrix of the drug product or minor changes of the chromatographic conditions during testing e.g. pressure deviations.

Question/Consideration:
Question 6
Dissolution: Provide a comparison study of multiple self-made batches for the in vitro dissolution behavior before and after the production site change, using 50 rpm, including dissolution curves and similarity comparisons.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 6:
Additional comparative dissolution data was recorded using a stirring speed of 50 rpm. Due to the poor solubility of the drug substance estradiol valerate, two approaches were included in the comparative study. First one batch from each production site was tested (n=12) in the dissolution medium water without SDS addition.
Secondly, three batches from each production site were tested in water + 0.3% SDS at 50 rpm.

In Figure 1, the obtained dissolution profiles in water (without SDS) are illustrated.
(Figure 1 table with time points and mean/c.v. values for Delpharm batch 952A and Weimar batch WEW76G.)
The dissolution profiles are visual similar. The data confirms the poor drug substance solubility, as only 3-4% are dissolved after a time of 75 minutes. Based on the high coefficients of variation, the f2-calculation was performed formally only, using the last three time points with the lowest variation of the individual values. The f2-value of 97 confirms the similarity of the dissolution profiles in water without SDS at 50 rpm.

Additionally, three individual batches of both production sites were tested in the dissolution medium water + 0.3% SDS, in order to operate under sink conditions, which is required according to USP <1092> and Ph. Eur. 5.17.1. Furthermore these dissolution profiles fulfill the evaluation criteria of the Chinese “Guidelines for CMC Change Study of Marketed Chemical Drugs (Trial)” and EMA Guideline on the Investigation of Bioequivalence CPMP/EWP/QWP/1401/98 Rev. 1 in order to calculate the f2-values.

The results are shown in Figure 2.
(Figure 2 table with time points and mean/c.v. values for Delpharm batches 952A/957A/960A and Weimar batches WEW76G/WEW76H/WEW95E.)
It can be seen, that all batches show a similar and continuous dissolution behavior, reaching the plateau of 80-100%.
The dissolution data of the three time points 30, 45 und 60 min fulfill all evaluation criteria of the above mentioned guidelines, and were used for the f2-calculation:
(f2-values table showing f2-values between 57 and 97 for batch comparisons.)
With f2-values between 57 and 97, the similarity of the dissolution profiles of all combinations of all batches could be confirmed in the dissolution medium water + 0.3% SDS.
It can be concluded, that all available data using a stirring speed of 50 rpm confirms the product equivalence based on the dissolution profile comparison & f2-evaluation in both dissolution media: water without surfactant and water with SDS.
keywords: dissolution; dissolution profile; Comparative dissolution; Dissolution Protocol; comparability testing

Question/Consideration:
Question 1
The stability acceptance criteria proposed for Purity by Reduced CE-SDS (purity and LMW) 
does not appear to be in line with the drug product (DP) stability data provided in the 
submission. Tighten the DP reduced CE-SDS stability specifications so that they better reflect 
the stability data, and update the necessary sections of the submission and the CPID-B where 
required.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1 (3.2.P.5.1, 3.2.P.5.6):
Based on further evaluation of DP long-term storage stability data, Bayer agrees to tighten the 
reduced CE-SDS Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL DP end-of-shelf-life (EOSL) 
specification:
• for purity from ≥ 91.0 to ≥ 91.5%, and
• for total LMW from ≤ 9.0 to ≤ 8.5%.
The tightened DP EOSL criteria are supported by the maximum observed decrease in purity 
and concomitant increase in LMW (by 1%) under the long-term storage condition (5 °C) 
through the 24-month shelf-life. Therefore, the tightened DP EOSL criteria for purity and 
LMW are 1% wider than the DP release criteria. It needs to be noted that this estimated 
decrease in purity and concomitant increase in LMW is based on a limited data set where only 
n=3 stability studies reached 24 months so far. A notably higher number of stability studies 
over the next years is required to derive a more robust estimate of the change across the shelf-
life and to carefully evaluate whether a further tightening of the EOSL criteria can be applied. 
Furthermore, it needs to be considered that the manufacturing variability can, in principle, 
generate batch release results of up to 92.5% purity and 7.5% LMW in the future. A 
respective safety margin across the shelf-life is therefore required and any further tightening 
of the EOSL criteria is therefore not considered to be supported by sufficient data at this point 
in time.
The CTD sections P.5.1.02-02 and P.5.6.01-02 have been updated accordingly.

Please find enclosed a statement with additional information related to QP declaration. Further, Bayer Weimar has access to the global database for audit management and to all inspection results. All responsibilities between Bayer AG and Bayer Weimar are regulated in the established Quality Assurance Agreement.

Additionally, the QP Declaration should be created according to art.º 59 of Decree Law 176/2006 and with Template for the qualified person’s (QP’s). This guideline states that the audit can be undertaken by the MIAH or corporate representative within the same group of company, in which case the auditing body column should be left blank. QAI is considered a corporate representative within the same group of companies and not a third party on behalf of the MIAH site, so the QP declaration can be considered well filled according the EMA Guideline.

Finally, the date of audit for one of the sites (Bayer AG Berlin) provided in the QP declaration expired on 19th November 2023. The new audit will take place 29th November 2023, and Bayer Weimar commits to provide and updated QP declaration once it is available.

You did not submit cycling stability data as suggested in the guideline Stability testing

Answer/Response:
Response: e000283 (0047-) - Response to questions 0047 (#5)
Summary of response:
The Sponsor has provided temperature cycling stability data to support potential 
temperature excursions of the drug product outside of the recommended storage 
temperature (please see response to Question 6 above).

Bayer Response to Question 1 (3.2.P.8.3):
In line with the cycling conditions studied and available results as reported in CTD section 
P.8.3.04-01 the following maximum cumulative excursions would be allowable during 
shipment and storage:
• Less than 96 hours between 1 and -20°C
• Less than 72 hours between 9 and 25 °C
• Less than 8 hours between 26 and 30°C
The allowed excursions are based on the following cycling conditions where a single cycle 
consisted of 24 hours at -20 °C followed by 24 hours at 25 °C 60% RH. Samples were 
exposed to three rounds of cycling, followed by a fourth round of cycling for 24 hours at -
20 °C followed by 8 hours at 30 °C. All tested parameters are within specification after the 
cycling and as well as after additional storage for 24 hours and 48 hours at 25 °C. 
Furthermore, all analyzed samples showed no significant differences for any of the purity 
results when comparing  pre-cycling and post-cycling samples.
The post-cycling samples are currently stored at 2-8 °C and will be tested again after 24 
months as well as after additional storage for 24 hours and 48 hours at 25°C following the 24 
months storage at 2-8°C. Data at the end of shelf life will become available by end of 
February 2024.

Based on the currently available data no trend towards out of specification is seen and the data 
suggest that the specification will be met also at the end of the intended shelf life of 24 
months.
As such, the sponsor would like to request for the allowable temperature excursion of:
• Less than 96 hours between 1 and -20°C
• Less than 72 hours between 9 and 25 °C
• Less than 8 hours between 26 and 30°C

Overall conclusion of Applicant: 
 
It is concluded that a potential risk exists for a contamination with N-nitrosamines in the finished product.

For both DP formulations (film-coated tablets and granules for oral suspension) a risk for 
potential nitrosamine contamination could not be excluded. The risk was identified for 
potential by-products present in the API and a potential degradation product of the API. 
Those compounds are vulnerable amines. They are covered by the specification parameter 
“any unspecified impurities”.

The manufacturing process conditions for tablets are not favourable for Nitrosamine 
formation.

Nevertheless, absence of the potential N-nitroso compounds of the respective amines, 
dimethyl-oxobutyl-oxamine, oxacarboxylic acid and chlorothiophene-hydroxymorpholinone, 
could not be proven in the risk assessment. Therefore confirmatory testing of the 
corresponding nitrosamines will be conducted with high priority including the following 
steps:
- 
Synthesis of reference material of the relevant Nitrosamine compounds
- 
Trace analytics down to the needed Acceptable Intake Limit (AI: 1500 ng/day 
according to CPCA published by EMA and other health authorities): Development of 
analytical method
- 
Validation of analytical method
- 
Confirmatory testing of representative batches
- 
Reporting on confirmatory testing upon availability of results

Compatibility studies of the proposed diluent syringe are provided with M3.2.P.2.6. Here,

reconstitute lyophilized Drug Product of 250 and 1000IU, respectively. Reconstituted solution

formats. Also here, Drug Product was reconstituted and remained in the syringe for four hours
