Response to 5.2.2
The experiment included 1.0% as an extreme scenario only, since the specified range for 
single impurities only spans < 0.1% to 0.2%. The differences between the Ph. Eur. (0.2% 
reference) and in-house tests (100% reference) at 1.0% spiking target are at most 0.1%, which 
is due to rounding effects and normal analytical variability. Due the structural homology 
between the different by-products, the results of the spiking experiment with oxaphthalimide 
and 4,5-dichloro compound are considered to be representative of all other by-products. That 
interpetation is also supported by the 6 comparison tests shown in Table 5-2 to 5-7 in P.5.3.20 
for the lowest and highest dose strengths. The limits for impurities (degradants and by-
products) were defined both historically and in the Ph. Eur. monograph without the use of 
response factors. It is not necessary to set the response factor.

Response to 5.2.3
Regarding liquid chromatography of related substances, the following changes have been 
made based on the European Pharmacopoeia RIVAROXABAN TABLETS.
・Change the test method from a standard solution using rivaroxaban standard substance to a 
solution diluted to 0.2% of the sample solution as the standard solution
・Measure all related substances, including by-products of the drug substance synthesis 
process, as individual related substances
・Change in the total amount of related substances specifications
・Delete of detectability
・Change in system performance and system repeatability
However, there are no changes to the test conditions for liquid chromatography and the 
specification for individual related substances (not more than 0.2%). The analytical method 
validation before the change is described in the application document (CTD 2.3.P.5.3.2) at the 
time of approval (June 2022) of the already approved Xarelto Tablets 2.5mg, and the 
calibration curve and Accuracy including specification value limits, repeatability and 
intermediate precision at a level equivalent to 0.05%, as well as detection limits and 
quantification limits are shown. Therefore, we think that there is no need to conduct new 
analytical method validation for the changed test method.

As described in 2.3.P.5.3.2 of Xarelto Tablets submitted at this PAA, the test results measured 
using the test method before and after the change using 2.5 mg of Xarelto Tablets and the 
results of spiking test of oxaphthalimide and 4,5-dichloro compound using the test method 
before and after the change and showed equivalent test results.
Following your instructions, we have also provided information on related substances with 
known structures below. Furthermore, as shown in the answer to this inquiry (2) 2), no 
response factor will be set.
Structure and relative retention time for Acetoxamide, bis-Oxamine-urea, Deschloro-
compound, Oxacarboxylic acid, Oxaphthalimide, 4,5-Dichloro-compound, Diamide and 
Triamide are shown in Table.

Response to 5.2.4
The method for each dose strength (2.5, 10, 15 and 20 mg coated tablets) only differs in the 
number of tablets used to prepare the test solution per test item, as explained further on. The 
nominal concentrations of the test solution are comparable, while the solvent is identical. 
Therefore, the method development is summarized in this document for all dose strengths. As 
shown in 2.3.P.5.3.2, the test conditions for liquid chromatography in the test method before 
and after the change are the same. Therefore, the specificity of each related substance 
(P.5.3.20_022966564_01, Figure 4-1) is the same as before the change, and the related 
substances (by-products) added as measurement targets can be determined using the test 
method before the change.
Since the test conditions for liquid chromatography in the test method before and after the 
change are the same, the limit of quantification of the test method after the change is 0.05%, 
which is the same as the limit of quantification shown in the test method before the change.
Test results "<0.1" shown in Comparison tests for 2.5 mg (P.5.3.20_022966564_01, Table 5-2 
to 5-4) and lot analysis (2.3.P.5.4) means less than 0.05% (below the limit of quantification), 
and actual measured values cannot be presented. In addition, test results are expressed in the 
same number of digits as the reporting threshold of 0.1% listed in the European 
Pharmacopoeia RIVAROXABAN TABLETS. The test results before and after the change 
were both below the quantification limit, so we consider that the results are equivalent.
As stated in the answer to this inquiry (1), the separation of each related substance has been 
confirmed and analytical method validation has been conducted. In the revised test method, 
all related substances including by-products in the drug substance synthesis process are 
measured as individual related substances, but the specification for any unspecified impurity 
(max. 0.2%) has not been changed and the specification for total impurities has been tightened
from max. 0.5% to max. 0.3%. Therefore, we consider that the revised test method is a test 
method that conducts more stringent evaluations.
Furthermore, the lowest (2.5 mg) and highest (20 mg) dose strength were selected as a 
bracketing approach. As explained in section 1 of TRD P.5.3.20, the HPLC method is 
identical for all dose strengths. As a result, a bracketing approach is considered to be 
scientifically justified.
Response to 5.3.1
The purpose of filtration in this test is to prevent damage on the HPLC system by undissolved 
particles, such as particles of the tablet which can be present in the test solution of the vessel. 
The filtration principle itself is not important and does not affect the determination of the test.
Filters such as a pore size of 0.45 μm RC filter , are used for the filtration.  Filtration using 
them is a standard method for dissolution test and is used by Bayer in a variety of products.
Therefore, we think that it is scientifically appropriate not to include the filtration principle in 
the test method.

Response to 5.3.2
The plate number is not set in Ph.Eur. Rivaroxaban tablets. In 
2.2.46.CHROMATOGRAPHIC SEPARATION TECHNIQUES, peak symmetry is defined as 
0.8 to 1.8. Plate number is not set in the application form as the approval matter and 
symmetry factor is set as 0.8 to 1.8, so we think that the separation performance of the system 
used will be properly ensured and will not affect the measurement results.
Response to 5.4.1
The actual data of the resolution was 5.4 (T.02.47_022970955_01). Japanese pharmacopoeia 
says that "Complete separation means the resolution of not less than 1.5". Since  the complete 
separation is confirmed between oxaphthalimide and rivaroxaban, the system to be used is 
ensured  and it does not affect the measurement results.

Responses to 5.4.2
Regarding the system performance after the change, the actual data of the resolution between 
oxaphthalimide and rivaroxaban was 5.4.  Furthermore, chromatograms related to system 
performance  are shown in Figures 1. See Chromatogram for the system performance (Fig 13-
3 of T.02.47_022970955_01)

Responses to 5.5
Regarding the change from in-house method to a test method that complies with the European 
Pharmacopoeia for the drug product, there are no major changes in the principles and test 
conditions of the test method, so the technical transfer will not be performed to the domestic 
testing sites. We are planning to perform the verification.

Question/Consideration: Considering that the drug is packaged in a multidose package (opaque HDPE plastic bottle 120 mL), the company must submit a stability study in use, in accordance with Section IV of RDC No. 318/2019, which describes the criteria to be followed in this type of study.
Answer/Response:
We hereby would like to further justify the shelf-life extension of the product Larotrectinib sulfate capsule 100 mg, from 24 months to 36 months, based on technical reasons and data from post-approval commitment.
Our request is motivated by the results obtained from long-term stability studies, which were conducted in accordance with applicable guidelines and regulations. However, we recognize that the in-use stability study, which would comprise stability data under climate zone IVb conditions, has not yet been carried out. Currently the available data for in-use stability study for this product was conducted under conditions of 25 °C (± 2 °C) / 60 % RH (± 5 % RH), according to the ICH guidelines Q1A (R2) ‘’Stability Testing of New Substances and Products’’ and Q6A ‘’Specifications: Test Procedures and Acceptance Criteria for New Drug Substances and New Drug Products: Chemical Substances’’, which the data shows that all results remain well within specification during in-use after first opening of the container after 24 months of storage.
The reason for the current request to extend the shelf life without in-use stability data at 36 months stems from the nature of our product, Larotrectinib sulfate capsule, which long term stability studies show to be very stable (P.8.3.01_022972764_05 and P.8.3.01_022973138_03).
The long-term stability study has been completed up to and including 36 months. The study protocol was not designed for in-use testing at shelf life and therefore the number of samples required for in use testing were not available.
Additionally, the comprehensive stability studies have demonstrated that the API maintains exceptional stability even when subjected to extreme environmental conditions, including variations in temperature and humidity. We have conducted rigorous testing protocols that adhere to internationally recognized guidelines and standards to ensure the reliability and robustness of our findings.
We understand the importance of the in-use stability study to confirm the quality and safety of the product under real conditions of use. To this end, we are committed to initiating a new in-use stability study during the current year with the intention of collecting relevant data. However, it is crucial to note that the complete data from this study will only be available after three years from the start of the new study, in accordance with ANVISA guidelines. We would like to assure ANVISA that our company is committed to the integrity and quality of its product and to mitigate any concerns and ensure that the product meets safety and efficacy standards throughout its life cycle, we are committed to conduct this additional in-use stability study as post-approval commitment.

Please find attached the complete company’s rational in the document: Shelf-life extension – Larotrectinib sulfate capsule.

Source:
Declaration Larotrectinib Capsules (Shelf-life extension)

Question/Consideration:
Question 4 – ES
Regarding dissolution, there are some issues pending (see below). Taking into account the 
status of the product (developed according to FDA and already marketed in third countries), 
the assessor would accept amending the spec and the method post-approval (by VAR):
4.1 Limit
The table of specifications should be amended in the following terms: A second earlier time-
point should be included in the specification (release and shelf life).
4.2 Dissolution test (by HPLC):
• Dissolution conditions.  
The amount of SDS for both dose strength should be reduced to 0.8% SDS instead of 
1.0% for 30 mg and to 1.0% instead of 1.5% for 120 mg)
• Amount dissolved by HPLC. The Assessor recommends including peak symmetry [0.8-
1.8] in the SST (dissolution-Quantification of the amount dissolved)
Please commit.
Answer/Response:
The applicant’s response:
4.1 Introduction of a second earlier time point
The applicant appreciates the openness of the RMS to discuss the dissolution method and 
parameters and is, therefore, grateful for the opportunity of exchanging views during informal 
telephone calls on 06 and 07 Feb 2024. The applicant furthermore acknowledges the 
assessor’s position that “for a MAA in EU, EMA guides should be followed”.
The presented specification was set following the principles described in the EMA reflection 
paper EMA/CHMP/CVMP/QWP/336031/2017. The applicant notes, however, that the focus 
of this reflection paper is on the dissolution specification for generic solid oral immediate 
release products with systemic action. It (softly) concludes that “similar principles may be 
considered for deriving the specification for innovator products”. Notwithstanding the fact 
that the nifurtimox tablet is an innovator product, the principles of the reflection paper, 
specifically chapter 2.1.4 (side batch approach), have been followed.
However, as summarized below, available in vitro and in vivo data scientifically justify the 
proposed single-point specification of Q=80% at 60 min. A second earlier timepoint does not 
increase safety and efficacy of the drug product for the patient.
A dedicated pharmacokinetic side batch study to generate safe space with respect to 
dissolution specification has been conducted, to identify the lowest specification, that still 
exhibits a comparable pharmacokinetic profile. The specification is also based on biobatches, 
namely phase 1 batches, of which pharmacokinetic data reveal sufficient exposure for 
efficacy, and pivotal phase 3 batches, that were efficacious and safe.
As shown by above mentioned clinical studies (refer to clinical part of the dossier, 2.7.1, 
summary of biopharmaceutics), Cmax is not driven by the dissolution.
The omission of a second earlier timepoint recommended in Ph. Eur. 5.17.1 and 
EMA/CHMP/CVMP/QWP/336031/2017 is justified for the following reasons:
(1) Upper limit omission: fast in-vitro dissolution is considered not critical because results of 
Study 16004 (comparison of tablet suspension vs. whole tablet) and Study 16007 (comparison 
of fast and slow dissolving whole tablets) indicated that faster in-vitro dissolution is not 
associated with higher Cmax values (for details refer to pharmaceutical development - 
dissolution profiles (P.2.2.02-04) and module 2.7.1).

As an additional argument for the omission of the second earlier timepoint we would like to 
point out that Nifurtimox is administered with food. This results in later Tmax values (4 h, fed 
state, vs. 3 h, fasted state; refer to SmPC, section 5.2, table 8) caused by a food induced longer 
residence time in the stomach and small intestine due to decreased gastric motility, delayed 
gastric emptying, and increased transit time. This contributes to the fact that faster dissolution 
does not correlate with higher Cmax values. Even at fasted state, a Tmax of 3 h does not suggest 
that a dissolution specification at 15 min is meaningful.
(2) Lower limit omission: primary stability data of the formulation stored in HDPE-bottles 
with desiccant capsules demonstrated good stability regarding dissolution with no occurrence 
of a lag time. Low dissolution in the beginning (21% at 15 min) leads to equivalent Cmax 
values as fast dissolution (59% at 15 min).
In summary, the available in vitro data, and human clinical pharmacokinetic, 
pharmacodynamic and safety data scientifically justify the proposed single-point specification 
of Q=80% at 60 min. A second earlier timepoint does not increase safety and efficacy of the 
drug product for the patient.
We would appreciate the Agency’s openness to revisit the request for a second earlier 
timepoint considering that the presented specification was set following the principles 
described in the EMA reflection paper EMA/CHMP/CVMP/QWP/336031/2017, specifically 
following chapter 2.1.4 (side batch approach).

4.2 Dissolution test
The dissolution method (including SDS amount) and specification have been developed and 
chosen based on the totality of in vitro and in vivo data available, according to EMA 
guidances and Pharm. Eur. Principles. This implies the consideration of physicochemical 
parameters of the API, in vitro dissolution profiles of the formulations (e.g., phase 1 side 
batches, phase 3 pivotal batches), as well as in vivo pharmacokinetic (phase 1, side batch 
study) and pharmacodynamic (phase 3 pivotal study). This holistic biopharmaceutical line of 
argumentation for both method and specification setting follows e.g., the EMA reflection 
paper on dissolution specification setting (EMA/CHMP/CVMP/QWP/336031/2017). As 
previously agreed with the agency in an informal call (06. Feb 2024), the amount of SDS 
remains therefore unchanged.
Regarding the peak symmetry, the applicant agrees to include the requirement [0.8-1.8] in the 
SST, respective documents are amended (P.5.2.02-02, P.5.3.02-02).

Source:
P.5.2.02-02 Test Procedure – Dissolution / Nifurtimox tablet 30 mg (#022982900; 
amended)
P.5.2.02-02 Test Procedure – Dissolution / Nifurtimox tablet 0.12 g (#022982901; 
amended)
P.5.3.02-02 Validation of Test for Dissolution / Nifurtimox tablet 30 mg (#022982911; 
amended)
P.5.3.02-02 Validation of Test for Dissolution / Nifurtimox tablet 0.12 g (#022982914; 
amended)

Please justify the use of Pseudomonas aeruginosa as the challenge organism used in the microbial challenge test. Bayer Response to Question 4 ( CTD section):
We followed the recommendations of PDA’s Technical Report No. 27 (TR27). Like some other micro-organisms described in the TR27, Pseudomonas aeruginosa was considered suitable due to small cell size, motility capabilities and in addition is an organism whose handling was well known in the laboratory, as it is one of our standard microorganisms
Background:
In the year 2006, TR27 emerged as one of the primary guidelines delineating the microbiological aspects of Container Closure Integrity Testing. Considering the evolving nature of regulatory standards and the absence of other comprehensive guidelines at that time, TR27 provided valuable insights into the microbiological CCIT landscape.
Consideration of PDA Technical Reports:
The industry often considers Technical Reports issued by reputable organizations such as the PDA to be authoritative references, reflecting the collective expertise and experience of professionals in the field. While not binding regulations, these reports serve as practical guides and interpretations of good manufacturing practices.
Microbiological CCIT and TR27:
TR27, being an early guideline on microbiological CCIT, played a crucial role in shaping industry practices. The principles outlined in TR27 have been widely adopted and integrated into industry standards, acknowledging the technical state of the art in the absence of specific regulatory requirements.

Question/Consideration:
Question 3
Acceptance criterion for "Pre-sterilization bioburden" action level is proposed to be widened 
from > 10 CFU per unit to > 100 CFU per set. This change is not line with “Guideline on the 
sterilisation of the medicinal product, active substance, excipient and primary container” 
EMA/CHMP/CVMP/QWP/850374/2015 as the requirement of the guideline 100 CFU/100 ml 
(g) of aqueous solution is not comparable to proposed 100 CFU/460 mg of implants. Also, 
widening of the bioburden limit cannot be justified by comparing parenteral Jadelle Sine 
Inserter implant to intrauterine delivery systems. Thus, widening of the pre-sterilization 
bioburden limit is not acceptable.
In addition, current wording “action limit” should be removed from the current "Pre-
sterilization bioburden" in-process control. Correct requirement is ≤ 10 CFU/set (mean value). 
As stated in the guideline EMA/CHMP/CVMP/QWP/850374/2015 bioburden acceptance 
criteria are specific for the test, thus no action levels are allowed for bioburden test.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 3 (3.2.P.3.3):
As communicated separately via e-mails between Bayer Oy and FIMEA is was acknowledged 
by FIMEA on 26th of March that the use of Action limit for the Pre-sterilization bioburden test 
of Jadelle was found acceptable.

Pre-sterilization bioburden of Levonorgestrel implant 75 mg without inserter (JADELLE) is 
routinely tested from primary packaged products prior to the actual sterilization step. This test 
is conducted at regular intervals (currently batchwise) as a part of microbiological monitoring 
program to detect adverse trends in the production. Alert (internal, based on trend) and action 
limits have been defined at Bayer Oy for the product bioburden before sterilization in line 
with EN ISO 11737 and EN ISO 11135. The use of these limits has been accepted by the 
authorities. Ethylene oxide (EO) sterilization cycle has been validated using a half cycle 
overkill approach using biological indicators resistant to EO that represent a worst-case 
bioburden. By this approach, a sterility assurance level (SAL) of 10-12 is achieved for routine 
sterilization cycles. A predetermined course of action will be taken if the bioburden limit for 
the batch exceeds. According to the current procedure, either exceeding once the action level, 
or subsequently twice the alert level, will trigger a root cause investigation even if the 
exceeding result is noticed on only one of the parallel sample filtrations. The investigation 
takes place both in the laboratory and in the production and includes an assessment of the 
criticality of the contamination regarding the release of the product in question.
The bioburden limit of 10 CFU/100 g is in opinion of Bayer Oy merely relevant for water 
solutions in which the level of aerobic bacteria may increase during the manufacturing 
process before the sterilization. Jadelle implant as a dry elastomer product does not support 
microbial growth, hence, the possible contamination before primary packaging will not 
increase in the packaged product before the sterilization step.
Furthermore, as the EMA guideline (EMA/CHMP/CVMP/QWP/850374/2015) mentions 
100 CFU/100 g as an acceptable limit for parenteral finished products in case of heat 
sterilized products, Bayer Oy thinks that a limit of 100 CFU/set would be acceptable for 
Jadelle implant. It should be noted also that the manufacturing of Jadelle implants contains 
heat treatments during the post-curing steps for both the drug core (ca. 3 hours at ca 150°C), 
and the tubing (4 hours at 150°C), to remove the peroxide residues originating from the 
polydimethylsiloxane materials. As also the assembly and primary packaging of Jadelle 
implant take place in cleanliness class C, where microbial contamination is typically due to 
the personnel and may not be evenly distributed in the batch. EN ISO 11737 –1 also notices 
that bioburden spikes can occur that may be a normal and consistent part of the bioburden but 
shall be evaluated for the impact as appropriate (A.8.5 Bioburden spikes). Bayer Oy thinks 
that the bioburden control is best accomplished utilizing alert and action limits, as is done 
currently, and also that the action limit 100 CFU/set (mean value) would be appropriate for 
use.
keywords: Sterility Testing; in-process control; risk assessment; root cause evaluation; Sterilization

Question/Consideration:
Question 7
Proposed change in sample preparation for endotoxin and sterility testing is not regarded as 
minor change and therefore justification should be provided for not cutting the implant in the 
proposed Jadelle Sine Inserter, FI/H/0189/001/II/028/G 19/19 RMS’s PVAR sample 
preparation method but instead using whole implants for testing considering that the effective 
surface-area of the implants decreases with the new sample preparation method and might 
have an effect on the results of the testing.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 7 (3.2.P.5.2):
Justification for not cutting the sample:
- 
The procedure is similar to insertion into patient: the implant is used intact. 
- 
USP <71>, Medical devices states: Articles can be immersed intact or disassembled. 
- 
The risk for laboratory contamination accomplished by the cutting phase will be omitted. 
- 
The surface area exposed to the culture medium will remain 56 % of the original. The 
ratio surface vs. growth medium is not increased by removing the cutting phase, which 
means that the change does not affect the validated status of the test. 
- 
The risk for detecting less microbes or bacterial endotoxins after the change is very small, 
as due to the handling and the heat treatments before assembling, the most probable 
location for microbial contamination is on the outer surface of the implant. 
- 
The risk for viable contamination or bacterial endotoxins within the product after 
sterilization is negligible based on following:
o materials do not support microbial growth. 
o bioburden level of Jadelle implants is generally very low   
o results for sterility test and bacterial endotoxin tests from several years have fulfilled
the specifications. 
o manufacturing of the components, assembly and primary packaging of Jadelle
implant take place in cleanliness class C. 
o heat treatments (3 hours at 150°C) are included in the manufacturing process.  
o no water is used in the manufacturing of the product or its components, and
endotoxin -carrying (Gram-negative) bacteria are rarely found in the production.  
o primary contact surfaces in the production are disinfected.  
o the steam used in EO sterilization is controlled for bacterial endotoxins, and the
results have been constantly negative.
o ethylene oxide penetrates the material easily, which is supported both by the
literature and tests made for Bayer Oy, the easy penetration of EO ensures the 
sterility of the product throughout

Question/Consideration:
Question 2
Validation of manufacturing process up to date.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 2 ( CTD section):
The manufacturing process of recombinant interferon beta-1b (rIFN beta-1b) as a drug 
substance for Interferon beta-1b lyophilized powder (Betaferon) at Boehringer Ingelheim RCV 
GmbH & Co KG is well-established for over 30 years and adequately monitored by in-process and 
release testing.
In order to assure adequate process performance and product quality, continuous process 
verification (CPV) is performed once every quarter to assess the quality of the output material as 
well as  system performance in a continuous manner.
The justification to delete the test parameter “content of rIFN beta-1b by ELISA after fermentation” 
is further explained below.
The test to analyze the content of rIFN beta-1b by ELISA after fermentation was originally 
implemented for monitoring purposes only. Consequently, the results of the ELISA test are not used 
for any process decision and do not prevent the proceeding from the fermentation step to the primary 
recovery step of the inclusion bodies. In addition, the test results from the ELISA assay are not 
included in the CPV documentation. Considering the above, all available data of  rIFN beta-1b 
content measured by ELISA was thoroughly analyzed and it was confirmed that no deviation from 
the registered limit (NLT 0.3 mg/mL) was identified over the past 80 manufactured batches. Please 
refer to Error! Reference source not found. below.
Moreover, in the subsequent manufacturing step (primary recovery of the inclusion bodies (IBs), 
the content of rIFN beta-1b is measured with the RP-HPLC and strictly controlled with an action 
limit of NLT 11 mg/g. Over the last four years, historical CPV data for the most recent 50 IB batches 
demonstrates that rIFN beta-1b content measured via RP-HPLC analysis was well within the 
control limits (12.55 – 23.09 mg/g) and above the low alarm limit (11.00 mg/g). Please refer to 
Figure 1 and Figure 33 below.

Figure 1: The  content of rIFN beta-1b measured by ELISA test after fermentation is
shown from 80 batches (manufactured  
between 2018-2023). All values are within the registered acceptable ranges (Mean = 0.5
mg/ml). LSL = Lower  
specification limit

Figure 2: The  content of rIFN beta-1b measured by RP-HPLC is shown from the last 50
batches (manufactured between  
2019-2023). All values are well within the registered acceptable ranges. LAL = Lower
Alarm limit, LCL = Lower control limit 
UCL = Upper control Limit

Figure 3: The  distribution (histogram) of  rIFN beta-1b content measured by RP-HPLC
is shown from the last 50 batches  
(manufactured between 2019-2023). All values were well within the registered acceptable
ranges. LSL = Lower  
specification limit

As the ELISA test shows higher variability in comparison to RP-HPLC analysis (intermediate 
precision for ELISA is 20 %  versus 3.0 % for RP HPLC) and both tests can be considered 
redundant, it is intended to monitor rIFN beta-1b content on the level of recovered IBs measured 
with the more precise RP HPLC analysis in future.
Notably, the deletion of this test is currently in the process of being registered globally. Until all 
approvals are obtained globally, this test is continued to be performed and thus no CPV data with 
the deleted ELISA test is currently available at this stage.
Bayer confirms that once all approvals are obtained for this variation globally, the ELISA test after 
fermentation is omitted from the drug substance manufacturing process and CPV (validation) data 
will be collected quarterly to continuously monitor the quality and process performance over time. 
Moreover, Bayer confirms that except for the deletion of the monitoring ELISA parameter at the 
end of fermentation, no further changes to the manufacturing process were introduced and no impact 
on CPV data is thus expected, also considering that the ELISA test was not part of the CPV 
documentation before.
Please also refer to the Declaration submitted within this response for further details.

Source:  Declaration Deletion of ELISA test after fermentation / Interferon beta-1b
lyophilized powder (Declaration Deletion of ELISA test after 
fermentation.PDF; new)

Question/Consideration:
Question 3
Method for process control updated with their respective validations, if applies.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 3 ( CTD section):
The only change in the process control is the deletion of the process parameter ‘rIFN beta-1b 
content at end fermentation’, which is analysed by the ELISA method, since it is considered a 
non-significant process test parameter, which can be omitted (see below). Bayer confirms that 
all other test methods remain unchanged and no new test method was included into the 
manufacturing process of Betaferon, which would require additional method validations.
Rationale for deleting the test parameter “rIFN beta-1b content at end fermentation” measured 
by ELISA:
As stated in our Response to Question 1, Bayer confirms that the ELISA test at the end of 
fermentation was established for monitoring purposes only. Consequently, the ELISA test does 
not have any impact on preventing the proceeding of the manufacturing process from the 
fermentation step to the primary recovery step of the inclusion bodies. Moreover, historical data 
from over 80 batches (between 2018 and 2023) confirm that the content of rIFN beta-1b was within 
the defined limits of NLT 0.3 mg/ml (observed range 0.3 – 0.8 mg/mL, mean 0.5). Please refer to 
Figure 1.
Finally, as stated before, the content of rIFN beta-1b will continue to be monitored with RP - 
HPLC data at the level of recovered inclusion bodies. RP-HPLC is also considered the more 
robust method in comparison to the ELISA test, as outlined in our Response to Question 1.
.
Irrespectively, Bayer commits to continue close monitoring of CPV data obtained from the 
manufacturing process, once the ELISA test at the end of fermentation is omitted from the 
manufacturing process. Trend analysis is performed quarterly to identify any potential risks on 
CQA performance as early as possible.
Please also refer to the Declaration submitted within this response for further details.
Source:  Declaration Deletion of ELISA test after fermentation / Interferon beta-1b
lyophilized powder (Declaration Deletion of ELISA test after 
fermentation.PDF; new)

Question/Consideration: Please provide the risk assessment elemental impurities of the finished product (formula, manufacturing process and packaging) related to the non-testing of heavy metal parameters in Sodium lauryl sulfate (in FI VI, testing of heavy metal in excipient Sodium lauryl sulfate is required) as per ICH Q2D elemental impurities.
Answer/Response:
The monograph in the Farmakope Indonesia (FI) for Sodium dodecyl sulfate / Sodium Lauryl Sulfate / Sodium laurilsulfate (excipient) includes two tests that are not performed routinely by the applicant:
• Arsenic <321> Method II, not more than 3 ppm
• Heavy metals <371> Method II, not more than 20 ppm.

The applicant has justified the omission of a routine test for both parameters by the existing compliance for excipients and products in general with the ICH Q3D guideline (Elemental impurities). Both arsenic and heavy metals are explicitly covered by the ICH Q3D guideline.

For more details please refer to technical documents P.5.6.01-02 as well as the P.5.5.02-02 risk assessment of elemental impurities of the finish product.

In addition the applicant performed an additional testing of elemental impurities on three batches of Sodium lauril sulfate excipient. For more details please refer to the technical document P.4.4.02-01.

It is concluded that all results for the batches of Sodium dodecyl sulfate excipient tested by ICP-MS were well below the limits according to ICH Q3D. The results demonstrate that the excipient meets the requirements of the Farmakope Indonesia.

Furthermore, in the technical document P.4.4.02-01 also a risk assessment to the elemental impurities specific for the Sodium lauril sulfate excipient is included which justified why a routinely testing on elemental impurities for this excipient is not required.

Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 6 (CTD section S.4.1 and P.5.1):
At release of the finished drug product (DP) and the drug substance (DS), both are tested for 
appearance and the color according to Ph. Eur.
Appearance
For batch release of the drug product the “Appearance” is tested for turbidity and visible 
particulates. Drug substance is tested only for turbidity within “Appearance”.
• Turbidity
Turbidity is specified as "Not greater than turbidity standard III" in section P.5.1 and S.4.1, 
respectively. The number “III” indicates the intensity of the solution which must not be 
greater than the intensity of the reference suspension solution III using a scale of standardized 
reference solutions I – IV. The test is carried out according to Ph. Eur. 2.2.1.

• Visible particulates.
The acceptance criterion for visible particulates is defined as “essentially free from visible 
particulates” in accordance with the provisions of Ph. Eur. 2.9.20.

As part of the renewal submission, the drug substance specification has been updated as 
provided with document S.4.1.01 in order to delete the non-significant in-process test 
“Appearance, b) visual assessment of particulates” applied during the manufacture of the 
finished product.

Color
In the similar way as for the appearance (turbidity), the color of the drug product and drug 
substance in solution specified as "Colorless to reference standard BY5” is tested in line with 
Ph. Eur. 2.2.2. In this context, BY is defined as a yellow-brownish color and 5 indicates the 
intensity on a scale of 1-7.
For reference, the relevant Ph. Eur. monographs are provided attached.

Response to b)

Response to c)
The preparation of samples and applied dilution for TAMC and TYMC tests are documented in P.5.3.06, Section 3.1.1 and 3.1.4:
A test solution was prepared by suspending 10 g of product in 100 mL buffered sodium chloride-peptone solution pH 7.0, resulting in a final of 1:10.
Two empty petri dishes were labeled for each organism. 6 x 10 mL of test solution was inoculated separately with 0.1 mL of each test organism suspension (100 CFU/mL). This results in a final dilution of 1:100.
The preparation of samples and applied dilution for determination of absence of E.coli is documented in P.5.3.06, Section 3.2.1:
10 g of the product was suspended in 100 mL NAPP. 10 mL (corresponding to 1 g) were used to inoculate 100 mL CSB for preincubation at 30-35 °C for 18 hrs. Subsequently a volume of 1 mL was transferred to 100 mL of MacConkey broth and incubated at 42-44 °C for 24 hrs.
After incubation, a loopful of each selective enrichment broth inoculated with the test organism was plated onto the corresponding agar medium (MacConkey agar) and incubated at 30-35 °C for 18 hrs.

Response to d)
Please note that no neutralizing agents are used, therefore no neutralization step is applied.

Response to e)
The information on incubation duration and time is documented in the following sections of P.5.3.06.:
Section 3.1.5 for TAMC and TYMC:
All Casein soybean digest agar (CSA) plates for bacteria were inverted and incubated aerobically at 30 – 35 °C for three days for detection of bacterial growth.
All Sabouraud Dextrose Agar (SADA) plates and sabouraud dextrose agar with chloramphenicol (SACA) plates were inverted and incubated aerobically at 20 – 25 °C for five days for detection of fungal growth.
Section 3.2.1 for determination of absence of E.coli:
10 g of the product was suspended in 100 mL NAPP. 10 mL (corresponding to 1 g) were used to inoculate 100 mL CSB for preincubation at 30-35 °C for 18 hrs. Subsequently a volume of 1 mL was transferred to 100 mL of MacConkey broth and incubated at 42-44 °C for 24 hrs.
After incubation, a loopful of each selective enrichment broth inoculated with the test organism was plated onto the corresponding agar medium (MacConkey agar) and incubated at 30-35 °C for 18 hrs.

Response to f)
"<50 CFU/g" for TAMC and TYMC is used as a reporting threshold for this method, that means that even if no colonies have been observed (raw data: 0 CFU/g), the result will be reported as "<50 CFU/g". Considering the specification limit of 1000 CFU/g for TAMC and 100 CFU/g for TYMC, the reporting threshold is considered sufficiently below specification limit.
With regard to reporting of microbiological testing results, the specification limit contains a semi-quantitative acceptance criterion: "Absence in 1g". That means if the test is conducted as described in the test instruction and no E.Coli bacteria colony could be identified, the result will be reported as "not detectable in 1g".

Response to g)
Refer to Ph.Eur 2.6.13. Test for specified micro-organisms. Copies of highlighted sections of Ph. Eur. are provided.
Section 4-2-3 (Ph.Eur 2.6.13):
Interpretation. Growth of colonies indicates the possible presence of E. coli. This is confirmed by identification tests. The product complies with the test if no colonies are present or if the identification tests are negative.

The calibration solution and the test solution for residual solvent have been evaluated to be stable for 20 hours for Acetone and Toluene as well as 24 hours for Acetic acid when stored at ambient temperature.
In detail, the confidence interval for the content of Acetone in the test solution has been evaluated during method validation within 0.361456 – 0.410795 % (refer to chapter 1.3.1).

The confidence interval for the content of Toluene in the test solution has been evaluated during method validation within 0.099460 – 0.115692 % (refer to chapter 1.3.2).

Question/Consideration: Please clarify and justify regarding changes in the purification stage, which is addition of 400 L and 50 L flexsafe bags and deletion of 16,6 bags.
Answer/Response:
Currently, Flexel film LevTech single use bags are used during the manufacture of the drug substance. The manufacturer proposes to start using the Flexsafe model of processing bag. The product contact layer chemistry will not change. It is low-density polyethylene (LLDPE) for both models.
The 400L bag is used during the last purification step (Step 15) Size Exclusion chromatography (SEC). It is used to collect the SEC pool until the initiation of the subsequent concentration step. 4.3. Since the substance is used for the production of injectable medicinal product, to explain 
the lack of control of active pharmaceutical substance by the indicators “Colority” and “pH”, 
which are mandatory in accordance with SP RF, PM.2.1.0391 “Gadobutrol Monohydrate” and 
SP RF, GPM. 1.1.0006 “Pharmaceutical Substances”, provide actual data on expired samples.
Answer/Response:
We would like to inform the agency that we have conducted the Color of Solution test according 
to EAEU Ph. GPM.1.2.1.0006, method 2, on three exemplary batches of Gadobutrol. The 
results are as follows:
Batch 
Color of solution 
UN619QS 
Colorless (< B9) 
UN61ALL 
Colorless (<B9) 
UN61C32 
Colorless (<B9)
The requirements for the Gadobutrol EAEU Ph. monograph, according to the general chapter 
of EAEU Ph., are fulfilled as the liquid is colorless. This demonstrates that the requirements of 
the EAEU Ph. Monograph are met when tested.
In the specification for Gadobutrol, the appearance is described as a white to off-white 
crystalline powder, excluding any coloring. Additionally, when tested for clarity of solution, 
the acceptance criterion is 'clear'. These combined results confirm that the requirements for 
substances used in the production of injectable medicinal products are fulfilled. Consequently, 
it has been confirmed that the requirements for "colority" according to EAEU Ph. are met when 
tested. Therefore, "Colority" will not be included in the routine specification for the API.
Regarding pH, Gadobutrol is a neutral compound within the physiologically relevant pH range 
(pKaI < 2.0) (reference S.1.3.01#019481504-03). The pH of Gadobutrol is considered an 
intrinsic property and characteristic rather than a test item, and therefore, it is not included in 
the quality specification.
Please find the detailed declaration and supporting documents attached for your reference

Question/Consideration: The stability testing frequency is not according to that recommended by ICH. Please clarify.

The stability testing is performed in accordance with ICH Guideline “STABILITY TESTING OF NEW DRUG SUBSTANCES AND PRODUCTS Q1A(R2)” in its current version. Long-term stability data are presented in P.8.3.01-04.
Bayer has been manufacturing a wide range of contrast agents for multiple years and therefore has a wealth of experience. The stability of the manufactured contrast media portfolio over the entire shelf life is well proven. In general, no quality issues are observed during stability studies. Very few exceptions, such as free amine content in Ultravist, are included in the stability studies and are monitored closely.
Based on the long-term experience a bracketing approach may be applied for some formats. The individual decision will however be based on the historic stability profile, the intended change and other factors and will be documented in the respective stability report.
For the purpose of the on-going stability studies the corresponding protocol fully covers the entire shelf life of the product as presented in document P.8.3.02-20.
. Based on the above mentioned long-term experience the testing frequency is reduced to 12-months over the registered product shelf life and justified.

Question/Consideration:
Question 1
Qualification of WCB (ICH Q5A and Q5D).
Answer/Response:
Kindly note that, as it is stated in the Declaration_Betaferon_ICH Q5A and Q5D guideline, the following ICH guideline “ICH Q5A(R2) - Guideline on viral safety evaluation of biotechnology products derived from cell lines of human or animal origin” does not apply to Interferon beta-1b lyophilized powder (Betaferon injection).
Recombinant IFN beta-1b protein is produced in a bacterial expression system, using Escherichia coli (E. coli) cells that have been genetically altered by insertion of a synthetically constructed sequence encoding for rIFN beta-1b.
Briefly, recombinant IFN beta-1b representing the final Drug Substance (DS) is expressed in E. coli bacteria, recovered, purified, and further processed to the final drug product. The fermentation process starts with inoculation of the main culture with the working cell bank culture, which is of bacterial origin. During the fermentation and purification process, no other cells or biotechnology products of human or animal origin are used. Consequently, ICH Q5A (R2) does not apply to Interferon beta-1b lyophilized powder (Betaferon injection).
The risk of potential contamination with animal-derived adventitious agents in Interferon beta-1b is discussed in A.2.01-04. Generally, the risk of any transmission is low, as rIFN beta-1b is produced by fermentation in Escherichia coli (E. coli) cells and therefore there is no significant risk of contamination with adventitious agents such as mammalian viruses or transmissible spongiform encephalopathy (TSE). Control of potential adventitious agents in rIFN beta-1b is exerted through control of raw materials, typical biological controls on the manufacturing process, and Drug Substance and Drug Product testing to ensure that the cell culture and resulting fermentation suspension are free from contaminating bacteria and other organisms. All media used during media fills in the filling facility are free of TSE material. Please refer to A.2.01-04 for further details.

Moreover, The currently used Master Cell Bank BBAMJ001, used to manufacture rIFN beta-1b Drug Substance, does not contain mammalian viruses, and has been shown to be free of bacteriophage. Please refer to S.2.3.50-03.
The currently used MCB has been characterized extensively 30 years ago in 1994 and has been used since its first implementation in 1997 without any change. Please refer to Response to Question 2 for further details.

Following the successful establishment of the MCB BBAMJ001 in 1994, Periodic Tests of Master Cell Bank were carried out as part of the continuous control and stability testing strategy. At BI RCV, MCB stability is ensured though the continuous testing of the WCBs, specifically, for defined Purity and Potency parameters (Culture Purity, Cell viability and Plasmid Retention). Please refer to S.2.3.50-03 for further details.

Following the establishment and characterization of the MCB, a WCB characterization is not performed for each WCB lot, since the tests listed in the attached CoAs are routinely performed as part of the new WCB qualification and testing program, which includes identity and purity testing according to ICH Q5D.

Specifically, the following parameters are tested:
- Identity: E.coli positive
- Culture purity: No confirmed contaminants
- Bacteriophage assay: Absence of bacteriophages
- Cell Viability: ≥ 1 x 108 CFU/mL
- Plasmid retention: ≤ 5 CFU / 300 CFU
- Plasmid Identity by Restriction Mapping: Map comparable to pSY2501 plasmid control
- DNA Sequencing: Identical to established DNA sequence of rIFN beta-1b

Please refer to the Certificates of Analyses for both new proposed WCB batches E23854 and E59204 provided within the response.

Moreover, evidence of stability under defined storage conditions for the Working Cell Bank has been provided in stability reports for the established MCBs, including the current MCB BBAMJ001. The retest period based on testing of several WCB lots incoming at the drug substance manufacturing site, BI RCV, between 2013 and 2023 was re-evaluated and defined with 06-Jun-2033.

In summary, Bayer confirms the adequate characterization and stability testing of the MCB, BBAMJ001, currently in use (please refer to S.2.3.50-03), as well as the adequate testing for identity and purity for in newly qualified WCB lots in accordance to ICH Q5D.

Source:  A.1.02-04 TSE Assessment / Interferon beta-1b lyophilized powder (A.2.01_005781849_04; unchanged)
S.2.3.50-03 Cell Banking System, Characterization and Testing - Master Cell Bank / Interferon beta-1b drug substance  (S.2.3.50_006926424-03; unchanged)
Certificate of Analyses Working Cell Bank Lot / E23854 (CoA_WCB_Lot E23854.PDF; new)
Certificate of Analyses Working Cell Bank Lot /  E59204 (CoA_WCB_Lot E59204  .PDF; new)
Declaration_Betaferon_ICH Q5A and Q5D guideline

Question/Consideration:
Question 2
Assessment on characteristics of cell bank of MCB/WCB and test results.
Answer/Response:
The manufacturing process of recombinant interferon beta-1b (rIFN beta-1b) as a drug substance for Interferon beta-1b lyophilized powder (Betaferon) is well-established for over 30 years and adequately monitored by in-process and release testing.
The Master Cell Bank (MCB) currently implemented and in use (BBAMJ001) has been generated and extensively characterized 30 years ago in 1994. For details on the characterization of the MCB, please refer to S.2.3.50-03. In order to meet market demands and planned production capacities during routine production of Interferon beta-1b lyophilized powder (Betaferon), aliquots from the established MCB are routinely taken (approximately twice a year) and used to establish new WCB lots, which are routinely tested for their defined specification parameters and subsequently stored at -70°C for 24 months.
Identity, Purity, Genomic stability and cell viability (Potency) of the WCB are tightly controlled by the following specification parameters, as stated in S.2.3.51-05.

Please find attached the Certificates of Analyses for both WCB lots attached for further details.

Moreover, the fermentation step of the WCB pre-culture and main culture is tightly controlled by the following process parameters:
Pre-culture: Temperature 37 ± 2 °C; Shaking speed 250 ± 20 rpm; Final OD 2.0 ± 0.5
Main culture: Temperature 37 ± 1 °C; Dissolved Oxygen >40% (setpoint 60%); Pressure 0.01-0.13 bar; Aeration 0.03-0.99 Nm³/h; Agitation 330-1370 rpm; pH 6.8 ± 0.2; Final OD550 25.0 ± 1.0
Moreover, fermentation time is closely monitored as part of the Continuous Process validation (CPV) control strategy. For both WCB lots, E59204 and E23854, the fermentation time was 583 min and 586 min, respectively.
Passage numbers and doubling times are not recorded as part of the CPV and control strategy, as monitoring of cell expansion is controlled by OD and dry cell weight.

Genomic stability throughout the culturing period is confirmed by plasmid control and sequencing analytics.
Moreover, a small scale study was done to mimic the doubling times at large routine production scale in 2007, which demonstrated around 20 doublings for the working cell bank. For further details please refer to S.2.3.51-05. For both proposed WCB lots, E23854 and E59204, the number of generations during WCB production were identical with 19.7 for both batches.
Finally, genomic stability throughout the culturing period is confirmed by plasmid control and sequencing analytics. An extended fermentation with 10 additional doublings was carried out and proven to have no impact on genetic stability of the host system. Please refer to S.2.3.50-03 for further details.
All MCBs in use are registered with lot number and freeze date, which will hold true for any additional MCB that might be registered in future. The WCBs generated from those MCBs are tested according to the test panel described in document S.2.3.51-05, and as long as the acceptance criteria are met they are suitable for drug substance production. Further, the consistent rIFN beta-1b protein formation during main culture fermentation confirms genetic stability of the cell substrate; it is proven by inclusion body in-process testing for rIFN beta-1b identity and content of rIFN beta 1b, and finally by rIFN beta-1b drug substance release testing.

Source:
S.2.3.50-03 Cell Banking System, Characterization and Testing - Master Cell Bank / Interferon beta-1b drug substance  (S.2.3.50_006926424-03; unchanged)
S.2.3.51-05 Cell Banking System, Characterization and Testing - Working Cell Bank / Interferon beta-1b drug substance  (S.2.3.51_021409846_05; unchanged)
Certificate of Analyses Working Cell Bank Lot / E23854 (CoA_WCB_Lot E23854.PDF; new)
Certificate of Analyses Working Cell Bank Lot /  E59204 (CoA_WCB_Lot E59204  .PDF; new)

(Regarding reply to question 2 in the 1st DL issued on Dec 26, 2023)
With regarding the content of minor changes notification dated May 30, 2016, regarding topic 
#3 about the manufacturing process 6, sterilization temperature in the approved application 
form were amended as "121°C or higher” by considering the accuracy of the temperature 
sensor even though it is actually specified as "122°C or higher". However, as stated in MBR, 
if the product temperature is actually sterilized to be "122°C" or higher, consider to specify  
the temperature (product temperature) that should be controlled in the application for approval 
as well.
Alternatively, if the sterilization temperature becomes 121°C, provide specific information 
that does not affect the sterilization requirements, explain the validity of the set temperature, 
and modify MBR.
Answer/Response:
Comment from BYL:
Question 2 in the 1st DL issued on Dec 26, 2023 was about the content of our minor change 
notifications related to the amendment of our approval application forms (AAF) submitted on 
May 30 and 31, 2016 based on our cross check of AAF and source TRDs/GMP document.
Among the content of our amendment, PMDA is requesting us to amend sterilization 
temperature in the approved application form as "122°C or higher", which is the same 
description in the MBR (please see the screenshot of below MBR which was provided from 
Bayer global during cross check of AAF and source TRDs/GMP document in the past).

During the cross check process, BYL got an explanation from Bayer global about the 
justification of "122°C or higher" as below

‘To confirm with the requirement of 121°C, we claim a temperature of 122°C because of the 
measuring inaccuracy of the temperature detector of +/- 0.5K and a safety under temperature 
limit of 0.5K. By doing so, we can guarantee that the product got sterilized at least 20 minutes 
at a temperature of 121°C in an overkill sterilization process’

Therefore, BYL will again explain above justification in our reply.

Bayer Response to Question 1 ( CTD section):
The response will be prepared by BYL by referring above comment from Bayer global. In 
case, PMDA still requests to set "122°C or higher" in our approval application form, we will 
discuss with Bayer global.
keywords: Sterilization; Manufacturing Process and Process Controls; Batch Record - Master; validation of test method; in-process control

Question/Consideration:
Question 2
Please provide letter to clarify if there is any change in DP & API specifications, testing method, 
and if there is change, please provide updated document. If there is no change, please further 
explain.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 2:
Regarding API specifications and testing methods, as mentioned in the submitted declaration 
letter, Drug substance, Gadopentetate dimeglumine, is formed during the formulation step of 
the Drug Product and cannot be isolated. The manufacturing process is a one-pot process with 
an in-situ formation directly taking place from the starting materials (gadolinium oxide, DTPA 
and meglumine). Hence, there is no dedicated specification and test procedure for drug

Question/Consideration:
5.13. Section 3.2.S.4.4 Batch analysis provides additional tests to the tests described in section 
3.2.S.4.1. Specs.
Answer/Response:
The submitted specification document (S.4.1.01-02; see sources) is the correct and current version 
of the release specification. The set of quality attributes contained in the specification has not 
changed since the beginning of commercial operations. Before testing conformance batches, 
updated product characterization methods were reviewed in detail for their applicability and 
capability to measure critical quality attributes. Final review of these methods was performed 
following the conformance campaign in order to set the final commercial specification. The 
specific changes in the specifications between the conformance campaign and the commercial 
submission with associated rationale are summarized here:
• 
The original method used to assess levels of sialic acid capping (the “Capping” test noted 
in S.4.4.01-01) was replaced in late-phase development by an updated method for 
commercial product release (“Sialylation Ratio (Oligomap)” in S.4.1.01-02). The rationale 
for migrating to the current method, including bridging study analysis, is described in 
S.4.5.01-02.
• 
The thrombin peptide map peak 2 area-to-height ratio (a measure of potential product 
methionine oxidation), was assessed against action limits for all conformance lots as noted 
in S.4.4.01-01, but was raised to a specification for commercial manufacturing as shown 
in S.4.1.01-02.  
• 
Alpha-galactose content was assessed against specification limits for all clinical and 
conformance batches as noted in S.4.4.01-01. As no quantitative results were observed for 
any clinical or conformance batch as noted in S.3.1.83-02 (i.e., all results were below the 
assay quantitation limit of 1%), this attribute was not included in the commercial 
specification.  
• 
HPLC-SEC Region 4 was revised to be an action limit for the commercial release 
specification (S.4.1.01-02). It is also included as an attribute monitored in the on-going 
stability commitment (S.7.2.01-02).  
• 
The glycosylation (Oligomap) qualitative pattern assessment was added to S.4.1.01-02. 
 
The shelf-life attributes noted in S.7.3.01-03 reflect the set of attributes monitored during the 
conformance campaign relative to the release attributes noted in S.4.4.01-01 in effect at that time. 
As was done with the release specification following the conformance campaign, the attributes 
and shelf-life specifications to be monitored for the on-going stability commitment (S.7.2.01-02) 
were reviewed/revised for the commercial submission. Thus, the on-going stability commitment 
data in S.7.3.02-04 reflect the current set of attributes and shelf-life specifications listed in 
S.7.2.01-02, which represents the appropriate criteria for monitoring the long-term stability of the 
rFVIII molecule.  It is noted that there are attributes in the on-going stability commitment 
(S.7.2.01-02) that are not included in the commercial specification (S.4.1.01-02). For clarity, these 
additional attributes are still tested for release of the active substance; they are evaluated against 
action limits as noted in S.2.2.91-02.

Question/Consideration:
5.14. In section 3.2.S.6 Container closure system, it does not provide technical specifications for 
ethylene vinyl acetate bags, the specifications must include description and identification (and critical 
dimensions with drawings, where applicable). It does not describe the type of material of the inlet pipe 
and tube seal. In addition, it does not submit studies of the suitability of the material for protection 
against humidity and light.
Answer/Response:
The container closure system for BAY 81-8973 Drug Substance is pillow style 12” x 18” 
EVA (ethylene-vinyl acetate copolymer) bag with spike port and tubing. The material is 
qualified for use in Drug Substance (DS) manufacturing and long-term storage using the 
criteria outlined in  USP and EP. Storage bags were chosen as the container due to their large 
surface area to volume ratio which facilitates freezing and thawing. The EVA bags are 
supplied in manifold format to allow a closed operation for DS filling. After each bag is filled, 
the inlet tubing is sealed to close the container before the bag is separated from the manifold 
for blast freezing and storage. The EVA bags were implemented based upon the rFVIII 
platform process. The BAY 81-8973 DS has a similar formulation and fill size to the rFVIII-
FS DS. Therefore no development work was required on the EVA container closure system. 
 
Extractables/Leachables Assessment: EVA bags 
The manufacturer of the EVA bags has tested the plastic extensively for biocompatibility 
(ISO 10993 and USP methods). Tests have been conducted on freshly irradiated EVA plastic 
material (ISO 10993-3 through -11 and USP <87> and <88>) as well as irradiated material 
that has been aged for 2 years (ISO 10993-4,-5,-6,-10, and -11). All tests met ISO and USP 
compliance for biocompatibility. Additionally, a toxicology assessment using the extractables 
data provided by the vendor for the EVA bags was performed. The concentrations of potential 
leachables in a patient dose were estimated based on the maximum observed levels of 
extractables, i.e., worst case conditions. The objective of this exercise was to estimate the 
maximum potential exposure to the patient, thus using a conservative approach with respect to 
patient safety. The daily exposure levels of all identified species in Drug Substance were 
evaluated against permitted daily exposure limits and were determined to be below acceptable 
levels.

Question/Consideration:
Question I.3
Please provide comparative information on the stability of the drug before and after the 
change.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question I.3:
The trend charts shown below refer to the stability indicating parameters of the shelf life 
specification: appearance, mean assay, degradation products, dissolution and Microbial purity. 
The stability data from the reports P.8.3.901#004443699 (=MX65ES70) and 
P.8.3.01_022971169_03 (Climen phase 1) and P.8.3.01_022971164_03 (Climen phase 2) are 
taken into account. Considering that China belongs to climatic zone II as per Bayer SOPs, the 
data shown bases on climate II conditions (25°C/60% RH). For other climate conditions 
(30°C/65% RH and 40°C/75% RH), no separate trend charts is prepared. From the stability 
data provided, there is no significant difference between the batches produced before and after 
the change, which are all well within the shelf-life specification.

Batches 8V26, 8V27 and 8V28 (blue) exemplify the product quality before the change. The 
batches WEV6DJ, WEV6DK and WEV6DL (brown) describe the product quality after the 
change; these three batches were manufactured at Bayer Weimar.

Please note: When the batch analysis data is the same, the spots in the trend charts will 
overlap, so it is possible that only one or two spots will appear for the three batches, and all 
analysis data is from the attached stability data.

Please note that the site transfer was accompanied by an analytical method update, i.e. the 
analytical method for determining the assay and the analytical method for determining the 
degradation products varies between batches 8V26, 8V27, 8V28 (before change) and batches 
WEV6DJ, WEV6DK, WEV6DL (after change). The respective specification limits also differ 
for assay and degradation products.

[Table of before/after change procedures and acceptance criteria as provided in DOCUMENT]

1. Appearance 
The appearance is identical for all batches at all time stations. A trend chart was therefore not 
created. There is no change in stability trend after the site change.
2. Assay of Estradiol valerate
The data is almost unchanged over the storage time. No difference in stability behavior is 
observable for both data sets after the change. With the site transfer, the specification 
requirement for assay became more restrictive.
3. Degradation products of estradiol valerate, any individual
Results <0.1% are reported as 0.08%
The data is almost unchanged over the storage time. No difference in stability behavior is 
observable for both data sets after the change. With the site transfer, the specification 
requirement for degradation products became more restrictive.
4. Degradation product of estradiol valerate, total
Results <0.1% are reported as 0.08%
The data shows a slight increase over the storage period. The level of degradation products is 
lower in the data set of the batches produced at the new site (data set after the change). In 
combination with the lower specification limit, the quality of the SC Weimar product is at 
least comparable to the previous product.
5. Dissolution of estradiol valerate
The data remains almost unchanged throughout the storage period. The level of the mean 
dissolution rate is higher in the data set of the batches produced at the new site (data set after 
the change). The quality of the new site product is therefore at least comparable to the 
previous product.
6. Microbial purity
The microbial contamination results for the previous product were reported as "passed test" 
rather than by reporting concrete results, e.g. 10 CFU/g. Therefore, the comparison between 
the product before and after the change is made on the results "passes test" or "failed test".

The microbial purity is identical for all batches at all time stations:
Total aerobic microbial count (TAMC): passes test
Total combined yeast/mold count (TYMC): passes test
Escherichia coli: passes test

A trend chart was therefore not created. There is no change in stability trend after the site 
change.

In conclusion, the stability of products manufactured after the change are comparable with 
that manufactured before the change, we will complete the stability study to cover the shelf 
life and provide the stability data to CDE once data is available.

tablet (CLIMEN) (site Delpharm) (#004443699, unchanged)

method was validated with regard to:
• Specificity  
• Linearity for the drug substance  
• Accuracy (recovery rate) for the drug substance  
• Accuracy (recovery rate) for impurities/degradation products  
• Limit of quantitation (LOQ) for the drug substance  
• Precision of the instrument for the drug substance  
• Precision of the instrument for impurities/degradation products  
• Precision of the method for the drug substance  
• Precision of the method for impurities/degradation products  
• Intermediate precision of the method for the drug substance  
• Robustness 
The data presented in the technical registration document T.02.47 show that the method is 
suitable for the determination of rivaroxaban (identity, assay) and its impurities in Rivaroxaban 
coated tablet 10 mg.

The method is proven to be specific and the criteria set for linearity are met.  
For Linearity, nine solutions were prepared, the concentrations of which correspond to 
0.05 %, 0.5 %, 5.0 %, 25 %, 50 %, 70 %, 100 %, 120 % and 150 % of the theoretical 
rivaroxaban concentration in the test solution (0.20 mg/mL).
From the obtained peak areas the calibration line was determined by linear regression, 
please see Table 2 in the T.02.47.
The results obtained show that all requirements are fulfilled. The calibration curve is 
linear in the investigated range of 0.05-150 % relative to theoretical rivaroxaban 
concentration in the test solution (0.20 mg/mL). Thus linearity of the analytical procedure is 
verified.
Accuracy/Recovery rate was verified for both test parameters: Assay and Impurities.  
For Assay, three solutions were prepared by adding suitable quantities of drug substance 
stock solution to a placebo mixture in order to obtain rivaroxaban concentrations, which 
correspond to approx. 50 %, 100 % and 150 %, based on the theoretical concentration of 
rivaroxaban in the test solution (0.20 mg/mL). Each solution was injected three times and was 
analyzed as directed in Test procedure (T.02.02). The results were compared to the results from 
corresponding solutions without placebo and the recovery rates were calculated.
The results for Accuracy / Recovery Rate (Assay) are shown in Table 3 in the T.02.47. 
The requirements for "Accuracy" are fulfilled if the confidence interval (99 %) of the mean for 
the recovery rate includes the 100.0 % value or if the complete confidence interval is between 
99-101 %. The results obtained show that the confidence interval of the mean includes the 100.0 
% value. Thus accuracy of the analytical procedure is verified.
For Impurities, the impurity Oxaphthalimid was used as surrogate because no degradation 
products are specified for Rivaroxaban coated tablet 10 mg. The sample solutions were obtained 
by adding suitable quantities of Oxaphthalimid stock solutions to samples prepared according 
to the Test Procedure (T.02.02) at 3 different concentration levels (about 0.05 %, 0.20 %, and 
0.24 % based on the theoretical concentration of rivaroxaban in the test solution of 0.20 
mg/mL). Each concentration level was prepared three times from independent stock solutions. 
The results were compared to the results from corresponding solutions of Oxaphthalimid 
reference standard and the recovery rates were calculated.
The test data obtained for accuracy of impurities/degradation products are shown in Table 
4 in the T.02.47.
Accuracy is considered given if the mean recovery for each individual concentration level 
does not differ by more than 4 times the respective variation coefficient of the method from the 
theoretical value (100 %) and the mean value of all recoveries does not differ by more than 2 
times the variation coefficient of the method from the theoretical value (100 %). Alternatively, 
the requirements for the criterion "accuracy" are fulfilled if the confidence interval (99 %) of 
the mean includes the 100.0 % value or is within 80 – 120 %.
All acceptance criteria for accuracy described above were fulfilled including the alternative 
acceptance criteria.

Precision of the instrument and method as well as intermediate precision were verified for 
both test parameters: Assay and Impurities.
For Assay, the precision of the instrument (apparatus) was checked by repeated analysis 
of a rivaroxaban solution. The control solution (100 % level based on the theoretical 
concentration in the test solution 0.20 mg/mL) was prepared as directed in Test procedure 
(T.02.02). The solution was injected six times in succession, and the coefficient of variation of 
the detector signals obtained was calculated.
The results for Precision of the Instrument (Assay) are shown in Table 6 in the T.02.47.
The requirements for "Precision of the instrument" are fulfilled if the coefficient of 
variation is  1.5 %. The obtained result of the coefficient of variation is 0.3 %, thus precision 
of the instrument is verified.
For the precision of the method, six samples were prepared with concentrations of drug 
substance corresponding to approx. 50 %, 100 % and 150 % based on the theoretical 
concentration of active ingredient in the test solution (0.20 mg/mL). These solutions were 
prepared by adapting the number of tablets accordingly. The coefficient of variation of the six 
test solutions was calculated.
The results for Precision of the Method (Assay) are shown in Table 10 in the T.02.47. 
The requirements for "Precision of the method" are fulfilled, if the coefficient of variation 
for each concentration level is  3.0 %. Based on the results obtained, the requirements are 
fulfilled. Thus, precision of the method for the analytical procedure is verified.
For Impurities, the criteria for “precision of the instrument (apparatus)” are 
fulfilled, if the coefficients of variation are ≤ 15.0 % for any level.
Because no degradation products are specified, the impurity Oxaphthalimid was used as 
surrogate. The sample solutions were obtained by adding suitable quantities of Oxaphthalimid 
solutions to samples prepared according to the Test Procedure (T.02.02) at 3 different 
concentration levels (about 0.05 %, 0.20 %, and 0.24 % based on the theoretical concentration 
of rivaroxaban in the test solution of 0.20 mg/mL). A single test solution was prepared for each 
concentration level and injected six times respectively.
The test solutions were injected six times one after another, and the coefficients of variation 
of the detector signals obtained were calculated for each concentration level.
The test data obtained for precision of the instrument for impurities/degradation products 
are shown in Table 7, Table 8 and Table 9 in the T.02.47.  
The obtained results demonstrate the requirements to be fulfilled. Thus, precision of the 
instrument for impurities/degradation products is verified.
The criteria for "precision of the method" are fulfilled, if the coefficient of variation is ≤ 
15.0 % for any level.
Because no degradation products are specified the impurity Oxaphthalimid was used as 
surrogate. The sample solutions were obtained by adding suitable quantities of Oxaphthalimid 
solutions to samples prepared according to the Test Procedure (T.02.02) at 3 different 
concentration levels (about 0.05 %, 0.20 %, and 0.24 % based on the theoretical concentration
of rivaroxaban in the test solution of 0.20 mg/mL). Six test solutions were prepared for each 
concentration level and each test solution was injected once. The test solutions were injected 
once one after another, and the coefficients of variation of the detector signals obtained were 
calculated for each concentration level.
The test data obtained for precision of the method for impurities/degradation products are 
presented in the Table 11, Table 12 and Table 13 in the T.02.47.
The obtained results demonstrate the requirements to be fulfilled. Thus, precision of the 
method for impurities/degradation products is verified.
For the test of the intermediate precision, six samples were prepared with rivaroxaban 
concentrations corresponding to 100 %, based on the theoretical concentration in the test 
solution (0.20 mg/mL), independently by two analysts (A and B) on four different days using 
different equipment. The mean assay and the coefficient of variation of each sequence were 
calculated.
The results for Intermediate Precision are presented in Table 14 in the T.02.47. 
The requirements for "Intermediate precision" are fulfilled if the coefficient of variation 
for each sequence is  3.0 %. The obtained results demonstrate the requirements to be fulfilled. 
Thus intermediate precision of the analytical procedure is verified.

Dissolution. The quantitation of drug dissolved from Rivaroxaban coated tablet 10 mg 
is measured by HPLC with UV/VIS detection or UV/VIS spectrophotometry. Both methods are 
validated. The validation covers the requirements given in the ICH-guideline Q2 (R1). The 
validation data demonstrate that the analytical procedure is suitable to measure dissolution of 
Rivaroxaban 10 mg in 900 mL of acetate buffer pH 4.5 + 0.2 % SDS.  
Please refer to the technical registration document T.02.50.
The HPLC method was validated with regard to:
• Specificity  
• Linearity: Linearity of standard solution and Linearity of test solution 
• Quantitation limit 
• Accuracy
