Question/Consideration:
Question 4
Specification of the products & material used in its manufacturing (Darolutamide 300 mg 
Film-coated Tablets)
Impurity DARO-IMP G & DARO-V are not found mentioned in the submitted Specifications. 
Please clarify.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 4 (P.5.5):
Regarding the impurity specification, Bayer would like to comment as follows:
DARO-IMP G and DARO-V have never been found at detectable levels in any long-term or 
accelerated stability studies of Darolutamide film-coated tablet 0.3 g. These degradation 
products have been observed only under artificial strong stress conditions. Therefore, in line 
with international guidance DARO-IMP G and DARO-V do not need to be individually 
specified and are instead controlled by the specification for any unspecified degradation 
products. Batch analysis data gathered since the original NDA approval / launch of the global 
product confirmed the absence of these impurities and hence proved the applied control 
strategy.

Question/Consideration:
Clarify and/or provide support corresponding to risk analysis, validation protocols, batch 
manufacturing date, IQ, OQ and PQ qualifications of equipment that were part of the 
manufacturing process, Cp and CpK analysis and status maintenance reports validated for the 
aseptic manufacturing and filling process for BAY 81 – 8973 DP as reference is made in the 
respective information to the validation of this process, which corresponds to a run divided 
into two batches with different closure of the secondary container (reconstitution cap and 
aluminum seal, Folio 1628, BAY 81-8973 DP).
Answer/Response:
BAY 81-8973 lyophilisate Process Validation and/or Evaluation is provided in stated in 
P.3.5.01#009825861_02. All conformance batches were filled into the proposed commercial 
primary packaging system (10 mL colorless glass type I siliconized glass vial with 
bromobutyl gray type I stopper for lyophilization). Selected 250 IU, 1000 IU, 2000IU, and
3000 IU batches were split and capped with secondary packaging systems (reconstitution cap 
and/or aluminum caps) for placement on a stability program. Since the secondary container 
closure does not have product contact, the only potential impact on product quality would be 
container closure integrity, which is independent of vial fill strength.
Furthermore, the license for BAY81-8973 drug product only identifies aluminum seals as the 
approved closure. Due to business reasons the reconstitution cap was not licensed for any 
market. We hereby confirm that the aluminium seal with plastic flip-off top is the licensed 
seal for primary container closure. Refer to P.2.4.01 #009825688 Pharmaceutical 
Development - Container Closure System.
Final product manufacturing is carried out in three facilities; The Sterile Fill & Finish Facility 
(SFF), Packaging, and Warehouse. All equipment is multi product use. The SFF is designed 
to mitigate the potential for mix-ups and cross-contamination via segregation of materials, 
personnel and process flow. The SFF production areas were qualified using environmental 
monitoring (EM) of surfaces, active and passive air sampling, total particulates at 0.5 μm and 
5.0 μm. The heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) system qualification included 
installation and operation qualifications (Installation Qualification [IQ] and Operation 
Qualification [OQ], respectively). Air flow visualization and system balancing were 
performed to ensure proper air cascades are maintained.

Major Equipment
Qualification of all systems included IQ, OQ, and Performance Qualification (PQ) unless
otherwise noted. IQ, OQ, and PQ include verification and/or tests of the following:
• 
Installation per engineering drawings and specifications 
• 
Materials of construction per specification 
• 
Proper operation according to design criteria and specified range of operation, including on-
board software and/or controllers 
• 
Proper interface and control with the distributed control system (DCS), if applicable 
• 
Instrument identification and calibration 
• 
Load verifications 
• 
Consistency of performance with operating ranges
Qualification of all major equipment met pre-defined criteria demonstrating acceptable
operation, state of control, and fitness for its intended use.
The BAY 81-8973 DP manufacturing process includes the Final Bulk Formulation, Filling, 
Freeze-Drying, and Vial Capping processes. The evaluation of the process validation was 
based on manufacturing process parameters and in-process controls. Each validation batch 
was tested for compliance with the specification. Process validation follows a lifecycle
approach which includes planning, design/development, validation testing, and maintenance 
of the process in a validated state. The process validation strategy involves process validation 
unit studies, manufacturing of conformance batches, and monitoring and validation of process 
changes following initial validation.

media during NLT 14 day incubation period. The test is in compliance with ICH Q4B Annex 
8 (Sterility Test General Chapter) and meets Ph.Eur. 2.6.1, Sterility, JP 4.06 Sterility Test and 
USP <71> Sterility Tests.

Question/Consideration:
Clarify and/or provide the viral safety validation study, where methods and tests are 
established that have statistically proven effectiveness and precision to detect a certain 
amount of viruses, that is, detection limits are established and quantification of viral particles 
in viability assays. Methods other than those provided for in the regulations must demonstrate 
their reproducibility, repeatability and linearity.
Answer/Response:
The virus clearance validation experimentation and summary results are described in A.2.4.50 
“Clearance Testing - Purification Process Clearance Testing,” and details are included in each 
individual study reports (A.2.50 “Study Reports of Virus Clearance Validation”).
A highly effective virus inactivation step employing Octoxinol 10has been integrated into the 
cell culture harvesting and membrane adsorption (MA) capture steps.  A viral filtration step
has been implemented at the end of the purification process that robustly removes viruses 
including parvovirus.  In addition, the upstream cell culture and downstream purification 
steps, before and after virus inactivation or removal, are physically segregated to avoid carry-
over of impurities or adventitious agents from one process step to the next.  These measures 
greatly minimize the risk of contamination of BAY 81-8973 final product by adventitious 
viruses.
The downstream manufacturing process for BAY 81-8973 has been validated for virus 
clearance capability using four model viruses and scaled-down systems representative of the 
cGMP manufacturing steps. The model viruses were xenotropic murine leukemia virus (X-
MuLV), pseudorabies virus (PRV), Reo 3 type virus (Reo3) and porcine parvovirus (PPV).  
The virus clearance capability of process steps was determined by measuring the 
log10reduction factor (LRF) for viral infectivity.  Virus infectivity was determined using 
cytopathic effect (CPE) based TCID50 assays to compare the amount of model virus 
introduced before the process step to the remaining amount of virus after the process step.
The virus clearance studies have demonstrated significant clearance of all four model viruses 
by the manufacturing process (Table 2-2 and A.2.4.50 “Clearance Testing - 
PurificationProcess Clearance Testing”).  The studies using naive membrane adsorber and 
column resins in the BAY 81-8973 manufacturing process gave a total log10reduction factor 
(LRF) of ≥ 17.12, ≥ 17.99, ≥ 6.13, and ≥ 8.73 for X-MuLV, PRV, PPV and Reo3 
respectively.  The studies using reused membrane adsorber and column resins achieved a total 
LRF of ≥ 13.72, ≥ 20.61, ≥ 7.22, and ≥ 8.94 for X-MuLV, PRV, PPVand Reo3 respectively.  
The “≥” sign in front of the LRF value indicates that it is the minimum LRF validated for the 
process based on the evaluated process steps and virus assay sensitivity.
Under the worst case scenario, the total number of endogenous retrovirus-like particles in the 
clarified tissue culture fluid (cTCF) harvest material used to produce a 4000 IU dose is 
approximately 107.32particlesper dose(7.32 log10). Therefore, significant retrovirus clearance 
by the BAY81-8973 manufacturing process provides a high level safety margin of ≥ 9.80 
log10with naive membrane adsorber and column resins and ≥ 6.40 log10for reused membrane 
adsorber and resins.  In addition, the effective and robust clearance of other adventitious non-
retroviruses by the manufacturing process, particularly by the virus filtration step which 
completely removed all 4 model viruses, has demonstrated that the BAY 81-7983 drug 
substance and final product are virologically safe.

Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1 (3.2.P.5.3):
This response document provides a strategy on a decision taken regarding handling of 
deficiency letter and the submission itself.
The dispatch of REC20874 to register Bayer Bitterfeld GmbH (BTF) as alternative 
manufacturing site for Xarelto coated tablet 10 mg took place in 2022 and comprised In-house 
Release and Shelf life specifications and methods, which were valid at that time before 
implementation of Release and Shelf life specifications and methods aligned with the Ph.Eur. 
monograph <3021> for Rivaroxaban coated tablets.
In course of submission’s review, the Nicaraguan Health Authority issued two deficiency letters 
(DLs) with the same request to provide chromatograms, and spectrum as support of the 
calculation of the linearity, precision and accuracy for the In-house methods of Assay, 
Impurities and Dissolution.
For the first one and a corresponding responses document, please refer to VV-RFI-002996. The 
response document provides references to the analytical data currently presented in respective 
technical registration documents for the method validation. However, these responses have 
been considered by the Health Authority as uncomplete, therefore the second DL is issued.
Two options have been considered by the team of local RA managers, QC experts and RA CMC  
to address the second request:
- 
Option 1: to provide the requested data by a due date; 
- 
Option 2: if Option 1 is not possible for any reason, to cancel the BTF submission to the 
HA in order to avoid its rejection and re-submit it again including Release and Shelf life 
specifications and methods aligned with the Ph.Eur. monograph.
According to the QC experts, the validation of the In-house methods is a compilation of past 
experiments from 2007 to 2019 and, therefore, its retrieval requires much efforts and time 
investment and, thus, is not considered possible. In addition, all manufacturing sites producing 
Xarelto coated tablet 10 mg have already implemented Release and Shelf life specifications and 
methods aligned with the Ph.Eur. monograph, which is regarded a quality standard now.
For this reason, Option 1 has been excluded while Option 2 has been chosen to proceed. 
According to local regulations, it is allowed to cancel a submission to the HA in order to avoid 
its rejection and re-submit it again supplemented by additional data if needed.

Question 4
Regarding the Dissolution profile, please explain
1. Why did you add SLS?
2. Do you have the dissolution profile of Drug product without adding “SLS”? If yes, please 
provide.
3. the Dissolution profile point that CV or RSD is more than 20%, please provide the 
Calculation detail of the multivariate for Evaluation
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 4 (P.2):
1. According to Ph. Eur. 5.17.1, a 3-10 fold sink condition is recommended for dissolution
tests. To reach the minimum 3-fold sink condition, 900 mg of darolutamide needs to be 
dissolvable. Since the solubility of darolutamide in aqueous buffer solutions in 
physiological pH is about 14-23 µg/mL, a surfactant is needed in the dissolution medium 
to dissolve 300 mg of darolutamide and to achieve three-fold sink conditions in the 
relevant volume. The amount of SLS in each medium was selected based on the data 
obtained from the solubility tests presented in document P.2.2.02 Pharmaceutical 
Development - Dissolution Profiles, Table 4-2.
2. Dissolution of Darolutamide 0.3 g tablet without Sodium Lauryl Sulfate (SLS) has been
evaluated in earlier studies. The evaluation of the conducted dissolution profiles 
confirmed that in none of the media without SLS a dissolution of significantly more of 
10% could be achieved due to the low solubility of darolutamide in aqueous media. 
Dissolution profiles for Darolutamide 0.3 g film-coated tablet in media without SLS have 
been presented in document P.2.2.02 Pharmaceutical Development - Dissolution Profiles, 
Figure 4-1.
3. For batch 2125122 in dissolution medium 0.1M HCl pH 1.2 1.0% SLS the RSD is more
than 20% at 10 min time point and f2 statistic therefore has been disregarded.
The similarity has been evaluated according to model independent multivariate confidence 
region where upper 90% confidence limit 5.1 is less than Similarity limit (10%) of 9.1. 
(Please refer to dissolution profile comparisons presented in P.2.2.02-02, Table 6-2, 
footnote c.) Similarity between dissolution profiles can be concluded on 10% level, if the 
upper confidence limit for the multidimensional distance is less than the similarity limit 
related to the corresponding accepted difference (10%), thus similarity was concluded.
For the batch 2125122 the first five time points were considered in the evaluation.
For the analysis of the dissolution profile with PhB pH 6.8 1% SLS the 10 min RSD value 
still fulfills the criteria for the f2-test as the rounded value is not more than 20 % as
requested in the guidance. Therefore, similarity evaluation has been conducted based on

Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1 (3.2.P.5.3, 3.2.P.8):
This response document provides a strategy on a decision taken regarding handling of 
deficiency letter and the submission itself.
The dispatch of REC20874 to register Bayer Bitterfeld GmbH (BTF) as alternative 
manufacturing site for Xarelto coated tablet 15 mg took place in 2022 and comprised In-house 
Release and Shelf life specifications and methods, which were valid at that time before 
implementation of Release and Shelf life specifications and methods aligned with the Ph.Eur. 
monograph <3021> for Rivaroxaban coated tablets.
In course of submission’s review, the Nicaraguan Health Authority issued two deficiency letters 
(DLs) with the same request to provide chromatograms, and spectrum as support of the 
calculation of the linearity, precision and accuracy for the In-house methods of Assay, 
Impurities and Dissolution.
For the first one and a corresponding responses document, please refer to VV-RFI-002997. The 
response document provides references to the analytical data currently presented in respective 
technical registration documents for the method validation. However, these responses have 
been considered by the Health Authority as uncomplete, therefore the second DL is issued.
Two options have been considered by the team of local RA managers, QC experts and RA CMC  
to address the second request:
- 
Option 1: to provide the requested data by a due date; 
- 
Option 2: if Option 1 is not possible for any reason, to cancel the BTF submission to the 
HA in order to avoid its rejection and re-submit it again including Release and Shelf life 
specifications and methods aligned with the Ph.Eur. monograph.
According to the QC experts, the validation of the In-house methods is a compilation of past 
experiments from 2007 to 2019 and, therefore, its retrieval requires much efforts and time 
investment and, thus, is not considered possible. In addition, all manufacturing sites producing 
Xarelto coated tablet 15 mg have already implemented Release and Shelf life specifications and 
methods aligned with the Ph.Eur. monograph, which is regarded a quality standard now.

For this reason, Option 1 has been excluded while Option 2 has been chosen to proceed. 
According to local regulations, it is allowed to cancel a submission to the HA in order to avoid 
its rejection and re-submit it again supplemented by additional data if needed.
keywords: analytical method validation; chromatograms; HPLC-method; drug product specification; Stability data

Question/Consideration:
Question 1:
To avoid rejection of the change of specifications, the local consultant has recommended to 
include the "acceptance criterion" of identity tests describing the criteria and meaning of Must 
Comply 
It is important to mention that this type of request was made for Finerenone product because 
the HA is reviewing this info. Could you please check the document Translation that we have 
uploade including the comments that we need in the modified TRD
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1:
In April 2021 a new monograph 3021 for <Rivaroxaban tablets> became valid in the 
supplement 10.4 of the 10th edition of the European Pharmacopoeia.
Bayer AG is the originator of Rivaroxaban tablets, therefore our former in-house test 
procedures and specification are also the origin of the Ph. Eur. Monograph 3021 
<Rivaroxaban tablets>. However, the specification and test procedure have been adapted to 
Ph.Eur. and are aligned now.
The identification tests “Identity A (Ph.Eur.) and Identity B (Ph.Eur.) are introduced as 
additional parameter to specification for Rivaroxaban tablets as required by the Ph.Eur. 
Monograph. These test parameters are already met with the former test “Identity (HPLC)” of 
current applied Bayer specification and test procedure for Rivaroxaban coated tablets. Test 
“Identity A (Ph.Eur)” is confirmed by the UV spectrum of the main peak in the HPLC 
chromatograms of the reference standard and the test item. The test “Identity B (Ph.Eur.)”is 
met by defining both main peak retention time and size in the HPLC chromatograms of the 
reference standard and the test item. If both results are met, the acceptance criteria is 
documented as “complies” in the certificate of analysis. By referencing in the technical 
registration document T.02.02 (Test procedure) to Ph.Eur., an additional description of the 
acceptance criteria is not necessary from our perspective.
Please find enclosed the Ph.Eur. monograph and the extract out of it below: 
 
IDENTIFICATION 
A. Record the UV spectrum of the principal peak in the 
chromatograms obtained with the solutions used in 
the assay, with a diode array detector in the range of 
210-400 nm. 
Results: the UV spectrum of the principal peak in 
the chromatogram obtained with the test solution is 
similar to the UV spectrum of the principal peak in the 
chromatogram obtained with reference solution (a). 
 
B. Examine the chromatograms obtained in the assay. 
Results: the principal peak in the chromatogram obtained 
with the test solution is similar in retention time and size
to the principal peak in the chromatogram obtained with 
reference solution (a). 
 
Source:  
Ph. Eur. monograph 3021 <Rivaroxaban tablets>

Request: Setup adequate formulas for corrected peak areas.
To do calibrations, actual calculations are needed to get corrected peak areas.
Answer/Response:
To do calibrations, actual calculations are needed to get corrected peak areas.
1. Calculate corrected peak of each standard solution (two of them)
Corrected peak area = Detected peak area * (Targeted amount of reference standard / Amount of reference standard actually taken) * (100 / Purity of reference standard in %)
2. Check whether two peak areas’ difference are within acceptance criteria defined in the description (NMT 2.5 % for this case).
3. Calculate average peak area of two corrected peak areas, calculated from #1
Average peak area = (Corrected peak area 1 + Corrected peak area 2) / 2

Among the steps described above, the calculation formula in #1 is described in local analytical procedure submitted.
Unless it is incorrect, the formula will be included in updated Korean license of Climen 21.

Answer/Response:
The IPC “Initial Viable Cell Density” at the step Thawing of the (Working) Cell Bank is a general quality attribute (GQA) as defined in S.2.4.01. The IPC (GQA) is intended to ensure consistent process performance and is not intended to have a direct impact on product quality.
In the S.2.4.01 is foreseen that IPC limits are reviewed during the product life cycle:
“On-Going Process Monitoring and Improvements in IPC Limits: As additional experience and data are gained during commercial manufacturing, the proposed IPCs and their action limits will be reevaluated. IPCs that are found over time to have limited predictive power will be removed from consideration. New IPCs may be also added when deemed appropriate”

The “Initial Viable Cell Density” IPC limit is widened as a result of this IPC review, using available data from all working cell bank (WCB) lots used in production. For production of Aflibercept drug substance intermediate (DSI), three WCBs were qualified according to the approved protocol (S.2.3.51). The most recent WCB (8005700007) generated data demonstrating that an initial VCD below the current Lower Action Limit still resulted in DSI material complying with the release specifications.

Question/Consideration: Based on justification regarding the elimination of main peak lift-off volume chromatography, please explain what is meant by transition analysis (TA).
Answer/Response:
Both lift-off volume and transition analysis are methods performed by Regeneron to monitor column performance and detect possible deterioration of the chromatography column.
Transition analysis (TA) is the analysis of the response at the column outlet following a step-change in the chromatography. For example, when a gradient is changed, this will - after transition through the column - result in the change in conductivity at the column outlet. The output signal change is then comprehensively analyzed (Regeneron analyses the parameters non-gaussian height equivalent of a theoretical plate (NGHETP) and skewness) and compared against historic limits.
This TA is part of a comprehensive review performed by Regeneron to ensure the chromatography columns continue to perform as expected.

In the previous response to request EREG100366VR12300162, Bayer provided the in Annex to question 1 the evaluation of the use of TA compared to lift-off-volume for historic Eylea batches showing that TA is more accurate in detecting column deterioration.
keywords: test method; analytical development of test method; Manufacturing Process Development; HPLC-method; system suitability test

Question/Consideration: To provide a risk assessment regarding the expansion of the permissible limits of the initial density of viable cells at the stage of thawing of the cell bank and confirmation of the lack of impact of the change on the quality of API.
Answer/Response:
In preparation of the proposed change to the IPC limit, an impact assessment was performed. The IPC “Initial Viable Cell Density (VCD)” at the step thawing of the cell bank is classified as a general quality attribute (GQA) per the aflibercept IPCs program summarized in the approved S.2.4.01 – Chapter 2 Critical and General Controls.
The purpose of the aflibercept seed expansion unit operations is to expand the aflibercept cell culture from the 500 mL shake flask to the 3,000 L bioreactor to achieve a sufficient number of cells to seed the 10,000 L production bioreactor. This quality attribute is categorized as a general (non-critical) attribute since it is used to monitor operational consistency and, historically, has not had a direct impact on the product quality when maintained within normal operating ranges. Of note, transfer of cells for the 20 L cell bag and for the 50 L, 500 L, and 3,000 L bioreactors is VCD-driven whereas the transfer of cells, to subsequent steps, for shake flask and the 2 L cell bag is time-driven. Therefore, the expansion of permissible VCD limit for shake flask initial VCD does not impact the transfer determinations for the cells. Furthermore, historical review of aflibercept drug substance production data showed that any variability seen in the early seed expansion unit operations does not persist into the production bioreactor (10,000 L), as the cell density is able to recover to levels that are in alignment with historical experience at the production bioreactor step.
Additionally, there are other IPCs in-place that ensure consistent cell growth and expansion. These include, but are not limited to, the initial VCD, final VCD and final viability of the 2 L and 20 L cell bags along with the respective IPCs of the 50 L, 500 L, and 3,000 L expansion bioreactors.
The evaluation confirmed that the process will continue to operate within the established process time limits which are well within the validated LIVCA Limit (839 hr:57min – 1068 hr:59min), therefore there is not a risk of experiencing population doublings beyond those proven with the LIVCA lot or a risk to the genetic stability of the cell culture as a result of the proposed updates to expansion times.
Therefore, with these controls in place, the Sponsor concluded that it is acceptable to modify the initial VCD for cell thaw as this change shows no impact to cell culture performance and product quality.
The currently approved limit was established based on guidance, practices, and data available at the time to be able to detect any variability outside historical experience. The reassessment of the shake flask initial VCD GQA is based on the approach defined in S.2.4.01 in section “On-Going Process Monitoring and Improvements in IPC Limits: As additional experience and data are gained during commercial manufacturing, the proposed IPCs and their action limits will be re-evaluated.”

Considering the low risk of the proposed change, formal validation runs were not performed. Data have been collected from multiple commercial lots produced within the expanded viable cell density (VCD) range (changed from 0.40-0.68 x 106 to 0.27 – 0.68 x 106). Data for eight commercial lots are provided in this response and demonstrate that there is no downstream impact to the process. Question/Consideration: In connection with changes in the production process, namely changes to the mixing bag, provide a statement confirming the absence of impact from changes in process parameters obtained from a previously approved risk assessment.
Answer/Response:
The Sponsor confirms that changes to the mixing time and mixing speed parameters for pooling and mixing, dilution, and the formulation process steps are not expected to impact product quality as justified below.
Changes to mixing time and mixing speed were implemented for process consistency among Regeneron’s manufactured products and were based on the performed validation studies. Mixing validation studies determined that the proposed mixing times and mixing speeds were appropriate independent of product or process area. The updated mixing times and mixing speeds (P.3.3.02  /P.2.3.02) are still considered to be general (non-critical) process parameters that, when maintained within a specified range, ensures operational reliability and consistency and are not expected to have a direct impact on product quality (SISPQ).
The change to FlexSafe bags is considered a process improvement as the FlexSafe bags have increased tensile strength, tear resistance, and flexibility. Furthermore, this change is considered to be low risk to aflibercept product quality because:
• The product contact material on the inside of the bag is the same in both bags.
• Extractable and leachable studies identified no components of concern and concluded that the two bags were functionally equivalent. (see S.2.5.01)
• Both bags have identical gas barriers and mixing impellers.
• The FlexSafe bag is expected to produce similar shear stresses, as the highest shear stresses are experienced around the impeller and both mixing systems operate at the same tip speed.
In summary, the changing of mixing time and mixing speed is of low risk and there is no expected impact to aflibercept product quality based upon this change.

Question/Consideration: In connection with the extension of the permissible limits of the specification of "Purity" of HLZ by the SE-UPLC method for the shelf life, provide a risk assessment regarding the lack of impact of the change on the quality of HLZ.
Answer/Response:
The shift of the limits for purity by SE-UPLC of 0.3% compared to the SE-HPLC method is based on the consistent shift introduced by the analytical method change. This was observed for both: 1) reference standard measurements indicative of the method performance itself and 2) also for 70 matched pairs of release and stability samples where both SE-UPLC and SE-HPLC were used to measure the same timepoint of the same batch. The change of the acceptance criterion therefore only corrects for this shift due to the analytical method without a change in the purity of the Aflibercept drug product or any impact on the other specification parameters.

Question/Consideration:
Question 2
Please pay attention to the peaks of degradation impurities (excluding excipient peaks) with 
relative retention times of ≤ 0.3. Please provide relevant research information in conjunction 
with the API to prove whether the excipient peaks cover up the degradation impurity peaks, 
and to prove the rationality of the deduction method of the excipient peaks.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 2 ( CTD section):
Please note that as it is stated in the Evaluation of Stability Data TRD T.05.15 and Stability 
Data / Light Sensitivity TRD T.05.05, under the defined storage conditions, only degradation 
by light is one of the possible causes of degradation products.
The resulting degradation product is Impurity A, which can be detected using the established 
analytical method within a runtime of approx. 6.4 minutes (RRT 0.86).
Document T.04.40 provides chromatograms of single compound injections, multiple 
compound injections and overlays of chromatograms.
From the document it can be seen that the excipients elute in the initial region (0 to 1 min) of 
the chromatograms, while nimodipine and the Impurity A elute beyond the 5 minutes.
In the area of relative retention times of ≤ 0.3, it is possible that at the beginning of a 
chromatographic run, injection peaks may be seen in the region of t0, which might come 
from:
• dissolving solvent for sample
• contamination from flow paths where mobile phases come into contact with valves, 
needles, columns, tubes, etc.,
• impurities in the sample
• acids, bases, salts in the sample

(Source: Waters Knowledge Base, 
https://support.waters.com/KB_Inst/Chromatography/WKB200815_What_is_an_injection_pe
ak)
These peaks might be visible in addition to the shown peaks in the T.04.40 document.

Potential degradation products of Nimodipine
Based on scientific literature it can be concluded that Nimodipine would form degradation 
products that are like nimodipine in their core structure. It can therefore be assumed that, with 
the established chromatographic method, they would elute in ranges beyond RRT<0.3. As 
example of this is impurity A, which elutes as a photolytic degradation product, in the range 
of RRT 0.86.

Acidic / Basic degradation products
In the paper: Brazilian Journal of Analytical Chemistry 2021, Volume 8, Issue 30, pp 43-58; 
doi: 10.30744/brjac.2179-3425.AR-52-2020, Nimodipine was treated with acid and base to 
generate degradation products. The paper suggests the following pathways for the formation 
of degradation products.
The following degradation pathways are suggested for the acidic and basic degradation.
Suggested acid degradation:

Source: Brazilian Journal of Analytical Chemistry 2021, Volume 8, Issue 30, pp 43-58; doi: 
10.30744/brjac.2179-3425.AR-52-2020

Suggested basic degradation:
Source: Brazilian Journal of Analytical Chemistry 2021, Volume 8, Issue 30, pp 43-58; doi: 
10.30744/brjac.2179-3425.AR-52-2020

It can be concluded from this and other papers, that parts of the nimodipine molecule are 
cleaved, but the core structure remains. Therefore, it is unlikely that an acid / base degradation 
product would eluate in the range of relative retention times of ≤ 0.3.

We would like to mention that the Nimodipine solution 0.02 % for infusion contains a buffer 
system of sodium citrate and citric acid, which maintains the pH of the solution in the range 
of 6.0 to 7.5. This buffer system keeps the solution in a range where it is unlikely that these 
conditions will cause acidic or alkaline degradation.

Thermal and oxidative stress
In the paper “Determination of Nimodipine in the Presence of its Degradation Products and 
Overall Kinetics through a Stability-Indicating LC Method” in the Journal of 
Chromatographic Science, Volume 51, Issue 6, July 2013, Pages 511–516, 
(https://doi.org/10.1093/chromsci/bms174).
Nimodipine was also exposed to oxidative and thermal stress. The following conditions were 
chosen:

“Oxidative degradation
Oxidative stress was performed in Nimodipine solutions diluted with 30% H2O2 
maintained at room temperature and protected from light. The sample was analyzed 
over seven days.

Thermal degradation
The thermal degradation was performed at 80 ± 2°C in a conventional oven (DeLeo 
797). Nimodipoine solutions in acetonitrile were maintained in amber vials that were 
hermetically closed with stoppers. Aliquots of the sample were collected and analyzed 
over 24 h.”

During the investigations for the above-mentioned publication, it was found that “No 
degradation was observed under thermal and oxidative stress conditions.”.

There are additional publications available that were able to generate degradation products, 
but under harsher conditions, e.g. thermal stress at 120°C for 4 h (Source: International 
Journal of Nanomedicine, 3407-3419, https://doi.org/10.2147/IJN.S130348)

Under the recommended storage conditions, we consider the risk of thermally or oxidatively 
induced degradation to be non-existent. Therefore, nimodipine degradation products are not to 
be expected in the relative retention times of ≤ 0.3.

Photolytic stress
In contrast to the above-mentioned API degradation pathways, it is more likely (for example 
due to inadequate handling) that the degradation product Impurity A is formed under the 
influence of light.

It is well-known that Nimodipine is sensitive to light, proven by various publications. 
Publications also show that one contamination is primarily formed under the influence of 
light. This is also stated in the European Pharmacopeia: “Exposure to ultraviolet light leads to 
the formation of a nitrophenylpyridine derivative.”
The nitrophenylpyridine derivative is known as Impurity A (according to European 
Pharmacopeia). Impurity A has a similar core structure like Nimodipine, with a retention time 
near to Nimodipine (Retention times: Nimodipine approx. 7.4 min.; Nitropyridine compound 
approx. 6.4 min.).
Which does not overlap with the ≤ 0.3 Relative Retention Time (RRT).

Summary and Conclusion
Under the stress conditions mentioned, it seems most likely that API degradation products are 
formed under the influence of light. This possible degradation pathway is well known and is 
also mentioned in the respective pharmacopoeias and needs to be taken into account. The 
resulting impurity (Impurity A) can be detected and quantified from the established 
chromatographic method. Impurity A elutes in the range > 0.3 RRT.
Based on the above stated information and with the help of the chromatograms provided in 
the document T.04.40, we are convinced that there are no API degradation products in the ≤ 
0.3 Relative Retention Time (RRT) range. The peaks located in the initial range of the 
chromatograms (0 to 1 min) are due to the excipients in the product, as the chromatograms 
provided in the T.04.40 document shows.

Question/Consideration:
Question 3
Justify the absence of forced degradation study in related validation.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 3 ( CTD section): P.8.3
The validation of any analytical method typically accounts for the effect of degradation that 
can reasonably occur during drug manufacturing, transport and storage. The type and level of 
degradation that is considered corresponds to the degradation during long-term and 
accelerated storage of the drug and during realistic deviations, e.g. temperature excursions 
during transport. The relevant validation parameters are typically specificity (for example 
does a degradant interfere with the determination of the active ingredient or another known 
impurity) and linearity of the method for the known degradants (for example can a trend due 
to degradation be detected during stability).
For Finerenone coated tablets, it was established that only type of degradation occurs, even 
under stress conditions that are well beyond those that can be considered realistic; please refer 
to the stress stability study P.8.3.04_022455084_01 but also to the method development 
mentioned in the technical document P.5.3.20_022944048_01. Please note that the data from 
the stress study mentioned in the P.8.3.04_022455084_01 can be consider as “forced 
degradation conditions”. Only the degradation product rac-amidonaphthyridine (BAY 
1040818) increases significantly, e.g. at high temperatures of 60°C and 80°C and hydrolytic 
stress. The method validation (P.5.3.01_022385499_02) covers this degradation product with 
respect to both specificity (see chapter 4.1) and linearity (see chapter 4.2.2). Furthermore, also 
in the method development P.5.3.20_022944048_01 the degradation products which are 
increased under stress conditions are considered (see chapter 2.3 and 2.4). As a result, using 
any stress samples for any further tests within the scope of the method validation has no 
additional informative value.

Question/Consideration: You are requested to provide a more detailed written description for the manufacture process of the drug substance, (reactions times, pH, temperatures, etc.).
Answer/Response:
BAY 2927088 hydrate micronized drug substance is manufactured through the following steps:
BAY 2927088 crude: To a suspension of (S)-dioxane-pyridyl-thioamide in methanol and sulfuric acid, an aqueous solution of hydrogen peroxide-urea-adduct is added at 45 °C and stirring is continued for 14 h. An aqueous solution of sodium hydroxide is added and the mixture is cooled to 20 °C. BAY 2927088 crude is isolated from the resulting suspension by filtration, washed with methanol and purified water, and dried at reduced pressure.
BAY 2927088 purified: BAY 2927088 crude and p-toluenesulfonic acid monohydrate are dissolved in a mixture of ethanol denaturated with toluene and purified water at 40 °C and filtered to remove particles. An aqueous solution of sodium hydroxide is added and the resulting mixture is cooled to 10 °C. BAY 2927088 purified is isolated from the resulting suspension by filtration, washed with ethanol denaturated with toluene and purified water, and dried at reduced pressure.
BAY 2927088 hydrate: BAY 2927088 purified is dissolved in tetrahydrofuran and purified water at 60 °C. Purified water is added over 2 hours and the mixture is cooled to 40 °C. BAY 2927088 hydrate is isolated by filtration, washed with purified water, and dried under reduced pressure.
BAY 2927088 hydrate micronized drug substance: BAY 2927088 hydrate is deagglomerated with a screening mill if necessary and then micronized by high-speed particle-to-particle impact with a fluid energy mill. The substance is ground to the particle-size stipulated in the product specification by adjusting the compressed nitrogen pressure and the feeding rate.

Question/Consideration: You are requested to include a discussion on the potential presence and control of alkyl tosylates in the drug substance. Include purge factors/justifications.
Answer/Response:
The control strategy for genotoxic impurities like alkyl tosylates is in line with the ICH M7 guideline, which states that the Threshold of Toxicological Concern (TTC) concept is not directly applicable in the case of a drug substance and drug product intended for advanced cancer indications as defined in the scope of ICH S9, which is relevant for BAY 2927088. In this case impurities could be controlled at acceptable levels for non-mutagenic impurities. In consequence the risk calculations in the course of the synthesis of BAY 2927088 were based on an acceptable limit of max. 0.15%, as this is the identification threshold for known organic impurities in the ICH Q3A impurity guideline.
The most likely alkyl tosylate to form is ethyl tosylate, given the employment of ethanol as solvent in the process of step BAY 2927088 purified. The other alkyl tosylate, which can theoretically be formed in the process of step BAY 2927088 purified is methyl tosylate from methanol as a residual solvent occurring in BAY 2927088 crude. However, the substantially greater amounts of ethanol present in the process as an employed solvent makes the formation of methyl tosylate insignificant.
Performed spiking experiments demonstrated that even 1 mole equivalent of ethyl tosylate (which represents the highest theoretically possible amount that could be formed in the process) is purged to levels of less than 0.1% in the isolated product BAY 2927088 purified when spiked to the reaction mixture. This amount is safely below the acceptable limit of max. 0.15%.
keywords: genotoxic impurities; Impurities; risk assessment; Potential process impurities; Impurities justification

Question/Consideration: You are requested to provide a more detailed written description for the manufacture process of the drug product (batch and continuous), including process parameters/controls (temperatures, times, blend speeds, sieve sizes, coating parameters etc.).
Answer/Response:
For the batch manufacturing the process is as follows:
Mixing, sieving and mixing
BAY 2927088 hydrate micronized, cellulose microcrystalline, crospovidone and lactose monohydrate are mixed at 15 rpm for 10 minutes, sieved (0.3 – 1.0 mm) and mixed at 15 rpm for 5 minutes to achieve a homogeneous powder blend.
Granulation
The powder blend is compacted on a roller compactor at 2 - 4 mm gap, specific compaction force of 4 – 12 kN/cm, roll speed between 2 – 4 rpm and grinded using 0.8 or 1.0 mm sieve.
Postblending
The dry granules are lubricated with sieved magnesium stearate (0.5 mm) by blending using a bin blender at 15 rpm for 5 minutes, resulting in the ready-to-press mixture.
Tableting
The ready-to-press mixture is compressed into tablets using a rotary press with an output of 15,000 – 170,000 tablets/hour, with a press force between 4 and 12 kN.
The uncoated tablets are tested for uniformity of mass, thickness, resistance to crushing, disintegration, and friability.
Coating
Ferric oxide red, hypromellose 5 cP and macrogol 3350 are combined with purified water in bulk to result in a homogeneous coating suspension.
The coating suspension is sprayed onto the tablets in a suitable coating device, e.g., perforated drum coater using an inlet air volume between 100-120 Nm³/h, an outlet air temperature of 40 °C (range 37 - 45 °C), a drum rotation speed of 15 - 16 rpm, a spray rate of 2.0 – 9.0 g/min and a spray pressure of 0.8 - 1.2 bar.
The coated tablets are tested for uniformity of mass, thickness, and disintegration.
Optionally, tablets with coating defects may be sorted out.
A batch of tablet cores may be divided into several sub-lots for coating.
For the continuous manufacturing the process is as follows:
Blending, sieving and blending
BAY 2927088 hydrate micronized, cellulose microcrystalline, crospovidone and lactose monohydrate are blended at 15 rpm for 10 minutes, sieved (0.3 – 1.0 mm) and blended at 15 rpm for 10 minutes again to achieve a homogeneous powder preblend. These steps are performed in batch mode.
Powder feeding
Preblend is fed and transported at a fixed throughput of 12 kg/h using rotating screw.
Granulation
The powder blend is compacted on a roller compactor at 2 - 4 mm gap, specific compaction force of 4 – 12 kN/cm, roll speed between 2 – 4 rpm and grinded using 0.8 or 1.0 mm sieve. This step is part of the continuous manufacturing process on an integrated line.
Postblending
The dry granules are lubricated with sieved magnesium stearate by blending using a ribbon blender at 100 rpm for 80 seconds, resulting in the ready-to-press blend. This step is part of the continuous manufacturing process on an integrated line and is performed in sublots of 0.5 to 1.5 kg.
Tableting
The ready-to-press blend is compressed into tablets using a rotary press with an output of 70,000 – 228,000 tablets/hour, with a press force between 4 and 12 kN. This step is done as a part of continuous manufacturing on an integrated line.
The uncoated tablets are tested for uniformity of mass, thickness, resistance to crushing, disintegration, and friability.
Coating
Ferric oxide red, hypromellose 5 cP and macrogol 3350 are combined with purified water in bulk to result in a homogeneous coating suspension.
The coating suspension is sprayed onto the tablets in a suitable coating device, e.g., perforated drum coater using an inlet air volume between 180-250 Nm³/h, an inlet air temperature of 60 to 90 °C, a drum rotation speed of 85 - 100 rpm, a spray rate of 40.0 – 60.0 g/min and a spray pressure of 0.8 - 1.2 bar.
The coated tablets are tested for uniformity of mass, thickness, and disintegration.
Optionally, tablets with coating defects may be sorted out.
This step is a part of continuous manufacturing on an integrated line. It is performed in sublots of 1 to 3 kg.
Control Strategy
Overall, the controls for the continuous manufacturing are the same as for the batch manufacturing with additional possibility of diversion of the sublots (postblending or coating) based on sublot weight, composition and individual tablet weight.
Design of experiment studies which are the basis to identify critical process steps and the final process parameter ranges are ongoing. This is done in laboratory scale and, later on in the final site in commercial scale. After identifying critical process steps, a control strategy for the commercial process will be established.
keywords: Drug Product; Description of Manufacturing Process and Process Controls; manufacturing description; coating process; in-process control

Urz. UE L 334, 12/12/2008, page 7, as amended) The President of the Office for Registration

The notification was accepted in terms of:

for the reasons described below:

1. In a negative opinion, the Marketing Authorization Holder was informed: "As part of the

introduction of a non-routine parameter test into the registration documentation (to Module

20thbatch or at least once a year. However, non-routine control of the microbiological purity 
parameter does not apply to the specification of the active substance used in a sterile 
parenterally administered medicinal product, because routine control of the above-mentioned 
parameter in this case is necessary to minimize the microbiological burden in the components 
of the medicinal product before its sterilization (in accordance with Guideline on the 
sterilisation of the medicinal product, active substance, excipient and primary container, 
EMA/CHMP/CVMP/QWP/850374/2015: The levels of bacterial endotoxins in the finished 
product can be impacted by the bioburden and bacterial endotoxins in the components (i.e. 
active substance, excipients and containers), and by microbiological contaminants introduced 
during manufacture. To ensure an acceptable level of bacterial endotoxins in the finished 
product, the level of microbiological contaminants of the components should be minimal.).
Moreover, the inhibitory properties of the active substance on the growth of microbiological 
contamination have not been demonstrated. Taking the above into account, non-routine 
testing of the microbiological purity parameter in the specification of the active substance 
used in a sterile parenterally administered medicinal product cannot be accepted and the 
above-mentioned remove non-routineness from the proposed registration dossier. Therefore, 
an appropriately amended application and registration documentation should be submitted in 
the above-mentioned form. scope (i.e. revised Modules: 3.2.S.4.1, 3.2.S.4.4, 3.2.S.4.5).”
As part of the response, the Marketing Authorization Holder did not submit the corrected 
documentation modules: 3.2.S.4.1, 3.2.S.4.4, 3.2.S.4.5 in the above-mentioned. extent and did 
not demonstrate the inhibitory properties of the active substance on the growth of 
microbiological contamination: "Moreover, the data presented in report P.2.5.01-01 
'Pharmaceutical Development – Microbiological Attributes' present a microbial test set-up for 
the drug product which can be considered worst-case conditions with respect to the water 
content compared to iopromide drug substance. After an experimental period of 24-30 hours, 
only two out of eight test microorganisms showed slight increases in the drug product 
solution. Thus, it can be stated that the drug substance iopromide does not explicitly exhibit 
inhibitory properties on microbial growth.”
The provided explanation “But, the substance itself as a dry powder is not capable of 
supporting microbial growth in the sense of ICH Q6A decision tree#6” cannot be accepted 
because active substance is used in a steril medicinal product and according to the Guideline 
on the sterilisation of the medicinal product, active substance, excipient and primary 
container, EMA/CHMP/CVMP/QWP/850374/2015: The levels of bacterial endotoxins in the 
finished product can be impacted by the bioburden and bacterial endotoxins in the 
components (i.e. active substance, excipients and containers), and by microbiological 
contaminants introduced during manufacture. To ensure an acceptable level of bacterial 
endotoxins in the finished product, the level of microbiological contaminants of the 
components should be minimal. Acceptance criteria for bioburden and, where relevant, 
bacterial endotoxins in components and bulk solutions should be specified.” Routine control 
of the microbiological purity parameter in the active substance specification in this case is 
necessary to minimize the microbiological load in the components of the medicinal product 
before its sterilization.

2. In addition, in accordance with Quality of medicines questions and answers, Part 2: What 
information should be included in marketing-authorisation dossiers regarding the actual 
testing that is carried out on any starting materials, e.g. active substances, excipients & 
packaging materials, on receipt by a finished product manufacturer?H+V Although some 
parameters should always be tested on receipt by the finished product manufacturer e.g. 
diethylene glycol in glicerol, what is actually tested on receipt is fully covered under good 
manufacturing practice and should be justified based upon risk assessment, based on 
historical data backed by supplier audit. Consequently, the relevant registered specifications 
in the marketing-authorisation application should not include any reference at all to reduce 
testing on receipt by the finished product manufacturer.
Taking the above into account, non-routine control of the microbiological purity parameter 
with the frequency: Conduct the test on every 20thbatch or at least once a year, for an active 
substance for which no inhibitory properties against the growth of microbial contamination 
have been demonstrated, used in a sterile medicinal product cannot be accepted in the 
documentation registration.

Question/Consideration:
Question 2-2):
The basis of storage condition and holding time of granules and uncoated tablet is not provided, please add.
Answer/Response:
The submitted registration documents of Rivaroxaban Tablets described: the holding time of granules and uncoated tablets is <= 42 days, this holding time is derived from the validation results and related registration documents of sending unit BAYER AG.

When BAYER AG conducted the holding time validation of granules and uncoated tablets, it was evaluated that since Rivaroxaban Tablets 2.5 mg has the lowest proportion of drug substance among the four dosage strengths (2.5 mg, 10 mg, 15 mg and 20 mg) and therefore the holding time was considered to be the most critical. The manufacturing process of the four dosage strengths was completely consistent. So the 2.5 mg strength was selected to conduct the holding time validation. The validation results of BAYER AG shown that all the test results meet the preset acceptance criteria. It was finally determined that the holding time for Rivaroxaban Tablets 2.5 mg, 10 mg, 15mg and 20 mg granules and uncoated tablets was <=42 days.

Our company, as the receiving unit of Rivaroxaban Tablets, the manufacturing process and the product quality are consistent with sending unit and the storage method and condition of intermediate (granules and uncoated tablets) are the same with sending unit. It will not affect the holding time of granules and uncoated tablets when the manufacturing site changed. We are planned to conduct the holding time validation for granules and uncoated tablets over the first commercial batch to further confirm that the change of manufacturing site will not affect the holding time.

The glass barrel is composed of Type 1 glass and meets pharmacopoeial requirements 
(USPNF, Ph. Eur., JP). The 5 mL glass barrel treated with ammonium sulfate complies with 
Ph. Eur., USP-NF, JP, EMEA/410/01 <Note for guidance on minimizing the risk of 
transmitting animal spongiform encephalopathy agents via human and veterinary medicinal 
products> , Commission Directive 94/62/EC <Heavy metals in packaging materials>. The 
ammonium sulfate is sprayed into the glass barrel prior to transfer to the annealing lehr. 
During annealing, sodium oxide on the inner glass surface reacts with the ammonium sulfate 
producing highly soluble sodium sulfate. AST results in dealkalization of the inner glass 
surface and prevents the leaching of ions from the syringe barrel into the sWFI solution. The 
AST glass barrel has identical dimensions to the non-AST glass barrel that is used in the 
current diluent PFS manufactured at Vetter. The container closure components have been 
demonstrated suitable to assure the quality and safety of the product for its shelf life.

To evaluate the compatibility of BAY 81-8973 DP with the 2.5 mL sWFI PFS and 5 mL 
sWFI PFS manufactured with the 5 mL AST barrel at Vetter, the 250 IU BAY 81-8973 DP 
and the 3000 IU BAY 81-8973 DP was reconstituted with the sWFI PFS using the vial 
adapter. The reconstituted DP was drawn back into the syringe and stored for 4 hours at room 
temperature. The reconstituted DP was then dispensed through the administration set into a 
sample container for testing. All data for potency, HPLC-SEC, clarity, and particulate matter 
met acceptance criteria. The results demonstrate the compatibility of the 2.5 mL and 5 mL 
sWFI PFS manufactured with the 5 mL AST barrel at Vetter with BAY 81-8973 DP. The 
results also confirm the compatibility of the approved reconstitution and administration 
devices for BAY 81-8973 DP with the 2.5 mL sWFI PFS manufactured with the 5 mL AST 
barrel at Vetter. The details are presented in P.2.6.

Container closure integrity was evaluated by dye leak test (dye ingress method) on three 
process validation batches each of 2.5 mL and 5 mL sWFI PFS with the 5 mL AST glass 
barrel. The test results of the batches are provided in Table 2–1 and Table 2–2. No dye was 
detected in any of the test samples. The container closure system met the requirements for 
integrity.

A screening leachable study was performed to identify and quantify substances possibly 
leaching from the AST barrel, plunger stopper and tip cap rubber material into sWFI stored 
for 6 months at 40 °C/75% RH in prefilled syringes. The sWFI PFS syringes contained 5 mL 
of sWFI, to maximize the contact surface area with the diluent and glass barrel. The selection 
of the syringes stored for 6 months at 40 °C/75% RH is based on ICH Q1A(R2) guidance for 
long term storage at 25 °C. The sWFI PFS stored for 6 months at 2-8 °C was used as a 
reference sample.
The results were reported for toxicological assessment. For organic leachable compounds no 
structural alerts for genotoxicity were detected. The safety limit for sensitizing compounds 
showed that all organic leachables were detected in concentrations below the daily dose 
related limit of 5 µg/d, and thus no compound specific toxicological assessment was required. 
Detected amounts of elements were shown to have negligible effects on daily intake, and no 
specific toxicological assessment or risk assessment per ICH Q3D was required for Na and Si.

stopper (West 4023/50 with ETFE foil), and a tip cap (West 4023/50) did not indicate the

packaging materials and dosing device components for sWFI diluent. Detailed information on

A prefilled syringe (PFS) containing sterile water for injection (sWFI) is used for storage and 
dosing of the diluent which is used for reconstituting lyophilized rFVIII drug products. The 
syringe consists of a 5 mL ammonium sulfate treated (AST) glass barrel, a plunger stopper, 
and a tip cap. The plunger stopper and tip cap are made from West 4023/50 bromobutyl 
rubber and the plunger is covered with a Flurotec film. A screening leachable study was 
performed to identify and quantify substances possibly leaching from the AST barrel, plunger 
stopper and tip cap rubber material into sWFI stored for 6 months at 40 °C/75% RH in 
prefilled syringes. The sWFI PFS syringes contained 5 mL of sWFI, to maximize the contact

Question/Consideration:
Question 2
The Company proposes to establish a control of the remaining solvents by gas chromatography 
and their maximum content in accordance with the requirements of ICH Q3C for the active 
substance manufactured by Newchem S.p.A., Italy, but in the submitted method validation 
report in module 3.2.S.4.3. the repeatability data are determined at 0,1 % solvent concentration.  
Internal laboratory repeatability (intermediate precision) data for acetone have been determined 
in samples at approximately 0.007-0.008% solvent concentration. Similarly, the submitted 
method validation report did not include internal laboratory repeatability data for methanol, 
ethyl acetate and methylene chloride. According to the requirements of guideline ICH Q2(R1), 
repeatability and internal laboratory repeatability should be determined at 100% test 
concentration with at least 6 measurements, or at least 9 measurements in 3 concentration areas 
each of which at least 3 measurements have been made. Please provide repeatability and 
internal laboratory repeatability validation data for residual solvents obtained at concentrations 
of residual solvents in accordance with the requirements of guideline ICH Q2(R1). Please note 
that, if necessary, the remaining solvents to be tested should be added to the samples to be 
analysed at the required concentrations (spiking).
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 2 (3.2.S.4.3.03 section):
We would like to explain that according to ICH Q2(R2), authentic homogeneous samples or, 
if unavailable, artificially prepared samples have to be used for determination of the precision 
of an analytical procedure. In the validation of the residual solvents determination of 
cyproterone acetate, an authentic homogeneous sample was used for determination of 
“repeatability” and “intermediate precision”. The authentic sample only contains acetone in 
detectable amounts and not the other three specified impurities methanol, ethyl acetate and 
methylene chloride. Due to the volatility of these compounds, the preparation of a stable and 
homogeneously spiked sample, containing all four impurities at the specification limit, is not 
possible with reasonable effort. Therefore, the residual solvent acetone was taken as surrogate 
substance to demonstrate the repeatability of one sample that is processed six times 
individually. The factors impacting the repeatability like weighing tolerance, headspace 
conditions and instrument set-up, will be the same for all solvents potentially present and 
therefore the results for acetone can be extrapolated to the other specified solvents. On the 
other hand, accurate recovery of all four solvents in the presence of the test substance was 
demonstrated within the chapter “accuracy”. For this parameter, solutions containing the 
sample and the respective solvents have been combined at three different concentrations 
before analyzing. Matrix effects can therefore be excluded for all four solvents. Altogether, 
accuracy and precision were demonstrated sufficiently within the presented validation report.

In addition, in the validation report data for “precision of the system” is presented. Here a 
reference solution containing all four specified residual solvents at the level at 0.1 % solvent 
concentration is used. This solution is injected six times and is used to check the precision of 
the chromatographic system. This is a parameter that is not described in ICH Q2(R2) and is 
presented in addition.

Source:  ICH Q2(R2) Guideline on validation of analytical procedures
S.4.3.03 Validation of Test Methods – Residual solvents / Cyproterone acetate 
micronized drug substance (#022978427_02 / unchanged)

Question/Consideration:
Question 4
(3.2.P.3.4) It is necessary to narrow the limit for biological load (bioburden) before final 
sterilization so that it reads: < iii = 100 CFU/100 ml in accordance with the guideline 
EMA/CHMP/CVMP/QWP/850374/2015, or provide explanation for the set wider limit: < or 
= 100 CFU/ml.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 4 ( CTD section):
Please note that the manufacturing process is fully in accordance with the guideline 
EMA/CHMP/CVMP/QWP/850374/2015. In the manufacturing process, the microbiological 
count of the product is ensured in several steps. The starting materials and raw materials are 
tested for microbial count (limit is defined at max. 10² CFU/g) in order to control the initial 
quality of the prepared injectable bulk solution as well. Furthermore, each batch of the bulk 
solution is tested for microbiological purity after preparation of the solution. The limit at this 
stage of manufacturing process is 100 CFU/mL of the bulk solution (test prior to filling). This 
also ensures that the subsequent filtration steps including a 0.2 μm filter (validated process 
step) results in a solution with a bioburden purity below 100 CFU/100 mL. During filling (last 
step before the final terminal sterilization step), a bioburden check is only occasionally carried 
out, especially during process validations. This is in accordance with the guideline. The first 
option in table 1 of the mentioned guideline describes, that this microbiological test is not 
absolutely necessary on routine basis; in case a terminal sterilization process takes place (NLT 
15 min. / at least 121°C).
Under the mentioned conditions described above (esp. as there is a terminal sterilization 
process in place), the microbiological quality is adequately ensured throughout the entire 
production process and in accordance with all the requirements of the guideline 
EMA/CHMP/CVMP/QWP/850374/2015.
keywords: Bioburden Control Strategy; Sterilization; in-process control; Process Validation and/or Evaluation

Question/Consideration:
Please provide details of sample or reference standard which is used for standardized against 
Primary standard lot RSVITV-7 including production quantity of primary reference standard 
and stability protocol/report.
Answer/Response:
The primary reference standard RSVITV-7 (13,199 vials) was derived from an aflibercept 
drug substance batch 8012700120 manufactured by Regeneron and it is the same reference 
standard which was used during the pivotal clinical studies for aflibercept solution 114.3 
mg/mL. RSVITV-7 was derived from an aflibercept drug substance (DS) lot produced using 
the aflibercept solution 40 mg/mL (DS) manufacturing process. The RS is composed of 
purified aflibercept recombinant protein in an aqueous buffered solution, pH 6.2, containing 
10 mM sodium phosphate. In the initial qualification of RSVITV-7 as a primary standard for 
aflibercept solution 40 mg/mL DS and DP material, RSVITV-7 was qualified against the 
existing primary reference standard RSVITV-4 at the time. All tests met the acceptance 
criteria as per the reference standard qualification program. An assessment was performed to 
determine the suitability of RSVITV-7 for use as the primary RS for aflibercept solution 
114.3 mg/mL FDS and DP samples. The conclusions from the analytical method assessment 
and the results of the supplemental qualification demonstrated that RSVITV-7 is also 
qualified for use to test aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL FDS and DP material. Details of the 
assessment and the qualification data are provided in CTD section S.5.05-02. Stability data for 
the primary reference standard is included in CTD section S.5.05-02.
Additionally, a typographical error was identified in S.5.01 where the potency by bioassay is 
calculated as mean result of 12 tests with a limit for the relative standard deviation %RSD. 
The bioassay applied for Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL actually reports the geometric 
mean with a limit for the geometric coefficient of variance %GCV as also reflected in the test 
procedure in S.4.2.01-01. Section S.5.01-02 has been corrected accordingly and is provided 
with this response.

unchanged)

Question/Consideration:
Please clarify why there is no Identity by Dot Blot test in stability study following Shelf-life 
specification.
Answer/Response:
As indicated in the DP shelf life specification P.5.1.02-01 via a footnote as well as in CTD 
section P.5.6.01-01, identity by dot blot is not tested during stability studies and only at 
release since identity is not expected to change during storage.
The specification for DP shelf life includes testing of those attributes that are susceptible to 
change during storage and handling and are likely to influence quality, safety and/or efficacy. 
In accordance with ICH Guideline Q5C, the proposed stability indicating profile should 
provide assurance that changes in the identity, purity, and potency of the product will be 
detected. Although the stability panel does not include an assay dedicated to confirming the 
identity of the aflibercept 114.3 mg/mL DP, the results of the stability indicating assays for 
potency, purity, and charge variants (by iCIEF) provide a profile that can indirectly verify the 
identity.
Source:   P.5.1.02-01 Shelf Life Specification / Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL in vial
for intravitreous injection (#022972970; unchanged)
P.5.6.01-01 Justification of Specification / Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL in

Question/Consideration:
Question 2-2):
The basis of storage condition and holding time of granules and uncoated tablet is not provided, please add.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 2-2)
The submitted registration documents of Rivaroxaban Tablets described: the holding time of granules and uncoated tablets is <= 42 days, this holding time is derived from the validation results and related registration documents of sending unit BAYER AG.
When BAYER AG conducted the holding time validation of granules and uncoated tablets, it was evaluated that since Rivaroxaban Tablets 2.5 mg has the lowest proportion of drug substance among the four dosage strengths (2.5 mg, 10 mg, 15 mg and 20 mg) and therefore the holding time was considered to be the most critical.
The manufacturing process of the four dosage strengths was completely consistent. So the 2.5 mg strength was selected to conduct the holding time validation.
The validation results of BAYER AG shown that all the test results meet the preset acceptance criteria.
It was finally determined that the holding time for Rivaroxaban Tablets 2.5 mg, 10 mg, 15mg and 20 mg granules and uncoated tablets was <=42 days.
Our company, as the receiving unit of Rivaroxaban Tablets, the manufacturing process and the product quality are consistent with sending unit and the storage method and condition of intermediate (granules and uncoated tablets) are the same with sending unit.
It will not affect the holding time of granules and uncoated tablets when the manufacturing site changed.
We are planned to conduct the holding time validation for granules and uncoated tablets over the first commercial batch to further confirm that the change of manufacturing site will not affect the holding time.

We acknowledge your request for criteria for informative tests such as humidity and hardness for our solid dosage form product. We would like to provide some clarification on these parameters and their relevance to our stability testing protocols.
The requested parameters of humidity and hardness are primarily monitored during the manufacturing process as part of our In-Process controls. Our stability testing protocols are designed to monitor the critical quality attributes of the product over its shelf life. These protocols are aligned with stability specifications registered in the market and focus on parameters that directly impact the products efficacy and safety.
It is important to note that the additional tests you have inquired about, including humidity and hardness, are sometime required for regulatory compliance in certain ASIAN markets.
These tests are included in CTD (Common Technical Document) 3.2.P.8.3 to meet the specific requirements of these regions.
However, for Panama, we adhere strictly to the stability specifications that are relevant and registered for Panama market. We assure that our stability testing for the Panama market is conducted in accordance with the stability specifications that are globally recognized and specific to the product’s performance and safety. The inclusion of additional tests like humidity and hardness in our documentation is to ensure compliance with specific regional requirements and does not reflect a deviation from our standard stability testing for Panama.

Question/Consideration:
Question 1
Based on the validation data, it is noted that the bioburden limits are not in line with those 
recommended in the guideline - Guideline on the sterilization of the medicinal product, active 
substance, excipient and primary container (EMA/CHMP /CVMP/QWP/850374/2015). 
Indeed, the limit is set at ≤ 100 CFU/10ml while the recommended limit is ≤ 100 CFU/100 ml 
for terminal sterilization. This needs to be further addressed as bioburden is a critical quality 
attribute that can impact the sterile quality of the finished product. Therefore, the bioburden 
limits must be tightened in accordance with the guideline for both manufacturing sites.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1 ( 3.2.P.3.5):
Before 2023, the internal specification limit for bioburden of parenteral drug products 
established at the drug product production site Berlimed S.A., Madrid, Spain was defined as 
100 CFU/ 10 mL based on the lowest acceptance level for non-sterile substances for 
pharmaceutical use given in Ph. Eur. 5.1.4. “Microbiological Quality of Non-Sterile 
Pharmaceutical Preparations and Substances for Pharmaceutical Use”. Since 2023 the limit 
for bioburden was tightened to 100 CFU/ 100 mL in accordance with the EMA guideline - 
Guideline on the sterilization of the medicinal product, active substance, excipient and 
primary container (EMA/CHMP /CVMP/QWP/850374/2015). Furthermore, to evaluate the 
status and registered limits a risk assessment was performed on the historical bioburden data 
base of terminally sterilized aqueous solutions produced at the Supply Center Alcàla (SCA; 
Berlimed S.A., Madrid, Spain) considering data from 2018 to 2021 because during 2022 the 
sterile liquids area was shut down at Supply Centre Alcalá. In conclusion, full control and 
sterility assurance was demonstrated.
New process validation data are provided in accordance with the recommended bioburden 
limit of ≤ 100 CFU/100 mL for terminal sterilization which were generated on the new 
manufacturing and filling line for the product Ultravist 370 at Berlimed S.A., Madrid, Spain 
(please refer to document P.3.5.01-01). For the product Ultravist 300 the process validation 
activities are still ongoing and will be amended when completed (please refer to Commitment 
for Ultravist 300).
For the drug product manufacturing site Bayer AG, Berlin, Germany, we acknowledge that in 
the validation data, the bioburden limit is set to ≤ 100 CFU/10mL, while the limit 
recommended by the EMA Guideline (EMA/CHMP /CVMP/QWP/850374/2015) is ≤ 100 
CFU/100 ml for terminal sterilization.
In a risk-based approach it was concluded, that the current established and globally registered 
action limit of 10 CFU/mL (corresponding to 100 CFU/10 mL) is higher than the limit of 100 
CFU/100 mL recommended by the EMA Guideline. Therefore, it was decided to reduce the 
internal action limit (defined as alert limit) to 10 CFU/10 mL (corresponding to 100 CFU/100 
mL).  It is ensured by a local procedure at manufacturing site Supply Center Berlin (SCB) that
an investigation including root cause analysis and evaluation of the bioburden resistance is 
also performed when an internal action limit (alert limit) is exceeded.
The current bioburden action limit at SCB is in accordance with Ph. Eur./USP for non-sterile 
products. Lowering of the internal action limit (alert limit) as described above also fulfills the 
requirement of EMA Guideline (EMA/CHMP/CVMP/QWP 850374/2015) and further 
increases product quality of Ultravist 300 and 370 at SCB (please refer to QP 
Statement_bioburden limit_SCB).

Question/Consideration:
Question 5 
 
a. Solvent stability study:  
- Present an update of the stability results available today , since they only present data up 
to 6 months under the three conditions of the study presented .
Answer/Response:
Labeling and assembly of the Kovaltry packaged drug product kit require packaging multiple 
components. Two of the major components are the drug product vial and the sterile water for 
injection (sWFI) pre-filled syringe (PFS). The expiration label for the Kovaltry packaged drug 
product kit is determined based on the expiration of components. Typically, the expiration 
date is the shelf-life of the drug product batch, however, there are occasions when the sWFI 
PFS batch could have an earlier shelf-life than that of the drug product batch. In the case 
where the sWFI PFS batch has a shorter shelf-life, the packaged drug product kit is labeled 
with the shorter shelf-life date.
The shelf-life stability studies for drug product are separate from the shelf-life stability studies 
of the sWFI PFS program. A stability study with all components of a packaged drug product 
kit combined is not performed.
The sWFI PFS stability studies are based on the ICH Q1A guidelines for finished 
pharmaceutical products. Specifically, the studies for the 2.5mL and 5mL sWFI pre-filled 
ammonium sulfate treated (AST) syringes consist of the below time points and conditions.
Storage Condition 
Time Points (months)
5 ± 3°C / ambient RH 
0, 48, 60
30 ± 2°C / 65 ± 5% RH 
0, 3, 6, 12, 24, 36, 48, 60
40 ± 2°C / 75 ± 5% RH 
0, 1, 3, 6

Testing at 30 months at either 5°C or 30°C is not included as part of the post-approval 
commitment. The sWFI pre-filled AST syringe (both 2.5 and 5 mL) results have remained 
stable up to 24 months at 30°C. The updated 36 months stability update at 30C/60% RH for 
batches BJUE 261A, BJUE 271A and BJUE 281A and for BJUE262A, BJUE272A and 
BJUE282A is provided with the response. A commitment is made to continue the long-term 
studies through the proposed shelf life of 48 months and to report to the competent authorities 
if stability indicates any batch is outside of approved specifications.

Question/Consideration:

b. Powder stability study: -The acceptance criterion for the Potency test is indicated as a 
range of 80-125% in the stability studies, and in the Specifications document for 
determination of useful life it is indicated as NLT 200 IU/vial or NLT 80 IU/vial. mL.
Answer/Response:
The reference to the range of 80-125% for rFVIII (recombinant Factor VIII) can be found in 
the European Pharmacopoeia monographs. The acceptance criteria of 80-125% in the stability 
studies constitutes a NLT 80% of the nominal dosage strength and NMT 125% of the nominal 
dosage strength.  
 
As an example, for 250 IU, 80-125% is applied as: 
 
250 IU*(0.8)=200 IU/vial 
250*(1.25)=313 IU/vial 
 
For nominal dosage strengths 250,500 and 1000 IU: 1 vial=2.5 mL 
 
Therefore: 
200 IU/vial*(vial/2.5mL)= 80 IU/mL 
313 IU/vial*(vial/2.5 mL)=125 IU/mL 
 
*Specifications have been rounded to appropriate significant figures.
