Bayer Response to Question 12 and 13:

Analytical Procedures

rFVIII Potency
Potency of BAY 81-8973 is measured using a Chromogenic assay. An in-house 
reference standard is used which has been assigned against the World Health Organization 
(WHO) International Standard (IS) for FVIII concentrates.
The chromogenic assay method consists of two consecutive steps where the intensity of color 
is proportional to the Factor VIII activity. In the first step, Factor X is activated to Factor Xa 
by Factor IXa with its cofactor, Factor VIIIa, in the presence of optimal amounts of calcium 
ions and phospholipids. Excess amounts of Factor X are present such that the rate of 
activation of Factor X is solely dependent on the amount of Factor VIII. In the second step, 
Factor Xa hydrolyzes the chromogenic substrate to yield a chromophore, and the color 
intensity is determined photometrically at 405 nm. The validity of the assay is confirmed by 
parallelism, and sample potency is calculated using a linear regression statistical method 
against the in-house reference standard of established potency. Activity is reported in 
International Units per mL (IU/mL).
The chromogenic assay method is performed by a robotic liquid handling platform. The 
robotic system performs dilutions, places the materials into a 96-well test plate, and performs 
a series of reagent additions and incubations to achieve the chromogenic reaction. The 
completed reaction is then read by a plate reader and results are uploaded to a validated data 
analysis system that calculates the samples' FVIII potency (IU/mL).

Total Protein Content
The Total Protein Content assay is carried out with a high performance size exclusion 
chromatography (HP-SEC) column and uses fluorescence detection (FLD). All protein 
greater than 15 kDa is quantitated as a single discrete peak. Protein concentration is 
determined by regression analysis on a linear fit standard curve and is reported in g/mL.

Chromatography Assays
Size Exclusion Chromatography
The principal components of rFVIII preparations are separated into 4 regions. The regions are 
defined within the run sequence by elution profile of the assay control sample. Quantitation is 
based on the Relative Percent Areas (RPA) of each region from the fluorescence signal of the 
chromatogram (emission at 340 nm after excitation at 276 nm). This procedure separates 
components according to their hydrodynamic volume, or molecular size, and is capable of 
resolving proteins over a wide range of molecular weights on the column. The high salt 
mobile phase was selected for minimal perturbation of the native distribution of the molecular 
weight profile of the protein.
The procedure reports results for High Molecular Weight (HMW) Region 1, Region 2 
(heterodimer), Region 3 (clipped heterodimer), and Region 4 (Free light chain and fragments).

Thrombin Digest Peptide Map
The rFVIII samples are digested with thrombin which yields 4 major fragments (B, A3C1C2, 
A1 and A2 domains) which are quantitated. Separation of the digested sample on a reversed 
phase chromatography column results in elution of the fragments in an order of increasing 
hydrophobicity where B-domain = peak 1, A3C1C2 light chain = peak 2, A1 domain = peak 3, 
and A2 domain = peak 4.
This method reports the relative percent peak areas of the 4 major peaks. Additionally, the 
peak area % to peak height % ratio is reported for the light chain (A3C1C2) peak to track any 
broadening of the peak that could indicate stability modifications.

Oligosaccharide Map
The N-linked oligosaccharides are released from rFVIII, which is bound to nylon membranes, 
using the enzyme PNGase F. The released N-glycans are then labeled with anthranilic acid 
(2-AA) using reductive amination with sodium cyanoborohydride as reductant. The 2-AA 
labeled glycan components of the preparations are separated into peaks by HPLC in normal 
phase/ion exchange mixed-mode and detected using fluorescence emission at 425 nm after 
excitation at 360 nm. This procedure separates the labeled components primarily according to 
their ionic charge (dependent on number of sialic acid groups) and also by their size/structure. 
Quantitative results are expressed as relative percent areas of peak groups, combined 
according to charge (level of sialylation). Additionally, a ratio is calculated from 
monosialylated and disialylated peak areas to monitor variation in sialylation against a 
specification.

Quantitation of Glycine and Histidine
The assay is a Reversed Phase High Performance Liquid Chromatography with Ultraviolet 
detection (RP-HPLC-UV) method using a commercial kit to label amino acids. The glycine 
and histidine levels are determined within the same chromatographic run. Concentrations are 
determined by linear regression against standard curves.

Quantitation of Sucrose
The sucrose assay is a hydrophilic interaction high performance liquid chromatography with 
charged aerosol detection (HILIC-HPLC-CAD) method. The concentration of sucrose is 
determined by regression analysis using a quadratic fit standard curve.

Quantitation of Imidazole
The imidazole assay is a liquid chromatography method with ultraviolet detection. The 
concentration of imidazole in the sample is determined by regression analysis using a linear 
fit standard curve.

Electrophoresis Assays
Quantitative SDS-PAGE Analysis
Proteins in the samples are separated into components by SDS-PAGE in a precast gel. The 
protein bands are visualized by Coomassie blue staining. The molecular species present in the 
gel are quantified by optical density (densitometry). Product integrity of the heavy chains and 
light chains of rFVIII is calculated from the integration data. Any new bands are reported.

Silver-stained Gel Analysis
Protein components of rFVIII samples are first separated by SDS-PAGE based on molecular 
weight in a precast gradient gel then silver stained. A visual comparison to the in-house 
reference standard is made; results are reported as comparable or not comparable.

Immunoassays
Quantitation of Host Cell Protein
BHK HCP is detected using HTRF. HCP in the sample binds to process-specific polyclonal 
anti-BHK HCP antibodies conjugated with europium cryptate (donor) and D2 (acceptor). The 
resulting HTRF signal is measured by a microplate reader; concentration is interpolated from 
a HCP standard curve using a four-parameter fit and regression analysis.

Quantitation of Mouse IgG
Residual mIgG is detected using HTRF utilizing rabbit anti-mouse IgG antibody conjugated to 
XL665 (acceptor) and Europium Cryptate (donor). Concentration is interpolated from a 
standard curve using a 2nd degree polynomial fit and regression analysis.

Microbial Purity
Test samples are filtered through a membrane filter, rinsed with sterile diluent, transferred onto 
plated media, incubated, and CFU counted. Per USP/Ph. Eur., JP.

Endotoxin
Kinetic LAL assay per USP/Ph. Eur./JP; onset time to reach predetermined parameter is 
inversely proportional to endotoxin amount; concentration calculated vs. standard curve.

Quantitation of Host Cell DNA
qPCR with target-specific primers and dual-labeled probe; CT measured against BHK DNA 
standard curve to quantify BHK DNA.

Quantitation of Sodium and Calcium
ICP-OES; samples diluted in nitric acid; sodium and calcium quantified via wavelengths and 
linear regression vs. standard curves.

Quantitation of Copper
Atomic Absorption; samples diluted in nitric acid; signal intensities compared to linear 
standard curve.

Measurement of pH
pH measured potentiometrically.

Color Determination
Color determined by visual comparison to reference solutions.

Quantitation of Osmolality
Vapor pressure osmometer; reported in mOsm/kg.

Quantitation of Polysorbate 80
Protein and salts precipitated with ethanol; residue extracted; ACTC complex measured at 
620 nm; absorbance proportional to Polysorbate 80.

1.1 Validation of Analytical Procedures
Method development was performed for assay use in the BAY 81-8973 control scheme. All 
acceptance criteria were met. All test methods are validated and acceptable for their intended 
use. Validation parameter coverage is described throughout (e.g., per ICH: accuracy, 
precision, linearity, range, specificity, detection/quantitation limits, robustness; with 
compendial verifications where applicable).

Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 5 ( CTD section):

Labeling and assembly of the Kovaltry packaged drug product kit require packaging multiple components. Two of the major components are the drug product vial and the sterile water for injection (sWFI) pre-filled syringe (PFS). The expiration label for the Kovaltry packaged drug product kit is determined based on the expiration of components. Typically, the expiration date is the shelf-life of the drug product batch, however, there are occasions when the sWFI PFS batch could have an earlier shelf-life than that of the drug product batch. In the case where the sWFI PFS batch has a shorter shelf-life, the packaged drug product kit is labeled with the shorter shelf-life date.
The shelf-life stability studies for drug product are separate from the shelf-life stability studies of the sWFI PFS program. A stability study with all components of a packaged drug product kit combined is not performed.
The sWFI PFS stability studies are based on the ICH Q1A guidelines for finished pharmaceutical products. Specifically, the studies for the 2.5mL and 5mL sWFI pre-filled ammonium sulfate treated (AST) syringes consist of the below time points and conditions.

Storage Condition

5 ± 3°C / ambient RH
0, 48, 60
30 ± 2°C / 65 ± 5% RH
0, 3, 6, 12, 24, 36, 48, 60
40 ± 2°C / 75 ± 5% RH

Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 12 and 13:

Analytical Procedures
rFVIII Potency
Potency of BAY 81-8973 is measured using a Chromogenic assay. An in-house reference standard is used which has been assigned against the World Health Organization (WHO) International Standard (IS) for FVIII concentrates.
The chromogenic assay method consists of two consecutive steps where the intensity of color is proportional to the Factor VIII activity. In the first step, Factor X is activated to Factor Xa by Factor IXa with its cofactor, Factor VIIIa, in the presence of optimal amounts of calcium ions and phospholipids. Excess amounts of Factor X are present such that the rate of activation of Factor X is solely dependent on the amount of Factor VIII. In the second step, Factor Xa hydrolyzes the chromogenic substrate to yield a chromophore, and the color intensity is determined photometrically at 405 nm. The validity of the assay is confirmed by parallelism, and sample potency is calculated using a linear regression statistical method against the in-house reference standard of established potency. Activity is reported in International Units per mL (IU/mL).
The chromogenic assay method is performed by a robotic liquid handling platform. The robotic system performs dilutions, places the materials into a 96-well test plate, and performs a series of reagent additions and incubations to achieve the chromogenic reaction. The completed reaction is then read by a plate reader and results are uploaded to a validated data analysis system that calculates the samples' FVIII potency (IU/mL).

Total Protein Content
The Total Protein Content assay is carried out with a high performance size exclusion chromatography (HP-SEC) column and uses fluorescence detection (FLD). All protein greater than 15 kDa is quantitated as a single discrete peak. Protein concentration is determined by regression analysis on a linear fit standard curve and is reported in g/mL.

Extended characterization was carried out to further investigate the physicochemical and 
biological properties of the BAY-81-8973 molecule. Characterization of clinical and 
conformance Drug Product (DP) lots was carried out alongside the BAY 81-8973 Product 
Reference Standard (STD 0090 RM2), as well as a licensed rFVIII-FS lot to identify any

binding of rFVIII measured by fluorescence anisotropy.

intrinsic fluorescence, far UV circular dichroism and differential scanning calorimetry show 
all lots to have equivalent conformational structure and thermal stability. It is also concluded 
that results are comparable to those obtained for the licensed rFVIII-FS product. With respect 
to biochemical characterization of the molecule, the results of the thrombin and FXa 
activation studies and FIXa and vWF binding studies indicate functional activity of the 
rFVIII product, with profiles and results that are consistent with the structure of the rFVIII 
molecule. All clinical and conformance DP lots have comparable results to the Product

Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 12 and 13:  
 
Analytical Procedures
rFVIII Potency
Potency of BAY 81-8973 is measured using a Chromogenic assay. An in-house 
reference standard is used which has been assigned against the World Health Organization 
(WHO) International Standard (IS) for FVIII concentrates.
The chromogenic assay method consists of two consecutive steps where the intensity of color 
is proportional to the Factor VIII activity.  In the first step, Factor X is activated to Factor Xa
by Factor IXa with its cofactor, Factor VIIIa, in the presence of optimal amounts of calcium 
ions and phospholipids. Excess amounts of Factor X are present such that the rate of 
activation of Factor X is solely dependent on the amount of Factor VIII.  In the second step, 
Factor Xa hydrolyzes the chromogenic substrate to yield a chromophore, and the color 
intensity is determined photometrically at 405 nm.  The validity of the assay is confirmed by 
parallelism, and sample potency is calculated using a linear regression statistical method 
against the in-house reference standard of established potency.  Activity is reported in 
International Units per mL (IU/mL).
The chromogenic assay method is performed by a robotic liquid handling platform.  The 
robotic system performs dilutions, places the materials into a 96-well test plate, and performs 
a series of reagent additions and incubations to achieve the chromogenic reaction.  The 
completed reaction is then read by a plate reader and results are uploaded to a validated data 
analysis system that calculates the samples' FVIII potency (IU/mL).
Total Protein Content
The Total Protein Content assay is carried out with a high performance size exclusion 
chromatography (HP-SEC) column and uses fluorescence detection (FLD).  All protein 
greater than 15 kDa is quantitated as a single discrete peak.  Protein concentration is 
determined by regression analysis on a linear fit standard curve and is reported in g/mL.
Chromatography Assays
Size Exclusion Chromatography
The principal components of rFVIII preparations are separated into 4 regions.  The regions are 
defined within the run sequence by elution profile of the assay control sample.  Quantitation is 
based on the Relative Percent Areas (RPA) of each region from the fluorescence signal of the 
chromatogram (emission at 340 nm after excitation at 276 nm).  This procedure separates 
components according to their hydrodynamic volume, or molecular size, and is capable of 
resolving proteins over a wide range of molecular weights on the column.  The high salt 
mobile phase was selected for minimal perturbation of the native distribution of the molecular 
weight profile of the protein.
The procedure reports results for High Molecular Weight (HMW) Region 1, Region 2 
(heterodimer), Region 3 (clipped heterodimer), and Region 4 (Free light chain and fragments).
Thrombin Digest Peptide Map
The rFVIII samples are digested with thrombin which yields 4 major fragments (B, A3C1C2, 
A1 and A2 domains) which are quantitated. Separation of the digested sample on a reversed 
phase chromatography column results in elution of the fragments in an order of increasing 
hydrophobicity where B-domain = peak 1, A3C1C2 light chain = peak 2, 
A1 domain = peak 3, and A2 domain = peak 4.
This method reports the relative percent peak areas of the 4 major peaks. Additionally, the 
peak area % to peak height % ratio is reported for the light chain (A3C1C2) peak to track any 
broadening of the peak that could indicate stability modifications.
Oligosaccharide Map
The N-linked oligosaccharides are released from rFVIII, which is bound to nylon membranes, 
using the enzyme PNGase F. The released N-glycans are then labeled with anthranilic acid 
(2-AA) using reductive amination with sodium cyanoborohydride as reductant. The 2-AA 
labeled glycan components of the preparations are separated into peaks by HPLC in normal 
phase/ion exchange mixed-mode and detected using fluorescence emission at 425 nm after 
excitation at 360 nm. This procedure separates the labeled components primarily according to 
their ionic charge, which is dependent on the number of sialic acid groups covalently bound to 
the oligosaccharides, and also by their size/structure. Quantitative results are expressed as 
relative percent areas of peak groups, combined according to charge (level of sialylation). 
Additionally, a ratio is calculated from monosialylated and disialylated peak areas to monitor 
variation in sialylation against a specification.
Quantitation of Glycine and Histidine
The assay is a Reversed Phase High Performance Liquid Chromatography with Ultraviolet 
detection (RP-HPLC-UV) method.  The method uses a commercial kit to label amino acids 
with a dye in order to then be detected.  The glycine and histidine levels are determined from 
within the same chromatographic run.  The concentration of glycine and histidine is 
determined by linear regression against standard curves.
Quantitation of Sucrose
The sucrose assay is a hydrophilic interaction high performance liquid chromatography with 
charged aerosol detection (HILIC-HPLC-CAD) method.  The concentration of sucrose is 
determined by regression analysis using a quadratic fit standard curve.
Quantitation of Imidazole
The imidazole assay is a liquid chromatography method with ultraviolet detection.  The 
concentration of imidazole in the sample is determined by regression analysis using a linear 
fit standard curve.
Electrophoresis Assays
Quantitative SDS-PAGE Analysis
Proteins in the samples are separated into components by SDS-PAGE in a precast gel.  The 
protein bands are visualized by Coomassie blue staining.  The molecular species present in the 
gel are quantified by optical density (densitometry).  Product integrity of the heavy chains and 
light chains of rFVIII is calculated from the integration data.  Any new bands are reported.
Silver-stained Gel Analysis
Protein components of rFVIII samples are first separated by polyacrylamide gel 
electrophoresis (SDS-PAGE) based on molecular weight in a precast gradient polyacrylamide 
gel then silver stained.  A visual comparison of the sample pattern to the in-house reference 
standard is made.  The results are reported as comparable or not comparable to standard.
Immunoassays
Quantitation of Host Cell Protein
BHK HCP is detected using HTRF. The assay involves a reaction using a fluorophore donor 
and a fluorophore acceptor. Europium cryptate, the fluorophore donor, is excited at 337 nm 
and emits at 620 nm with a long fluorescence half-life.  D2, the fluorophore acceptor, emits 
light at 665 nm efficiently, but with a very short half-life if no energy is transferred from a 
donor. When the two fluorophores, donor and acceptor, are in close proximity, as a result of a 
biomolecular interaction, the donor induces a long-lived emission from the acceptor which 
can be clearly distinguished from the donor signal by using time resolved detection.  
Additionally, time resolved detection minimizes background fluorescence.
In this procedure, HCP present in the sample(s) binds to a BAY 81-8973 process-specific 
polyclonal anti-BHK HCP antibody conjugated with europium cryptate and to a BAY 81-
8973 process-specific polyclonal anti-BHK HCP antibody conjugated with D2. The bound 
complex generates an HTRF signal that is measured by a microplate reader.  The 
concentration of the HCP species in the sample is interpolated from a HCP standard curve 
using a four-parameter fit and regression analysis.
Quantitation of Mouse IgG
Residual mIgG in BAY 81-8973 samples is detected using Homogeneous Time-Resolved 
Fluorescence (HTRF). The assay utilizes an affinity purified rabbit anti-mouse IgG polyclonal 
antibody conjugated to XL665 (XL, a modified allophycocyanin) as the fluorescence 
acceptor, and Europium Cryptate as the fluorescence donor, to generate the HTRF signal. The 
concentration of the mIgG in the sample(s) is interpolated from a standard curve using a 2nd 
degree polynomial fit and regression analysis.
Microbial Purity
Test samples are filtered through a membrane filter followed by a rinse with a  sterile diluent.  
The membrane is transferred onto the surface of plated media.  After incubation, the Colony 
Forming Units (CFU) are counted and reported as CFU/test volume. The test is performed in 
accordance with current compendia requirements (USP/Ph. Eur., JP)
Endotoxin
The Kinetic LAL assay detects gram negative bacterial endotoxin and is performed according 
to the harmonized test methods described in USP, Ph. Eur., and JP.  The kinetic test measures 
the time (onset time) needed for the reaction mixture to reach a predetermined parameter. The 
time is inversely proportional to the amount of endotoxin present.  The concentration of 
endotoxin in the sample is calculated by comparison to a standard curve containing known 
concentrations of an endotoxin standard.
Quantitation of Host Cell DNA
The Quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction method is based on DNA amplification using 
target-specific oligonucleotide primers.  The levels of amplified DNA are determined using a 
dual labeled fluorogenic probe with both reporter and quencher dyes attached. The PCR 
primer set defines an 87-base pair (bp) fragment in the highly conserved region of the rodent 
Alu B1 repeat nucleotide sequence which is specific and not likely to cross-react to 
non-rodent nucleotide sequences. The DNA in the samples acts as a template for primer 
extension, then during thermal cycling extension, DNA polymerase cleaves the reporter dye 
from the probe, which results in an increased fluorescence. A fluorescence detector 
determines a reporter dye fluorescence value (RN) for each sample well during each 
amplification cycle (Real-Time). During PCR amplification, there is an exponential increase 
of the fluorescence signal above its baseline that eventually reaches a plateau due to rate 
limiting reagents. It is this threshold cycle (CT) number at the plateau, or the point at which 
the signal is detected above the background in the exponential phase, that defines the amount 
of BHK DNA present in the Drug Substance (DS) test samples. Sample DNA is quantified by 
measuring threshold cycles (CT) against a BHK DNA standard curve.
Quantitation of Sodium and Calcium
Quantitation of sodium and calcium is carried out by inductively-coupled plasma optical 
emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES).  Samples, standards and controls are diluted into 2% (v/v) 
nitric acid prior to analysis.  Sodium is determined at wavelength 589.592 nm and calcium at 
422.673 nm.  The concentrations of sodium and calcium are determined by regression 
analysis using a linear fit standard curve for each ion.
Quantitation of Copper
The presence of copper is tested for by Atomic Absorption.  The system is comprised of an 
atomic absorption spectrophotometer, a burner-nebulizer system and an autosampler.  
Samples are diluted in 1% (v/v) nitric acid prior to analysis.  Signal intensities of copper are 
compared to a linear standard curve for quantitation.
Measurement of pH
The pH is measured potentiometrically.
Color Determination
The color of the sample is determined by visual comparison to reference solutions against a 
white background.
Quantitation of Osmolality
The Vapor Pressure Osmometer determines the osmolality of a solution by sensing the vapor 
pressure above the solution in a closed chamber. A precision thermocouple hygrometer 
measures the dew point temperature depression which is a function of the water vapor 
pressure in the chamber. This measurement is reported in milliosmoles of solute per kilogram 
of water (mOsm/kg).
Quantitation of Polysorbate 80
Protein and salts in the sample are first precipitated by mixing the sample with ethanol.  After 
mixing and centrifugation, the upper liquid phase is collected and evaporated.  The resulting 
residue is mixed with dichloromethane and an aqueous ammonium cobaltothiocyanate 
(ACTC) solution.  The Polysorbate 80 forms an intermolecular complex with the ACTC, and 
the resultant complex partitions into the dichloromethane phase.  The amount of ACTC 
carried into the dichloromethane phase is determined by its absorbance at 620 nm.  Under the 
conditions of the assay, this absorbance is directly proportional to the amount of 
Polysorbate 80 present in the sample.

the responsibility to perform the conformity assessment (CE-certificate is issued to West and

of the “real” manufacturing site) , but no quality changes or changes which affects safety and 
performance are addressed.

Question/Consideration:
Question 3
To provide the technical contract agreement between the manufacturing sites as the submitted 
mentions Bayer Consumer Care/ Switzerland which is not a manufacturer for Nexavar.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 3 ( Module 1):
Nexavar is a triangulated product.  See below for further explanation of this concept.
General Overview of BCC AG's Triangulation Model
Bayer Consumer Care AG (“BCC AG”), as the principal company and intellectual property 
holder (“IP Holder”), controls critical business processes across the pharmaceutical value chain, 
including R&D, manufacturing, procurement, marketing, sales, and logistics functions.

It collaborates with both related and non-affiliated manufacturers to produce healthcare 
products on its behalf, and then sells these goods to affiliated companies for further distribution 
to local end customers.
Specific Model for Nexavar
The specific model for Nexavar involves a collaborative process between BCC AG (IP Holder), 
Bayer AG (MAH), and Patheon (Manufacturer).

In this model, Bayer AG manufactures the active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) on behalf of 
BCC AG. The API is then provided to Patheon France for bulk manufacturing through toll 
manufacturing. The bulk is subsequently returned to Bayer AG for packaging of the finished 
goods, also through toll manufacturing. BCC AG then sells the finished goods to their affiliated 
companies. This model involves the quality oversight through BCC AG too.
BCC AG transmits the pharmaceutical requirements of Bayer AG (MAH) to the manufacturers 
of active ingredients, importers, carriers, providers of storage services, and of the manufacturers 
of the Products involved by entering into corresponding quality agreements with those parties 
subject to the prior consent of Bayer AG (MAH) to such quality agreements. BCC ensures by 
way of quality agreements entered into with Patheon and Bayer AG and their affiliates that 
production, processing, packaging, control and release is in accordance with the agreed 
formulation or instruction.

Question/Consideration:
Question 7
With regards to the comparative dissolution, to justify why the study done with the QC media 
has paddle speed as 100 rpm noting that as per FDA’s database the paddle speed must be 75 
rpm for QC media and to provide the JFDA with comparative dissolution with QC media at 
paddle speed 75 rpm.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 7 ( Module 3, P.2.2 ):
The study design for the comparison of dissolution profiles follows the recommendations 
stated in the ICH guideline M9 on biopharmaceutics classification system based biowaivers 
(EMA/CHMP/ICH/493213/2018) as stated in section 2.1 of the supportive document 
T.02.40#022974051-01 (Proof of Dissolution of the Active Drug Substance).
As presented in the Study Performance section 3.3 of the supportive document 
T.02.40#022974051-01 (Proof of Dissolution of the Active Drug Substance), the agitation 75 
rpm was applied for all dissolution profiles collected in pH 1, pH 4.5 and pH 6.8.
• ICH M9 specifies using 50 rpm for a paddle apparatus (T.02.16) but coning is known 
to occur for this product at that speed. All profiles in buffer without SDS were 
therefore collected at the lowest possible agitation (75 rpm), while 100 rpm was 
maintained for the QC medium, in line with the registered test procedure.
• In the development phase of the analytical method for dissolution different stirring 
speeds have been tested (see page 17, T.02.38). Finally, it was decided to perform the 
method validation with 100 rpm (see T.02.50 and T.02.16). The dissolution method 
with 100 rpm stirring speed which is described in the validated test procedure T.02.16. 
The mean dissolution profiles obtained at 75 rpm and 100 rpm are comparable and 
demonstrate that the discriminatory power of the dissolution method is maintained at 
the higher rotation speed (see T.02.38).

Question/Consideration:
Question 8 
 
Container-closure system: Results of the tightness test, since it was not presented.
Answer/Response:
Results of the Dye leak test can be found in documents M3.2.P.3.5, Process Validation and/or 
Evaluation and is carried out as IPC. The results comply, 100% of samples passed the test. 
Only the capsule fill weight has been identified as the critical process parameter of the 
manufacturing process. This CPP is controlled as an integrated part of the capsule filling 
process as an IPC during routine production. Other (i.e. non-critical) process parameters (e.g. 
leak tests) are tested only for information during process validation and not during routine 
manufacturing. The manufacturing process is very simple: The capsules are filled with pure 
API without any excipients. Each capsule shell is weighted and filled with API while being 
placed on a balance during the continuous manufacturing process. Therefore, the fill weight of 
each capsule is recorded. Capsules having a fill weight outsite the range of +/- 5% are 
automatically discarded by the process.

As a result, it has been decided in the technical transfer team to initiate a bracketing approach,

Question 4
In accordance with Appendix 1 of the Rules, provide information on development studies 
conducted to prove that the dosage form, composition, manufacturing process, packaging 
(closure) system, microbiological characteristics, instructions for preparation of the final 
dosage form suitable for immediate use, correspond to the intended use specified by the 
applicant in the registration dossier of the medicinal product. Critical formulation parameters 
and process characteristics that may affect batch reproducibility, medicinal product potency and 
quality should be identified and described. The compatibility of the active pharmaceutical 
substance with excipients, as well as the main physicochemical properties of the active 
pharmaceutical substance that may affect the performance of the medicinal product, should be 
justified; the choice of excipients should be justified, especially with regard to their respective 
functional characteristics and content; a description of the medicinal product development 
should be provided, taking into account the proposed route of administration and method of 
use; any physicochemical and biological properties and any parameters affecting the 
performance of the medicinal product should be specified and justified; information on the 
selection and optimization of the manufacturing process should be provided.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 4 (CTD section P.2):
We acknowledge the Agency comment.
We would like to inform the Agency that the development studies conducted for the drug 
product aimed to confirm that the formulation, composition, manufacturing process, and 
packaging system align with the intended therapeutic use specified in the registration dossier. 
A comprehensive approach was taken through pre-formulation, formulation optimization, and 
process validation stages.

Critical Formulation Parameters and Process Characteristics:
Formulation parameters:
• API concentration: The concentration of the active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) 
was optimized to ensure efficacy while minimizing potential side effects. 
• Excipients selection: From stability results, it was derived that Iopromide is compatible 
with the excipients chosen, and that their physicochemical characteristics do not 
influence the performance of the drug product.
The details of the excipients along with their function used for the drug products is summarized 
below:
Excipients 
Functions
Sodium Calcium Edetate 
Acts as a chelating agent, helping to stabilize the 
formulation by binding metal ions that could 
catalyze degradation.
Trometamol 
Used as a buffering agent to help maintain the pH 
of the solution, ensuring it remains stable and 
effective during storage and use
Sodium Hydroxide, 25% 
Also used for pH adjustment, helping to maintain 
the desired acidity or alkalinity for stability and 
efficacy
Hydrochloric acid 10% 
Used to adjust the pH of the solution to ensure 
stability and compatibility with bodily fluids
Water for injection 
Serves as the solvent for the solution, ensuring 
proper dilution and delivery of the active 
ingredients.

Process characteristics:
• Sterilization methods: The chosen sterilization method was validated to ensure the 
absence of microbial contamination. 
• Filling process: The filling process was designed to maintain sterility and ensure 
accurate dosing.
Microbial attributes:
• Sterility testing: Conducted according to pharmacopeial standards to confirm the 
absence of viable microorganisms in the final product. 
• Bioburden testing: Initial microbial load assessments were performed to establish 
baseline contamination levels.  
• Endotoxin testing: Evaluated to ensure levels of bacterial endotoxins are within 
acceptable limits for injectable products.
Microbial stability studies: Evaluated the formulation’s stability in relation to microbial growth 
over time, confirming that preservatives are effective in preventing microbial proliferation 
throughout the shelf life.
Physicochemical and Biological Properties:
• Stability studies: Conducted to confirm that the formulation maintains its potency and 
safety over the proposed shelf life under defined storage conditions.
Manufacturing Process Selection and Optimization:
• Process selection: The manufacturing method was selected for its ability to produce a 
sterile product, with thorough validation to support scalability. 
• Optimization: In-process controls were established to monitor critical parameters and 
ensure batch-to-batch consistency. 

The development studies provide robust evidence supporting the formulation, manufacturing, 
and packaging of the injectable medicinal product. All critical parameters have been addressed, 
demonstrating the product's safety, efficacy, and compliance with regulatory requirements.

Question/Consideration: Copy of finished product specification  and complete method of analysis for all tests.
Answer/Response:
We hereby conform that the proposed variation does not impact the specifications to the 
finished drug product. The new optimized method has been validated to replace the current 
method for testing Sodium at wavelength 589.592 nm with a radial plasma view mode. There 
was no change to the wavelength and view mode at which Calcium is detected. In addition, 
duplicate sample preparations were changed to single sample preparation that is read three 
times on the instrument. The reported value of a sample is the mean of the triplicate readings. 
The standard curve range from 0.5 to 5 ppm was extended to 0.5 to 10 ppm for both Sodium 
and Calcium. Differences between the two test methods are presented in Table 5–1.
This is an excipient content assay. Per ICH guidelines, the validation of the Sodium and 
Calcium assay covered the following assay parameters: Accuracy, repeatability precision, 
intermediate precision, linearity, specificity, range, sample stability and robustness. The same 
system and sample suitability criteria in the current method were confirmed suitable 
for the new method in the assay development studies and used for the assay validity 
assessment for the new method validation. A new preliminary control chart was then 
established with the new method for validation. The same acceptance criteria for each 
validation characteristics used for the current method were used for the new method 
validation. All validation criteria set forth in the validation protocol were met for each of the 
characteristics evaluated. A summary of the validation parameters tested for this method is 
provided in Table 5–2.

The validation was performed in the Quality Control (QC) laboratories. Successful 
completion of this validation and the comparability studies qualified the assay for its intended 
use to determine the Sodium and Calcium content in the BAY 81-8973 DP and DS samples. 
A single sample preparation was used in this validation. The standard curve was from 0.5 
ppm to 10 ppm. 
The validation studies were carried out with 250 IU DP and DS samples. The protein 
concentrations of the 250 IU DP and DS bracket other fill sizes of the DP. 
The determination of Sodium and Calcium is not a recombinant Factor VIII (rFVIII) product 
specific method. The differences of the protein concentration in the samples are insignificant 
compared to the concentration of analyte and have no impact on the determination of Sodium 
and Calcium content. Therefore, it is concluded that the validation for determination of 
Sodium and Calcium in DS sample is applicable to the DP sample types. 
 
The assay for determination of sodium and calcium concentration by ICP-OES has been 
shown to have acceptable accuracy, repeatability and intermediate precision, linearity, 
specificity and range, sample stability, and robustness to assess and release the DP samples. 
The comparability studies demonstrated that the new method generated comparable results 
with the current method for both Calcium and Sodium with reduced assay variation for 
Sodium. Successful completion of the validation and comparability studies also documented 
the qualification of the optimized new method in the QC Laboratory.
The requested validation reports for determination of Sodium and Calcium Concentration by 
ICP is provided with the response.

Question/Consideration:
Question 2
To have equivalent test documents attached to replace specifications/methods analysis of the 
“Residue on ignition” test which was not carried out on the Sucrose excipient.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 2:
Residue of ignition refers to the amount of non-volatile inorganic components in an organic 
sample. In other words, it is the sum of all mineral impurities in an excipient such as sucrose.
The applicability or relevance of the test depends on the use of the excipient in a given drug. 
If, for example, sucrose is used in a parenteral formulation, the residue is likely to be quality 
attribute.

For Cyclo-Progynova however, sucrose is only part of the sugar coating for an oral 
formulation. It is mixed with minerals (calcium carbonate and talc) intentionally for that 
purpose. Therefore, the residue on ignition is not a quality attribute for sucrose alone as an 
excipient for this type of formulation. Performing the test is of course possible, but the results 
are not expected to be of informative value for product quality. It is therefore considered 
acceptable to omit this test for this application of sucrose as an excipient. But besides the fact, 
that the method is omitted for sugar testing because of the function of the excipient in the 
production of Cyclo-Progynova, the manufacturer of Sucrose is testing it regularly.
Südzucker performs the method for the Ash content according to ICUMSA Method GS1-10 
(1998) (ICUMSA Method GS1-10 (1998) - ICUMSA). The method is suitable for the 
determination of the ash content of raw sugar samples with ash levels below 0.05g/100g. 
Sulphation of the sugar is undertaken prior to ignition at 525°C – results are expressed as 
sulphated ash. The absolute difference between two results obtained under repeatability 
conditions should not be greater than 0.030g/100g and under reproducibility conditions not 
greater than 0.054g/100g.
As a result, we see it as suitable to omit the test residue of ignition as the test is performed at 
the manufacturer for sucrose with a tighter limit as requested in the Indonesian Pharmacopeia.
keywords: Excipient Specifications; specification; pharmacopeia; Test Procedure; QC testing

The submission of variation for changes in Release and shelf life specifications, and in
analytical test methods, used for release and stability studies aims to upgrade our processes to
meet the current authority requirements.
Specifically, we have replaced the current TLC purity test method with new Ph. Eur.
compendial HPLC purity test method for Levonorgestrel dug substance to enhance the
accuracy and reliability of our impurity testing. The new Ph. Eur. compendial HPLC purity
test method, adapted to use for Jadelle implant,  provides a more robust and precise
determination of impurities.
We have tightened the acceptance criteria for “Sum of all impurities” in the Shelf life
specification from max. 2.0 % to max. 1.0 % because new test method includes only
levonorgestrel related degradation products but not any more synthesis related impurities like
current test method. Acceptance criterion for "Any individual impurity" remains unchanged in
Shelf-Life Specification.
The acceptance limit for the sum of all impurities is based on the USP monograph of
Levonorgestrel. Ph.Eur has published compendial HPLC purity method, Related substances A
in the 01/2014:0926 monograph and this method has been implemented for Levonorgestrel
drug substance quality control (QC) testing. Therefore, also the drug product HPLC purity
method applies the Ph. Eur. method. The extraction procedure and HPLC method has been
validated for the drug product. The synthesis impurities that are not potential degradation
products are controlled at levonorgestrel drug substance QC testing and are omitted in the
drug product test results according to ICH Q3B guidance. The potential known and
unidentified levonorgestrel degradation products above ≥ 0.1% reporting threshold are
included in the test results.
Due to inherent stability of levonorgestrel, Impurity test parameters will be deleted from
release Specification. The long history of the production has verified that levonorgestrel
remains virtually unchanged in the manufacturing process of the drug product, and also
during the stability studies. This is demonstrated by comparison of the results for six drug
product stability batches to the corresponding drug substance batch results . Comparison table
provided in P.5.6.01_02 Justification of Specification.

Justification for the non-inclusion of the impurity parameters into the release specification
provided in CTD section P.5.6.01_011789356_02

Specification: Unsatisfactory - For those batches with lot number with prefix of DP-ARR or 
DP-APS, the acceptance criteria for Potency/ Label Claim, Total Impurities, Individual 
Unspecified Impurities, Water Content stated on the stability report are different from those 
registered in the shelf-life specification. Please clarify.
Answer/Response:
The batches with lot number prefix of DP-ARR or DP-APS are all batches from development. 
These batches used in the studies were performed to generate supportive stability data for 
Larotrectinib sulfate capsule 25 mg and Larotrectinib sulfate capsule 0.1 g used in clinical 
trials according to ICH Q1A(R) “Stability Testing of New Substances and Products” 
requirements. Larotrectinib sulfate capsules used in clinical trials have the same composition 
as the commercial formulation. The investigated material varies in drug product 
manufacturing batch size as well as the size of the primary packaging container, i.e. HDPE 
bottle size and capsule count. Furthermore, the contained larotrectinib sulfate drug substance 
originates from different manufacturing processes, i.e., version 1 (v1), version 2 (v2), or 
version 3 (v3; commercial drug substance manufacturing process) as described in M.2.3.S.2.6 
“Manufacturing Process Development”. Test Parameters and acceptance criteria are the 
approved specifications at the time of testing and therefore do not necessarily correspond to 
the current approved specifications, set after more experience has been gained with the 
product. To make it more transparent which batches were used for which stability studies, 
Bayer has split the registration documents and its existing content into separated documents 
for a better overview.

Source:

Question/Consideration:
Question 1
Lack of declaration of conformity to safety and efficiency standards (ISO standard)
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1 (3.2.R):
The inserter is an integral part of the combination product Mirena and is placed on the market 
in such a way that drug and the device constituent part form a single integral product which is 
intended exclusively for use in the given combination and is not reusable. Consequentially, 
the stand-alone device part itself (inserter) has no medicinal purpose and cannot be used 
without the drug part (and vice versa). Therefore, a declaration of conformity cannot be issued 
for the inserter separately.
According to EU-legislation the manufacturer of an integral drug-device combination product 
(like Mirena) has to identify all relevant General Safety and Performance Requirements (acc. 
to Annex I EU Medical Device Regulation) and demonstrate compliance for the combination. 
Bayer has done this exercise for the product family Intrauterine Systems covering Mirena, 
Jaydess and Kyleena. Please find the relevant GSPR-check list VV-QUALDHF-3525 for the 
IUS family enclosed.
In case of new marketing authorization applications or in case of substantial changes in the 
design or intended purpose of the device constituent part of the combination product (this 
would constitute an impact on the safety and performance of the device part) an evaluation of 
the compliance with the GSPR performed by a Notified Body would become necessary. For 
the IUS family there were no such substantial changes since the EU-MDR came into force 
and therefore no Notified Body Opinion has been created so far.
Source:  VV-QUALDHF-3525

Question/Consideration: Clarify whether the analytical method validation used the single-point calibration or the proposed method (BYL Note: the two-points calibration with 50% and 100% standard solutions) for each validation item. Additionally, explain whether any results of analytical method validation performed with the proposed method are available separately (in internal documents, etc. other than the documents submitted to support the NDA approval).
Answer/Response:
The results of initial validation for dissolution test with UV method (T.02.50#022972950-05) are summarized as shown below.
Linearity of the method was evaluated by using standard solution containing sorafenib tosylate at 10%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%, 125% and 150% level, and test solution containing sorafenib tosylate at 20%, 50%, 75%, 100%, 125% and 150% level with placebo, respectively. Each calibration curve obtained from the standard solution and test solution was found to pass almost through the origin, and the correlation coefficients were found to be 1.0000 under each condition. The results indicate that good linearity over the measurement ranges was given for each solution.
Separately, accuracy (50%, 75%, 100%, 125% and 150% level test solution), and repeatability/intermediate precision (50%, 100% and 150% level test solution) were investigated and good accuracy and precision in the concentration range of 50 to 150% level were found.
The procedure to prepare the calibration curve is changed from single standard solution (100% level) to two standard solutions (50% and 100% level). No additional validation studies have been performed for the method change. However, the testing can be performed with the same accuracy and precision since the concentrations of the two standard solutions are within the validated range.

Question/Consideration:
Question 10

Clarification of the intent of S.2.4 Batch analysis data for intermediates, Table 2: Batch 
Analyses of Aflibercept Intermediate (DSI) lots used in Process Validation for Transfer of 
Manufacturing to PA9, Hold Time Study
Answer/Response:
Batches 8088100080 a 8088100081 a 8088100082 in S.2.4.05 are additional Aflibercept 
intermediate batches manufactured to confirm extended hold times at Regeneron, Raheen, 
Ireland as described in S.2.2.02. 
Please refer to the process validation S.2.5.01 chapter 2.5:  
  
2.5 Process Performance Qualification – Extended Hold Time 
 
As part of the overall process validation, manufacturing is also performed, under protocol,  
using extended processing times to establish maximum time limits of production for each  
step.  
Three consecutive PV DSI lots were subjected to extended holds for each downstream pool to 
establish time limits for production. Each downstream process hold point was sampled for  
product quality, with respect to chemical stability, and microbial control once the entire pool  
was collected and mixed, and then again at the end of each hold. Samples were taken and  
analyzed for bioburden and endotoxin levels to demonstrate microbial control of the held  
material. The chemical stability of the held downstream pools was assessed by comparing the 
results of product aggregation (SE-UPLC), product fragmentation (SDS-PAGE), and charge  
variant heterogeneity (iCIEF) from samples taken at the start of the hold, with the results of  
the samples taken at the end of the hold. Additionally, material was compared to DSI release  
specification. The cumulative effect of the extended holds on the final concentrated pool, at  
the end of the UF/DF step, was also assessed.

results along with individual data (n=12), mean, RSD values and dissolution profiles.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 5:
During method development, dissolution studies in different media were investigated with
clinical batches, according to USP requirements. The drug substance rivaroxaban is
practically insoluble in aqueous media and the solubility is almost pH-independent over a
range from pH 1-6.8 (refer to P.5.3.21, Section 2.2., Table 3).
In line with the pH-independent solubility of the drug substance, the drug product
Rivaroxaban granules also show a pH-independent dissolution behavior over a broad pH-
range from pH 1-6.8 (refer to P.5.3.21, Section 2.2.2., Fig. 1), and an overall very robust
dissolution performance (e.g. pH- and rotation speed independent). The individual dissolution
results can be found in section 4.
As explained in P.5.3.21, pH 4.5 media was selected as dissolution medium for Rivaroxaban
granules 2% oral suspension, as in this buffer system the drug substance is sufficiently stable.
For more details on the dissolution profile performed with clinical batches refer to P.2.2.02.
The individual data are documented in section 2.

reference to clinical batch KM600PC ((P.5.3.21 and Module 2.7.1, p.33).

Question/Consideration:
Question 1
4) PRODUCTION PROCESS
4.1) In the changes presented in the production process, it is detected that the integrity test of 
the seals is replaced by the integrity of the container and the closure (Band 180). Justify
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1 :
The current burst test for Integrity of seals is replaced by more accurate Container closure 
integrity test, Strip 180° -test.
Current burst test (according to ASTM F1140) measures the pressure at which the package 
will burst and determines the ability of package to withstand internal pressurization. Testing 
of seal strength by the Strip test, however, is more relevant as a process control of primary 
packaging step., It does not only control the opening force and package integrity, but it 
measures the ability of the packaging process to produce consistent and durable seals.
The new IPC strip test is based on ASTM F88/F88M Standard Test Method for Seal Strength 
of Flexible Barrier Materials and EN 868-5 Packaging for terminally sterilized medical 
devices – Part 5: Sealable pouches and reels of porous materials and plastic film construction 
– Requirements and test methods. In the test seal made in primary packaging phase is opened 
with universal mechanical testing machine (UMTM) or a tensile testing machine (TTM). The 
force needed to open the seal is recorded and the average force of opening is reported.
keywords: Container closure system; in-process control; Description of Manufacturing Process and Process Controls; Process Validation and/or Evaluation; Sterilization

Question/Consideration:
Question 2
5) ANALYTICAL METHODOLOGY AND SPECIFICATIONS: You must justify the 
changes made in the analytical methodology and specifications, with particular attention to 
the following:
5.1) It is detected that the test of related substances for release is removed from the 
specifications.
5.2) It is detected that the tests of cyclohexane, ethylene oxide, ethylene chlorohydrin are 
removed from the shelf life of the product.
5.3) According to the update of specifications, the sterility and endotoxin tests will not be 
carried out throughout the shelf life of the product.
5.4) The identification test is not included in the shelf-life specifications, it is not appropriate, 
it must be part of the tests carried out during the shelf life.
5.5) Given the change in the specifications for the test of related substances for the shelf life 
of the product, clarify specifications for impurities at a local level and provide the 
corresponding CoA model.
5.6) Expand information regarding the results of the specificity test in the report "validation 
for content testing" (P.5.3.09-01) with respect to impurities 10,13 and 16 that co-elute with 
the active ingredient.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 2 :
5) The proposed new impurity test performed by HPLC is superior compared to the current 
impurity test by TLC. In this context the tightening of the requirement for the Sum of 
impurities from 2% to 1% ensures effectively the quality of Jadelle throughout the whole 
shelf-life. The Levonorgestrel drug substance of Jadelle is verified to be very stable. Based on 
stability studies by TLC the Sum of impurities has remained constantly below the proposed 
requirement of max 1.0% even though the synthesis impurities have also been taken into 
account in the analysis. In the prosed HPLC method only actual degradation products, in 
accordance with the Health Authority guidelines, will be considered.
Jadelle implant has been on the market for more than 30 years already. Hence, the quality 
characteristics of the product are well known and have been established for a long time 
already. Due to the known and proven excellent stability of Levonorgestrel Bayer Oy 
considers it justified to perform the impurity testing for Jadelle implant during the stability 
studies/shelf-life only.
Impurity testing is not included in Release Specifications of Jadelle, but it is performed during 
the stability studies for the product. As the results of impurity testing are constantly fulfilling 
the requirements set at the end of the shelf-life, it is clear that a batch of Jadelle would comply 
with the requirements if it would be tested for impurities at release.
Organic impurities arising from degradation of the new drug substance and impurities that 
arise during the manufacturing process for the drug product should be monitored in the new 
drug product. Acceptance limits should be stated for individual specified degradation 
products, which may include both identified and unidentified degradation products as 
appropriate, and total degradation products. Process impurities from the new drug substance 
synthesis are normally controlled during drug substance testing, and therefore are not included 
in the total impurities limit. However, when a synthesis impurity is also a degradation 
product, its level should be monitored and included in the total degradation product limit. 
When it has been conclusively demonstrated via appropriate analytical methodology, that the 
drug substance does not degrade in the specific formulation, and under the specific storage 
conditions proposed in the new drug application, degradation product testing may be reduced 
or eliminated upon approval by the regulatory authorities.

5.1) Due to inherent stability of levonorgestrel, Impurity test parameters will be deleted from 
Release Specification. The long history of the production has verified that levonorgestrel 
remains virtually unchanged in the manufacturing process of the drug product, and also 
during the stability studies. This is demonstrated by comparison of the results for six drug 
product stability batches to the corresponding drug substance batch results . Comparison table 
provided in P.5.6.01 Justification of Specification.

5.2) We have tightened the acceptance criteria for “Sum of all impurities” in the Shelf life 
specification from max. 2.0 % to max. 1.0 % because new test method includes only 
levonorgestrel related degradation products but not any more synthesis related impurities like 
current test method. Acceptance criterion for "Any individual impurity" remains unchanged in 
Shelf-Life Specification.

5.3) Sterility testing
“Sterility” test parameter will be deleted as redundant from the Shelf-life Specification as 
sterility testing will be replaced with container closure integrity tests in stability studies. The 
maintenance of the sterile barrier integrity, and hence the sterility throughout the shelf life is 
demonstrated during stability studies by testing the integrity of the primary package. This is in 
accordance with the principles of European Medicines Agency (ref. to EMA Quality of 
medicines questions and answers: Part 2). This approach is in accordance also with FDA 
guidance document for industry (February 2008); Container and Closure System Integrity 
Testing in Lieu of Sterility Testing as a Component of the Stability Protocol for Sterile 
Products.
Endotoxins test
“Endotoxins” test parameter will be deleted as redundant from the Shelf-life Specifications 
because endotoxins test is not considered a stability indicating test by European Medicines 
Agency (ref. to EMA Quality of medicines questions and answers: Part 2)
5.4) Identity test will be deleted from the Shelf-life Specifications because  it is not 
considered a stability indicating test. Identity of drug substance can not alter or change during 
the shelf-life of a batch. If the identity test would be performed during the Shelf-life it would 
comply with the requirements set in Release Specification. From that perspective the 
requirement can be seen to be valid throughout the whole shelf-life of Jadelle, though the test 
is not specified in Shelf-life Specification.

5.5)  Testing specifications for related substances included in the local CoA correspond to the 
original shelf life specifications.

5.6)   Of the 17 levonorgestrel related drug substances, impurities 10, 13 and/or 16 are not 
fully separated from levonorgestrel in all cases. Of these, impurity 10 has in practice no 
response at 240 nm, 13 is not anymore described in levonorgestrel micronized drug substance 
TRDs S.3.2.1-04 (Potential impurities) and S.7.3.903-02 (Stability Data – Stress Tests) as 
potential levonorgestrel synthesis or degradation product and hence not relevant impurity in 
Levonorgestrel implant 75 mg. Also, impurity 16 is not relevant impurity in Bayer AG 
levonorgestrel manufacturing process. However, in S.7.3.903-02; Stability Data – Stress 
Tests) its amount increased slightly after 30 days stress in hot alkali (80°C, pH13) conditions. 
All other impurities are either adequately separated from levonorgestrel or do not have 
significant UV response at the 240 nm wavelength that is used in the assay test. No peaks that 
would interfere the assay of levonorgestrel were observed in the blank and placebo samples 
and the peak purity analysis of the stressed Levonorgestrel implant 75 mg samples suggested 
homogeneous levonorgestrel peak. As a conclusion adequate specificity is established for the 
intended purpose of levonorgestrel assay in Levonorgestrel implant 75 mg.
In all test cases of stressed samples, high temperature and UV light, Levonorgestrel peak 
purity is considered to be pure as Purity angle is less than Purity Threshold.
The stability of levonorgestrel drug substance in Jadelle implant, and overall in levonorgestrel 
containing drug products of Bayer, has been verified to be excellent. No significant 
degradation occurs during the product’s shelf-life. An updated version -02 of the Stability 
report P.8.3.01 for the new analysis methods is provided to the competent Health Authority 
for review.

Question/Consideration:
On variation description the existing Magnesium stearate per tablet changed from  0.3 to 0.4 
mg/tablet whereas on regulatory documents it was changed from 0.2 mg/tablet to 0.4 
mg/tablet, please explain which value is correct and what is the rationale for the difference 
between 0.2/0.3?
Answer/Response:
With the change 202109341, the magnesium content of 0.4 mg/tablet was validated in 2021 
(see P.3.5.01_007096748_03).
After this validation, the old manufacturing description (MD) was replaced. This document 
contained a description of the single dosage form (chapter “Basic unit” [mg/unit]), a chapter 
“Batch size” ([kg/batch]), and a description of the manufacturing process as one document. 
The possible magnesium stearate range was only explained verbally in the chapter “Batch 
size”. The described batch size in the MD referred to a magnesium stearate amount of 0.3 
mg/tablet and thus corresponded to the production in Weimar. This is the amount that was 
used when the product was initially validated at the production site Weimar in 1999 (see 
P.3.5.901_004452335_01, page 12, point 4.2).
When the MD FE004 was created 26 years ago, in the chapter “Basic unit”, the smallest 
amount of the range of magnesium stearate was generally given for the description of the 
dosage form (0.2 mg magnesium stearate per tablet).
In the chapter “Batch size”, however, the optimal amount of magnesium stearate was 
specified, which was also used in production (0.3 mg magnesium stearate per tablet). It is 
stated in the same chapter that a magnesium stearate-range of 0.2 to 0.4 mg per tablet applies 
depending on the excipient’s quality (see P.3.2.901_004432444).
The new validation replaces the existing magnesium stearate range, which was never used. 
All MBRs in Weimar referred to 0.3mg. Since the new tablet presses today have a higher 
capacity than 26 years ago, the magnesium stearate content per tablet was increased to the 
maximum amount of 0.4 mg/tablet to ensure the associated faster supply of the granulate and 
the manufacturing process was thus revalidated in 2021. At the same time, the switch from 
MD to TRD took place. The newly created TRDs after the latest manufacturing validation 
(P.1.01_005762468 and P.3.2.01_022963945) now both refer to the current and correct 
magnesium content of 0.4 mg/tablet as a single value without range. Thus, a concise 
description of the drug product and its manufacturing process is registered with the 
authorities.

Question/Consideration: On August 17, 2023, we requested that you provide a clinically relevant  justification for the chosen specifications for the Detachment Force test. In response to this request, you state that the specification for this test was based on physical-technical data. However, this is not a clinically relevant justification. Therefore, it is not clear if the results of this test supports the safe and effective use of the subject product. Please provide a clinically-relevant justification for the chosen specification, that demonstrates the safe and effective use of the subject product. Specifically, please provide a justification that demonstrates that the forces observed will not lead to patient injury during insertion and ease of use of the product for users during insertion.
Answer/Response:
The quality control test “Detachment force” with the proposed specifications has been defined for Mirena to verify that the IUS can easily be released from the insertion tube prior the withdrawal step. The purpose of the Detachment Force test is to confirm that the IUS releases from the inserter with a minimum force ensuring that the IUS remains in the uterine cavity when the inserter is retracted after the insertion. The measured detachment force is the force of friction between the IUS, thread, and the inserter. Performance of Detachment force test in MIRENA release analysis for every batch ensures the correct positioning of the IUS during the insertion, and hence safety of the use of MIRENA for the patient. The proposed specification for detachment force is an upper limit derived from measurements with the inserter used in the original clinical trials where correct placement was verified. Hence, the requirements set verify the link between the test and the clinical performance of Mirena. Detachment forces below this limit have been demonstrated to not alter the positioning of the T-body when withdrawing the inserter.

It has been demonstrated in the clinical study that MIRENA IUS with the inserter is safe and effective in women who undergo the IUS insertion. The data from clinical studies confirmed successful insertion and proper positioning of the IUS in the uterine cavity. The requirement for the force is set low enough to exclude the T body’s possibility of bending from T-shape to slight Y-shape during the inserter withdrawal, which could compromise the correct positioning of the IUS. Proper position of the IUS in the uterine cavity is an important pre-requisite for ensuring the efficacy of the product. IUS must be in situ to provide MIRENA’s contraception efficacy.

The Detachment Force test confirms easy detachment of the IUS from the inserter during the insertion. The IUS must slide out of the inserter without significant peak forces, which is confirmed with the detachment force test. Verification of the adequacy of this force provides justification that the T-body position will not change during the inserter withdrawal, and that the IUS remains in correct position in the uterine cavity.

Determined detachment force results at release and during shelf-life have reliably verified that only very low forces are needed to detach the IUS from the inserter. Detachment force is independent of storage time. Therefore, testing of Detachment force at batch release only is justified. Two stage approach is applied to the test. A description of the test performance is provided in P.5.2.01_022975951_04 (Test Procedures) on page 26 of 31.

The Detachment force Test was performed for 22 batches of Mirena and the results are presented on page 32 of 120 of document P.5.6.01_022975985_02 (table 2-7). The sample size from each batch ranges from 40 samples to 100 samples. In total, 1486 samples were tested for the Detachment force. All the results, which are well in the proposed specifications confirm that the detachment force level from batch to batch fulfills the set requirements, thus providing assurance for the safe insertion of Mirena. Mirena IUS complying with the specifications can be stated safe to be inserted and used.

In point 2.3.P.1 Description and Composition of the Drug Product (MAGNEVIST®, Solution) of CPID-CE the molecule “Diethylenetriamine pentaacetic acid meglumine salt” is referring to the salt form of the DTPA (also known as Pentetic acid) bounded to meglumine.

Diethylenetriaminepentaacetic acid (Pentetic acid)
Meglumine

5 molecules of meglumine are bounded to Diethylenetriamine pentaacetic acid, forming the corresponding salt that can be also called “Pentetate pentameglumine”. Therefore the terms “Diethylenetriamine pentaacetic acid meglumine salt” and “Pentetate pentameglumine· are in fact equivalents.

Also for your reference see below the structure of the API (made in situ while manufacturing the Finished product – cannot be isolated) “Gadopentetate, dimeglumine”:

Additionally, kindly consider that Meglumine is used not only to form the dimeglumine salt but moreover to neutralize the excess of DTPA (pH adjustment). The excess of DTPA is added to ensure that no free gadolinium ions are present.

Question/Consideration: RFI2 Q.11 In response to RFI1 Q.13 you have justified the use of stability data from all storage temperatures for use in a single regression model based on poolability of data to estimate the shelf-life parameter for purity (RP-HPLC). In the same response you have referred to poolability being assessed as per ICH Q1E. Although ICH Q1E does discuss poolability, this is with regard to individual batch data subject to different factors such as container closure types and drug product strengths; there is no implication in ICH Q1E that poolability should be applied to stability data from different storage temperatures. Please provide regression analysis that only considers stability data from the long term refrigerated storage condition. The shelf-life limit for purity (RP-HPLC) should only be justified based on long term storage data regression analysis.
Answer/Response:
It is important to note that an additional change was meant to be included with this submission bundle and the CMN Form B.  The purpose of the additional change is due to a commitment made to EMA    Explain change
For drug product purity, the batches could be pooled to estimate the common slopes at 5°C, 25°C and 30°C. The storage conditions were not pooled to create one estimate, rather batches and strengths were pooled to create slope estimates for each storage condition.
Shelf-life limit is justified based on the storage condition of 18 months at 5°C followed 6 months at 25°C, this is the worst-case situation of the licensed storage condition which specifies: Store in a refrigerator (2 °C ¬ 8 °C) for 2 years. Within its overall shelf life of 2 years, the product (when kept in its outer carton) may be stored at up to 25 °C for a limited period of 6 months.

Question/Consideration:
Question 2
Bayer has confirmed that Dotagraf is stable and not degraded. However, upon reviewing the attached documents, dividing the stressed sample numbers mentioned on pages 1, 3, or 5 by the unstressed sample number on page 7 results in a degradation percentage exceeding 10%. Please provide justification for this discrepancy.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 2:
Bayer would like to explain that as described in the literature and proven by many years of manufacturing (start of supplying the markets since first approval in Germany in 2015, present in more than 50 countries around the globe), the metalorganic complex formed by Gadolinium and ligand DOTA is very stable and is produced by a robust manufacturing process (i.e. temperature of 70 - 80°C, pH of above 7 during formation of the Gd-DOTA complex). In general, the active substance is therefore stable in the final product over the entire shelf-life.

The results of the stress tests as part of the method validation (using samples foreseen for HPLC investigation) show that degradation occurs to a greater extent under the used extreme conditions, i.e. exposure to H2SO4, NaOH, oxidative stress by H2O2, high temperatures and light for a longer time. However, the degree of degradation achieved has no influence on the routine analysis of the final product samples. It is only a routine programme of stressing drug products samples to learn the stability behaviour of the HPLC samples in general. Hence, it should not be concluded from the results of the a.m. stress tests whether or not the final product stored under the recommended storage conditions is stable with regard to the formation of degradation products.
As a result, when the drug product is stored as recommended, no such degradation takes place.
In addition, in stability studies at 40°C/75% RH no signs of severe degradation or increase of impurities outside the specifications were observed.

Additionally, for your information only, please find enclosed the updated stability data till 36 months.

Source:  M3.2.P.8.3-08 Stability Data / Gadoterate meglumine solution 0.5 mol/L in glass vials for injection(DOTAGRAF) (#010689025; updated)
keywords: stability data DS; Stability data; Stability Summary and Conclusion; stress conditions; HPLC-method

Question/Consideration:
Please provide in-use stability data to substantiate the in-use shelf-life of 10 hours after first opening or provide relevant ref. or guideline in support of
(a) "the chemical and physical stability of Iopromide solution (ULTRAVIST) after first opening is demonstrated by the long-term and accelerated stability data" as stated in reply letter and
(b) the requirement, result and limits set for the microbiological attributes.
Answer/Response:
a)
As confirmed in our answer to the first HA request regarding our application for change of registered particulars (dated 09 Feb 2023, 25 Sep 2023, 31 Oct 2023 & 18 Apr 2024) the chemical and physical stability of Iopromide solution (ULTRAVIST) after first opening is supported by the long-term and accelerated stability data. Please find attached again as reference the long-term and accelerated stability reports for the 500 ml bottle in P.8.3.01_006768452_04 and P.8.3.02_008054946_22, which were submitted in our answer dated 2024-04-15. Furthermore, documents P.8.1.01_006775326_03 `Stability Summary` and P.8.3.11_022968677_01 `Stability Data – Additional Data` are amended. These data are strongly supportive of the in-use shelf life of 10 hours. No changes of the physico-chemical qualities would be expected in this timeframe, taking into account that Ultravist is a liquid solution.
Additionally please find attached a stress test for high temperature conditions during transport. A cycle test was performed for this purpose to demonstrate that Ultravist 370 (as a worst case) is not prone to crystallization under these conditions (P.8.3.903_004463921_01). Temperature changes between 15 °C and 40 °C were applied over a time period of 3 weeks without provoking any sign of crystallization.

b)
The microbial challenge test uses a set of standard micro-organisms and site isolates to represent a broad spectrum of contamination germs. We consider this test setup to be worst case, since it proves that the solution itself resists microbial infestation and prevents the growth of all test organisms within a period of 10 hours.
This test qualifies for an in-use test, and is independent from the injection equipment and pharmaceutical form of the product. The microbiological stability is confirmed also in these cases for 10 hours. None of the used test organisms showed growth within the targeted in use time of 10 hours. Therefore an in use time of 10 hours can be justified for both solutions, Ultravist 300 and Ultravist 370. Please find attached in addition to the previously provided P.2.5.01-01 and In-Use Stability Declaration the relevant detailed working report for Ultravist 300 and 370: Ultravist microbiological challenge test (QCB_A001_E01).

The microbiological characteristics of the product and its change over 30 hours of inoculation are displayed in Table 2, 3 and 4 of the report QCB_A001_E01. The results show that the analysed Ultravist solutions are not susceptible to growth of the test microorganisms within the test period of 30 hours. For all tested microorganisms, no multiplication in growth was detected in the test solutions. Therefore an in-use time of 10 hours at 20°C to 25°C after first opening of the container can be accepted.
Source: P.8.1.01-03 Stability Summary / Iopromide solution 0.3 g _Iodine/mL in vial and bottle for parenteral use (ULTRAVIST 300) (P.8.1.01_006775326_03; new)

Question/Consideration: Provide relevant ref. or guideline in support of the bracketing approach based on the historic stability profile.
Answer/Response:
In general, the selection of stability testing conditions underlies several factors, e.g. dosage form, primary container, storage conditions, market to be supplied (climatic zone) and is performed in accordance to the ICH Guideline “Stability Testing of New Drug Substances and Products Q1A(R2)” in its current version. Respective stability data evaluation is performed according to ICH Guideline Q1E.
As all fills have identical formulation bracketing was used as described by ICH Q1D. It is the design that only samples on the extremes of the container size and/or fill are tested (smallest and biggest). The design assumes that the stability of any intermediate levels is represented by the stability of the extremes tested. Nevertheless, intermediates are tested in ongoing stability studies.
All batches are packaged in the commercial packaging materials (vials: glass type I; bottles: glass type II; chlorinated butyl rubber, gray).
As the respective container closure system is generally considered hermetic (i.e. impermeable to water vapor) the current data support a shelf life of 36 months for climatic zones I to IV.

As outlined in response to Question 2 above, the selection of stability testing conditions underlies several factors like e.g. dosage form, primary container, storage conditions, market to be supplied etc. Stability studies are conducted in accordance with ICH Q1 guidelines which also includes bracketing approach due to the fact that all fills have identical formulation. During the bulk production of Ultravist solutions, sodium hydroxide (NaOH) solution is used (if necessary) for the adjustment of the pH value which is in approximately 2% of the batches produced the case and had been ever since original product registration. In document P.8.3.01-04 the stability data of one batch are provided as an example where the pH adjustment of bulk solution was done with NaOH to demonstrate that the product stability is not affected by any pH adjustment during production. These Stability Data (P.8.3.01-04) were already generated in the past, but as there was no change in process, these data are still valid and thus registered shelf life is justified.
