Question/Consideration:
Question 4
Considering the information in the stability data document submitted during initial registration 
and additional data fulfillment is different, the Aflibercept intermediate stability protocol 
should be submitted and clarification should be given regarding the primary packaging system 
(vial/polycarbonate vial/other) and long-term storage temperature (-20 or -30 degrees Celsius) 
for Aflibercept intermediate from the approved and submitted facility.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 4 (S.2.4):

In the commercial process, Aflibercept intermediate is stored in polycarbonate bottles (see 
S.2.4.10) at -30°C set point ±10°C, (equivalent to  ≤-20 °C) for up to 12 months. The is the 
same for both the approved US site and new Ireland site.
With the submission of the new site Regeneron, Raheen, Ireland, document 
S.2.4.82_021669382_05 was provided which contains the data for 3 PPQ validation batches 
manufactured at the new site (batches 8088100085, 8088100088, and 8088100089). These 
studies were performed at -30°C in polycarbonate vial consistent with the commercial process.
In the initial Eylea NDA application and in the current dossier, the Aflibercept intermediate 
storage temperature was stated as “≤-20 °C” to only state the upper limit.
The initial stability studies for Aflibercept intermediate batches from 2007 (batches 
C07003M500, C07004M500 and C07005M500) were also performed in EVA bags and 
polycarbonate vials as well as the additional data from 2014 also in polycarbonate vials (batches 
8088100008, 8088100014, 8088100023). They were performed both at -20°C and -30°C (set 
point) to cover temperature excursions of ±10°C from the -30°C set point - up to -20°C.
These studies are shown in the S.2.4.82#021847926_01 (amended to S.2.4.82#022951206_02 
with the response from 10th August 2024).
To clarify the storage temperature, the same document is further amended to 
S.2.4.82_022988528_03 with this response to state the storage condition of Aflibercept 
intermediate as:

Based on the results provided in this document, Aflibercept intermediate was assigned a shelf
life of 12 months when stored at set point of -30 °C (acceptable range of -20 °C to -40 °C).

Question 1
Keeping point 2 from the previous rejection: adjusting to nton 19 013 - 20 annex f item 8.3 c5

of at least three batches of final product manufactured with the new process, one for the dlccm 
and he another for file.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1 ( CTD section):
Please note that as it was already explained Bayer confirms that batch data with the omitted 
ELISA test is currently not available at this stage, as the change is not approved globally in all 
countries yet. Following the approval in all countries globally, the ELISA test after fermentation 
will be omitted from the manufacturing process and batch data will be continuously collected 
and available through the quarterly analysis of CPV data.

Bayer AG commits to submit the CoAs with the analytical results as soon as they will be 
available by June 2025.

We would like also to highlight that the manufacturing process of recombinant interferon beta-
1b (rIFN beta-1b) as a drug substance for Interferon beta-1b lyophilized powder (Betaferon) at 
Boehringer Ingelheim RCV GmbH & Co KG is well-established for over 30 years and adequately 
monitored by in-process and release testing.
In order to assure adequate process performance and product quality, continuous process 
verification (CPV) is performed once every quarter to assess the quality of the output material as 
well as  system performance in a continuous manner.
The justification to delete the test parameter “content of rIFN beta-1b by ELISA after fermentation” 
is further explained below.
The test to analyze the content of rIFN beta-1b by ELISA after fermentation was originally 
implemented for monitoring purposes only. Consequently, the results of the ELISA test are not used 
for any process decision and do not prevent the proceeding from the fermentation step to the primary 
recovery step of the inclusion bodies. In addition, the test results from the ELISA assay are not 
included in the CPV documentation. Considering the above, all available data of  rIFN beta-1b 
content measured by ELISA was thoroughly analyzed and it was confirmed that no deviation from 
the registered limit (NLT 0.3 mg/mL) was identified over the past 80 manufactured batches. Please 
refer to Error! Reference source not found. below.

Moreover, in the subsequent manufacturing step (primary recovery of the inclusion bodies (IBs), 
the content of rIFN beta-1b is measured with the RP-HPLC and strictly controlled with an action 
limit of NLT 11 mg/g. Over the last four years, historical CPV data for the most recent 50 IB batches 
demonstrates that rIFN beta-1b content measured via RP-HPLC analysis was well within the 
control limits (12.55 – 23.09 mg/g) and above the low alarm limit (11.00 mg/g). Please refer to 
Figure 1 and Figure 33 below.

Figure 1 Histogram of rIFN beta-1b content measured by ELISA (n=80 batches)

Figure 1: The  content of rIFN beta-1b measured by ELISA test after fermentation is
shown from 80 batches (manufactured  
between 2018-2023). All values are within the registered acceptable ranges (Mean = 0.5
mg/ml). LSL = Lower  
specification limit

Figure 2 Content of rIFN beta-1b measured by RP-HPLC (n = 50 batches)

Figure 2: The  content of rIFN beta-1b measured by RP-HPLC is shown from the last 50
batches (manufactured between  
2019-2023). All values are well within the registered acceptable ranges. LAL = Lower
Alarm limit, LCL = Lower control limit 
UCL = Upper control Limit
Figure 3 Histogram of rIFN beta-1b content measured by RP-HPLC (n = 50 batches)

Figure 3: The  distribution (histogram) of  rIFN beta-1b content measured by RP-HPLC
is shown from the last 50 batches  
(manufactured between 2019-2023). All values were well within the registered acceptable
ranges. LSL = Lower  
specification limit

As the ELISA test shows higher variability in comparison to RP-HPLC analysis (intermediate 
precision for ELISA is 20 %  versus 3.0 % for RP HPLC) and both tests can be considered 
redundant, it is intended to monitor rIFN beta-1b content on the level of recovered IBs measured 
with the more precise RP HPLC analysis in future.
Notably, the deletion of this test is currently in the process of being registered globally. Until all 
approvals are obtained globally, this test is continued to be performed and thus no CPV data with 
the deleted ELISA test is currently available at this stage.
Bayer confirms that once all approvals are obtained for this variation globally, the ELISA test after 
fermentation is omitted from the drug substance manufacturing process and CPV (validation) data 
will be collected quarterly to continuously monitor the quality and process performance over time. 
Moreover, Bayer confirms that except for the deletion of the monitoring ELISA parameter at the 
end of fermentation, no further changes to the manufacturing process were introduced and no impact 
on CPV data is thus expected, also considering that the ELISA test was not part of the CPV 
documentation before.

Please also refer to the Declaration submitted within this response for further details.

Question/Consideration:
Question 1
There is a discrepancy between the results of ‘Sum of all degradation products’ in Shelf-Life 
Specification (3.2.P.5.1 Specification) and in the Stability data (3.2.P.8.3 Stability Data) - max. 
1.0 % vs to max. 2.0 %. The HA asks to specify the difference and provide the relevant in 
documentation.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1 ( CTD section): 3.2.P.3.2
Please note that the discrepancy between the limits is related to the start of the stability study 
with the pilot batches in 2017, which was during the development phase of the Finerenone 
product (please refer to table 1-1 in the stability reports P.8.3.01_022846388 v02 and 
P.8.3.01_022846389 v03). In general, during the development phase the limits for the 
degradation products are broader than for market products.
Nevertheless, in the submission package of the initial NDA, Bayer also submitted stability 
data for the commercial batches in blisters in which the tighter limit, with max. 1.0%, is 
reflected (please refer to the stability reports P.8.3.01_022952778 v06 and 
P.8.3.01_022952779 v06). This data is reflecting the submitted shelf-life specification for the 
market product.
The pilot batches are generated for the NDA submission and reflect the development phase 
status which is used to justifying the stability profile of the drug product.
Additionally, the stability results of the pilot batches comply with the tighter specification 
limit of 1.0%. The product quality is therefore confirmed.

Question/Consideration: Submit pharmacopeial monograph and highlight the ranges of specifications
Answer/Response:
At the time of renewal submission in , the Release Specification with Code T.02.28-06 and Shelf Life Specification with Code T.02.01-06 were the current versions of drug product specification (“in-house method”). Stability study of all batches presented in T.04.02 (see Question 1) was based on this previous (in-house) specification.
The exemplary Certificate of Analysis (batch BXJCR71) submitted with the response to authority request from Oct 2020 was also based on specification T.02.01-06.
The requested pharmacopeial monograph was not valid at the time of renewal submission. Thus, we do not consider it to be relevant for this response letter.
Background information:
In April 2021 a new monograph 3021 for <Rivaroxaban tablets> became valid in supplement 10.4 of the 10th edition of the European Pharmacopoeia. Bayer AG is the originator of Rivaroxaban tablets, therefore Bayer AG’s current in-house test procedures and specification are also the origin of the Ph. Eur. Monograph 3021 <Rivaroxaban tablets>. However, the Ph. Eur. test procedure and method requirements have been adapted from the in-house method in many aspects.
For implementation, a variation was submitted in May 2023  to change the drug product specification and control tests of Rivaroxaban coated tablets, in order to reflect and to comply with the requirements of the new monograph in Ph. Eur.10.4 monograph 3021 <Rivaroxaban tablets>. Approval for this variation was reached in February 2024. The next batches provided to Egypt will be tested and released according to the new specifications.
The before mentioned documents have been replaced by the Release Specification with Code T.02.28-01 and Shelf Life Specification with Code T.02.02-01 which are submitted here as new, supporting documents.

Question/Consideration: 2.7. In the sections “Impurities” and “Assay” in the decoding of the S1 multiplier, to specify “...on the chromatograms of standard solutions R1 or R2...” instead of “... R1 and R2...”.
Answer/Response:
Bayer response to Question 2.7 (CTD section):
We would like to inform Agency that similar question was responded in 2021 during the review of the variation REC 10935, and the response is accepted by health authority. We are providing the same response below for Agency’s reference.

Response provided for question 1.5.3: Please be informed that it was decided not to amend this section which means that in the interpretation of the Scp factor, the wording “… on chromatograms of standard solutions R1 and R2…” remains unchanged. The reason is that this formulation reflects the analytical procedure of the test “assay” correctly.
Background
The Iloprost content is determined by means of HPLC by using one sample solution S and two reference solutions R1 and R2.
For the sample solution S, the drug product solution (Iloprost 10 µg/mL solution for inhalation) is used which contains both Iloprost isomers, E(4R)-Iloprost and E(4S)-Iloprost, in an unknown quantity. Therefore, the Iloprost content in the sample solution is unknown and is subject to the HPLC determination. In terms of Iloprost content determination, the sample solution is injected into the chromatographic system and chromatograms are obtained indicating peaks for both isomers, E(4R)-Iloprost and E(4S)-Iloprost. Consequently, the mean peak area of Е(4R)-Iloprost [S1] and the mean peak area of Е(4S)-iloprost [S2] is calculated.

The reference solutions R1 and R2 only contain the Iloprost isomer E(4S)-Iloprost in a concentration of approx. 0,005 mg/mL. For preparing reference solutions R1 and R2, an exactly weighted amount of E(4S)-Iloprost working standard [a0] is diluted in a defined solvent volume [V] which means that the content of E(4S)-Iloprost in both reference solutions R1 and R2 is known. The known content of E(4S)-Iloprost in the reference solutions is used to determine the unknown Iloprost content in the sample solution.
For this determination, the sample weight of E(4S)-Iloprost working standard [a0] in reference solution R1 is entered into the chromatographic software as well as the corresponding dilution volume. Separately, the same values are entered for reference solution R2 (no averaged sample weights are used) to allow the software the calculation of the E(4S)-Iloprost content in each reference solution. After injecting reference solution R1 and R2, two chromatograms are obtained with a specific peak area corresponding to the E(4S)-Iloprost content in each solution.

The values of the peak areas for reference solutions R1 and R2 are summed up and the mean peak area of Е(4S)-iloprost [Scp] is calculated. The mean peak area Scp is than used to calculate the assay according the formula:
Content of Iloprost (µg/mL) = (S1 + S2) x a0 x P x 1000 / (Scp x V) = (S1 + S2) x a0 x P x 10 / (Scp x V)

Response provided for question 1.10.6: Please be informed that it was decided not to amend this section which means that in the interpretation of the S1 factor, the wording “… on chromatograms of reference solutions R1 and R2…” remains unchanged. The reason is that this formulation reflects the analytical procedure of the method “related substances/degradation products of Iloprost (except Z-isomers)” correctly.

Background
The determination of related substances (degradation products of Iloprost) is performed by means of HPLC by using one sample solution S and four reference solutions R1, R2, R3 and R4.
For the sample solution S, the drug product solution (Iloprost 10 µg/mL solution for inhalation) is used which contains both Iloprost isomers as well as degradation products of Iloprost in an unknown quantity. Therefore, the content of degradation products of Iloprost in the sample solution is unknown and is subject to the HPLC determination. In terms of degradation product determination, the sample solution is injected into the chromatographic system and chromatograms are obtained indicating peaks for both Iloprost isomers as well as respective degradation products. Consequently, the mean peak area of each respective degradation product is calculated [S].

For reference solutions R1 and R2, the solutions as described in 1.5.3 are used and are diluted appropriately (please see above for a detailed explanation). For the determination of related substances, the sample weight of E(4S)-Iloprost working standard [a0] in reference solution R1 is entered into the chromatographic software as well as the corresponding dilution volume. Separately, the same values are entered for reference solution 2 (no averaged sample weights are used) to allow the software the calculation of the E(4S)-Iloprost content in each reference solution. After injecting reference solution R1 and R2, two chromatograms are obtained with a specific peak area corresponding to the E(4S)-Iloprost content in each solution.
The values of the peak areas for reference solutions R1 and R2 are summed up and the mean peak area of Е(4S)-Iloprost [S1] is calculated. The mean peak area S1 is than used to calculate the content of related substances/degradation products of Iloprost (except for Z-isomers and 15-oxo-iloprost) according the formula:
Related substances (%) = S x a0 x P / (S1 x L x V x 100)
and the content of 15-oxo-Iloprost according the formula:
15-oxo-iloprost (%) = S x a0 x P / (S1 x L x V x 100 x 1.95)

Source: P.5.2.01-06 Test Procedure / Iloprost solution 10 μg/mL 2 mL for inhalation (#020782666-06; changed)
keywords: HPLC-method; chromatograms; assay; releated substances; calculation formula

Question/Consideration: Please compare the drug substance manufacturing process at prechange and postchange sites. Please compare prechange/ postchange manufacturer equipment manufacturers, models, materials, principles, and critical technological parameters and specify fitness of prechange/postchange manufacturing equipment for the manufacturing process.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1 ( CTD section): S.2.2, S.2.4, S.2.5
Comparison of manufacturing process of dicyano cinnamic acid ester (step 1) and Ethyl-pyridinone (step 2) at the manufacturing sites Bayer AG, Wuppertal and Bayer AG, Bergkamen
Regarding the intermediates Dicyano cinnamic acid ester (step 1) and Ethyl-pyridinone (step 2), the manufacturing process for the manufacturing sites Bayer AG, Wuppertal and Bayer AG, Bergkamen is described in one technical document: please refer to S.2.2.02. Thus, the manufacturing process is performed identically at both manufacturing sites. It should be noted that the quantities are specified for a typical batch size and can be adapted to the size of the apparatus. In this case, the stoichiometric ratio of the reaction components remains constant and are always based on the process development studies.
As described in the technical document S.2.4.01, no critical process parameters have been identified regarding the manufacturing of the intermediates Dicyano cinnamic acid ester and Ethyl-pyridinone.
In addition, the results of three batches of the intermediate Ethyl-pyridinone produced at manufacturing site Bayer AG, Wuppertal have been compared to three batches produced at manufacturing site Bayer AG, Bergkamen. Please refer to the process evaluation document S.2.5.03. No differences have been found regarding batch results between the two manufacturing sites and – from a product quality point of view - Ethyl-pyridinone cannot be distinguished between the two manufacturing sites.
A detailed comparison of the equipment used for the manufacturing of the intermediate dicyano cinnamic acid ester and Ethyl-pyridinone at the two manufacturing sites Bayer AG, Wuppertal and Bayer AG, Bergkamen has been described in the technical document S.2.2.11.
The manufacturing process used at both manufacturing sites is identical and batch results obtained from the two manufacturing sites demonstrate that no difference in the quality profile could be observed. Therefore, the manufacturing process capability and the quality of the intermediates Dicyano cinnamic acid ester and Ethyl-pyridinone produced at both manufacturing sites is evaluated to be equivalent.

Question/Consideration: Providing information on genotoxic impurities that may be present in the finished product

Based on the investigated drug substance batches analysis data indicate that genotoxic impurities (i.e. 4-(4-Nitrophenyl)-3-morpholinone, 4-Anilinomorpholinone, Epoxyphthalimide and Hydroxyaminophthalimide) were not even found in traces.

Furthermore, the equipment used in the manufacturing and the excipients of the formulation do not introduce mutagenic impurities to the product. For above assessment, it can be concluded that there is no risk of potentially introducing mutagenicity by the potential impurities in the drug product.

Question/Consideration: It has been observed that the acceptance criterion for the enantiomeric purity parameter in the drug substance specifications has not been specified and should be added and in this regard; the current and proposed changes should be presented in the form of a comparative table with emphasis and the relevant studies showing the compliance in terms of quality and the relevant section(s) of the dossier (in CTD format) edited according to the change should be presented.
Answer/Response:
Bayer´s specification T.03.01 includes two test items which includes the following:
Test item: Identity (enantiomeric purity)

specification: must comply
Test item: Enantiomeric purity

specification: min. 99.0 % EE
Please note, that the test item “Identity (enantiomeric purity)” was added to the specification as according to Ph. Eur. Monograph of Rivaroxaban, enantiomeric purity is required as identity test. This evaluation is binary and expressed as “complies” or “not complies”. Nevertheless, this qualitative evaluation requires that the quantitative determination for enantiomeric purity was performed before. The acceptance criterion for the quantitative determination is described below.
The quantitative parameter “Enantiomeric purity” remains in the specification and is specified with “min. 99.0 % EE (enantiomeric excess)”. This limit is equivalent to the Ph. Eur. acceptance criterion for enantiomeric purity. The enantiomeric excess (EE) is the difference between the relative abundance of two enantiomers in a mixture of enantiomers. The Ph. Eur. limit of 0.5 % impurity A corresponds to a mixture of 0.5 % R-enantiomer (Impurity A) and 99.5 % S-enantiomer (rivaroxaban). The enantiomeric excess of this mixture is 99.5 % - 0.5 % = 99.0 %. Consequently, the acceptance criteria of 0.5 % impurity A and 99.0% EE are equivalent.
In summary, the submitted specification fully complies with the requirements of the Ph. Eur. monograph of Rivaroxaban and no proposed changes are ongoing with this regard.

Question/Consideration: Presentation of data on flow tests (Carr Index, Hausner ratio, etc.) performed on ready-to-fill granules in the pharmaceutical development department,
Answer/Response:
The development of the fluidized bed granulation process with subsequent bottle filling primarily focused on the particle size distribution (PSD) of the granulate. Bulk and tapped volume were measured only for a limited number of batches (see P.2.3.01 table 4). A calculation of flow indices (Carr Index, Hausner ratio) was not carried out. PSD was measured throughout the whole development phase and during validation. The decision to focus on the PSD instead of flow indices to characterize granule properties was based on the following scientific rationale.
The PSD is an important parameter influencing the physical properties of the granulate and its behavior during processing. A well-controlled PSD ensures good flowability and consistency in filling, which is essential for automated bottling processes. The granulation process was optimized to reduce fines to avoid particle size separation and consequently potential inhomogeneity in rivaroxaban and sodium benzoate content of filled bottles.
The bulk and tapped volumes are less relevant for a mass-controlled bottle filling process, since the filled quantity of each bottle is checked by a scale. While poor-flowing powders may affect processing efficiency, they do not significantly impact filling accuracy when the PSD is well managed. By focusing on particle size, a robust manufacturing process was developed that ensures high accuracy in bottle filling.

Question/Consideration: Addition of rheological studies with the suspended product to the pharmaceutical development section,
Answer/Response:
The provided documents on pharmaceutical development (P.2.2.01) and the development of the manufacturing process (P.2.3.01) include details on the rheological properties of the drug product. The extent of viscosity is caused by the thickeners microcrystalline cellulose and carmellose sodium and xanthan gum. The amount of these excipients has been optimized to ensure short suspending and re-suspending time on the one hand and to minimize sedimentation of the suspension during the in-use phase on the other hand. Related investigations including homogeneity of suspension have been reported in P.2.2.01.
Viscosity of the reconstituted drug product is relatively low, and comparable to edible oil of low viscosity, such as olive oil with a viscosity of about 40 mPas at 40°C (Shreya N. Sahasrabudhe et al.). Measurements of a variety of batches of the reconstituted drug product (see P.2.2.01 chapter 2.3.2 Robustness Test) gave a value of 32 mPas for a lab batch with only 90% of thickener (batch 10G-180802-202) and a value of 41 mPas for a lab batch with 110% of thickener (batch 10G-180801-201). Within a systematic investigation (design of experiment) at lab scale on granulation conditions the influence of the various granulation parameters on the quality attributes (responses) of the formulation was investigated. The viscosity of in total 20 batches measured, was in the range of 44 mPas to 50 mPas (see P.2.3.01 chapter 1.4).
Batches with intended composition in final scale had viscosities between 36 and 46 mPas at room temperature. Based on the presented data, the rheological properties are considered to be sufficiently characterized.

Question/Consideration: Addition of the parameter “viscosity of suspension” to the finished product specifications and submission of the relevant studies and the relevant section(s) of the dossier (in CTD format), showing the current and proposed changes in a comparative table with emphasis on the quality compliance,
Answer/Response:
The applicant proposes to omit viscosity testing based on the following rationale.
Viscosity has been measured for almost all developmental and clinical batches of the reconstituted drug product. According to ICH Q6A, for relatively low viscous solutions or suspensions, it is not required to include rheological properties (viscosity/specific gravity) in the specification. Viscosity of the reconstituted drug product is relatively low, and comparable to edible oil of low viscosity, such as olive oil with a viscosity of about 40 mPas at 40°C (Shreya N. Sahasrabudhe et al., INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF FOOD PROPERTIES, 2017, VOL. 20, NO. S2, S1965–S1981).
Measurement of a variety of batches of the reconstituted drug product gave a value of 32 mPas with for a lab batch with only 90% of thickener (batch 10G-180802-202) and a value of 41 mPas for a lab batch with 110% of thickener (batch 10G-180801-201). Batches with intended composition in final scale had viscosities between 36 and 46 mPas at room temperature.
The extent of viscosity is caused by the thickeners microcrystalline cellulose and carmellose sodium and xanthan gum. The amount of these excipients has been optimized to ensure short suspending and re-suspending time on the one hand and to minimize sedimentation of the suspension during the in-use phase on the other hand. Related investigations including homogeneity of suspension have been reported in P.2.2.01.
Moreover, viscosity is sufficiently low to ensure administration with the liquid dosing device and easy application via a nasogastric tube.
In addition to the constant composition of the product, the quality of the relevant excipients microcrystalline cellulose and carmellose sodium and xanthan gum are confirmed by testing according to pharmacopoeia monographs. This ensures that the viscosity will constantly be suitable for the intended use.
The quality of the reconstituted drug product with respect to viscosity is thus sufficiently controlled, measurement of each batch can be omitted.

Question/Consideration: You need to provide us with explanation of the limits set for the parameter uniformity of content in the specification of the finished product that does not comply with Ph. Eur. In the monograph Ph. Eur. 2.9.40. it was prescribed the method of expression for the uniformity of the dosage units trough the uniformity of the content beyond the maximum permissible acceptable values (L1=15 and L2=25, respectively).
Answer/Response:
The current Uniformity of content test of Mirena is in accordance with the Ph. Eur. general chapter 2.9.6 Uniformity of content. European Directorate for the Quality of Medicines (EDQM) states in it’s answers to Frequently Asked Questions, concerning the implementation of the general chapter 2.9.40 Uniformity of dosage units, the following:

“From a pharmaceutical quality point of view, the approach taken in the harmonized general chapter on uniformity of dosage units (2.9.40) is considered equivalent to the requirements in general chapters 2.9.5 and 2.9.6. Thus, the decision on which approach to take is left to the user. Either 2.9.40 or 2.9.5 and 2.9.6 may be applied to demonstrate compliance with the Ph. Eur. with regard to the uniformity of dosage units.”
(https://faq.edqm.eu/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=1376931)

Uniformity of content / Uniformity of dosage units -test of Mirena will be updated in an analytical variation to be submitted to the competent Health Authority in near future. This new test will be in accordance with the principles of the new Ph. Eur. 2.9.40 general chapter, though the requirements to be applied for Mirena will be slightly tighter.

Question/Consideration:
Question 2
Please explain why the potential hazards for “Sterilization temperature” and “Sterilization time” were set 
to “5” while the potential hazard for “Continuous sterilization of temperature ≧121°C” was not set to 
“5.” In the above explanation, please includes an explanation on differences in the meanings of 
“Sterilization temperature” and “Sterilization time” between “Continuous sterilization of temperature 
≧121℃” in your explanation.
Answer/Response:
Company response to Question 2
The sterilization cycle of a radiopharmaceutical drug is determined by temperature and time, not by F0.
The terminal sterilization process of Radium-223 chloride solution for injection was validated for 
maximum and minimum autoclave loads with product vials by three consecutive sterilization runs per 
load pattern, with temperature monitors and biological indicators.
The main acceptance criteria for the sterilization validation were:
 
All temperature monitors (data loggers) in product vials must meet a minimum of 121 °C for a 
minimum of 15 minutes according to Ph. Eur. / USP. 
 
All Biological Indicators (BI’s) must meet the requirements specified in Ph. Eur.: No BI’s (BI) 
with > 5x105 spores of type Geobacillus stearothermophilus should show growth after incubation. 
D121 value must be > 1.5 minutes. 
 
The Sterility Assurance Level (SAL) should meet the pharmacopoeia requirement of 10-6 or 
better.
Since “sterilization temperature” and “sterilization time” are both critical to ensure SAL of 10-6 or better, 
their potential hazards were set to 5.
At Cardinal Health the autoclave cycle of 20 minutes was validated, whereas at Agilera Pharma a 22 
minute autoclave cycle was validated, as the biological indicator supplier required a 22-minute kill cycle.
For routine commercial production the sterilization phase of 25 minutes is used and has been validated at 
both sites. Because the sterilization phase used during routine production is longer than the initial 
validation, the Key parameter “Continuous sterilization temperature ≥ 121 °C” with the acceptance 
criterion “test is “pass” (the sterilization phase must be within qualified conditions)” was added. As 
always, the autoclave documentation will be assessed for each autoclave cycle, should a minor dip in 
temperature below 121 °C occur at the beginning or very late during the sterilization phase, this event will 
not lead to an immediate batch rejection, but the investigations may justify release of the batch. 
Therefore, the hazard for this criteria was set to 4.

Question/Consideration:
Question 6
For the Water Content test you must declare a minimum range to be met, which the 
laboratory established to perform this test. Remember that this is a test established in the 
current regulation RTCA 11.03.04:10 Pharmaceutical Products. Studies of Stability of 
Medicines for Human Use, section 5.3.1.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 6: 
 
Control of water content is necessary during manufacture, especially for the quality of the 
tableting process. Therefore, the humidity of the granulate is monitored by in-process 
control tests (IPC), which usually check the loss on drying instead of the water content. 
The procedure of the IPC test and the limits are specified in the manufacturing instruction 
to ensure the quality of the dosage form (see P.3.3.02). The resulting quality of the tablets 
is confirmed by the process validation and no further testing/specification of the water 
content is required to ensure the quality of the drug product. Consequently, a specification 
of this parameter would be exclusively informative. 
 
High barrier foil blisters (HBF) have a barrier for water vapor, but it is limited. Since the 
sugar-coated tablet formulation is not hygroscopic, this leads to an equilibrium of the water 
content during storage, depending on the ambient humidity. 
However, any critical intake of water during storage would affect at least one of the key 
quality parameters: appearance, assay, dissolution or degradation products. Since these 
parameters do not reflect a critical quality either at the release of the drug or during the 
reported period of the stability study, a possibly minor change in the water content of the 
Diane35 tablets packaged in HBF blisters must be assessed as non-critical. 
 
The analysis of the water content is therefore not carried out for quality-related reasons, 
but for formal reasons to meet the requirements of the ASEAN Guideline. For this reason, 
unlike during production, there is no acceptance criterion. The data is reported for 
information purposes only.
keywords: in-process control; stability study and pharmaceutical form; Shelf Life ＆ Storage Condition; Container closure system; Stability data

Question/Consideration:
You answered that the significance of " Continuous sterilization of temperature≧121 °C" was 
set to "4", because the duration of the routine sterilization process is longer than the initial 
validation. Considering that the severity of the sterilization itself is not altered even if the 
sterilization time is set longer (it should be considered that it is the occurrence of deviation 
that decreases due to the long sterilization time). Therefore, please give a score of “5” to the 
severity of the "Continuous sterilization of temperature≧121 °C" and define it as a critical 
parameter, and then modify CTD2.3.P accordingly.
Answer/Response:
As explained in the previous response to Question 2 of the second deficiency letter issued on 
October 4, 2024, the severity score in the FMEA was evaluated based on the following 
criteria for each parameter, rather than an assessment of the sterilization process itself.

A score of 5 corresponds to parameters that 'directly affect product quality, cannot be 
corrected. This results in an immediate batch rejection which cannot be overturned.

In contrast, a score of 4 corresponds to parameters that directly affect product quality but can 
be corrected, or product quality may be affected to an extent that does not allow batch release. 
The decision to whether the product can be released or not will be based on a thorough risk 
assessment, and based on the conclusion a release/rejection decision will be made.

The parameter “Continuous sterilization of temperature ≧121 °C” is a parameter in addition 
to the critical parameters with severity score 5, namely “Sterilization temperature ≥121 °C” 
and “Sterilization time ≥15 minutes”. It is intended to assess the impact of any small dips in 
the temperature curve during the first or last few minutes of the 25-minute sterilization cycle 
defined for routine commercial production, which is requalified annually.

Moreover, based on the results of deviation investigations, lots may be released if the holding 
time above 121 °C meets the established acceptance criteria (Cardinal Health: 20 minutes or 
more, Agilera: 22 minutes or more). As an example, the manufacturing record of the 
sterilization process for lot CH10224 released by Cardinal Health is attached. Although a 
temperature alarm occurred 2 minutes after the sterilization plateau was reached, the lot was 
released because the continuous temperature ≥121 °C was maintained for more than 20 
minutes.

Based on the above, it is reasonable to assign a severity score of 4 to “Continuous sterilization 
of temperature ≧121 °C” with the acceptance criteria “The sterilization phase must be within 
qualified conditions”.

The removal of DS test parameters originate from a variation application, through a thorough justification and risk assessment based on statistical calculations the omission of DS test parameters were deemed acceptable, including osmolality and citrate testing. The variation in analytical results of parameters (osmolality and citrate) in radium-223 chloride drug substance and drug product has been evaluated statistically to consider the proposed deletion of osmolality and citrate from for the drug substance specification.
Batches originating from manufacturing of recent consecutive batches have been measured and described by common statistical methods to investigate the batch-to-batch variation during a significantly long period of time. The Z score probability is p ≤ 0.0012 for drug substance and far below p = 0.0010 for drug product. Citrate in CAH drug substance has slightly above the probability level with p=0.0012, whereas the probability level for Agilera was p=0.0003. The variation in citrate CAH drug substance had a low influence on the corresponding citrate CAH drug product having p ≤ 0.000003. It represented the general observation that the influence of variation in DS parameters in the manufacturing process on the risk of DP parameters to exceed specifications, were minimal. The statistical analysis supports the deletion of osmolality from the drug substance specification
The consistent analytical results within specification (p ≤ 0.000003) at Agilera and CAH for as many as 359 drug product batches, in addition to the restriction in holding time for batches with high radioactive concentration, indicated that it should result in a low risk to exclude citrate from the drug substance specification.

Question/Consideration:
Question 3
LABELING:
corrected secondary labeling containing the storage condition of the product (indicates without restriction).
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 3:
The stability of Xofigo (radium-223 chloride solution for injection) is well documented with data for the whole shelf-life (28 days) tested according to ICH guidelines at real time (25°C/60%RH), accelerated (40°C/75%RH), thermal stress (60°C/ambient) conditions, and three freeze/thaw cycles over 3 days at -20°C/ambient.
The active component radium-223 is present as free 223Ra2+ ions in the drug product formulation, and cannot degrade, but decays according to a given decay scheme that is not affected by physical and chemical environment. Thus, the stability of Xofigo, in terms of deterioration of the product relates to the stability of the vehicle (sodium citrate solution 28 mmol/L in sodium chloride 0.11M). The stability indicating parameters for Xofigo (radium-223 chloride solution for injection) are defined as appearance, particulate matter, pH, osmolality, citrate, assay, bacterial endotoxins and sterility.
The stability indicating parameters tested were all well within the specification limits. The only change seen during shelf-life is a slight pH increase and a slight decrease in citrate concentration, which in both cases is attributed to radiolysis of water. Both parameters remain, however, well within specification limits for 28 days storage for all conditions tested, including 60°C for 28 days.
The results demonstrate that the drug product remains stable under long-term- accelerated and thermal stress conditions for the whole shelf life of 28 days, and after three freeze/thaw cycles. the drug product is therefore evaluated to be stable in all climatic zones (1, II, III, and IV) with no need for storage precautions.

Question/Consideration:
Please to provide detail explanations about background of the changes of:
Sum of all impurities: Deletion of specification parameter from release specification
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1 ( 3.2.P.5.6):
The synthesis impurities that are not potential degradation products are controlled in LNG 
release testing and are therefore omitted from the drug product specifications. The potential 
known and unidentified LNG degradation products above ≥ 0.1% reporting threshold are 
included in the proposed Shelf-life test and in the corresponding stability study test results.
Levonorgestrel is inherently stable. The long history of Mirena IUS has verified that LNG 
remains virtually unchanged in the product manufacture, and during the shelf-life. This is 
demonstrated by comparing results of five MIRENA IUS drug product stability batches with 
the results for corresponding drug substance batches (Table 2–4 in P.5.6.01). The results for 
drug substance batches in accordance with the Ph. Eur. method indicate for Mirena IUS actual 
low amount of the potential degradation products, from which the synthesis related impurities 
are omitted. Even at the end of Shelf-life the level of degradation products is negligible. This 
outstanding stability of LNG justifies the non-inclusion of the impurity test into the release 
specification.

Source:  P.5.6.01-02 Justification of Specification / Levonorgestrel intrauterine delivery
system 52 mg with inserter(MIRENA) (#008081237;  unchanged)
keywords: impurities; justification of specification; Release Specification; Shelf Life; stability data

Question/Consideration:
Please to provide detail explanations about background of the changes of:
Ethylene oxide: Deletion of specification parameter from shelf life specification
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 2 ( 3.2.P.5.1):
Only parameters which have relevance with regard to product quality during the Shelf-life, 
and therefore tested in stability studies, are included in the shelf life specification.
According to ICH Topic Q 1 A (R2) Stability Testing of new Drug Substances and Products 
parameters of the drug product that are susceptible to change during storage and are likely to 
influence quality, safety, and/or efficacy should be included in stability studies.
Ethylene oxide (EO) which is used as a sterilization agent for sterilization of the product is 
removed from Mirena IUS during the process, and therefore it does not exist anymore in the 
finished IUS product. It will suffice to determine the EO residues at release only, as they can’t 
increase during storage, and therefore are not tested during the Shelf-life.

Source:  P.5.1.01.-07 Release Specification / Levonorgestrel intrauterine delivery
system 52 mg with inserter(MIRENA) (#022984913;  unchanged)
P.5.1.02_07 Shelf-Life Specification / Levonorgestrel intrauterine delivery 
system 52 mg with inserter(MIRENA) (#022984914;  unchanged)
keywords: ETO sterilization; Shelf Life ＆ Storage Condition; Release Specification; Stability data; Sterilization

Question/Consideration:
Question 1
(With regard to Inquiry 2 (1) (3) dated July 8, 2024) If the endotoxin test is established, it is 
necessary to provide not only the results of the studies on the gel-clot technique, but also the 
results of the test for interfering factors, measurements and results of preparatory testing (test 
for assurance of criteria for the standard curve) for the turbidimetric technique and 
chromogenic technique. Provide these results.
Answer/Response:
The response to the Inquiry 2 (4) dated July 8, 2024 mentions that the specification for 
endotoxin was established as “< 3.5 EU/mL” in accordance with the calculation in JP <G4-5-
131> with 70 kg as the alternative average body mass of an adult. However, the specification 
was reconsidered from the perspective of consistency with JP <G4-5-131> mentioning 60 kg 
as the average body mass. The endotoxin limit was decided to change to “< 3.0 EU/mL” in 
accordance with the following calculation.
Endotoxin limit = K/M = 5.0EU/kg/(100mL/60kg) = 3.0 EU/mL

The Maximum Valid Dilution (MVD) is determined to be “10” when the endotoxin limit is 
set as 3.0 EU/mL in accordance with the calculation below.
Maximum Valid Dilution = (endotoxin limit × concentration of test solution) / λ   
= (3.0 EU/mL × 0.1 mg/mL) / 0.03 EU/mL  
= 10

As shown in Table 2 (data on dilution factor extracted from P.5.3.07_022976737_02) in the 
response to Inquiry 2 (1) dated, dilution 1:4, 1:8 and 1:11 were tested. The results indicate 
that the dilution 1:11 only was qualified and dilutions 1:4 and 1:8 were not. Gel-clot testing 
would not be qualified or show low precision if MVD 10 established by the new endotoxin 
limit were applied. Therefore, the development of test methods other than Gel-clot method 
was considered. Testing by chromogenic method has not been tried because no analytical 
instrument for the method is available. Turbidimetric kinetic method has been developed in 
accordance with Ph. Eur. 2.6.14 (BACTERIAL ENDOTIXINS) harmonized with USP <85> 
and JP <4.01>.

The triplicate determinations of endotoxin test generated from 3 lot of Biliscopin DIC 50 
(MA04M4S, MA04JLB and MA03S80) by turbidimetric kinetic method are shown in Table 1 
below along with the results of assurance of criteria for the standard curve and test for 
interfering factors.

1) Assurance of criteria for the standard curve
The standard curve was evaluated by standard endotoxin solution with 5 concentrations from 
16 λ to λ (0.005 EU/mL). The absolute value of the correlation coefficient of the standard 
curve (R-value) generated using the five standard solutions was found to be greater than or 
equal to 0.98. Based on the results, the test is considered valid.

2) Maximum Valid Dilution (MVD)
MVD was estimated to be 60.00 in accordance with the equation below. A dilution of 1:30 
which is not exceed 1:60 as MVD was applied to turbidimetric kinetic method.
Maximum Valid Dilution = (endotoxin limit × concentration of test solution) / λ
endotoxin limit：3.0 EU/mL
concentration of test solution: 0.1 mg/mL
λ：0.005 EU/mL

3) Test for interfering factors
For 3 lots of Biliscopin DIC 50 (MA04M4S, MA04JLB and MA03S80), test for interfering 
factor was performed by using the solutions prepared in accordance with Table 2.6.14.-4 in 
Pr. Eur. 2.6.14 (corresponds to Table 4.01-4 in JP <4.01>). Note that 4λ solution (0.125 
EU/mL) was used as solution B (the middle of the standard curve). The results indicated that 
the test was valid because the results met the following conditions specified in Ph. Eur. 
2.6.14.
– the absolute value of the correlation coefficient of the standard curve is greater than or equal 
to 0.980.
– the result with solution D does not exceed the limit of the blank value required in the 
description of the lysate reagent employed, or it is less than the endotoxin detection limit 
(0.005 EU/mL) of the lysate reagent employed.
Also, the test solution was decided to be free of interfering factors because the recovery was 
found to be within 50-200% specified in Ph. Eur. 2.6.14.

4) Results on endotoxin testing
As shown in Table 1 above, the results obtained from the triplicate determinations of 3 lots of 
Biliscopin DCI 50 indicated that all results are found to be “< 0.1500 EU/mL” and met the 
specification of “< 3.0 EU/mL”. Based on the results, specification for endotoxin is to be 
changed from “< 3.5 EU/mL (Gel-clot method)” to “3.0 EU/mL (Turbidimetric method, Ph. 
Eur.)”.

Question/Consideration:
Question 3
The adequacy of the control of PEG-Mal to ensure the consistency of the finished product
must be demonstrated.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 3 ( Module 3: S.4.1 and S.4.2 ):
Polyethylene Glycol Maleimide (PEG-MAL) is a protein pegylation polymer used in the
rFVIII-N drug substance (DS) manufacturing process. The supplier of the PEG-MAL raw
material is the Nippon Oil and Fat Company (NOF). PEG-MAL is considered a critical raw
material and subject to release criteria at both NOF and Bayer Berkeley. PEG-Mal
manufacturing process has been validated at NOF with 3 lots, with each lot meeting all
acceptance and release criteria. Each lot of PEG-MAL manufactured at NOF undergoes
testing for identity by FTIR, trace metals, bioburden, with terminal activity, polydispersity,
high and low molecular weight % (MW) as critical quality attributes (CQA). Additional
internal testing for identity, trace metals and bioburden is performed at Bayer Berkeley with
release specifications. To ensure expiry is appropriately assigned to the PEG-MAL raw
material, stability of PEG-Mal is monitored through accelerated and real time stability studies.
Further, PEG-Mal raw material is qualified to be used in the rFVIII-N Drug Substance
commercial manufacturing process.

The PEGylation process covalently attaches a polyethylene glycol (PEG) polymer chain to the
B-deleted domain of rFVIII (BDD-rFVIII). The purity of the PEGylated product is tested and
controlled through Reverse Phase HPLC analytical method, ensuring the quality and
consistency of the final product. This method utilizes Reverse Phase-High Performance
Liquid Chromatography (RP-HPLC) to separate protein and PEGylated protein molecules on
a non-porous polymeric column. The percent peak area of PEGylated Light Chain (LC) and
Heavy Chain (HC) proteins is measured to determine rFVIII-N purity (% PEG-rFVIII-BDD).
The RP-HPLC analytical method testing and control strategy, monitors PEGylation
efficiency, detects process-related impurities, and verifies consistency of the final product,
guaranteeing the purity and quality of the PEGylated product (S.4.2.81).
To ensure the consistency of the finished product, the adequacy of unreacted PEG-Mal
control is demonstrated through its effective removal during the manufacturing process.
Specifically, unreacted PEG-malemide reagent is removed by the SP Sepharose HP column
during load flow-through and wash steps, with minimal non-specific binding. Subsequent
testing of the Drug Substance using Reverse Phase Chromatography (S.4.2.81) confirms that
PEG-Mal levels are below the specification limit of 10 ppm (S.4.1.01), thereby ensuring the
quality and purity of the final product through rigorous quality control measures in the QC
Chemistry Lab.
Source: S.4.2.81-01 / Damoctocog alfa pegol Method for Reverse Phase
Chromatography (2.5μm) (#DocID 012707203; unchanged)
S.4.1.01-05 Specification / Damoctocog alfa pegol solution (#DocID
016520694; unchanged)
keywords: Control of Materials; analytical procedures; HPLC-method; specification; Stability data

a) Merging different formulated drug substance (FDS) lots during the drug product (DP) manufacturing is an option permitted for maximizing usage of the FDS material and to avoid waste. Every lot of FDS is individually tested and needs to comply individually to the FDS specifications panel before being released for further processing. The pooling and merging of FDS at the DP manufacturing site will apply the validated process parameter ranges (thaw time, mixing speed and mixing duration) regardless of the FDS batch source to ensure homogeneity of the solutions as instructed by the Manufacturing Records. The starting volumes for production will remain within the validated ranges guaranteeing the uniformity of the FDS starting material for the DP process as it was demonstrated by the process performance qualification at Catalent. An additional document is provided to support the uniformity during DP processing (CTD section P.3.5.01-01). That means, the merging of different FDS batches does not change the validated batch size range and the range for which pooling has been demonstrated to be validated. In addition, no change on validated ranges for process parameters like holding times, filter contact time or Time Out of Refrigeration is foreseen due to merging of FDS batches. As such, the applicant considers the existing collective validation data sufficient since the validated process parameters are not changed due to the merging of the different FDS lots during the DP manufacturing process.

Question/Consideration: Please explain whether there are any differences between Aflibercept intravitreal injection solution 114.3 mg/ml FDS, DP JS specification and the approved 40 mg/ml JS specification. If there are differences, please explain the reasons.
Answer/Response:
The approved aflibercept drug substance intermediate (DSI) is the identical precursor material for production of either Aflibercept solution 40 mg/mL or Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL products. The subsequent Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL manufacturing process (manufacture of formulated drug substance (FDS) and drug product (DP)) is different from the Aflibercept solution 40 mg/mL process, and as such, Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL is being developed as a new product. In order to support the higher protein concentration, an alternative formulation of buffers, pH, and stabilizing agents has been developed for Aflibercept solution 114.3. mg/mL compared to 40 mg/mL. As a result, Eylea 40 mg/mL and 114.3 mg/mL differ in certain quality characteristics due to the different concentrations and compositions. Moreover, the new Aflibercept solution 114.3. mg/mL formulation was studied in a thorough analytical, stability, preclinical, and clinical program. Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL was subjected to in-depth characterization of biochemical, biophysical, and structural attributes. New FDS and DP specifications, stability studies, and associated acceptance criteria have been implemented for Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL based on formulation and process development studies and are appropriately justified (S.4.5.01-03 and P.5.6.01-03). A summary of notable differences between Aflibercept solution 40 mg/mL and 114.3 mg/mL is provided in Table 2.

A direct comparison of the specifications including the evaluation of differences is provided in the following Table 3 and Table 4.

Question/Consideration: Please provide historical release testing data for FDS and DP of multiple batches of 114.3 mg/ml Eylea and compare it with the release testing data of approved 40 mg/ml strength. Conduct statistical analysis to confirm that the quality of the 114.3 mg/ml is not inferior to that of the approved 40 mg/ml.
Answer/Response:
Eylea 114.3 mg/mL is considered a new product and has not only a different concentration than Eylea 40 mg/mL, but also a different formulation including different excipients (CTD section P.1.01-01) to stabilize the higher protein concentration as well as different manufacturing processes and DP sites. The drug substance intermediate is the same for both. While this submission falls under the scope of a variation to the original Eylea 40 mg/mL registration and not of a New Drug Application, the submission package for this new strength consists of non-clinical and clinical data in addition to the quality documentation. The holistic clinical data demonstrated that Eylea 114.3 mg/mL, with its individual quality characteristics compared to Eylea 40 mg/mL, is efficacious and safe to use. The specifications for Eylea 114.3 mg/mL are justified for this product as described in the response to Question 9 and CTD sections S.4.5.01-03 and P.5.6.01-03.
Therefore, considering the quality characteristics and the clinical development, a direct statistical comparison of analytical data from both products is not considered meaningful.
Both, 8mg FDS and 2mg Formulated Bulk (FB), are the final formulated solutions for Eylea 114.3 mg/mL and Eylea 40 mg/mL DP, respectively. Those solutions only undergo fill and finish operations at the DP sites and there are no changes in the composition.
Despite the aforementioned limitations to a direct comparison of both products, the applicant nevertheless conducted a statistical evaluation of historical DP release data from Eylea 114.3 mg/ml and Eylea 40 mg/mL, which is provided in Table 5, as the DP is the most representative product stage as it is used for the administration to patients. All vial batches of both strengths that were released after 09/2019 were included in the comparison. Due to the large number of more than 250 batches tested per item, the individual results per batch are not included in the table. However, number (N), mean and standard deviation (SD) per test item are provided as an overview of the entire dataset. Note that the different numbers (N) for the individual Eylea 40 mg/mL attributes is due to changes in test methods throughout the Eylea 40 mg/mL lifecycle management after marketing approval as well as data availability at the time of the evaluation provided below.

Question/Consideration:
Question 1
Calculation method for the composition ingredients mentioned within the CPID and comparing 
it with the approved Composition
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1:
The API of Magnevist is Gadopentetate, dimeglumine also known as Gadopentetic acid, 
dimeglumine salt. The amount of the mentioned API is 469.01 mg per 1 mL of solution (see 
point 1 for this calculation). This amount corresponds to 78.63 mg of Gadolinium (see point 
2 for this calculation).
Additionally, for your reference, please find enclosed a statement confirming that there is no 
change in the composition of Magnevist.

Point 1:
The concentration of the product is 0.5 mol/L (0.5x10-3 mol/mL), therefore each mL of solution 
contains 0.5x10-3 mol of API.
To obtain this amount in mg we need to multiply this concentration by the relative molecular 
mass of the API (938.01 g/mol = 938.01x103 mg/mol)

[0.5x10-3 mol] x [938.01x103 mg/mol] = 469.005 (469.01) mg

Point 2:
To calculate the amount of Gd contained in the 469.01 mg of API, we need to consider the 
molar mass of the Gd (157.25 g/mol = 157.25x103 mg/mol) and follow this formula:
𝐴𝑚𝑜𝑢𝑛𝑡 𝑜𝑓 𝐴𝑃𝐼 (𝑚𝑔) 𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑡𝑎𝑖𝑛𝑒𝑑 𝑖𝑛 1 𝑚𝐿 𝑜𝑓 𝑠𝑜𝑙𝑢𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑥 𝑀𝑜𝑙𝑎𝑟 𝑀𝑎𝑠𝑠 𝑜𝑓 𝐺𝑑( 𝑔
𝑚𝑜𝑙𝑜𝑟𝑚𝑔
𝑚𝑜𝑙)
𝑅𝑒𝑙𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑣𝑒 𝑚𝑜𝑙𝑒𝑐𝑢𝑙𝑎𝑟 𝑚𝑎𝑠𝑠 𝑜𝑓 𝐴𝑃𝐼 ( 𝑔
𝑚𝑜𝑙𝑜𝑟𝑚𝑔
𝑚𝑜𝑙)

Therefore:
469.01 𝑚𝑔 𝑥 157,250 𝑚𝑔/𝑚𝑜𝑙
938,010 𝑚𝑔/𝑚𝑜𝑙
 = 78.625 (78.63) mg

Notes:
• Molecular formula of API: C28H54GdN5O20
• Relative molecular mass of API: 938.01 g/mol (938,010 mg/mol = 938.01x103 
mg/mol )
• Molar mass (Gd):  157.25 g/mol (157,250 mg/mol = 157.25x103 mg/mol)

Question/Consideration:
Question 4
In in process validation report:
- Conclude about the maximum acceptable filling time.
- Conclude about the product holding time after filling and before terminal sterilization.
- Identify the temperature range of product terminal sterilization in the autoclave (>121ºC), with submitting the process validation for product terminal sterilization in the autoclave.
- Justify the >100% filling yield for BN#51001.
- Clarify the root cause and the preventive action for OOS related to extractable volume in BN#51002 and OOS related to stopper insertion in BN#51001.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 4 (P.3.5):
Please see the corresponding responses below:
1) Conclude about the maximum acceptable filling time.
Holding time of the bulk solution is defined from start of the filtration of the bulk into the 
holding tank until terminal sterilization of the last pre-filled plastic syringe. The maximum 
allowable holding time of Primovist bulk solution is 168 hours (7 days). All filling activities of 
pre-filled plastic syringes are performed within the holding time of the bulk solution. Adherence 
to the maximum allowable holding time is checked the batch record review process.
2) Conclude about the product holding time after filling and before terminal sterilization.
The maximum product holding time after filling and before sterilization is 24 hours. Adherence 
to the maximum allowable holding time is checked the batch record review process.
3) Identify the temperature range of product terminal sterilization in the autoclave (>121ºC),
with submitting the process validation for product terminal sterilization in the autoclave.
During the 20 minutes sterilization phase the acceptable temperature range in the autoclave is 
122 – 124 °C. If the temperature deviates below the lower threshold the timer is automatically 
stopped and only continues once the temperature re-enters the acceptable temperature range. If 
the temperature exceeds the upper threshold the sterilization process is automatically aborted. 
All temperature excursions automatically generate an alarm and are reported in the sterilization 
protocol. Every sterilization protocol is checked by the operators and during the batch record 
review process
4) Justify the >100% filling yield for BN#51001.
As described in the P.3.5.01 section, the slight overfill complied with the yield calculation 
procedure as described in the local SOP. The exceedance had no quality impact and therefore 
no deviation was initiated.
5) Clarify the root cause and the preventive action for OOS related to extractable volume in
BN#51002 and OOS related to stopper insertion in BN#51001.
Due to the OOS result of the parameter extractable volume of Primovist PFSP 5/10 mL batch 
#51002 a deviation was initiated, a comprehensive root cause analysis and an appropriate 
CAPA were performed. The root cause was insufficient process knowledge in conjunction with 
non-representative sample handling: Technical interventions during the filling of the batch and 
the subsequent downtimes generated air bubbles in the filling tubes. These air bubbles were not 
removed before filling activities were resumed and thus caused underfilling in the syringes. 
Syringes intended for commercial use are subjected to 100% visual inspection. During the 
visual inspection process underfilled syringes are reliably detected and rejected. As part of the 
process validation 18 additional pre-filled plastic syringe samples for extractable volume were 
taken during the filling process (6 each from the start, middle and end of the batch). These 
additional samples were not subjected to 100% visual inspection before the performance of test 
of “extractable volume” by QC. Two of the six samples from the middle of the batch showed 
OOS results for extractable volume.
To verify that OOS results were a singular event and not indicative of a systematic error of the 
manufacturing process, the extractable volume of 30 additional 100% visually inspected 
syringes from the middle of the batch was tested. All results for extractable volume of the 
additional test samples and results during release testing complied with the specification. A 
systematic error during filling was ruled out.  The deviation was therefore finally classified as 
minor. As a preventive action the operators of the filling line were trained and instructed on 
how to properly vent the filling tubes. As the samples where only taken as additional samples 
as part of the process validation and are not part of the routine commercial manufacturing 
process no further CAPAs with regards to the sampling process were necessary.

Due to the OOS result of the parameter stopper insertion depth of Primovist PFSP 5/10 mL 
batch #51001 a deviation was initiated and a comprehensive root cause analysis was performed. 
As part of the process validation 90 additional pre-filled plastic syringe samples for stopper 
insertion depth were taken (30 each from the start, middle and end of the batch). The stopper 
of one syringe from the start of the batch was slightly slanted. This resulted in different 
measurement values during testing of the stopper setting depth of this sample. The worst case 
value was reported (acceptable range: 36.5 – 38.5 mm; reported value: 38.60 mm). The results 
of all other samples were within the specified range.
To verify that the OOS result was a singular event and not indicative of a systematic error of 
the manufacturing process, the stopper insertion depth of 10 additional samples taken from the 
start of the batch was tested. All obtained values were within the specified range (acceptable 
range: 36.5 – 38.5 mm; reported values minimum: 36.83 mm; maximum: 37.32 mm). A 
systematic error was ruled out. A specific root cause could not be found. Hence, no preventive 
measure could be defined. The deviation was therefore finally classified as minor.

Source:  P.3.5.01-01  Process Validation and/or Evaluation/ Sodium gadoxetate
solution 0.25 mol/L in prefilled plastic syringe for parenteral use 
(PRIMOVIST) (#009930664;/unchanged)
keywords: Process Validation and/or Evaluation; holding time; in-process control; Batch Report; Sterilization

Question/Consideration: In the Certificate of Analysis (CoA), the specification limit for unidentified/individual product decomposition and sum of product decomposition are given as max 0.10 % and 3.0% respectively. Does this test belong to the TLC method or HPLC? Please kindly specify the formula/calculation for this test.
Answer/Response:
We acknowledge Agency’s comment.
Please find below the details regarding Calculation of decomposition products
The sum of decomposition products is calculated by adding all individual decomposition products. The result of decomposition product B is gained by HPLC analysis (as part of the assay test) and the decomposition products C, D, E, F and G are gained by TLC analysis. Additionally, it is searched for unidentified decomposition products.
The limit of quantification for TLC analysis is 0.05 %, however these results are rounded up to 0.1 % for the CoA.
The formula for calculation is as follows:
Dec. prod. B (by HPLC) ≤ 1.5 % + Dec. prod. C (by TLC) ≤ 0.5 % + Dec. prod. D (by TLC) ≤ 1.0 % + Dec. prod. E (by TLC) ≤ 0.5 % + Dec. prod. F (by TLC) ≤ 0.2 % + Dec. prod. G (by TLC) ≤ 0.1 % + Unidentified, individual dec. prod. (by TLC) ≤ 0.10 % = Sum of dec. prod. ≤ 3.0 %
keywords: CoAs; related substances; LoQ; HPLC-method; calculation formula

Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1:
a) To present the extractable volume results numerically rather than simply stating 
"Complies." This request also applies to the batch analysis.
We acknowledge your query regarding the presentation of extractable volume results in 
stability data and batch analysis, and we would like to provide the following clarification:
The extractable volume results in the submitted stability data and batch analysis were stated 
as "Complies" in accordance with our acceptance criterion, which specifies that the individual 
volume must be ≥ nominal volume. This complies with established regulatory guidelines, 
ensuring that the product meets the required specifications.

analysis are within specification and meet the required acceptance criteria. We commit to

43003, and 43004 for the 7.5mL pack size.
We acknowledge your query regarding the provision of osmolality and viscosity results at the 
end of shelf life.
Please note that osmolality and viscosity are not considered stability-indicating parameters for 
this product. As such, these parameters are not included in the shelf-life specifications. The 
stability of the product is assured through other validated stability-indicating tests, which are 
part of the established shelf-life specifications.

• 
ICH Q6A: Specifies that only stability-indicating parameters, which are directly 
relevant to the product’s quality, safety, and efficacy, are required as part of the 
stability testing program.
•

stability studies, focusing on parameters that are most likely to be affected by storage

Holding time of the bulk solution is defined from start of the filtration of the bulk into the

pre-filled plastic syringes are performed within the holding time of the bulk solution. Adherence

autoclave.

stopped and only continues once the temperature re-enters the acceptable temperature range. If

Question/Consideration: In relation to the revision of the Assay of system limit, it is noted in the supporting batch data that the lowest observed assay result is 51 mg. Considering the historical data, you are requested to tighten the proposed limit for Assay of system from 47 - 57 mg to 50 -57 mg.
Answer/Response:
The most important quality attribute of Mirena IUS is the Release Rate of Levonorgestrel. Steady, slowly decreasing, drug release rate from the IUS ensures the efficacy of Mirena in its intended use. From this perspective the amount of Levonorgestrel in the IUS does not play such an important role, as it does not directly influence the release characteristics of Mirena. The release of Levonorgestrel from the hormone core is mainly defined by the parameters of the membrane surrounding the core. MIRENA is a "reservoir type" drug product, which means that the drug core must be loaded with an excess of drug substance.

During the intended usage time of the product, only part of its Levonorgestrel content is consumed. The cumulative Levonorgestrel release is about 52 % during five years usage and about 74 % during eight years usage. The residual content of Levonorgestrel is still about 13.5 mg at eight years calculated using nominal Assay 52 mg, and about 8.5 mg if evaluated using initial assay of the proposed lower limit 47 mg.
The variability sources of assay are Levonorgestrel impurities, mixing of the hormone-elastomer mass, extrusion process of the drug core to a tube, and cutting of the hormone core into appropriate pieces in the assembly step of the IUS.

Assay (batch average) and uniformity of content specification is supported by historical batch data. Assay values of 40 consecutive batches were analyzed statistically (Table 3–1) in CTD section 3.2.P.5.6. The assay results (total average 53.1 mg) of the batches ranged from 51.1 to 55.7 mg. Based on variability of the data the specification was set to 47 - 57 mg, which is slightly tighter than ± 10% of nominal content (52 mg).
From the long-term Assay data for 1515 Mirena production batches the actual manufacturing variability is clearly seen (Figure 1). The average Assay of 1515 batches from recent years is ranging from 47.9 mg to 54.3 mg, and the distribution indicate suitable process performance for commercial manufacturing. Total average 51.7 mg is in practice in the target 52 mg.

Figure 1. Histogram of Long-term Assay Results. Data is not Normally Distributed (AD test p<0.05), but Normal Distribution is Fitted for Information.
Furthermore, it should be noted that the product is stable and no significant decrease in the amount of Levonorgestrel in an IUS during the Shelf-life is observed.

Based on the above Bayer Oy considers the proposed Assay limits of 47 - 57 mg per IUS system appropriate and well justified.

Justification for the proposed change should be provided: deletion of the parameters "Heavy 
metals" and "Arsenic" from the specification of the active substance amidotrizoic acid 
dihydrate. If such a document has already been submitted for the change in question, please 
indicate where it is located.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 2:
The Japanese Pharmacopoeia (JP) 18th edition has introduced updates under General Notice 
No. 34 regarding the control of elemental impurities. This update aligns with ICH Q3D (R1) 
guidelines for elemental impurity risk assessment and control in pharmaceutical products. 
According to General Notice No. 34: 
• JP drug products are expected to comply with elemental impurity controls as described in 
the general test sections of the pharmacopoeia. 
• When drug products are controlled according to these guidelines, it is not necessary to 
perform routine testing for elemental impurities (e.g., heavy metals and arsenic) in drug 
substances, excipients, or drug product monographs. 
Therefore, the need for separate tests for arsenic and heavy metals in the drug substance 
specification has been eliminated as long as compliance with elemental impurity requirements 
is demonstrated. In line with ICH Q3D (R1) guidelines, a comprehensive risk assessment for 
elemental impurities has been conducted for the drug product. The results confirm that all 
elemental impurity levels, in limits when evaluated in the context of the drug product’s 
intended use and patient safety. The proposed change aligns with regulatory guidelines and 
practices, ensuring harmonization across markets while maintaining the highest standards of 
safety and efficacy for the drug product. 
General note No.34 in the Japanese Pharmacopoeia 18th Edition (JP18) is enclosed in the 
response.

At this time, analytical testing provided evidence that NMPA is contained in Gastrografin product with Star Anise Oil.

To examine the source of NMPA in the formulation, an additional investigation was performed during method development. This included individual testing of API and excipient solutions. For this purpose, aqueous solutions of each component in the formulation with concentrations matching those of the drug product were prepared and tested and the amount of NMPA assessed. The result of the investigation was that only the solution containing star anise oil provided an NMPA signal, therefore, it was concluded that star anise oil is most likely the NMPA source. A test performed with the star anise oil-free formulation which is currently marketed in Japan showed an absence of NMPA.

Bayer have contacted the manufacturer of the star anise oil (Destilaciones Bordas Chinchurreta, S.A.). Further investigations are currently ongoing, including testing of star anise oil batches which were supplied to produce Gastrografin with star anise oil.

Ongoing investigations with the manufacturer may take some more time. Therefore, in order to rectify the situation most expeditiously, we seek to obtain regulatory approvals and supply the new formulation in markets as soon as possible.

Answer/Response:
We acknowledge the agency’s comment.
The Estradiol drug substances are tested regarding microbiological purity as it is a GMP requirement for most APIs. This is ensured with internal documentation. Only in case microbiological purity is a requirement from the Pharmacopeia it is stated in the CoA for the respective active pharmaceutical ingredient. Otherwise, it is only mentioned in our internal documentation.

Also, Microbiological Purity is not required according to ICH Q6A decision tree #6 because Estradiol hemihydrate is not capable of supporting microbial growth or viability. Therefore, microbiological tests are not introduced into the drug substance specification of Estradiol hemihydrate.
Anyway, each year, an ongoing stability study is started and within the test scope microbial contamination is tested at the beginning of the study and at the end of the study. Therefore, every year a start and end value is evaluated. Therefore the results from the yearly stability program to evaluate the batches during storage, demonstrate that no microbial contamination is observed and that Estradiol hemihydrate is not capable of supporting microbial growth or viability.

Question/Consideration: Could not find zone 4 b stability report for Magnevist 20 ml.
Answer/Response:
Please note that Magnevist is an aqueous based contrast media solution presented in glass vials (10 and 20 mL).
Glass vials may be considered as semi-permeable containers, however internal experiments have demonstrated that the actual water or weight loss is neglected and therefore they are in fact, hermetic containers (impermeable).
Furthermore, based on the long-term data experienced with stability studies at higher relative humidity, no effect on the quality parameters could be observed linking to the relative humidity itself. Thus, data gained at 75 % relative humidity can be considered as equivalent to 65 % relative humidity. For this reason, stability studies for Magnevist 20 mL vials are conducted only at 65% RH (results equivalent to 75% RH). Please see enclosed the corresponding justification letter for your convenience.

Additionally, please find enclosed the most up-to date on-going stability data (P.8.3.02 section) for your reference.
Source: Justification on humidity conditions for stability testing of aqueous based contrast media

Question/Consideration: Could you please provide to the TGA what alternative products or methods could be used for each of the approved clinical uses of Gastrografin?
Answer/Response:
Gastrografin is primarily indicated for gastrointestinal examinations where barium sulfate is unsatisfactory, undesirable, or contraindicated (Gastrografin PI, date of revision 13 February 2019). It can be administered both orally and rectally.

Alternative contrast agents are available in Australia for similar gastrointestinal indications:
• Omnipaque (Iohexol): "Omnipaque is indicated in adults, children, and premature babies for studies of the gastrointestinal tract" (Omnipaque PI, date of revision 20 December 2023).
• Ioscan (Sodium Amidotrizoate): "Ioscan is a contrast medium for Computerised Axial Tomography examination of the gastrointestinal tract. It is indicated primarily for use when barium sulfate is not appropriate" (Ioscan PI, date of revision 12/04/2018).

It should be noted that Gastrografin is a hyperosmolar contrast agent, whereas Omnipaque and Ioscan are low osmolar contrast agents.

Gastrografin is also indicated for the treatment of uncomplicated meconium ileus (Gastrografin PI, date of revision 13 February 2019), taking advantage of its high osmotic pressure. We are not aware of any other product indicated in Australia for this specific use.
keywords: Drug Product; manufacturer; specification; stability data; Risk Asessment

Question/Consideration: You have requested to increase the Magnesium stearate from 0.2 to 0.4 and accordingly decrease lactose monohydrate from 37.430 to 37.230 per tablet. However on dissolution studies the amount mentioned is 0.3, and it seems like the data doesn’t match with your request. Please advise.
Answer/Response: The magnesium stearate content was validated at 0.4 mg/tablet in 2021, replacing the older manufacturing description and range (0.2-0.4 mg /tablet) used since 1999. Original manufacturing documents from 26 years ago, the chapter “Basic unit”, the smallest amount of the range of magnesium stearate was generally given for the description of the dosage form (0.2 mg magnesium stearate per tablet). Previously prior to the change 0.3 mg/tablet was the optimal amount specified for production at Weimar. The updated manufacturing validation have higher capacity for the tablet production requirements, leading to an increase to 0.4 mg /tablet. At the same time, the switch from MD to TRD chapter format took place. The newly created TRDs for P.1.01 and P.3.2.01 after the latest manufacturing validation now both refer to the current and correct magnesium content of 0.4 mg/tablet as a single value without range. In Dissolution studies comparative data provided for the current and proposed formulation of magnesium stearate (0.3 mg tablet vs 0.4 mg /tablet). It ensures the consistency and accuracy in the product description registered with authorities.
