homogenous in the elastomer mixture.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1 ( P.3.3.01 ;P.3.5.01):
There is no actual change in the manufacturing process of Mirena in connection of the 
deletion of mass homogeneity IPC.  Furthermore, the IPCs, Concentration of levonorgestrel 
and Homogeneity, can’t be considered as two separate IPC tests, as they are both obtained and 
calculated from exactly the same blend analysis.
Bayer has manufactured Mirena batches for 30 years already and hence the mixing process is 
well established, and therefore proven to produce homogenous levonorgestrel-elastomer 
mixtures. In order to support the IPC deletion the actual mixing time (at least 40 minutes) 
applied on the product over the years was added and specified as an IPC to substitute the 
homogeneity test. Therefore, the proposed IPCs are only adapting to the actual conditions of 
the manufacturing process.
An updated process validation report P.3.5.01_02 in which the mixing time of min. 40 
minutes has been observed and reported is provided to the competent Health Authority for 
review. In this validation study homogenous mixtures were achieved with the mixing time of 
40 minutes.
As a further assurance of the continuously homogenous mixtures achieved in the mixing step 
of Mirena data on recent 283 batches (manufactured between 03.01.2024 and 31.01.2025) of 
Mirena is provided. The data refers to average results of 4 IPC samples collected from these 
283 batches, which means that the data in graphs and histograms is based on 1132 blend 
samples in total.
The requirement for the average levonorgestrel concentration is 48 – 52 %, and the RSD of 4 
determinations must be ≤ 2 %. The average results of 283 batches fall between 47.9 and 50.8 
%, with the average of all determinations as  49.4 %. Average of the calculated RSD values is 
0.4 %. maximum observed RSD has been 1.6 %.
The data provided reliably verifies that mixing process of Mirena results into a homogenous 
mixture when mixed for 40 minutes. Therefore, Bayer considers deletion of the homogeneity 
IPC justified.

Question/Consideration:
Question 2
Variation number 6:
The IPC bioburden limit was widened, apparently without any justification or discussion. 
Justification for the widening of bioburden IPC should be provided.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 2 ( CTD section):
The action limit for pre-sterilization bioburden of Levonorgestrel intrauterine delivery system 
52 mg with inserter (MIRENA), max 100 CFU/unit, has been widely accepted by the 
authorities.
Alert limits (internal, based on trend) and action limits for Mirena have been defined in line 
with EN ISO 11737 and EN ISO 11135. For the action level, Bayer Oy refers to ISO 11737-1 
Table C.1, where max 100 CFU is considered as a low bioburden, and the EMA guideline 
(EMA/CHMP/CVMP/QWP/850374/2015) that mentions 100 CFU/100 g as an acceptable 
limit for parenteral finished products in case of heat sterilized products.
Manufacturing of MIRENA takes place in a clean room and contains steps that may reduce 
microbial contamination, thus exceeding the action level seldom happens. However, 
bioburden spikes can occasionally be detected, that according to EN ISO 11737-1 may be a 
normal and consistent part of the bioburden but shall be evaluated for the impact as 
appropriate (A.8.5 Bioburden spikes). In cleanliness class C, microbial contamination is 
typically due to the personnel and may not be evenly distributed in the batch. The 
contamination will be eliminated by the validated overkill sterilization process. In any case, 
according to the current Bayer Oy procedure, exceeding either the action level or two 
subsequent times the alert level, will trigger a root cause investigation both in the laboratory

executed after the approval of the competent Health Authority.

Question/Consideration:
Question 1
The specifications provided do not include the sterility specifications for shelf life, which upon 
reviewing the approved stability study were executed in that study.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1 (P.5.1.02):
In the document P.8.2.01 “Post-Approval Stability Protocol and Stability Commitment” it is 
stated concerning the sterility test the following: “The sterility test will be replaced by other 
tests confirming the primary package integrity, i.e. visual “Package seal integrity” -test and 
“Sealed joint strength” -test will be performed to substitute the Sterility test during the Shelf-
life.
In stability report P.8.3.01#006245392 compiled for the stability studies performed on the 
Jaydess pilot/primary batches the sterility test has been part of the study only with the purpose 
to support further the approach to omit the sterility test from the subsequent stability studies 
to be performed on Jaydess IUS. However, from 2011onwards, sterility testing was excluded 
from the stability specification and replaced with two package tests, which are included in the 
Shelf-Life specification of the product. This approach is also described in the stability 
commitment for post-approval batches. Sterility was tested only on the pilot batches which 
were placed into stability studies before approval of the product on the market. Hence 
presence of sterility data in report P.8.3.01#006245392  does not indicate a requirement for 
ongoing sterility testing as it has been demonstrated in the stability commitment for post-
approval batches. Ongoing stability data in report P.8.3.02_018975275 does not tested the 
sterility.
Therefore, Bayer Oy does not include Sterility test in the Shelf-life Specification of Jaydess 
IUS but substitutes this test with the two package tests included in the Shelf-life specifications 
of the product. This approach is accepted by EMA, as well as by FDA.
EMA, Quality of medicines questions and answers: Part 2 / Stability - Endotoxin testing and 
sterility testing at the end of shelf-life: “Sterility testing should be performed at least at the 
end of Shelf-life, but it can be replaced by testing of the container closure integrity.”

Question/Consideration:
Question 2

Please explain and provide evidence that removing the plastic tray covering the syringe does
not affect the stability of the drug.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 2:

We propose to replace the current blister packaging with a cardboard divider for the pre-filled
syringes (PFS) and plunger rods. The new packaging design will securely hold the plunger
rod and PFS in place by automatically inserting the cardboard divider into the folding box.
This ensures that both units remain fixed, preventing movement and reducing the risk of
breakage.

The cardboard divider offers protection equivalent to the current blister by stabilizing the
components inside the folding box, ensuring product integrity. This change is being
implemented to improve packaging efficiency and sustainability while maintaining the same
level of protection.

Please note that the new packaging design does not affect the quality or stability of the
medicinal product throughout its storage period. Secondary packaging including the blister
has no impact on product stability of Gadovist PFS during shelf life. Gadovist stability
samples are routinely stored in climate chambers without blister or any other secondary
packaging material such as plunger rods, cardboard boxes, or other country-specific
packaging. Therefore, this change does not impact our ongoing stability commitments.

Additionally, this modification aligns with our sustainability goals by reducing plastic usage
and minimizing associated costs, contributing to an environmentally responsible packaging
solution.
keywords: Container closure system; Secondary packaging; Shelf Life; Stability data; stability commitment

Question/Consideration:
Question 1

Relevant regulation: paragraph 1-2-C-4) of article 7 (requirements) (3.2.P.5.6)

Reasons for request: insufficient assessment of the feasibility of changing impurity specification and the impact of changing quality control specification on safety

Supplementation request: submit the feasibility data for the change.
Answer/Response:
With this application, Bayer proposes to widen the limits for purity by SE-UPLC % main peak and % aggregate at the end of shelf life by 0.3 % to account for differences resulting from a method change from SE-HPLC to SE-UPLC in September 2019.
Comprehensive analysis of available data has shown that when analyzing the same reference standard and the same stability batches, the new SE-UPLC method is 0.3% more sensitive to the high molecular weight (HMW) / aggregate species compared to the previous SE-HPLC data.
Therefore, the proposed change to the end of shelf-life specification is made to account only for the change in analytical method.

As described in P.5.6.01 - To enable a 0.3% shift, an additional decimal place is proposed to be introduced for aggregates and main peak. Note in this respect that the previous shelf-life specification limits of ≥ 97% (main peak) and ≤ 3% (aggregate) translate into 96.5% and 3.5% considering the current limits before rounding (96.50% for rounding to 97%, 3.49% for rounding to 3%). The current and proposed shelf-life acceptance criteria are summarized in Table 3-3.
Table 3-3 from P.5.6.01: Proposed Aflibercept Drug Product Specification for SE-UPLC

The following data support the change in SE-UPLC % main peak and % aggregate at the end of shelf life by 0.3 %. This limit (original for SE-HPLC and shifted for SE-UPLC) continues to be supported by toxicological, clinical and market surveillance data.

Analytical Comparability data:

The shelf-life acceptance criteria for purity by size exclusion chromatography were initially set using SE-HPLC data and kept unchanged when the SE-HPLC method was replaced by SE-UPLC in the approved Korean dossier in September 2019.
In 2022, a review of a more comprehensive data set (comprising both reference standard measurements and 70 pairs of DP release and stability samples, measured with SE-HPLC and SE-UPLC in parallel) revealed a method offset of approx. 0.3% (see justification in P.5.6.01). These data are summarized below:

Recent complete 24 months stability data continue to support the specification limits (as amended for SE-UPLC):
P.8.3.01_022949324_04 - Stability data 3x batches manufactured March 2020
P.8.3.01_022974828_04 – Stability data 3x batches manufactured November 2021
P.8.3.01_022979202_03 – Stability data 3x batches manufactured July 2022

Supporting toxicological data:

The limit (%aggregate) for the HMW species (≤ 3.8% as amended for SE-UPLC) continues to be supported by toxicology studies with higher doses and higher exposure to HMW species than in human patients. To support the initial registration of Eylea 2 mg, reference was made in P.5.6.01 to the relevant toxicology study VGFT-TX-05011. With this response, this section in P.5.6.01 is further clarified.

In a 8-month pivotal IVT study in monkeys (Module 4.2.3.2, VGFT-TX-05011) conducted to support the marketing authorization of aflibercept 2 mg, aflibercept doses ranging from 0.5 to 4 mg/eye (in 50 µL/eye) were administered bilaterally every 4 weeks for 9 doses in total, followed by a 5-month treatment free recovery period. Ocular findings were limited to non-adverse mild and transient ocular inflammation up to and including the high dose of 4 mg/eye. When normalized for the smaller vitreal volume in monkeys compared to humans (approximately 2 vs. 4 mL), the 4 mg/eye are expected to produce an initial vitreal concentration which is equivalent to that expected following an approximate 8 mg dose administered to a human eye. With an approximate high molecular weight species (HMWs) concentration of 1-1.5% the 8 mg dose corresponds to an initial HMWs dose of 0.08-0.12 mg/human eye, and further, to a HMWs concentration in aflibercept 2 mg (40 mg/mL) of 1.6-2.4 mg/mL (for 1% HMWs: 0.08 mg HMWs/50 µL injection volume =x/1000 µL; x = 1.6 mg HMWs/mL, for 1.5% HMWs: 2.4 mg HMWs/mL). This concentration is equivalent to a content of 4-6% HMWs (for 1% HMWs: 100%/40 mg/mL = x/1.6 mg/mL; x = 4%; for 1.4% HMWs: 6%), which is covered by this 8-month pivotal IVT study in monkeys on aflibercept 2 mg.

Supplemental toxicology data at a higher dose is now also available from study VGFT-TX-20170. While the study was performed to support the registration of Eylea 8 mg, reference is now also made in P.5.6.01 for Eylea 2 mg as explained below:
An additional study, intended to investigate the tolerability of high concentrations of HMWs to support the specification of aflibercept 8 mg, covers even higher HMWs – equivalent concentrations in humans. In this 3-month IVT toxicology study in monkeys utilizing the high concentration aflibercept formulation enriched with approximately 6% and 10% HMWs (Module 4.2.3.2, VGFT-TX-20170), doses of 5.6 mg/eye (in 40 µL/eye) were administered bilaterally every 4 weeks for a total of 4 doses. Consistent with findings noted in the study mentioned above, repeated IVT administration of 5.6 mg aflibercept per eye containing approximately 6 or 10% HMWs was well tolerated, with no adverse ocular inflammation evident. When normalized for the smaller vitreal volume in monkeys compared to humans (approximately half), the 5.6 mg/eye are expected to produce an initial vitreal concentration which is equivalent to that expected following an approximate 11.2 mg dose administered to a human eye. With a maximal HMWs content of 10% the 11.2 mg dose corresponds to an initial HMWs dose of 1.12 mg/human eye, and further, to a HMWs concentration in aflibercept 8 mg (114.3 mg/mL) of 16 mg/mL (1.12 mg HMWs/70 µL injection volume =x/1000 µL; x = 16 mg HMWs/mL). This concentration is equivalent to a content of 14% HMWs (100%/114.3 mg/mL = x/16 mg/mL; x = 14%), which is covered by this 3-month IVT study in monkeys.
In conclusion, HMWs contents of up to 14% are covered by toxicological data and were well tolerated.

Source:
P.5.6.01 Drug product - Justification of Specifications, 40 mg/mL vial, justification valid for both vial and PFS.

Supporting evidence from clinical and market surveillance data:

In P.5.6.01 (submitted during the initial registration of Eylea 2 mg), reference was made to two sets of clinical studies, the pivotal VIEW 1 and VIEW 2 with treatment doses of 0.5 mg and 2 mg, where 2 mg is the marketed dose and 0.5 mg was a lower dose. This has now been clarified in the P.5.6.01 document. The evidence contributed by these studies is that they showed no evidence of a dose response in safety outcomes.
In addition, reference was made to an early clinical study, where a cohort of patients received a dose higher than 2 mg:

In addition, a cohort of patients that were injected with a dose of aflibercept dimer (equivalent to 4-5.4% in a 2 mg dose) exceeding the proposed expiry specification of 3.8%, did not reveal any unusual tolerability issues, consistent with the lack of a dose response of safety signals to dimer dose in the larger VIEW studies.
Here reference was made to study VGFT-OD-0603, a phase I clinical trial to assess the safety and tolerability of repeated doses of intravitreal administration of two VEGF Trap formulations in subjects with neovascular Age Related Macular Degeneration. Patients received 4 mg aflibercept every 4 weeks for 12 weeks, then as needed through week 52.
The safety profile of the N=20 patients who all received 4 mg Aflibercept did not indicate a safety concern. No intraocular inflammation (IOI) was reported through week 52, please see Table 14 below.
(Protein aggregation in biological medicines bears the potential to trigger an immune response. For intravitreally administered biological agents this could result in the development of an immune mediated intraocular inflammation (IOI)).

In addition, post-marketing pharmacovigilance data was evaluated from the time of initial submission until the end of 2024.
The safety profile for IOIs with Eylea 2 mg is continuously monitored. No significant change was seen in the rate of IOI in the period before and after the introduction of the SE-UPLC method (1.2 cases per 10 000 injections and 1.0 case per 10 000 injections respectively).
Overall, no new safety concern potentially related to protein aggregate formation in terms of IOIs was observed from 2020 and onwards for Eylea 2 mg.

Summary:

Comprehensive analysis of the SE-HPLC and SE-UPLC data has shown that when analyzing the same reference standard and the stability batches, the SE-UPLC method introduced in 2019 is 0.3% more sensitive to the high molecular weight (HMW) / aggregate species. This data was not available at the time of method change. Therefore, the change is made now to change to the end of shelf-life specification by 0.3% to account only for the change in analytical method.

Data from the initial registration of Eylea 2 mg, as well as recent toxicology data on aflibercept with a higher content of HMW species, ongoing post-marketing surveillance data and stability data continue to support the specification limits.
keywords: justification of specification; drug product specification; HPLC-method; Analytical, validation; Stability data

Question/Consideration: Regarding serial number 102, explain the appropriateness of classifying the spray rate of granulation liquid (0.90 kg/min) and the inlet air temperature (85°C) in Step 2 (Granulation and Drying) and the screen size for sieving of magnesium stearate (1.0 mm) in Step 3 (Sieving and Blending) as matters to be addressed in minor change notifications, indicating the control ranges specified in the Product Master Formula, proven acceptable ranges, etc.
Answer/Response:
The manufacturing process development included a comprehensive design of experiments (DoE) in laboratory scale and commercial scale (manufacturing site: Bayer AG, Leverkusen). The DoE study in commercial scale was performed on the three process parameters - spray rate, spray pressure and product temperature and the impact on the quality attributes of the granules and tablet cores was thoroughly investigated. All granule batches could be compressed to tablets complying with the specification. Consequently, the final process risk analysis indicated a reduced risk associated with the granulation parameters (please refer also to information in the technical document P.2.3.01_022872031_02). On that basis, the process parameter ranges were established for the manufacturing site in Leverkusen (please refer also to information in the technical documents P.3.3.01_022822890_01 and P.3.3.01_022822891_01).

For the implementation of the manufacturing process at the new manufacturing site Delpharm, Milano, appropriate process parameters (spray rate, inlet air temperature) were defined based on the prior knowledge gained during the development phase. The appropriateness of these parameters was demonstrated in a manufacturing process validation (please refer also to process validation report P.3.5.01_022982751_01). All manufactured batches (three per dose) met the pre-defined acceptance criteria which included the drug product specifications, in-process controls and additional testing such as blend uniformity testing and content uniformity testing.

The addition of magnesium stearate occurs during the post-blending step (i.e. preparation of the ready-to-press-mixture). A sieve is used to eliminate potential aggregates of the raw material before addition. According to the initial risk analysis, no post-blending parameter was found to impact the Critical Quality Attributes (CQAs) of the tablet (please refer also to information in the technical document P.2.3.01_022872031_02). Therefore, a change in screen size will not impact any CQA of the drug product. This was successfully demonstrated within the aforementioned manufacturing process validation at the manufacturing site Delpharm, Milano where a sieve size of 1.0 mm was utilized. The process parameters for the manufacturing process at the manufacturing site Delpharm Milano were defined accordingly (please refer also to information in the technical documents P.3.3.01_022982208_01 and P.3.3.01_022982185_01).

In summary, the comprehensive process development and subsequent manufacturing process validation have demonstrated that the defined process parameters, including the spray rate, inlet air temperature, and screen size for magnesium stearate, do not adversely impact the critical quality attributes of the final drug product. Therefore, these parameters are appropriately classified as minor changes.

Question/Consideration:
Question 2

Risk assessment reports for nitrosamine impurities in the active substance and finished 
product have been included in our records. Risks for nitrosamine impurities "NO-
oxacarboxylic acid (EMA N-nitrosorivaroxaban open ring acid)" and "NO-chlorothiophene-
hydroxymorpholinone (EMA N-nitroso-rivaroxaban amide)" associated with the active 
substance rivaroxaban were identified. It has been declared that assay and, if necessary,
verification tests will be carried out for these impurities and the results of the analysis should 
be submitted during the marketing authorization process.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 2 (CTD section S.3.2 P.5.5):
Confirmatory testing was conducted on representative commercial batches of both drug 
formulations of Rivaroxaban (tablets and granules for oral suspension) that are manufactured 
and marketed by Bayer AG. The testing is still ongoing and not finalized yet.
The objective of our method development was to encompass both amine precursors 
(oxacarboxylic acid and chlorothiophene-hydroxymorpholinone) and their respective N-
nitrosamines (N-nitroso-chloro-thiophene-hydroxy-morpholinone and N-nitroso-
oxacarboxylic acid).  The results from method development indicated that three out of four 
analytes (both precursors and N-nitroso-oxacarboxylic acid) can be determined quantitatively 
within the appropriate ppm range (LOQ NLT 5.0 ppm), using a single LC-MS/MS method. 
However, the fourth analyte (N-nitroso-chlorothiophene-hydroxymorpholinone) could not be 
quantified due to co-elution with the main rivaroxaban peak in the LC chromatogram.

We are still in the process of developing a method to quantitatively determine N-nitroso-
chlorothiophene-hydroxymorpholinone.
Exploratory results indicate a significantly higher presence of oxacarboxylic acid compared to 
chlorothiophene-hydroxymorpholinone in the API (approx. 3:1). Therefore, Bayer initiated 
confirmatory testing on Xarelto coated tablets and Xarelto granules, using the method 
validated for  N-nitroso-oxacarboxylic acid,  oxacarboxylic acid and chloro-thiophene-
hydroxy-morpholinone.
The analytical limit or analytical evaluation threshold (AET) for any given N-nitrosamine is 
determined by its acceptable intake (AI in ng/day) and the maximum daily dose (MDD) of the 
API for the drug in question. This results the following:
𝐴𝐸𝑇𝑔𝑟𝑎𝑛𝑢𝑙𝑒𝑠= 75.0 ppm for Rivaroxaban granules
Present results of Confirmatory test All tested batches of granules for oral suspension (n = 
6) showed N-nitroso-oxacarboxylic acid above 5.0 ppm, with a maximum of 10.0 ppm, 
equating to maximum 13% of the AI.
The absence of N-nitroso-oxacarboxylic  from the film-coated tablets suggests that the API is 
an unlikely source of its presence in the granules. The manufacturing process for the granules 
is likely to origin of either N-nitrosamine. Preliminary conclusions are as follows:
• Granules: The potential risk for granules for oral suspension was confirmed, with levels 
of N-nitroso-oxacarboxylic acid above 10 % of the AI but well below the AI. N-nitroso-
oxacarboxylic acid is classified as category 4, indicating low carcinogenic potency.

Mitigating actions are required, though no immediate risk to patient safety is indicated. 
No field actions are required. 
• The API is the source of the amine precursors but is unlikely the source of either N-
nitrosamine. The root cause is expected to lie in the manufacturing process of the 
granules.
We will notify the Health Authority once the method for N-nitroso-chlorothiophene-
hydroxymorpholinone confirmatory testing is completed, and data generated for Rivaroxaban 
granules for oral suspension.

Please find enclosed the technical registration document where updated risk assessment of 
nitrosamines is documented for Rivaroxaban micronized drug substance.

drug substance (Site Wuppertal) (S.3.2.07_022982890; new)

Question/Consideration:
Question 3
HISTORICAL DATA:
Must be brought the historical data of the parameters and/or controls of the manufacturing 
process of the intermediate product and/or finished product, which statistically justifies the 
change, considering that it is an imported product as required in section 9.5.12, or a technical 
justification of why it is not provided that supports the requested modification
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 3 ( CTD section 3.2.P.3):
In Colombia, Bayer AG in Leverkusen, Germany (LEV) and Bayer Healthcare Manufacturing 
S.r.l., Garbagnate in Italy (GAR) were already registered as sites for bulk manufacturing, 
packaging, testing and release to the market.
The main reason for implementation of bigger alternative equipment at manufacturing site 
Garbagnate was an increased efficiency of the process (increase of production capacity). The 
coating of a batch got possible in just one run (when using alternative bigger coater (GS) instead 
of coating in three sub-lots (with the smaller coater Accela Cota). The new coater has the same 
capacity as the coating machine registered in Leverkusen, Germany.

For the alternative manufacturing equipment, adaptation of the single production parameters 
was necessary. It was shown in comparative dissolution tests and validation of the 
manufacturing processes that current and new alternative bigger equipment reach a product of 
same quality compared with the product from smaller equipment.

The document Proof of Product Equivalence after Change of Production Process/Site with 
TRD Code T.02.75-01 provides the mentioned comparative dissolution tests. Validation 
batches ITA56TX, ITA56TZ and ITA56U0 produced with the proposed new alternative bigger 
equipment for granulation and coating were compared with three batches ITA53AC, ITA53AD 
and ITA53AE from current smaller equipment for granulation and coating.

The document Validation of the Manufacturing Process with TRD Code T.08.19-02 in dossier 
section 3.2.P.3 shows the comparability of validation batches using the proposed new 
alternative bigger equipment for granulation and coating (ITA56TX, ITA56TZ and ITA56U0) 
with the validation batches from 2014 and 2015 produced with current smaller equipment for 
granulation and coating (ITA2BAV, ITA2CCL, ITA2CCN). Process variables for granulation 
and blending are described in Table 4-3, Table 4-4, Table 4-5 (for small granulator batches) 
and Table 4-6 (for big granulator batches). Process variables for coating are described in Table 
4-9 (for small coater batches) and Table 4-10 (for big coater batches). It is visible that the spray 
rate has changed for the alternative bigger granulator. The inlet air temperature and spray rate 
are different for the two alternative coaters at site Garbagnate.

Response to a) and c)
As described in Proof of Product Equivalence after Change of Production Process/Site with TRD 
Code T.02.75-03, Dissolution tests were carried out by different QC laboratories. The 
dissolution data of Leverkusen batch BXA4K1F was recorded in March 2010, the data of 
Garbagnate batches in 2012 and those of Bitterfeld batches in 2017. The claim of comparability 
between these three sites are given and represented in T.02.75-03.
More detailed information about these dissolution results is described in three new, different 
Additional Batch-Related Information documents, each of them having the TRD code T.02.80 
with different DocID.
The document Additional Batch-Related Information with TRD Code and DocID 
T.02.80#022992718-01 from site Garbagnate provides batch-related raw data and dissolution 
profiles of Garbagnate batches ITA0KTU, ITA0KTV, ITA0KTT using the QC dissolution 
medium (pH 4.5 + 0.4% SDS) and 4 additional dissolution media (HCl 0.1 N + 0.4% SDS, pH 
6.5 + 0.4% SDS, pH 7.5 + 0.4 % SDS and water + 0.4% SDS.
The document Additional Batch-Related Information with TRD Code and DocID 
T.02.80#022992865-01 from site Bitterfeld provides batch-related raw data from dissolution 
testing of Bitterfeld batches BTT1GZW, BTT1GZX and BTT1GZV using the QC dissolution 
medium pH 4.5 + 0.4% SDS and 4 additional dissolution media (HCl 0.1 N + 0.4% SDS, pH 
6.5 + 0.4% SDS, pH 7.5 + 0.4% SDS and water + 0.4% SDS). The second part of this document 
includes additionally absorbance raw data and calculated absorbance data.
The document Additional Batch-Related Information with TRD Code and DocID 
T.02.80#022992533-01 from site Leverkusen outlines the results of dissolution testing for batch 
BXA4K1F conducted by the external laboratory Eurofins PHAST GmbH, located in 
Homburg/Saar, Germany. This contract laboratory is a well-established service provider for the 
pharmaceutical industry. It has, for example, been accredited by FDA.

For the studies referenced in T.02.80#022992533-01, UV-Vis semi-automated dissolution 
system was used applying a paddle (USP apparatus 2). 12 samples were drawn at time point of 
10, 15, 20, 30, 45 and 60 minutes. The tablets dissolved completely resulting in a plateau phase 
at approximately 20 minutes reaching nearly 100 %. The average data of the coefficient of 
variation percentage (CoV) at time points up to 10 minutes are not more than 20% and at other 
time points not more than 10%, as shown in the statistics. This complies with acceptance 
criteria. For each analysis, in each medium, the CoV values on 12 individual values were very 
low and this demonstrates the precision of the results in the dissolution profiles.
CoV values are reported in document T.02.75-03 in chapter 3.2 and 3.3 or the respective tables 
of T.02.80-01 documents attached as source. All comparative dissolution tests were carried out 
and evaluated according to SUPAC requirements. SUPAC allows the use of mean data, if CoV 
at earlier time points (e.g. 15 minutes) is not more than 20% and CoV at later time points is not 
more than 10%, Both conditions were fulfilled as shown in T.02.75-03. The data comparison 
according to SUPAC was done by equal time points (i.e. 15, 30, 45 and 60 min).
Response to d)
It is important to note that, at the time of testing, a validation for the additional dissolution 
media was not performed. However, the data collected was recorded in a GMP-QC laboratory 
under consistent test conditions. A semi-automated dissolution system, utilizing a peristaltic 
pump and a UV-spectrophotometer, was employed to determine the dissolution profile, 
ensuring that the stability of the test solution was not a concern.
The data collected is traceable and complete. Following the testing procedure of T.02.16-01, a 
linear regression curve was generated using a multipoint calibration with 50% and 100% 
standard solutions, from which the y-intercept (relative error) and the correlation coefficient 
(r²) were calculated. As described in testing procedure T.02.16-01, for each dissolution test the 
limit of the relative error as one of the system suitability parameters must not exceed </= 3 %. 
This requirement has also been applied to the analyses of presented comparative dissolution 
tests which have been collected in all non-QC media. This ensures that linearity in the range of 
50 - 100% is also given for the analyses in this media.
The presented data also show a complete drug release at the final timepoint, so it can also be 
assumed, that the accuracy of the analytical method in all non-QC-media with the addition of 
0.4% SDS is sufficiently given. This is in line with the solubility data presented in Information 
on Method Development / Dissolution with TRD Code T.02.38-02. System precision is also 
calculated as a system suitability parameter by 6 values per dissolution test and is limited to </ 
= 1.5%.
To support all these facts, Bayer Bitterfeld GmbH has issued a Justification about analytical 
validation for dissolution profiles explaining that the validation study in the QC medium (pH 
4.5 +0.4% SDS) reported in T.02.50-01 sufficiently supports the results obtained from the 
comparative dissolution profiles reported in T.02.75-03. See source files.

Response to e)
As described in T.02.16-01, before sampling, the filter unit is thoroughly rinsed with the 
dissolution medium. This ensures that no residues from previous tests or contaminants affect 
the sample. The requirement to withdraw a sufficiently large amount through a filter unit that 
removes particles approximately 10 μm or larger highlights the importance of filters in the 
testing procedure. The use of a sintered glass filter G 4 or a similar filter is necessary to ensure 
the clarity of the sample and to secure the accuracy of the analysis. This leads to the conclusion 
that filter effects do not have to be considered.

Question/Consideration:
Question 7
Regarding the study: T.02.75-01:
a) Technically justify the non-compliance of the comparative dissolution profiles for the 
dissolution medium 0.1 N HCl + 0.4 SDS of batches BXA84T9, BXA84ST, BXA84SP, 
BTB7FZ0 (Pages 662 and 663), pH 4.5 + 0.4% SDS of batches BXA84ST, BTB7GK0 and 
BTB7FZ0 (Folios 667 and 668) and dissolution medium Phosphate buffer pH 6.8 + 0.4% 
SDS of batches BXA84T9, BXA84ST and BXA84SP (Folio 672); the above, since it is 
evident that the dissolution data have a percentage variation coefficient greater than 20% for 
the first time point (5 minutes); (Numeral 10.6, technical annex, resolution 1124 of 2016).
b) Provide 20% of the instrumental supports for the UV spectrophotometry quantification 
method of the comparative dissolution profiles at pH: 0.1 N HCl + 0.4% SDS, pH 4.5 + 0.4% 
SDS and pH 6.8 + 0.4% SDS with information that allows traceability (Reading date, sample 
identification, characteristic absorption units for each reading, etc.) in accordance with 
Section 7.8 of technical annex 1 of Resolution 1124 of 2016.
c) Justify why, for the calculation of f2, only the data from time points 10, 15, and 20 minutes 
are included.
d) Please clarify why they do not present validation in the dissolution media pH 0.1 N HCl + 
0.4% SDS and pH 6.8 buffer+ 0.4% SDS, taking into account that they present dissolution 
profiles for these media.
e) Additionally, it should be noted that the validation identified with code T.02.50-03 does not 
include the filter effect parameter.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 7 (CTD sections 3.2.P.2 and 3.2.P.5):
Response to a) and c)
The coefficient of variation (CoV) ≤ 20% for early time points is a prerequisite for f2 
calculation. In table 3-2 on page 7 of T.02.75-01 it is stated that the 5 min timepoint was 
collected for information only. As already stated in section 3.3 on page 8 in T.02.75-01 the 
calculation of the similarity factor (f2) is among other things based on the condition that it is 
allowed to use mean data, if the coefficient of variation (CoV) is ≤ 20% at early timepoints (up 
to 10 minutes) and ≤ 10% at other time points. This is why 5 min was not included for 
calculation. Thus, this is no non-compliance.
A graphical comparison of all profiles together with all dissolution results is presented for each 
medium in chapters 4.2, 4.3 and 4.4 of T.02.75-01. As also visible in these sections, all 
calculations of f2 values for comparative dissolution testing were performed with data from 
comparison time points 10, 15 and 20 minutes for each dissolution medium (covering a range 
of pH 1 to pH 6.8 according ICH M9 guideline). Section 3.3 of T.02.75-01 is describing the 
conditions for f2 calculation in general.

Following the recommendations given in ICH M9 1 guideline for f2 calculation (or Numeral 
10.6, technical annex, resolution 1124 of 2016), (http://www.invima.gov.co Bogota - 
Colombia), calculation is based on the following conditions:
• A minimum of three time points (zero excluded).
• The time points should be the same for the two products.
• Mean of the individual values for every time point for each product.
• Not more than one mean value of ≥ 85% dissolved for either of the products.
• If dissolution at the 20 minutes time point is close to 85%, the f2-value is also 
calculated with an additional timepoint.
• To allow the use of mean data, the coefficient of variation (CoV) is ≤ 20% at early 
timepoints (up to 10 minutes) and ≤ 10% at other time points. When the coefficient of 
variation is too high, the f2-calculation is not applicable for comparison of profiles.
Two dissolution profiles are considered similar when the f2-value is ≥ 50.
When both test and reference products demonstrate that ≥ 85% of the labelled amount of the 
drug is dissolved within 15 minutes, comparison with an f2-test is not required and the 
dissolution profiles are considered similar. If this case applies, the f2-test is performed for 
information purposes only.

Question/Consideration:
In the current proposed table in dossier 32r (page.6) presented in Annex-4, it appears that additional changes (dose interval, dose line color, mean volume) have been made, and although the variation is stated to be editorial, an explanation of the changes in the current - proposed table needs to be submitted.

If the change in question is an editorial change, a signed statement must be submitted that there is no change in the packaging available on the market.
Answer/Response:
The change in the dose line position is the result of the applicant undertaking efforts to reduce the variability of dosing and extreme values of expelled drug from the Aflibercept solution 40mg/mL in prefilled syringe for intravitreous injection (Aflibercept 40mg/mL PFS). The applicant would like to highlight that the table under discussion does not reflect the changes that are proposed to the CMC dossier (Module 3 of the CTD; 32r in annex-4), but is part of the Notified Body Opinion that was provided with the submission as STED.1.03-01. Therefore, the applicant is considering this part of the variation to be editorial and will provide a signed statement for confirmation (refer to Aflibercept 40mg/mL PFS_Declaration_Dose Line).

Background 
A medical device dossier was compiled for the change in the dose line position of Aflibercept 40mg/mL PFS and was submitted to the Notified Body BSI in 10/2023 to obtain a Notified Body Opinion, which is mandatory for submitting CMC variations affecting integral drug-device combination products to EMA.
As per EU medical device regulation (MDR (EU) 2017/745) requirements, the medical device dossier is much more focused on technical aspects and more detailed in certain areas, including dose range, dose line color and mean volume, which were impacted by the change in the dose line position. The applicant provided a present-proposed table of the medical device dossier to the Notified Body, who ultimately included a high-level summary of it in their Notified Body Opinion Report. The positive Notified Body Opinion was received on 05/2024, confirming the compliance with general safety and performance requirements of the Aflibercept 40mg/mL PFS with the new dose line.
The Notified Body Opinion was provided to EMA as supportive documentation for the CMC variation of the integral drug-device combination product and an approval was obtained on 07/2024. Similarly, the applicant provided the Notified Body Opinion to the Turkish Health Authority as supportive documentation for the medical device aspects of the Aflibercept 40mg/mL PFS.

The actual present-proposed situation and the impact on the Turkish CMC dossier of the drug product is reflected in Pp-DL3_ROW. As indicated, the exact position of the dose line was not part of the dossier so far, therefore, the applicant proposed to include a definition of the dose line position in CTD section P.7.02-03 and applied for a variation of type IB (B.II.e.4.c) to register the change accordingly. Dose range, dose line color and mean volume are not specified in the CMC dossier and were therefore neither pointed out in the present-proposed table nor classified as individual changes. However, the underlying change in the position of the dose line was included in the variation application for the CMC dossier.

The change in the dose line position is the result of the applicant undertaking efforts to reduce the variability of dosing and extreme values of expelled drug from the Aflibercept 40mg/mL PFS. Therefore, the lower and upper bounds of the volume delivered by the PFS were reevaluated, and the target delivered dose volume range was adjusted from the absolute minimum and maximum volumes of  0.05 mL – 0.1 mL to 0.045 mL – 0.072 mL based on the currently available clinical evidence. As a consequence, the dose line position on the syringe barrel has been adjusted to consistently obtain a delivered volume between 0.045 mL – 0.072 mL.
The delivered dose volume was tested successfully as part of these design verification activities. It has been proven that the syringe system consistently provides the delivered dose within the acceptable dose range. The results were presented in section P.2.4.04-02.

The change in the position of the dose line and the tightening of the target volume range impact the mean delivered volume and bring the mean closer to the target dose with less variation. The volume is within the lower and upper tolerance limits that were applied during the clinical studies, i.e., 45 µL and 72 µL, respectively. Therefore, there is no impact on efficacy or safety expected due to the change in the mean volume.

The color of the dose line changes from black to red to avoid mix-up at the manufacturing sites during the transition period used for change implementation. The dose line color is not considered to be critical for safe and efficacious use of the Aflibercept 40mg/mL solution for intravitreal injection with the PFS, as the dose line on the syringe is clearly visible and physicians are very well experienced with the usage of prefilled syringes with a dose line regardless of its color.

In summary, the changes in delivered volume range, mean volume and dose line color are not impacting the CMC dossier because they are not detailed in it. However, the changes present an improvement for the drug product as the mean delivered dose volume is closer to what has been tested in the clinic and is now controlled within tighter limits. The position of the dose line and its allowable margins during printing on the glass barrel determine the delivered volume. Therefore, the applicant included the exact position of the dose line in the CMC dossier which ensures appropriate control for the other parameters.

Bayer Response to Question 1:
Please be informed that Microbial purity test is included in both Release Specifications and 
Shelf-life specifications section (P.5.1.01 and P.5.1.02), along with the acceptance criterion 
and the method used. It is also included in the Test procedure section (P.5.2.01).
The medicinal product Diane-35 does not demonstrate antimicrobial activity under the test 
conditions. All ingredients are provided by qualified suppliers and regularly tested for 
microbial purity. The manufacturing process of the drug product is conducted under defined 
cleanliness classes and regularly controlled by appropriate environmental monitoring.
Please find the response below for Microbial Purity with the additional information which 
includes description of sample preparation indicating the diluent, dilution of the medicinal 
product, inoculation method.
Microbial purity:
The method for the microbiological purity is sufficiently described in the Ph. Eur. 2.6.12, 
USP <61> or JP 4.05 (harmonized method). The test for specified microorganisms are 
described in detail in Ph. Eur. 2.6.13, USP <62> or JP 4.05 (harmonized method) as well.
Procedure:
Weigh out not less than 10 g of the test product. Fill up with the appropriate amount of Casein 
soya bean digest broth (CSB) to obtain a 1:10 dilution (solution 1).
For TAMC prepare 2 petri dishes with each 1 mL of solution 1 and fill with 15-20 mL liquid 
Casein soya bean digest agar (CSA) (approx. 45°C). Incubate 3 – 5 days at 30 – 35°C. (Pour-
Plate Method of the Plate-Count method).
For TYMC prepare 2 petri dishes with each 1 mL of solution 1 and fill with 15-20 mL liquid 
Sabouraud-dextrose agar with chloramphenicol (approx. 45°C). Incubate 5 – 7 days at 20 – 
25°C. (Pour-Plate Method of the Plate-Count method).
For the test for absence of Escherichia coli, add 10 mL of solution 1 to 100 mL of Soya bean 
digest broth (CSB) to obtain solution 1.1. Incubate 18 – 24 h at 30 – 35°C. After incubation, 1 
mL of solution 1.1 is diluted in 100 mL MacConkey Broth and incubated 24 - 48 h at 42 -
44°C. After this incubation step, plate an aliquot on MacConkey agar and incubate 18 - 72 h 
at 30 – 35°C.

Question/Consideration:
Question 1
The regulation states that the following test must be performed to implants (Jadelle). We must include the tests in the specifications or provide a justification document.

• Organoleptic characteristics
• Average weight*
• Uniformity of Dosage Units.
• Identification of active ingredient(s)
• Assay potency, concentration or activity of the active ingredient(s)
• Impurities: degradation products or related substances
• Sterility
* The tests described will only be performed when there is a change in the physical characteristics of the dosage form
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1 ( CTD section):
• Organoleptic characteristics
Organoleptic characteristics, predominantly Odor may be applied on oral formulations, especially liquids where sensory attributes impact patient compliance. These tests are not, however, relevant for an implant product, which is inserted into the patient’s arm. This kind of a product does not interact with taste or smell receptors. Only appearance of the product is evaluated visually during the Quality Control of Jadelle implant.

• Average weight*
Average weight of the implant is not determined in the Quality Control of Jadelle, as average weight of a set of two drug cores is regularly determined during the assembly process of Jadelle implant as an in-process control (IPC) measurement. As the homogenous hormone-elastomer mass is extruded to a rod, which outer dimension is controlled, the levonorgestrel amount correlates well with the mass of the core. Therefore core length is controlled by weighing in IPC.

• Uniformity of Dosage Units.
These tests ensure content uniformity in oral dosage forms, but Jadelle implant delivers the drug via controlled release delivery system, not by unit weight -based dosing. Assay test performed for Jadelle implants At release verifies that the amount of drug substance is adequate for the whole usage time of 5 years. In case of Jadelle implant Release Rate testing verifies that the set of 2 implants provides adequate drug delivery over the time, even for 5 years.

• Identification of active ingredient(s)
Identity test will be deleted from the Shelf-life Specifications because it is not considered a stability indicating test. Identity of drug substance cannot alter or change during the shelf-life of a batch. If the identity test would be performed during the Shelf-life it would comply with the requirements set in Release Specification. From that perspective the requirement can be seen to be valid throughout the whole shelf-life of Jadelle, though the test is not specified in Shelf-life Specification.

• Assay potency, concentration or activity of the active ingredient(s)
Assay test performed for Jadelle implants At release verifies that the amount of drug substance is adequate for the whole usage time of 5 years. Naturally, assay of the product is determined during the Shelf-life also in order to verify that no unexpected decrease in the drug substance assay occurs during the Shelf-life. Drug substance assay complying with the specification limits ensures that the amount of drug substance in the product is sufficient for the whole usage time of 5 years.

• Impurities: degradation products or related substances
Due to inherent stability of levonorgestrel, Impurity test parameters will be deleted from Release Specification. The long history of the production has verified that levonorgestrel remains virtually unchanged in the manufacturing process of the drug product, and also during the stability studies. This is demonstrated by comparison of the results for six drug product stability batches to the corresponding drug substance batch results . Comparison table is provided in P.5.6.01 Justification of Specification.
The proposed new impurity test performed by HPLC is superior compared to the current impurity test by TLC. In this context the tightening of the requirement for the Sum of impurities from 2% to 1% ensures effectively the quality of Jadelle throughout the whole shelf-life. The Levonorgestrel drug substance of Jadelle is verified to be very stable. Based on stability studies by TLC the Sum of impurities has remained constantly below the proposed requirement of max 1.0% even though the synthesis impurities have also been taken into account in the analysis. In the prosed HPLC method only actual degradation products, in accordance with the Health Authority guidelines, will be considered.
Jadelle implant has been on the market for more than 30 years already. Hence, the quality characteristics of the product are well known and have been established for a long time already. Due to the known and proven excellent stability of Levonorgestrel Bayer Oy considers it justified to perform the impurity testing for Jadelle implant during the stability studies/shelf-life only.
Impurity testing is not included in Release Specifications of Jadelle, but it is performed during the stability studies for the product. As the results of impurity testing are constantly fulfilling the requirements set at the end of the shelf-life, it is clear that a batch of Jadelle would comply with the requirements if it would be tested for impurities at release.
Organic impurities arising from degradation of the new drug substance and impurities that arise during the manufacturing process for the drug product should be monitored in the new drug product. Acceptance limits should be stated for individual specified degradation products, which may include both identified and unidentified degradation products as appropriate, and total degradation products. Process impurities from the new drug substance synthesis are normally controlled during drug substance testing, and therefore are not included in the total impurities limit. However, when a synthesis impurity is also a degradation product, its level should be monitored and included in the total degradation product limit. When it has been conclusively demonstrated via appropriate analytical methodology, that the drug substance does not degrade in the specific formulation, and under the specific storage conditions proposed in the new drug application, degradation product testing may be reduced or eliminated upon approval by the regulatory authorities.

• Sterility
“Sterility” test parameter will be deleted as redundant from the Shelf-life Specification as sterility testing will be replaced with container closure integrity tests in stability studies. The maintenance of the sterile barrier integrity, and hence the sterility throughout the shelf life is demonstrated during stability studies by testing the integrity of the primary package. This is in accordance with the principles of European Medicines Agency (ref. to EMA Quality of medicines questions and answers: Part 2). This approach is also in accordance with FDA guidance document for industry (February 2008); Container and Closure System Integrity Testing in Lieu of Sterility Testing as a Component of the Stability Protocol for Sterile Products.

Question/Consideration:
Question 9
With regard to the dissolution limits, in view of the results observed, the differences in 
intervals for the limits at D2, D5 and D8 are not justified. In fact, the release of AS is constant 
over time (approximately 20 µg/day - median 21.2 - 22.8 µg for an individual min value of 
17.9 µg (D5) and an individual max value of 27.6 µg (D2)). Consequently, an identical 
interval seems sufficient for the 3 days of testing.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 9 (3.2.P.5.1):
Bayer agrees that the Release rate results at different days are quite similar. There are, 
however, small differences in the Released amount of Levonorgestrel during the 8 days’ 
period. Therefore, slightly different limits are set, and justified, for the specified testing points 
(Days 2, 5 and 8).
A minorly decreasing trend in median of results (22.8 µg - 21.2 µg - 21.2 µg) and a minorly 
decreasing variation of the results (Standard deviation: 2.2 - 1.6 - 1.5) are seen during the 
testing period. These differences justify the small distinction in the calculated, specified limits 
for the three sampling days.
Secondly, the completely new sampling points, Days 2 and 5, and their requirements are 
based solely on the batch data currently available. This data is collected in a reasonably short 
period of time. Therefore, some space is needed for long-term variability arising from routine 
manufacturing and analytics for the complex product in question. Thirdly, the most important 
sampling point of the new method, Day 8, corresponds to the single point, Day 15, of the 
current method and their results are very comparable, almost superimposed. This has been the 
target for the new Release Rate method’s development. Earlier there were limits only for 
individuals, but now the limits are set for the batch average, with the addition of the Level 
testing procedure which is now set for the test.
In general, the new specification is tighter than the current specification as the new limits are 
set for the 3-points whereas the current method had limits for the single point only. The Level 
testing procedure is set applying by Ph. Eur. chapter 2.9.3. including criteria for batch average 
and a tighter Level L3 ranges are set than required by the pharmacopoeia (±15% is applied 
instead of ±20%). In the Level testing procedure, the batch average limits are the limits for 
individuals in the Level L1 and this is a tight criterion and therefore a powerful way to ensure 
the long-term performance of the release rate is maintained.
Based on the above Bayer considers the proposed specification as well justified. The new 
specification can be applied to Mirena IUS without compromising the quality of the 
production batches.

Figure 1:  Plot of Individual Release Rates of the 42 Batches by the 3-Point Method. 
All Results are in µg/day Units. Lines are Fitted between Medians and Averages. 
Green markers are added to visualize the limits set for individuals in the Level L1 
(note, they are the limits for the batch average in Levels L2 and L3).

Source:  P.5.6.01-03 Justification of Specification / Levonorgestrel intrauterine delivery
system 52 mg with inserter (MIRENA) (#007344957; unchanged)
keywords: dissolution; justification of specification; Evaluation of Stability Data; Specification Value; Comparative dissolution

Question/Consideration:
Question 10
With regard to the dissolution limits, an explanation is requested as to why a fairly early point 
(<24 h) was not tested, given that it may be more discriminating.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 10 (3.2.P.5.1):
The first sampling point of the proposed release rate method is Day 2. The test starts on Day 1 
and the cumulative release of the hormone is analyzed from the dissolution solution on Day 2, 
therefore the sample contains all API released during the first 24 hours (no solution is 
discharged, all released material is analyzed). The Day 2 results are slightly higher but very 
similar as the results on Day 5 and 8 (see Question 9) verifying the release during the first 24
hours is stable. Based on tests on IUSs with defects, e.g., membrane defect causing 
abnormally high release (burst) or low hormone load causing abnormally low release, Day 2 
is discriminating, and no separate sampling point earlier than at 24 hours is needed. Also, it 
should be noted that the release rate is specified as micrograms (ca. 20 µg only) of 
levonorgestrel released per day (24h, i.e. µg/day).

Therefore, Bayer Oy considers the proposed testing point selection of the Release Rate 
method justified.
Source:  P.5.6.01-03 Justification of Specification / Levonorgestrel intrauterine delivery
system 52 mg with inserter (MIRENA) (#007344957; unchanged)
keywords: dissolution; Comparative dissolution; justification of specification; Test Procedure; Specification

Question/Consideration:
Question 11
For impurity limits, these must be included in the release and expiry finished product 
specifications for individual impurities (specified and unspecified) and total impurities. 
Therefore, removal of total impurities at release is not acceptable. On the other hand, the 
tightening from max 2.0% to max 1.0% is acceptable.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 11 (3.2.P.5.1):
The test procedure for impurities in Mirena IUS has been revised to include only 
levonorgestrel (LNG) related degradation products, not any more synthesis related impurities 
as the current test. This approach is in line with the EMA guideline CPMP/ICH/2738/99 (ICH 
Q3B). The guideline states: “impurities present in the drug substance need not be monitored 
or specified in the drug product specifications unless they are also degradation products”.
This new test is removed from Release Specifications, i.e. it will be included in the shelf life 
testing only. To support the change, the acceptance limit for the sum of the degradation 
products is tightened from NMT 2.0% to NMT 1.0%. The potential known and unidentified 
LNG degradation products above ≥ 0.1% reporting threshold are included in the test results.
Levonorgestrel is inherently stable. The long history of Mirena IUS has verified that LNG 
remains virtually unchanged in the product manufacture, and during the shelf-life. This is 
demonstrated by comparing results of five MIRENA IUS drug product stability batches with 
the results for corresponding drug substance batches (P.5.6.01). The results for drug 
substance batches in accordance with the Ph. Eur. method indicate actual low amount of the 
degradation products for Mirena IUS as the synthesis related impurities need not to 
be included in the results. This is shown to be true for the drug product batches listed, as the 
maximum result for the Sum of degradation products is only 0.1 %.
The daily dose released from a Mirena IUS is ca. 20 μg. According to the EMA guideline 
CPMP/ICH/2738/99 the identification threshold for impurities in a drug product with a 
maximum daily dose of 1 mg is 1.0% or 5 μg Total Daily Intake (TDI), whichever is lower.
The potential known and unidentified LNG degradation products above 0.1% reporting 
threshold are included in the specifications of Mirena. Calculated as daily intake an impurity 
at 0.1 % level in Mirena provides a daily intake of 0.02 μg only. The level of possible 
unspecified degradation products in Mirena are therefore far below the identification 
threshold of 5 μg TDI. Even the sum of all degradation products calculated as daily intake 
(1.0 % of 20 μg daily dose) is ca. 0.2 μg (TDI) only.
Based on the arguments above the non-inclusion of the impurity test into the release 
specification of Mirena is well justified.

Source:  P.5.6.01_03 Justification of Specification / Levonorgestrel intrauterine delivery
system 52 mg with inserter (MIRENA) (#007344957, unchanged)
keywords: Impurities; Degradation Products; Release Specification; Shelf Life; justification of specification

The following additional explanatory information regarding  the test method “Microbial 
purity” used for Rivaroxaban coated tablets (2.5 mg, 10 mg, 15 mg and 20 mg) will be 
provided in the updated version of the normative document:
Reduce sample mechanically before weighing. Prepare a test solution by suspending 10 g of 
product in 100 mL buffered sodium chloride-peptone solution. From this dilution, transfer 10
mL in another 100 mL buffered sodium chloride-peptone solution, resulting in a final dilution 
of 1:100 (solution 2).
TAMC: Plate 2 x 1 ml solution 2 with casein soya bean digest agar
TYMC: Plate 2 x 1 ml solution 2 with Sabouraud-dextrose agar
Incubate according to Ph. Eur./USP/JP:
TAMC: Incubate 3 – 5 days at 30 – 35°C
TYMC: Incubate 5 – 7 days at 20 – 25°C

For the test for the absence of Escherichia coli, suspend 10 g of the product in 100 mL 
buffered sodium chloride-peptone solution (solution 1). 10 ml of solution 1 is used to 
inoculate 100 mL Casein soya bean digest broth (solution 2) for preincubation at 30-35 °C 
for 18-24 h. After incubation transfer 1 ml of solution 2 to 100 ml MacConkey Broth and 
incubate 18 - 72 h at 30 – 35°C.

The suitability of the counting method was demonstrated in the presence of the product 
according to the harmonized method Ph. Eur./USP/JP (Ph. Eur. 2.6.12). Validation studies 
have been performed with all four dosage strengths. See document Validation of Test for 
Microbial Purity with TRD code T.02.34-02 from dossier section 3.2.P.5 which provides 
additional details about the microbial enumeration test.

Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 6 (CTD section S.3.2, S.4.1, S.4.2):
Please find enclosed the technical registration documents T.03.01 and T.03.03, which document the specification and test procedure adapted to Ph.Eur. Monograph 2932 <Rivaroxaban>. The equivalency of specification and test methods of former in-house and adapted TRDs are discussed in T.03.37.
The monograph 2932 <Rivaroxaban> has become valid in Ph. Eur. 10.3 on 1st of January 2021. With this variation the current specification for Rivaroxaban is updated to reflect the requirements of the new monograph.
• The acceptance criteria for water, organic impurities and sum of all organic impurities are tightened to the Ph. Eur. limits.
• The assay acceptance criterion is adapted to 98.0 – 102.0 %. This is regarded as a formal adaptation to compendial standards.
• Furthermore, acc. to Ph. Eur. monograph, an additional identification via “enantiomeric purity” is required, which has already been met with the test “enantiomeric purity” of current Bayer specification for Rivaroxaban micronized. Therefore, the additional identification test “enantiomeric purity” is introduced to the specification as required by the monograph.
The test procedures currently applied remain unchanged.
• Further, in accordance with monograph 2932 <Rivaroxaban>, no requirement for heavy metals and palladium tests are included. Thus, in compliance with ICH Q3D (Guideline for Elemental Impurities) with the introduction of the Risk Assessment for elemental impurities, the tests for heavy metals and palladium are deleted from the drug substance specification.
The Risk Assessment for elemental impurities according to ICH Q3D (S.3.2.05 - Risk Assessment of Elemental Impurities) demonstrates that the palladium content is consistently found in amounts below the reporting threshold (0.3 ppm), which justifies deleting the test from the specification.
The change is made exclusively to fully comply with the pharmacopoeia. All the tests in the specification correspond to the pharmacopeial standard after the change, except additional supplementary tests.

Question/Consideration:
Question 14
Justify the indication “Do not freeze” in the storage conditions of the medicinal product. Provide relevant supporting data (Decision of the Board of the Eurasian Economic Commission dated 10.05.2018 Nо. 69 “On Approval of the Requirements for Stability Studies of Medicinal Products and Pharmaceutical Substances”). The change must be classified in accordance with Appendix VI of Annex No. 19 of the Rules (submit relevant documentation).
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 14:

Freezing aqueous solutions or suspensions can result in significant alterations to their physical and chemical properties, including but not limited to solubility, viscosity, and other critical characteristics. These changes can adversely impact several important parameters, such as the ability to re-suspend the product effectively, the rate of sedimentation, effectiveness of the microbial preservation and the accuracy of dosing, which are essential for ensuring proper administration and therapeutic efficacy and safety.
Additionally, it is important to consider that the freezing process may lead to the expansion of the liquid within the glass container, potentially causing the glass bottle to crack or shatter.
Given these risks and the potential consequences for product quality and safety, it is imperative to include a warning label stating 'Do not freeze' to prevent any adverse effects on the medicinal product.

Question/Consideration:
Question 10
Transport chain validation is submitted; however, this only covers internal routes inside USA. 
Validation that supports the transportation chain to Chile (or another in the region that 
represents a worst-case situation) must be submitted.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 10 (3.2.R):
The impact of transportation on the final packed drug product was assessed by a shipping 
simulation study. This study was performed according to ASTM D4169 “Standard Practice 
for Performance Testing of Shipping Containers and Systems” and covers global transport by 
truck, ship and aircraft as worst-case conditions. Maximum load and minimum load 
configurations were subjected to the simulations.
The executed study was performed as a shipping simulation to apply controlled and 
reproducible conditions regarding shock, vibration and pressure ensuring that the edges of the 
real-world transport were tested. The simulation approach was chosen to demonstrate product 
stability in a reproducible and controlled worst-case scenario as otherwise selected road 
conditions, driver, route, etc. may limit the outcome of the study or its applicability.
The shipping simulation study provided evidence for maintaining the drug product quality as 
well as functionality and integrity of the finished product samples during worldwide 
transportation. The study is summarized in CTD section R.5.02-01 provided with this 
response.
As the chosen conditions reflect a worst-case shipping scenario that is more challenging than 
a real-world transport, the study supports worldwide transportation including shipments to 
Chile.
Source:  R.5.02-01 Description of Shipping (Transportation) Studies  / Aflibercept
solution 114.3 mg/mL in vial for intravitreous injection (#022991707; new)

Question/Consideration:
Question 5
Based on Container Closure Functionality data in CTD 3.2.P.2, it was concluded that “The 
defined fill volume of the syringe assures that the intended dose of 50 μL can be delivered.”
The low limit of the acceptance criterion for delivered dose volume is 0.045 mL, which is 
below the intended dose of 50 µL (0.050 mL). Please justify how a delivery dose of 0.045 mL 
(low limit of the acceptance criterion for delivered dose volume) meets the intended dose of 
0.050 mL.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 5 ( CTD section):
Maximum efforts have been made to reduce the variability of dosing and extreme values of 
expelled drug from the Aflibercept 40 mg/mL PFS.  The range around the mean, in this case, 
the minimum expelled volume, was chosen because a considerable amount of Bayer Phase 3 
clinical evidence is available on the efficacy and safety of early Aflibercept 40 mg/mL PFS 
generations which had a lower tolerance limit of 0.045 mL.  Specifically, four clinical studies 
within the Eylea clinical development program, each of which has an intended administered
dose of 0.050 mL, provide evidence of the suitability of the lower tolerance limit of 0.045 
mL. It was observed from the use of the previous Aflibercept 40 mg/mL PFS generations that 
the lower bound could be as low as 45 μl without signals of loss of efficacy or safety 
concerns. The efficacy and safety of regular dosing of Aflibercept 40 mg/mL using a PFS 
with a lower tolerance limit of 0.045 mL was shown in the VISTA Study (Phase 3 DME, 
N=466), the VIBRANT Study (Phase 3 BRVO, N=183), VGFT-OD-0702 (Phase 2 nAMD, 
long-term N=323) and the VIEW 1 Extension Study (Phase 3b wAMD, N=323).  Based on 
the currently available evidence, it is concluded that the positive benefit-risk ratio of 
Aflibercept 40 mg/mL is not altered when administered with a PFS with a lower limit of 
acceptance of 0.045 mL.

Question/Consideration:
Question 14
Biological Characterization: The firm has to submit the biological characterization in specific 
such as specific activity/potency.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 14 (Module 3: S.3.1 and P.2.2):
In the section P.2.2 under product development for specific activity and potency, details of 
characterization of drug substance has been included. Potency Measured by a One-Stage 
Coagulation Assay, Coagulation Potency, Study to Set the “Chromogenic–Adjusted (CS-ADJ)” 
Labelled Potency, and Study to Set the “Chromogenic–Adjusted (CS-ADJ)” Labelled Potency.
The studies concludes that results obtained by physicochemical analyses for each clinical and 
conformance DP lot using intrinsic fluorescence, far UV circular dichroism and differential 
scanning calorimetry show all lots to have equivalent conformational structure and thermal 
stability. It is also concluded that results are comparable to those obtained for the licensed 
rFVIII-FS product.
Microflow imaging analyses for study of subvisible particles show that the particle 
concentrations in the 2-10 μm size range present in the clinical, conformance and reference 
standard lot were all comparable in magnitude, with similar vial to vial variability. A significant 
proportion of the particles measured appear to be silicone oil droplets due to contact of the 
lyophilized cake with the stopper. There is no observed increase in particles related to storage 
under shelf-life or accelerated conditions.
With respect to biochemical characterization of the molecule, the results of the thrombin and 
FXa activation studies and FIXa and vWF binding studies indicate functional activity of the 
rFVIII product, with profiles and results that are consistent with the structure of the rFVIII 
molecule. All clinical and conformance DP lots have comparable results to the Product 
Reference Standard and the licensed rFVIII-FS lot.
The comparisons of the Chromogenic assay with the One-Stage Coagulation assay, tested under 
a variety of conditions, indicate that the assays are well aligned regardless of standards used. 
While the initial data (conducted with 3 lots of Kogenate–FS and 4 lots of BAY 81-8973) 
indicated the ratio of the CS to OS results was 1.23, further testing over the years, using a 
variety of standards and assignments, indicates the assay results are closer together with the 
ratio being approximately 1.1.
In the section S.3.1 Biological characterization tests for potency like  One-Stage Coagulation 
Potency (Relative to Chromogenic Potency) is performed, and it concludes that Clinical and 
conformance lots of BAY 81-8973 have expected protein size distribution, backbone sequence, 
mass, disulfide bond linkages and post-translational modifications, including glycan structures, 
sialylation and tyrosine sulfation. Physicochemical properties, including conformation profiles, 
and biological properties including binding, activation and potency, are also as expected relative 
to both product reference standard and rFVIII-FS.

LC-MS Analysis of Thrombin Digests was performed and the results concludes that there is no 
significant difference in results for activity and binding were observed for lot 270LP3G.
Section S.3.1 In the clinical development of BAY 81-8973 a study was conducted to test the 
BAY 81-8973 DP lots by each of two potency assays; the Chromogenic (CS) assay used for 
release of BAY 81-8973 and the One-stage (OS) Coagulation assay being used at that time for 
the release of the predecessor product Kogenate (rFVIII-FS). This assessment was used to set 
the labeled potency for the “Chromogenic – Adjusted (CS-ADJ)” arm of the clinical trial.
The OS Coagulation assay was subsequently used to test each of the DP production lots as 
extended characterization. In addition, a special study was conducted to compare the CS with 
the OS results using the same standard assigned against the WHO International Standard. There 
are 2 sets of results, one using the WHO 7th International Standard and one using the WHO 8th 
International Standard.
The comparisons of the CS assay with the OS assay, tested under a variety of conditions, 
indicate that the assays are well aligned regardless of standards used. While the initial data 
indicated that the mean of the ratio of the CS to OS results was 1.23, further testing over the 
years indicates the assay results are closer together with the ratio being approximately 1.1.
Section P.2.2.04 provide details with respect to the biochemical characterization of the 
molecule, the results of the thrombin and FXa activation studies and FIXa and vWF binding 
studies indicate functional activity of the rFVIII product, with profiles and results that are 
consistent with the structure of the rFVIII molecule. All clinical and conformance DP lots have 
comparable results to the Product Reference Standard and the licensed rFVIII-FS lot.
Additional characterization information is provided in the P.2.2.04.

Question/Consideration:
Question 15
Specifications: The firm has to provide specification of the DS combined, whether test of 
distribution of N-Glycan is not part of the specification.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 15 (Module 3: S.3.1 and S.4.1):
The Specifications for the drug substance are presented in S.4.1-01.
Multiple glycosylation sites are present on the BAY 81-8973 structure, predominantly within 
the B-domain of the molecule. It is known (Bovenschen, N. et al) that sialylation of the terminal
galactose residues on the multiple N-glycan structures within the protein are important in the 
half-life of the molecule. Since glycan sialylation can affect the clearance of the molecule in 
the body, this attribute is tested as part of release specifications. Therefore, the ratio of 
sialylation is used as quantitative parameter for the distribution of N-Glycans of BAY 81-8973. 
The specification for the Sialylation ratio has been obtained from correlation analysis of this 
ratio to the sialylation ‘Capping’ values determined during clinical and conformance lot testing. 
The value of 0.8 corresponds to a ‘Capping’ value of approximately 89%.

The current shelf life of the drug substance is 24 months based on long-term stability data from 
three conformance batches of BAY 81-8973 Drug Substance in ethylene vinyl acetate (EVA) 
bags at the real-time storage conditions of ≤-36°C as well as at an alternative storage condition 
of ≤-60°C.

81-8973 Drug Substance is stable and meets all acceptance criteria when stored at the real-time 
storage condition of ≤-36°C as well as at the alternative storage condition of ≤-60°C.
As per ICH guidelines, accelerated and stress studies were performed at 5°C and 25°C, 
respectively. The results are presented in S.7.3.01-03.

development/stability data Query: The firm has to provide the Justification of final

Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 26 (Module 3: P.1 and P.2.2.):
The development objective was to provide a parenteral formulation of BAY 81-8973 drug 
product (DP) suitable for intravenous injection with optimum long-term storage stability and 
high patient safety. A lyophilized dosage form for injection has been selected as the dosage 
form.
The BAY 81-8973 drug product is designed to have the same formula strengths, 
container/closure, and fill sizes (2.5 mL and 5 mL) as the predecessor product known by the 
names of KOGENATE Bayer, Kogenate FS, Helixate, Helixate FS, Helixate NEXGEN and 
Helixate N2V (rFVIII-FS).
The licensed rFVIII-FS product formulation has shown satisfactory stability with at least 30 
months of shelf-life at 2-8°C and has demonstrated an excellent safety profile for patient use. 
It was therefore decided that the identical platform formulation was used in the clinical trials 
and continuing into the commercial application. The composition of the drug product 
containing all ingredients, quality grade, function and the amount needed for each dosage 
strength is presented in P.1.02.
In the composition of Kovaltry Glacial Acetic Acid is used to adjust pH as required, quantity 
of rFVIII is based on nominal fill volume i.e. 2.5 mL for 250, 500, and 1000 IU potencies; 5 
mL for 2000 and 3000 IU potencies. Quantities of Sucrose, Histidine, Glycine, Sodium 
Chloride, Calcium Chloride Dihydrate, and Polysorbate 80 are based on actual fill amount i.e. 
2.73 g/vial for 250, 500, and 1000 IU potencies; 5.25 g/vial for 2000 and 3000 IU potencies.

Question/Consideration:
Question 37
Consistency and analysis of batches: 1. The firm has to state why SE-HPLC is not one of the 
parameter for purity and impurities - aggregates. 2. The firm is required to submit APQR for 
last three years (2021, 2022 and 2023) for DS and DP.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 37 (Module 3: S.3.2):
1. The BAY 81-8973 species classified as product-related impurities are dissociated free
FVIII light chains (LC) and aggregates. The company confirms that these are 
quantitatively analyzed by SE-HPLC and are included in the specifications of DS and 
DP. The chromatogram consists of 4 regions.  
Region 1: high molecular weight (HMW) peak representing aggregates in BAY 81-
8973 contains a low level of both FVIII chains.  
Region 2: The main SEC peak contains the heterogeneous glycoforms of the intact BAY 
81-8973 molecule and active rFVIII that has been partially cleaved in the C-terminal 
region of the heavy chain B-domain.  
Region 3: The peak also contains active BAY 81-8973, with the majority of the peak 
identified as the fully B-domain deleted (BDD) material, not a product related impurity.  
Region 4: Non-complexed (free) light chain elutes in the Region 4 peak. 
For DS only Region 1 and 4 have a specification and for the DP all 4 region have 
specifications. 
2. As requested APQR for last three years (2021/22, 2022/23 and 2023/24) for DS and DP
are provided in the response.
