Question/Consideration:
Question 3
General description and history of starting material (Strain,Gene Construct, System of 
seed/Cell Line/master/working banks,Embryonated eggs and other cell substrates).
Answer/Response:
Mammalian cell line baby hamster kidney 21 (BHK-21) acquired from the American Type
Culture Collection (ATCC catalog number CCL-10) was used as the parent cell line, and
tested negative for microbial growth, mycoplasma and non-endogenous virus (adventitious
virus and mouse minute virus) before being used for the cell line development as described in
S.2.3.54 Source, History and Generation of Cell Substrate.

Construction of the expression system (BHK-21 clone W20-19-38 transfected with expression
vector pBET14A-PEG14W) for the production of B-domain deleted recombinant Factor VIII
(BDD-rFVIII) variant K1804C is described in S.2.3.54 Source, History and Generation of
Cell Substrate. Site-directed mutagenesis was performed to make the K1804C mutation by
introducing cysteine in place of lysine at position 1804 in the BDD FVIII. The expression
system or vector does not have a quality certificate. The DNA construct and vectors were
created and verified as described in S.2.3.54.
Post-translational modification of the BDD-rFVIII protein is inherent in BHK-21 mammalian
cell line and not introduced as a genetic mutation. Endotoxin production is not expected from
a mammalian cell line. Endotoxin level is monitored and maintained within acceptable limit
in the upstream and downstream manufacturing process.
Preparation and characterization of the Master Cell Bank (MCB) and Working Cell Bank
(WCB) are described in S.2.3.50 Cell Banking System, Characterization and Testing - Master
Cell Bank and S.2.3.51 Cell Banking System, Characterization and Testing - Working Cell
Bank, respectively. The description includes the culture medium used in growing the cells for
the preparation of the MCB (S.2.3.50) and WCB (S.2.3.51). Culture conditions (process
parameters controlled and performance attributes measured) for the cell expansion step
described in S.2.2.62 Manufacturing Process - Process Controls for fermentation/cell culture,
including the initial or seeding cell density, incubation temperature, pH, culture time or
passage duration and cell viability, were followed in growing the cells prior to the
cryopreservation step.

Analyses performed to characterize and establish quality of the MCB were non-viral tests
(identity, mycoplasma and sterility) and viral tests (in vitro, in vivo and species specific 
nonendogenous
adventitious agents, and retrovirus and other endogenous virus) as described in
S.2.3.50. Analyses performed to characterize and establish quality of the WCB were nonviral
tests (identity, mycoplasma and sterility), while analyses performed for WCB end of
production (EOP) cells characterization were non-viral tests (mycoplasma and sterility) and
viral tests (in vitro, in vivo and species specific non-endogenous adventitious agents, and
retrovirus and other endogenous virus) as described in S.2.3.51.
No animal or human derived materials were used in the medium for the preparation of the
MCB and WCB. These cell banks can be regarded as safe with respect to the risk of
contamination by potential transmissible spongiform encephalopathy (TSE) agents, mitigated
through raw material selection and control, as described in A.2.01 TSE Assessment.

performance attribute ranges, and can consistently produce product meeting in-process and 
release specifications. The process steps covered in this validation include cell expansion, 15 
L scale-up bioreactor and 200 L production bioreactor operations.
The validation protocol was designed to cover the maximum process duration (maximum cell 
culture age in cell days) and capacity for production (maximum number of 200 L bioreactors 
in parallel). Critical process parameters (CPPs) and key process parameters (KPP) were 
controlled within operating ranges, and process performance attributes and critical quality 
attributes (CQA) were monitored to demonstrate the consistency and reproducibility of the 
cell culture process.
All runs were maintained within defined process parameters with the exception of the process 
excursions that were assessed and resolved through the deviation management process and 
found to have no impact on the validated state of the process. All CPPs and KPPs were
assessed and deemed acceptable. All acceptance criteria for CQAs were met. The individual 
and collective impact of all deviations was evaluated and it was determined that there was no 
adverse impact to the overall outcome of the validation. Together, this data demonstrates the 
consistency and reproducibility of the cell culture process. Based upon the result of the 
validation, the process is considered to have been successfully validated.
As described in S.2.5.71 Process Validation – Harvest and Isolation, a full-scale conformance 
campaign was conducted in order to demonstrate that the Damoctocog Alfa Pegol harvest and 
isolation processes can be maintained within established operating parameters and 
consistently produce product meeting in-process and release specifications. The harvest 
process is implemented using a continuous cell separation unit operation and the isolation 
process is implemented using a membrane adsorber unit operation.
The prospective validation was designed to cover the maximum cell culture duration (75 cell 
days) and capacity for production (six 200 L bioreactors operating in parallel). Two 200 L 
bioreactor batches (originating from two different vial thaws) were run up to 75 cell days 
(days from vial thaw) in order to validate the maximum cell age. The protocol also called for 
six 200 L bioreactors to be harvested in parallel for a minimum of 7 days to demonstrate that 
the process was in control at maximum capacity. The harvests from all 200 L bioreactors 
were continuously clarified and then processed by membrane adsorber chromatography to 
MAEF. Of the 232 MAEF batches generated during the conformance campaign, 226 were 
successfully produced (97%). Six of the 232 MAEF batches were either partially or fully 
discarded. Each incident was investigated and determined not to impact the validation.
As described in S.2.5.81 Process Validation – Purification, a full-scale conformance Drug 
Substance (DS) manufacturing campaign was conducted to demonstrate that the Damoctocog 
Alfa Pegol purification processes can be maintained within established operating parameters 
and consistently produce Drug Substance (DS) meeting in-process and release specifications.
The purification process starts with the thaw of frozen Membrane Adsorber Eluate 
Formulated (MAEF) and ends with the transfer of the blast frozen DS to storage.
The process validation protocol was designed to evaluate purification of DS manufactured 
from material produced during a maximum 75 day cell culture campaign. Critical and key 
process parameters were controlled within the defined ranges and process performance 
attributes were monitored to demonstrate the consistency and reproducibility of the 
purification process. Data generated were used to demonstrate that the commercial 
manufacturing process for the production of Damoctocog Alfa Pegol is consistent, 
reproducible, and produces DS material meeting pre-defined quality attributes for identity, 
quality, safety, purity, potency, strength, and composition. All conformance batches met 
process validation acceptance criteria. Of the fifteen DS batches manufactured during the 
process validation, four were placed on stability.

Chromatography resin use life and tangential flow filtration (TFF) membrane use life 
validation protocols were executed concurrently with the process validation, during which the 
performance and cleanability of each of the chromatography columns and TFF membranes 
used for DS purification at the commercial scale were evaluated.
All acceptance criteria were met with the exception of the deviations which were assessed and 
were determined not to adversely impact the outcome of the validation. During validation of 
the Damoctocog Alfa Pegol DS manufacturing process, CPPs and KPPs were controlled 
within defined process ranges; performance attributes (e.g., step yields) were within defined 
process limits; DS test results met all acceptance criteria demonstrating that the commercial 
purification process results in in-process intermediates and DS meeting in-process and final 
release specifications. The manufacturing process has demonstrated robustness and 
consistency and has been successfully validated.
Additional information about process parameters and in-process tests is provided in S.2.4.60 
In-Process Control of Critical Steps – Fermentation/Cell Culture, S.2.4.70 In-Process 
Control of Critical Steps – Harvest and Isolation and in S.2.4.80 In-Process Control of 
Critical Steps – Purification. As described in these documents, the cell culture, isolation and 
purification manufacturing processes do not include reprocessing steps.
Information pertaining to the analytical procedures and method validations have been 
provided in CTD sections S.4.2 and S.4.3.

Question 7
Biological Characterization data not submitted. Please submit data for biological 
characterization w.r.t. biological activity, binding assay, activation in comparison with 
reference std.
Answer/Response:
The Damoctocog Alfa Pegol conformance run Drug Substance and drug product batches were 
evaluated in an extended characterization program for primary, secondary and tertiary protein 
structure characteristics compared to the Phase 3 clinical material. The testing included SDS-
PAGE analysis for evaluation of the heterodimer of BDD-rFVIII with PEGylation on the A3 
domain in the heavy chain. Peptide mapping using LC/MS techniques for protein sequence 
identification, verification of post-translational modification such as tyrosine sulfation, N-
linked and O-link glycosylation, disulfide bonds, and methionine oxidation. Secondary and 
tertiary structure evaluation were conducted using physical chemical techniques such as UV 
circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy, fluorescence spectroscopy, and differential scanning 
calorimetry (DCS). All of the testing results show that the Drug Substance and drug product 
batches produced in the commercial facility are comparable to the Phase 3 clinical material 
(S.2.5.03).
Characterization of the impurities included host cell proteins (HCP) by SDS PAGE gels and 
westerns, aggregates by SEC-MALS and AFFF-MALS, trace elements (metals) by ICP-MS, 
monosaccharides, API purity by SDS-PAGE gels, tryptic map LC/MS and thrombin map 
LC/MS, and PEGylation site ID by N-terminal sequencing all confirm that the commercial 
material is comparable to the Phase 3 clinical material (S.2.5.03).
Finally, the commercial API in the conformance drug product batches were compared to the 
Phase 3 clinical drug product batches in different functional testing methods. This included 
binding to vWF, one-stage coagulation potency testing, thrombin activation, FXa activation, 
FIXa binding, and APC inactivation. All of the functional characterization results show that 
the conformance batches are comparable to the Phase 3 clinical batches (S.2.5.03).

Question/Consideration:
Question 9
The firm is required to submit the protocol and report of validation of analytical testing 
parameters related to identity, purity and potency.
Answer/Response:
Reverse Phase High Performance Liquid Chromatography RP-HPLC
(2.5 µm)
The purpose of this procedure is to determine the purity and the ratio of light chain relative to
heavy chain in Damoctocog Alfa Pegol DS samples. The purpose of the assay is also to
determine the identity of DS. The method is used for testing release and stability DS samples
from commercial manufacturing.
The assay is a Reverse Phase High Performance Liquid Chromatography (RP-HPLC) method
that uses fluorescence detection. Damoctocog Alfa Pegol is a heterodimer composed of a
heavy chain (HC) and a PEGylated light chain (LC). This procedure uses RP-HPLC
separation on a non-porous polymeric column to separate the principle components of
Damoctocog Alfa Pegol preparations according to their hydrophobic properties. Fluorescence
detection is used and the percent peak area of LC and HC proteins is determined. All other
protein peaks are integrated as impurities. Damoctocog Alfa Pegol purity, LC/HC ratio and
identity are reported.

Reverse Phase High Performance Liquid Chromatography RP-HPLC
(10 µm)
The purpose of this procedure is to determine the purity and the ratio of light chain relative to
heavy chain in Damoctocog Alfa Pegol Drug Substance (DS) samples. The purpose of the
assay is also to determine the identity of DS. The method is used for testing release and
stability DS samples from clinical and conformance manufacturing.
The assay is a Reverse Phase High Performance Liquid Chromatography (RP-HPLC) method
that uses fluorescence detection. Damoctocog Alfa Pegol is a heterodimer composed of a
heavy chain (HC) and a PEGylated light chain (LC). This procedure uses RP-HPLC
separation on a C18 polymeric column to separate the principle components of Damoctocog
Alfa Pegol preparations according to their hydrophobic properties. Fluorescence detection is
used and the percent peak area of LC and HC proteins is determined. All other protein peaks
are integrated as impurities. Damoctocog Alfa Pegol purity, LC/HC ratio and identity are
reported.

High Performance Liquid Chromatography Size Exclusion Chromatography (5
μm)
The High Performance Liquid Chromatography Size Exclusion Chromatography (HPLC SEC
5 μm) assay is a method for the determination of total protein and molecular size distribution
in Damoctocog Alfa Pegol DS samples. This assay is used to estimate the relative amounts of
high molecular weight protein (HMW) and low molecular weight protein (LMW) in
Damoctocog Alfa Pegol DS samples. This assay is used for testing release and stability
samples from commercial manufacturing.
The HPLC SEC (5 μm) procedure separates the principle components of Damoctocog Alfa
Pegol preparations according to their hydrodynamic volume, or molecular size, and is capable
of resolving proteins over a wide range of molecular weights. Total protein concentration is
determined by regression analysis on a linear fit standard curve of the total integrated peak
area versus protein concentration, calibrated with a Damoctocog Alfa Pegol reference
standard. The high molecular weight protein region elutes prior to the product main peak.
The integrated peak areas with retention times in the high molecular weight proteins window
are used to calculate and report the relative percent (%) area of high molecular weight product
related impurities, including aggregates. The low molecular weight product related impurities
include a portion of the main peak tail side and a protein peak eluting after the main peak in
the chromatogram.

High Performance Liquid Chromatography Size Exclusion Chromatography (10
μm)
The High Performance Liquid Chromatography Size Exclusion Chromatography (HPLC SEC
10 μm) assay is a method for the determination of total protein and molecular size distribution
in Damoctocog Alfa Pegol DS samples. This assay is used to estimate the relative amounts of
high molecular weight protein (HMW) and low molecular weight protein (LMW) in
Damoctocog Alfa Pegol DS samples. This assay is used for testing release and stability
samples from clinical and conformance manufacturing.
The HPLC SEC (10 μm) method separates the principal components of the Damoctocog Alfa
Pegol preparations, which includes intact conjugate active ingredient and product related
impurities such as low molecular weight (LMW) protein species, non-conjugated
rFVIII-BDD, free light chain, free heavy chain and high molecular weight (HMW) protein
species including aggregates. Separation of these components is dependent on the
hydrodynamic volume or molecular size of the individual species. Low molecular weight
impurities are reported as the sum of the relative percent peak areas of all proteins smaller
than intact Damoctocog Alfa Pegol. The high molecular weight impurities are reported as the
sum of the relative percent peak areas of all proteins larger than the intact Damoctocog Alfa
Pegol. Total protein concentration is determined by regression analysis on a linear fit
standard curve of the total integrated peak area versus protein concentration, calibrated with a
Damoctocog Alfa Pegol reference standard.

Tryptic Digest Peptide Map
The Tryptic Digest Peptide Map (peptide map) assay is a procedure by which Damoctocog
Alfa Pegol DS samples are digested with trypsin and analyzed by Reversed Phase High
Performance Liquid Chromatography (RP-HPLC) to evaluate the protein for identity. The
assay determines identity of DS, distinguishing Damoctocog Alfa Pegol from Bayer’s full
length recombinant Factor VIII (rFVIII) products, BAY 81-8973 and Antihemophilic Factor
(recombinant) Formulated with Sucrose (rFVIII-FS).
The peptide map assay enzymatically cleaves Damoctocog Alfa Pegol into a number of
peptides which can then be separated and characterized in order to confirm the identity of a
protein. In this assay, the Damoctocog Alfa Pegol is denatured and then digested by the
protease trypsin. Separation of the peptides in the digested sample is achieved by RP-HPLC,
and the eluted peptides are visualized with fluorescence detection. The resulting
chromatographic profiles are integrated and the ratios between certain key peptides are
calculated and reported. This method compares the internal Damoctocog Alfa Pegol peak
ratios for peaks 8, 14, and 19 to those from a reference standard analyzed in the same run.
This information is utilized to confirm the identity of the Damoctocog Alfa Pegol protein, and
allows for its differentiation from other full-length rFVIII products.

PEG-Maleimide
This qualitative analysis method is used to identify and control the residual amount of a
process-related impurity, Polyethylene glycol-Maleimide (PEG-Maleimide), in Damoctocog
Alfa Pegol DS samples.
The assay is a Reverse Phase High Performance Liquid Chromatography with Charged
Aerosol Detection (RP-HPLC-CAD) method. It uses a water/acetonitrile gradient with
Trifluoroacetic Acid on a reverse phase HPLC column. Protein is precipitated by addition of
acetone and the resultant supernatant is dried down and analyzed by reverse phase HPLC.
The presence of trace PEG-Maleimide is determined by comparing the response (peak area)
of sample to the lowest response of the 10 ppm PEG-Maleimide Assay Working Standard
injections.

Potency and Content
The chromogenic potency assay is used to measure the recombinant factor VIII (rFVIII)
activity in release and stability samples of Damoctocog Alfa Pegol DS and MAEF
intermediate. The measured values (IU/mL) of the DS are then used, along with the total
protein concentration (µg/mL), to calculate the specific activity (IU/mg) of the DS.
The chromogenic reaction consists of two consecutive steps where the intensity of color is
proportional to the Factor VIII activity. In the first step, Factor X is activated to Factor Xa by
Factor IXa with its cofactor, Factor VIIIa, in the presence of optimal amounts of calcium ions
and phospholipids. Excess amounts of Factor X are present such that the rate of activation of
Factor X is solely dependent on the amount of Factor VIII. In the second step, Factor Xa
hydrolyzes the chromogenic substrate to yield a chromophore and the color intensity is
determined photometrically at 405 nm. The validity of the assay is confirmed by parallelism
of the standard curve with the sample dilutions and sample potency is calculated using a linear
regression statistical method against the in-house reference standard. The in-house reference
standard has an assigned value based on the World Health Organization (WHO) International
Standard for FVIII concentrates. Activity is reported in International Units per mL (IU/mL).
The method is performed using a robotic liquid handling platform. The robotic system
performs dilutions, places the materials into a 96-well test plate and performs a series of
reagent additions and incubations to achieve the chromogenic reaction. The completed
reaction is then read by a plate reader and results are uploaded to a validated data analysis
system that calculates the samples' FVIII potency (IU/mL).

Host Cell Protein
The purpose of this procedure is to determine the levels of baby hamster kidney (BHK) Host
Cell Protein (HCP) present in Damoctocog Alfa Pegol Q Eluate samples, an in-process step
prior to pegylation, using a Homogeneous Time-Resolved Fluorescence (HTRF)
immunoassay.

Host Cell Protein (Specific)
The purpose of this procedure is to determine the levels of baby hamster kidney (BHK) Host
Cell Protein (HCP) present in Damoctocog Alfa Pegol Q Eluate samples, an in-process step
prior to pegylation, using a Homogeneous Time-Resolved Fluorescence (HTRF)
immunoassay.

Mouse IgG
The purpose of this procedure is to determine the level of residual C7F7 mouse
immunoglobulin (mIgG) present in Damoctocog Alfa Pegol Q Eluate samples.

Host Cell DNA
The purpose of this method is to measure the amount of residual host cell DNA from Baby
Hamster Kidney (BHK) cell lines in Damoctocog Alfa Pegol MAVF samples using
Real-Time Quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR).

Mouse Minute Virus
The purpose of this procedure is to detect the presence of Mice Minute Virus (MMV) DNA in
BHK cell culture samples from the Damoctocog Alfa Pegol manufacturing process by
polymerase chain reaction (PCR).

Silver Stain Analysis
The silver stain analysis is used as an identity test to confirm the identity of incoming bagged
Damoctocog Alfa Pegol DS relative to other rFVIII products after receiving from off-site
storage.

According to the provisions of numeral 4.2, of the RTCA of stability studies in force, the frequency of the analyses must be carried out and presented in the study in the following periods of time: INITIAL-INTERMEDIATE-12 MONTHS- 24MONTHS-36 MONTHS-48 MONTHS-60 MONTHS, the latter being the maximum period of useful life granted to a drug by this regulatory entity. Question/Consideration:
Question 1
A) In the process validation of Regeneron Ireland, Justification of acceptance criteria of
protein concentration in UF/DF process
B) TMP limit and result of UF/DF process in all batches
C) Hold time data of Intermediate (microbial and physicochemical stability data per

Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1 (3.2.S.2.5):
A) In the FDS process validation of Regeneron Ireland, Justification of acceptance
criteria of protein concentration in UF/DF process
During manufacturing process development, the acceptable manufacturing range for the target 
final concentrated pool (FCP) protein concentration was established based on development 
and characterization studies, and historical manufacturing experience. A high protein 
concentration in the FCP would be diluted through the sucrose adjustment and formulation 
unit operations to acceptable levels. A low protein concentration at the FCP stage could cause 
over-dilution during formulation, potentially leading to a formulated drug substance (FDS) 
that is below the specified range. The established range for commercial manufacturing (165-
184 g/L) is considered a non-critical process condition to be met during routine manufacture 
to ensure process consistency.
Typically in Biotech processes, the final concentrated pool after ultrafiltration/diafiltration, is 
set clearly higher than the actual minimal needed concentration.

In addition to the target FCP protein concentration, the lower limit for the FCP protein 
concentration was then set and classified as a critical quality attribute (CQA).
The CQA (≥ 128.8 g/L) is the minimum FCP protein concentration necessary to ensure that 
the material produced will have a concentration that is compatible with further product 
dilution and formulation steps. Additional details are provided in Table 1 below.
Following the ultrafiltration/diafiltration (UF/DF) unit operation, during the formulation step, 
there is a dilution due to the addition of the sucrose buffer, excipient buffer and dilution 
buffer. The acceptance criteria (≥ 128.8 g/L) was established as the minimal concentration 
needed at the FCP stage to ensure that the FDS will be within the final release specifications 
(103 - 126 g/L) after the addition of the three buffers.

Question/Consideration:
Question 19
S.2.2 Manufacturing process and process control
It is noted that this higher strength share the same manufacturing process as the registered 
lower concentration. Please highlight if the changes to the manufacturing process differs.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 19 (3.2.S.2; 3.2.P.1):
Aflibercept solution 40 mg/ml and Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL share the same drug 
substance intermediate (DSI) and the manufacturing process until the DSI stage is identical 
(as described in S.2.2.02_022971469_03).
The subsequent manufacturing steps are similar but there are differences related to the higher 
protein concentration and different composition as summarized below:
• More DSI is used as starting material for Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL FDS 
compared to Aflibercept solution 40 mg/ml drug substance (DS)/formulated bulk (FB) 
due to higher concentration of protein in the new strength. The amount of DSI used 
during process validation for Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL FDS is included in 
S.2.5.01_022972866_02.
• The size exclusion column is run for more cycles (as there is more material to 
process) as shown in S.2.6.01_022972998_01.
• The tangential flow filter concentrates the product to a higher concentration (160 – 
200 g/L vs. 55 g/L) due to the higher protein concentration for Aflibercept solution 
114.3 mg/mL FDS  as described in S.2.2.02_022972987_02.
• The final drug substance concentration is different (114.3 g/L vs. 40 g/L) as described 
in the product composition in P.1.01_022982760_01.
• The formulation uses different excipient buffer due to differences in the composition 
(P.1.01_022971855_01).
• There is no isolated unformulated DS in the Aflibercept solution 114.3. mg/mL 
process which corresponds to the Aflibercept 40 mg/mL drug substance, only a direct 
formulation from DSI to FDS, and the formulation process is described in Module 
3.2.S.2.2 (S.2.2.02_022972987_02). However, for the approved Aflibercept solution 
40 mg/mL the unformulated DS is described in Module 3.2.S and considered the final 
drug substance, whereas the formulation is described in Module 3.2.P and the 
formulated bulk (FB) is considered a DP intermediate from dossier perspective.

Question/Consideration:
Question 27
S7: Stability
a. Please explain why endotoxin content, bioburden, polysorbate content and osmolality
are not tested for stability study.
b. It is noted that the protein content increases to more than the limit when stored at 25C.
Please explain.

c. It is noted that the purity results while stored at the accelerated conditions. Please
explain.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 27 (3.2.S.7):
a) Endotoxin content, bioburden, polysorbate content, and osmolality are not included in the 
stability studies as those are not stability-indicating parameters and do not change at real time 
storage condition of - 80°C over the shelf life of 36 months.

b) An increase in total protein concentration of up to about 20 mg/mL was observed for all 
lots; this is likely due to evaporative loss of water from the polycarbonate vials when stored at 
the accelerated condition. The real time storage condition is -80°C and no change in protein 
content was observed until end of shelf life.

c) As aggregation and fragmentation are the main degradation pathways it is expected that 
those impurities will specifically increase under the accelerated condition. The real time 
storage condition is -80°C and no meaningful change was observed for these parameter until 
end of shelf life.

mg/mL (#022972888; amended)

solution against a defined reference solution. The reference solution is getting more diluted

reported for the batches in P.5.4.01-01 is more stringent and complies with the acceptance

Question/Consideration: (iv) the visual inspection is not included as part the QC testing, please clarify and justify the alternative sites.
Answer/Response:
Visual inspection is a GMP required step to provide a 100% control in order to eliminate all damaged or defective PFS, which shares similar characteristics with a quality control testing.
During the steps conventionally summarized under “Manufacturing”, there is direct access to the medicinal product itself as long as it is not yet in its primary packaging. An error (e.g. mixing up excipients) could have massive impact on the composition of the medicinal product.
In contrast, visual inspection concerns the primary packaged medicinal product without direct access to the product. The visual inspection is a control measure which eliminates damaged or broken PFS. In this respect it is similar to quality control testing which collects information about the product without altering it.
Vetter Pharma Fertigung GmbH is a highly skilled contact manufacturing organization (CMO) with a large number of clients and a high workload. To ensure the uninterrupted manufacturing and associated testing, it is required to establish redundant capacities in case of non-availability of resources at one site. Non-availability can be the result of planned maintenance or unexpected equipment failure.
Especially biotech products need rapid processing due to the sensitivity of the protein and the resulting need of reduced time out of refrigeration (TOR). The visual inspection is a time-consuming process and cannot be pushed out arbitrarily but requires rapid execution. Therefore, the establishment of alternative sites is mandatory. Once a manufacturing process is started, it must be guaranteed that the final product is not jeopardized by the failure of any device or apparatus. It must be made sure the process and all its required tests can be completed as the limited availability of resources would have a high impact on safe market supply. This is why Vetter Pharma Fertigung GmbH as a CMO has contractual obligations to keep alternative sites available for these cases to ensure robust supply continuity at all times, and all sites are governed by the same Quality Assurance system to make sure a change of sites would still warrant the same result.
keywords: QC testing; Manufacturer; Site Responsibilities; facilities and equipment; Control of Drug Product

Question 1:
3.2.P.2.2 – Dissolution method (initial Q1): The use of prior knowledge of the development 
of a dissolution method should correlate with the pharmaceutical form being developed. Film-
coated tablet formulation and granules for oral suspension of Riociguat differ. Thus, the full

3.2.P.2.02-01 (with data presented in Tables 4-2 to 4-6), showing an average drug release 
between 93 – 100% in 15 minutes using the current QC method (Phosphate buffer pH 6.8 
with 0.1% SLS), the dissolution acceptance criterion of Q = 80% in 15 minutes is considered 
too widely when the principles of “Reflection paper on the dissolution specification for 
generic solid oral immediate release products with systemic action” are considered. You are

Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1 (P.2.2.01, P.2.2.02, P.5.1.01, P.5.1.02, P.5.2.01, P.5.2.02, 
P.5.3.02, P.5.3.21, P.5.4.01, P.5.6.01, & P.8.3.01):
Based on Bayer AG history of the dossier’s granularity, the dissolution method development 
of the granules is described in section P.5 and identified as P.5.3.21. The reason why we 
provide this information here is because it was performed during the pharmaceutical 
development and, at the same time, it also supports the validation of the dissolution test 
P.5.3.02.
By reviewing P.2.2.02 approved by Swissmedic for other Bayer products, we found that 
P.5.3.21 was also referenced here. Therefore, we have amended the P.2.2.02 document from 
version 01 to 02 by adding further information under section 1 (Introduction) seen for those

In the P.5.3.21 you can find the selection of various parameters including the dissolution

0.12 %), dissolution apparatus, volume of suspension applied (tested from 1 to 11 mL) and

Question/Consideration:
Question 2:
3.2.P.2.2.1 – Viscosity of xanthan gum (initial Q7): It can be seen that the highest viscosity 
grade of Xanthan gum (1850 mPa s) shows a lag in dissolution at all points until 30 minutes 
compared to the medium (1600 mPa s) and low viscosity (1440 mPa s) grades of Xanthan 
gum containing granules. Considering a proposed specification of Q = 80% in 15 minutes, the 
grade of Xanthan gum should be specified, unless it can unambiguously be demonstrated 
(with for example, the testing of several batches) that the variation in grade of Xanthan gum 
in the formulated granules does not significantly affect dissolution. Please specify in 3.2.P.1 
the viscosity range and / or grades of Xanthan gum that can be used to ensure consistent drug 
release or please provide additional data to show that high viscosity grades of Xanthan gum 
do not affect the dissolution of the formulated product.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 2 (P.2.2.01):
The dissolution profiles using different viscosities of the excipient Xanthan gum were 
measured with two different time profiles. The dissolution of the batch with the highest 
viscosity of Xanthan gum (1850 mPa s) was only measured after 15, 30, 45 and 60 minutes, 
whereas the other two batches were measured with additional timepoints after 5 and 10 
minutes. This might give the impression of a lag time. Even though the dissolution of the 
highest viscosity grade is slightly slower than the others (89.2 % compared to 96.7 and 97.7% 
at 15 min), the dissolution is still very rapid (≥ 85% after ≤ 15 minutes), but well within the 
specification at time of testing, and would likely comply with stage 2 with the tighter 
specification, for example be considered comparable without the calculation of an f2 value.
Due to the fact that the dissolution of the final drug product has been tightened and specified 
with Q = 85% after 15 minutes, the viscosity of the excipient Xanthan gum does not need to 
be specified.

kit. Ten (10) samples of drug product in bottles, and four (4) kits labelled as placebo with 
empty bottles together with the proposed measuring device, Liquid Dosing Devices (LDD), 
along with the initial instructions for use (IFU) booklet have been shipped to your laboratory

To ensure optimal availability of the drug product for patients, it is essential to prepare a

errors are detailed in several test reports. These include evaluations of shaking time (see

Regarding the usability of the medical devices and the re-suspension process – including

pictogram showing the activity which corresponds to the text in the IFU “Gently tap

Question/Consideration:
Question 7:
3.2.P.8.3 (and 3.2.P.5.3) – Stress tests -mass balance (initial Q47):
While peak purity is confirmed for thermal conditions (3.2.P.8.3.11-01) and for other stressed 
conditions 3.2.P.8.3.04-02), no mass balance calculation is presented discussing the decrease 
in assay under all stressed conditions (thermal, oxidative, acid, alkaline) in relation to the 
increase in degradation products in module 3.2.P.8.3 – Stress tests.
Table 19 of the response to Q47 presents the mass balance calculation under various stress 
conditions. Significance difference in assay loss (17.2% for temperature, 7.4% for humidity, 
14.0% for alkaline hydrolysis and 29.4% for oxidative degradation) is indicated as being 
possible due to the use of two wavelengths (260 nm and 342 nm). The degradation products 
are not accounted for, with respect to the loss in assay. This leads to the conclusion that the 
current method is not stability indicating and therefore not considered suitable. The method 
should be updated / re-developed and validated as necessary. Please updated 3.2.P.8.3 – Stress 
tests accordingly to include the mass balance calculation, an explanation for any difference 
observed between the loss in assay and the degradation products (as reported in the response 
document) along with the updated analytical method (3.2.P.5.3) demonstrating the stability 
indicating capabilities of the chosen method.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 7 ( S.1.3.01, P.5.1.01, P.5.1.02, P.5.2.01, P.5.3.01 & P.8.3.04):
a)
Chosen wavelengths
To ensure correct quantitation of all components, different wavelengths were selected.
Besides the assay of riociguat and its degradation products, the assay for sodium benzoate
must be determined, as it is used as a preservative in the formulation.
As shown in Figure 1 below, the UV spectrum of riociguat presents the most prominent
absorption maxima at 210, 260 and 326 nm.
The determination of riociguat and sodium benzoate is carried out at a wavelength of 260 nm,
guaranteeing baseline separation between the two peaks. Since this wavelength is not an
absorption maximum of sodium benzoate, this procedure allows for parallel quantitation of
both components despite the approximately 12-fold higher concentration of sodium benzoate
in the formulation.
For the determination of degradation products of riociguat, a wavelength of 324 nm was
selected. This wavelength is a good compromise between the absorption maxima of known
riociguat impurities and degradation products as exemplified by the spectra of
Methoxycarbonyltrisamine, Dihydropurinone, Methyldihydropurinone, Mono-methyl
compound, Isopropyl carbamate and 4-Amino-6-hydroxy riociguat. At the same time, sodium
benzoate shows only negligible UV absorption at 324 nm, thus allowing for sufficiently
sensitive and reproducible detection and quantitation of the relevant riociguat degradation
products.
Both quantitation of riociguat and its degradation products are performed using a riociguat
reference standard only, since the main component is generally considered a suitable
surrogate for the quantitation of its unknown degradation products. As documented in
3.2.P.5.3.01, relative response factors (RRF) have been determined for all degradation
products, which are relevant for product stability under accelerated conditions (40 °C / 75%
RH) and stable enough for isolation, namely Dihydropurinone and 4-Amino-6-hydroxy-
riociguat. For discussion of the influence of these RRFs on quantitation, please refer to the
section “Evaluation of mass balances”.

Source:  P.5.3.01-02 Validation of Test for Assay and Impurities / Riociguat granules
0.3%for oral suspension (#022974277; amended)

b) Evaluation of mass balances
The applicant acknowledges the absence of plausible mass balances in the presented stress
study data set. The gap between the loss in Assay and Sum of all Degradation Products is
found to be as high as 15%, apparently suggesting that the HPLC method for Assay and
Degradation Products is not qualified for detecting and / or quantitating all potential API
degradation products.
However, the following points need to be taken into consideration.

Study design and sample appearance
The data presented in section P.8.3.04 (Stress test stability data for drug product) were
obtained applying generic stress conditions with the primary goal of evaluating the impact on
drug product quality, which may not only be compromised by the formation of degradation
products but also through changes in physico-chemical properties. Consequently, the
experimental setup was not designed to necessarily prove the analytical capabilities, i.e.
stability-indicating properties of the HPLC-UV method for Assay and Degradation Products.
Indeed, certain stress conditions resulted in obvious changes in granule properties that
rendered the samples unfit for HPLC analysis.

Sample preparation
Samples of granules subjected to alkaline, acidic and oxidative stress were prepared in
solvents similar to the solvent described in P.5.2.01 (Water pH 1.6 / Acetonitrile 4+1), but
substituting water pH 1.6 with 0.1 N NaOH, 0.1 N HCl or 3% H2O2, respectively.

I.1. Evaluation of thermal stress
Thermal stress at 60°C for 6 months results in a loss of approximately 14% in riociguat assay.
This strong decrease in assay values is likely related to the formation of sticky and discolored
lumps, which could not be dissolved by using the sample preparation according to the test
procedure. Such a change in sample appearance from free-flowing white granules to brownish
agglomerates clearly indicates the formation of polymeric degradation products of higher
molecular mass. The potential formation of polymeric degradation products was also found to
be a plausible degradation pathway based on theoretical calculations. Due to their limited
solubility, discrimination in the course of filtration and / or strong adherence to reversed-
phase HPLC column materials, such compounds usually evade HPLC detection, contributing
to an implausible mass balance. The document P.8.3.04 was revised in order to more clearly
describe the consequences of the change in sample appearance on the mass balance obtained
by HPLC.
In a realistic setting, sample material of obvious discoloration and aggregation would not be
subjected to HPLC analysis, but already rejected due to its violation of the specification for
product appearance (P.5.1.01 and P.5.1.02: Formulation, Color (visual), Color of suspension
(visual)). Concludingly, batches not discriminated by the HPLC analysis are still safely
recognized as not complying to the P.5.1 specification.

Source:  P.5.1.01-06 Release Specification / Riociguat granules 0.3% for oral
suspension (#022974253; amended)
P.5.1.02-06 Shelf Life Specification / Riociguat granules 0.3% for oral
suspension (#0022974254; amended)
P.8.3.04-03 Stability Data - Stress Tests / Riociguat granules 0.3% for oral
suspension (#022974495; amended)

I.2. Evaluation of alkaline stress
For alkaline stress conditions, an unstressed sample was listed in the respective P.8.3.04,
reflecting an assay value of 100%. At the same time, the prepared alkaline stress sample was
analyzed at the beginning of the experiment testing at a significantly lower assay value of
87.7%. This lower assay value does not reflect a degradation in riociguat but rather the
known, considerably lower solubility of riociguat in basic media (please also refer to
S.1.3.01-01 General Information – General Properties / Riociguat micronized substance).
In order to correctly judge the mass balance under basic stress conditions, the results obtained
after 3 days of stress need to be compared to the initial value of 87.7 %, which reflect an
identical composition of sample solution. After 3 days, the loss in assay is approximately 1%
(87.7% vs. 86.8%) which complements the detected sum of degradation products of 1.1%.
Concludingly, NaOH leads to moderate degradation of riociguat while a gap in mass balance
could not be observed. The document P.8.3.04 was revised in order to provide an
unambiguous explanation of the obtained data.

Source:  S.1.3.01-01 General Information - General Properties/ Riociguat micronized
drug substance (#006607609; unchanged)
P.8.3.04-03 Stability Data - Stress Tests / Riociguat granules 0.3% for oral
suspension (#022974495; amended)

II.
Influence of unknown relative response factors
Evaluation of Oxidative Stress:
Oxidative stress applied through H2O2-containing solutions results in considerable
degradation of riociguat in the granules. All peaks resulting from the respective degradation
products are well separated from riociguat. Purity plot of the riociguat peak confirms absence
of co-eluting components. Following 7 days of stress application by H2O2, degradation of
riociguat to an extent of approximately 28 % is observed by loss in assay. However, the sum
of all observed degradation products amounts to 18.9 % only (compound at RRT=0.77 ~17%).
There is a difference of 10 %.
A potential root cause is absorption coefficients differing between riociguat and unknown
degradation products. While unknown degradation products are commonly quantitated using
RRF=1.0, in this case RRFs determined for Dihydropurinone and 4-Amino-6-hydroxy-
riociguat are higher (1.4 and 1.5). Based on this, oxidative stress data were re-evaluated by
assuming RRF=1.5 for all unknown degradation products, increasing sum of degradation
products from 18.9% to 28.3% and effectively closing the mass balance gap (remaining ~1%).

Conclusion
The applicant concludes that the validated analytical method setup (including chosen
wavelengths) allows accurate quantitation of main components and relevant degradation
products (with validated RRFs); peak purity confirms selectivity; some stress conditions
affected sample suitability for HPLC (thermal and alkaline), but appearance specifications
would identify noncompliant batches; oxidative stress suggests RRFs >1.0 may apply to
unknown degradants. The applicant is convinced the stress study does not question stability-
indicating properties, but acknowledges the experimental setup did not allow evaluation under
all conditions. The applicant amended P.5.2.01 to incorporate the revised procedure of
quantitation.

Source:  P.8.3.04-03 Stability Data - Stress Tests / Riociguat granules 0.3% for oral
suspension (#022974495; amended)
P.5.2.01-05 Test Procedure / Riociguat granules 0.3 % for oral suspension
(#022974261; amended)

for the M0003 series in the dissolution medium of 1.2, the coefficient of variation 
(RSD, %) exceeds 20% (in the medium with pH 1.2 at the 5th minute - 28.2%);
For series M0004 in dissolution medium 4.5, the coefficient of variation (RSD, %) 
exceeds 20% (in medium pH 4.5 at the 5th minute - 29.6%) and 10% (at the 10th 
minute - 10.7%).
for series M0004 in the dissolution medium ND, the coefficient of variation (RSD, %) 
exceeds 20% (in the ND medium at the 5th minute - 21.6%);
Thus, the use of f2 is not applicable to the aforementioned results. An assessment of 
the comparability of dissolution profiles using an alternative method (e.g., Bootstrap) 
with appropriate statistical justification must be provided.
12.3 In accordance with Clause 39 of Appendix N 4 to the Decision of the EEC Council
dated November 3, 2016, No. 85, provide justifications for the non-compliance, 
specifically: the paddle stirrer indicates a speed of 75 revolutions per minute, whereas 
the Decision specifies a speed of 50 revolutions per minute.
12.4 Since in media with pH 1.2 and 6.8, the release of more than 85% of the active
substance was not achieved for some series from both the test and reference products, 
it is necessary to additionally provide an evaluation of the comparability of the 
corresponding dissolution profiles using the difference factor fl (indicating the 
calculation method and acceptance criteria for the specified factor) or to use 
alternative methods to confirm the comparability of dissolution profiles;
12.5 In accordance with the provisions of paragraph 13, Section II of Annex No. 5 to the
Rules approved by Decision No. 85 of the EEC Council dated November 3, 2016, 
provide confirmation of the validation of the statistical software used for the 
mathematical processing of the obtained data;
12.6 The reports on the results of CDKT should include all necessary documents and
appendices (in particular: CDKT programs (protocols), analytical reports, a sufficient 
number of representative chromatograms, etc.).
12.7 It is required to attach all quality certificates for each batch participating in the CDKT.
12.8 In accordance with Clause 4 of Appendix No. 5 of Decision 85, the intervals between
sample collections must be sufficiently frequent (at least every 15 minutes); therefore, 
it is necessary to provide results with missing sampling times for 90 and 115 minutes.
12.9 Provide a justification for the sampling time within 120 minutes, with references to
literary sources.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 12 (3.2.P.2.2):
The comparison study presented in P.2.2.02-IQMS-256250_1.0 (P.2.2.02_022983259_01) 
provided in variation documentation follows the ICH guideline M9, as applicable to the 
product in question. Bayer considers ICH M9 to be equivalent to the relevant sections of 
Decision No. 85 of the EEC council.
12.1 – number of batches
The process validation at the newly introduced production site Delpharm Milano S.r.l., Italy 
included 3 batches per dose strength, as explained in section 3.2 of the above-mentioned 
P.2.2.02_1.0. The same number of comparison batches were selected from the current site 
Bayer AG, Kaiser-Wilhelm-Allee, Leverkusen, Germany. This approach means that the 
complete set of process validation batches from Delpharm Milano S.r.l., Italy is assessed for 
comparability between the two sites, using sufficient batches from the Bayer AG, Kaiser-
Wilhelm-Allee, Leverkusen, Germany site. This study design exceeds the EEC requirements 
of comparing only 2 of the validation batches against a single batch from the Bayer AG, 
Kaiser-Wilhelm-Allee, Leverkusen, Germany site.

12.2 – values for coefficient of variation (RSD, %) at the 5th and 10th minute in dissolution 
media at pH 1.2 and pH 4.5.
It is explained in section 3.3 of the document that “ICH M9 states that not more than one 
mean value of ≥ 85% is included in an f2 test. To ensure that two data points at < 85% mean 
dissolution are available, t = 5 min is included for the QC medium alone. This measure is not 
required or meaningful for the other test conditions and has been determined for information 
only.”
In other words, dissolution results at t = 5 min at pH 1.2 were collected but for information 
only. Since the t = 5 min data points are part of the raw data of this study, they were presented 
in the above-mentioned P.2.2.02_1.0 of the sake of completeness only.
Each single profile overlay (e.g. Fig 5-1) shows a table (e.g. Table 5-1) in which the data 
points are stated that were used in the f2 test of the profiles shown in the overlay. None of the 
comparisons at pH 1.2 use the t = 5 min data point. The RSD values > 20% at this data point 
are therefore not relevant for the data analysis and the purpose of the study. Likewise, none of 
the comparisons at pH 4.5 use the t = 5 min data point.
A few t = 10 min data points show RSD values > 10%, while a single t = 15 min time point 
shows an RSD value > 15%. In all cases, all time points with a mean dissolution < 85% were 
included in the respective f2 tests, since it offers the most stringent case for the purpose of the 
test, as explained below.
Excluding the t = 5 min data point, as explained above, the largest difference in mean 
dissolution, in any medium, between any set of profiles of LEV and DEL batches is observed 
between 10 and 20 min. All profiles, in all media, show highly similar results once the mean 
dissolution exceeds 85%. The f2 test reflects the difference in mean dissolution between two 
profiles, as shown in section 3.3 of the above mentioned P.2.2.02_1.0. Therefore, selecting 
data points with lower mean differences automatically reduces the stringency of the f2 test. 
For that reason, the ICH M9 requires not more than one data points with a mean dissolution ≥ 
85% to be included in the f2 test, while two data points with a mean dissolution < 85% are 
included, if possible.
Both the ICH M9 and the EEC guideline (No. 85) set a limit for the RSD value per time point, 
because a high variability per unit (high RSD) is evened out in the mean result (n = 12). 
Therefore, high RSD values in the selected data points can reflect genuine differences 
between batches that are masked by the mean results. The limits for the RSD values (max 
20% up to t = 10 min and max 10% for t = 10 min and further) are general benchmarks to 
limit the impact of this effect on the comparison. In summary, the RSD limits serve to 
maximize the stringency of the f2 test.
In this study, the maximum stringency for the f2 test is achieved by including all data points 
at t = 10, 15 and 20 min or at t = 10, 15, 20 and 30 min, depending on the dissolution medium. 
As a result, the lowest (most stringent) f2 values are presented that can be obtained from the 
data presented. It was confirmed that using other (later) time points yield higher (less 
stringent) f2 values. Overall, varying the selected data points does not change the outcome of 
the study. It was thus decided to only present the most stringent approach in the above-
mentioned P.2.2.02_1.0.
12.3 – stirring speed
Section 3.3 of the above-mentioned P.2.2.02_1.0 contains the following statement:
Agitation: all profiles were collected with an agitation speed of 75 rpm, in accordance with 
the QC method (…).
Finerenone tablets are known to show coning in the dissolution vessel at 50 rpm, leading to 
higher tablet-to-tablet variability and lower discriminatory power. This effect at 50 rpm 
would introduce a laboratory artefact into the equivalence assessment of the two 
manufacturing sites. Using 75 rpm is therefore considered optimal for the purpose of this 
study.
A lower agitation speed typically increases the discriminatory power of the dissolution test. 
However, coning is a known effect at low speeds for immediate release drugs. Coning negates 
any potential benefit that a lower speeds may have regarding discriminatory power. ICH M9 
sets 50 rpm as the default speed. If an effect such as coning occurs however, the default is not 
suitable for the drug in question. This case applies to this study.

12.4 – less than 85% mean dissolution at pH 1.2 and 6.8
Only the 20 mg dose strength shows < 85% mean dissolution at t = 60 and t = 120 min in 
dissolution medium pH 6.8. All batches from the newly introduced production site Delpharm 
Milano S.r.l., Italy site and Bayer AG, Kaiser-Wilhelm-Allee, Leverkusen, Germany site 
show essentially the same behavior. In line with ICH M9, all data points were used in the f2 
tests. All pairwise comparisons shows f2 values > 50.
There is no specific reason not to use the f2 test for this condition. Furthermore, similarity of 
the profiles can be judged visually from the presented overlays of the profiles. The level of 
similarity is comparable to the other test conditions. Using other means of statistical 
comparison does not offer more informative value for this test condition.

12.5 - statistical software
The only quantitative analysis presented in the above-mentioned P.2.2.02_1.0 is the 
calculation of the f2 values. A validated Microsoft Excel sheet was used for this purpose.
The correctness of the f2 value of a given profile pair can be verified using the mean 
dissolution values at the given data points for each profile. All data (single as well as mean 
results) are presented in full in the above-mentioned P.2.2.02_1.0.
12.6 CDKT results
The study design and performance is described in detail in section 3 of the above-mentioned 
P.2.2.02_1.0. As stated in Tables 3-3 and 3-4, quantitation was done by HPLC, according to 
the registered P.5.2.02_IQMS-247514_3.0 (P.5.2.02_022974879_03) and P.5.2.02_IQMS-
247513_3.0 (P.5.2.02_022974878_03) test procedures. The latter documents contains 
representative chromatograms of the dissolution method.

12.7 quality certificates
The batches from Delpharm Milano S.r.L. are presented in the corresponding 
P.3.5.01_IQMS-252511_1.0 (P.3.5.01_022982751_01) and P.5.4.01_IQMS-252763_1.0 
(P.5.4.01_022982792_01) and P.5.4.01_IQMS-252764_1.0 (P.5.4.01_022982825_01) all 
provided in variation documentation.. The batches from Bayer AG, Kaiser-Wilhelm-Allee, 
Leverkusen, Germany were selected from commercial production, intended for global market 
supply. Relevant release test results for all batches are presented and evaluated in section 4.1 
of the above-mentioned P.2.2.02_1.0.

12.8 intervals between sample collections
The number and intervals between data points meet the ICH M9 requirements. Collecting 
additional data points will not yield any information that would affect the outcome of the 
study.

12.9 120 minutes sampling time
The profiles were only extended to 120 min for the 20 mg dose strength in dissolution 
medium pH 6.8. This option was foreseen in the study design, as explained in section 3.1 of 
the above-mentioned P.2.2.02_1.0.
Finerenone is a weak base (pK ca. 4.4), which means that its solubility decreases rapidly 
above pH 3. At pH 6.8 without surfactant, the maximum solubility is ca. 24 mg / 1000 mL at 
37 °C. The 20 mg dose is therefore not expected to fully dissolve within 60 min. To ensure 
that the dissolution profile is as close to a plateau as possible within technical constraints, the 
sampling time was extended to 120 min. A further extension, e.g. to t = 360 min, is not 
considered meaningful for the purpose of this study.

Question/Consideration:
Question 1.1.1.1
Establish a validated requirement for the signal-to-noise ratio for the main peak on the electropherogram of the monoclonal IgG solution to assess system sensitivity (reduced conditions);
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1.1.1.1:
The Applicant proposes a system sensitivity criterion based on the IgG standard for reduced conditions consistent with that previously proposed for non-reduced conditions. Monoclonal IgG is the established system suitability standard for the method and supports the existing criteria.

During method validation, the limit of quantitation (LOQ) of the aflibercept CE-SDS test method was determined through the analysis of the signal/ noise (S/N) of the main peak of a monoclonal IgG system suitability standard under non-reduced conditions. The monoclonal IgG system suitability standard was chosen since the heavy chain peak of IgG standard has better resolution than aflibercept sample under electrophoresis, which makes the S/N evaluation more accurate. Also, the migration time of the main peak of IgG standard is similar to the typical size variants observed for aflibercept. The LOQ is the lowest amount of analyte in a sample that can be determined with acceptable precision and accuracy under the stated experimental conditions.

In answer to the response by the Expert Institution, the Applicant proposes to add a sensitivity standard and system suitability criterion based on the similarity in response of the IgG standard under reduced and non-reduced conditions, and the validated LOQ for the diluted monoclonal IgG standard under non-reduced CE-SDS conditions.

This sensitivity standard solution should be prepared from the monoclonal IgG standard at a concentration of 0.01 mg/ml and analyzed under reducing conditions.

Therefore, the following system suitability criterion and preparation of solutions are proposed and added to the normative document.:
-
The signal-to-noise ratio calculated for the main peak of the Monoclonal IgG solution for system sensitivity assessment electropherogram under reducing conditions should be not less than 10.**
Preparation of solutions:

Monoclonal IgG stock solution for system sensitivity assessment (0.05 mg/mL) (to be used in preparation of reduced and non-reduced Monoclonal IgG solutions for system sensitivity assessment):

Add 40 µL of monoclonal IgG SST stock solution (2.5 mg/mL) to 1960 µL of MiliQ-water and mix thoroughly.
Use the solution freshly prepared.

Reduced monoclonal IgG solution  for system sensitivity assessment (0.01 mg/mL):

In a separate tube, make a single preparation by combining 40 µL of the Monoclonal IgG stock solution for system sensitivity assessment (0.05 mg/mL) with 160 μL of Dilution Buffer (Reducing) for a final concentration of 0.01 mg/mL.

Record all dilutions.

Source:  Normative Document (VV-REGQUAL-065844, amended)
keywords: system suitability test; LoQ; LOD/LOQ; Validation of Analytical procedures; Analaytical Procedures

Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 3.4.2 (M1):
1) Orion’s Certificates of Analysis (CoAs) are generated from Orion’s SAP ERP (Enterprise 
Resource Planning) system. The specification number including a valid from date indicated in 
the CoA of batch 2057146 refers to a unique identifier within the ERP system, used for 
managing the quality requirements of the product. The specification in the system is aligned 
with the approved regulatory specification, thereby ensuring compliance.

3) Dissolution specification contains all 3 stages S1, S2 and S3 which are specified in 
pharmacopoeias and according to specification testing will proceed to next stage testing if 
requirement for S1 (each of the tested 6 unit is not less than Q+5 per cent) is not fulfilled.

4) For clarification, the drug product Certificate of Analysis describes the degradation 
products (impurities) in three parts. First line refers to keto-darolutamide impurity (< 0.1%); 
second line provides the sum of any unspecified impurities (<0.05%); and the third line 
provides the sum of total impurities (< 0.1%).
Only degradation products of at least 0.1 % (reporting threshold) are reported. Peak areas that 
are at least 0.05 % (limit of quantitation) are evaluated. Results for individual degradation 
products that are below the reporting threshold of 0.1 % are stated as "< 0.1 %". 
Degradation products are reported with the accuracy of specification.
For keto-darolutamide and each unspecified impurity (any unknown impurity peaks), results ≥ 
0.05 % are reported with the accuracy of specification. Peaks < 0.05 % (LOQ) are reported as 
< 0.05 %.
For total degradation products, the amounts of keto-darolutamide and unspecified impurities 
(any unknown impurity peaks) ≥ 0.05 % are calculated together and reported with the 
accuracy of specification.

Bayer Response to Question 5 (P.8):

The batches 18B-220725-402 and MSAT230906 were manufactured under non-GMP. 
However, the stability studies incl. the testing of these samples were performed under GxP.
The batches KM603NA and KM60481 were manufactured under GxP. In addition, the 
stability studies as well as the analytical investigation of these samples were performed under 
GxP.

The batch MSAT230906 (12 tbl./bottle) and the batch KM60481 (25 tbl./bottle) are 
supportive batches for the extrapolation of the shelf life for the to be marketed packaging 
design of 120 tbl./bottle. All five commercial scale batches (MSAT230906, KM60481,

The lower fill level of these batches represent a worst case scenario as it results in a larger 
head space volume that allows for an increased exposure to oxygen and moisture. This greater 
headspace can promote degradation processes, making the stability results from the smaller 
fill quantity particularly conservative and relevant for assessing the shelf life of the larger fill 
quantity.

primary batches.
Since the supportive batches show a similar stability profile as the primary batches, the 
extrapolation of the shelf life from the supportive batches is considered to be justified and will 
be verified by the primary batches.

Bayer Response to Question 1 ( CTD section P.3.5):
Background:
In April 2025, a Type 1 meeting request was submitted to the CDE to seek approval for a 
rolling submission of the process validation report. On May 22, 2025, we received written 
feedback from the CDE, which indicated that they do not support Bayer's participation in a 
rolling submission of the validation report during the NDA review process. The CDE clarified 
that the validation report must be included in the initial NDA submission package, in 
accordance with current regulations in China, specifically, Article 34 of the Current Drug 
Registration Regulation, which states: "After completing the research on pharmacy, 
pharmacology, and toxicology, as well as clinical trials of drugs that support the marketing 
authorization registration, determining drug specifications, completing the commercial-scale 
production process validation, and preparing for the acceptance of drug registration 
inspection and testing, the applicant shall submit the drug marketing authorization 
application along with the relevant research data in accordance with dossier requirements."
From May 2025-July 2025, the process validation activities were expedited.
It is concluded that the manufacturing process for BAY 2927088 coated tablet 10 mg can 
consistently produce batches that meet all quality requirements.  The process has thus been 
successfully validated.
This data has been incorporated into the attached Process Validation (PV) Report TRD 
(P.3.5.01) and is attached to this RFI.

Question/Consideration: For pharmaceutical products related to the removal of the specification for heavy metals and arsenic, a risk assessment should be carried out according to the section "2.66 Elemental Impurities" given in the general monograph of the Japanese Pharmacopoeia and the relevant report should be submitted.
Answer/Response:
The Japanese Pharmacopoeia (JP) 18th edition has introduced updates under General Notice No. 34 regarding the control of elemental impurities. This update aligns with ICH Q3D (R1) guidelines for elemental impurity risk assessment and control in pharmaceutical products.
According to General Notice No. 34:
• JP drug products are expected to comply with elemental impurity controls as described in the general test sections of the pharmacopoeia.
• When drug products are controlled according to these guidelines, it is not necessary to perform routine testing for elemental impurities (e.g., heavy metals and arsenic) in drug substances, excipients, or drug product monographs.
Therefore, the need for separate tests for arsenic and heavy metals in the drug substance specification has been eliminated as long as compliance with elemental impurity requirements is demonstrated.
However, according to section "2.66 Elemental Impurities" given in the general monograph of the Japanese Pharmacopoeia; a risk assessment should be carried out and would be focused on assessing the levels of elemental impurities in a drug product in relation to the Permitted Daily Exposures (PDEs). These PDEs are established to protect the health of all patients based on the evaluation of the toxic data of elemental impurities, and more strict limits are not needed if elemental impurities in drug products do not exceed the PDEs.
In line with ICH Q3D (R1) guidelines a comprehensive risk assessment for elemental impurities has been conducted for the Urografin 76% drug product. Please refer to TRD P.5.5.01_01 for the same. The results confirm that all elemental impurity levels, in limits and do not exceed PDEs when evaluated in the context of the drug product’s intended use and patient safety. The proposed change aligns with regulatory guidelines and practices, ensuring harmonization across markets while maintaining the highest standards of safety and efficacy for the drug product.
Source: 1) TRD P.5.5.01_01 Impurities in the Drug Product/ Meglumine amidotrizoate + Sodium amidotrizoate solution for parenteral use (UROGRAFIN)/ (#020368210/unchanged)
2) General notices No.34 JP18
3) General monograph No. 2.66 JP18
keywords: ICHQ3D; elemental impurities; arsenic test; impurities; risk assessment

Question/Consideration: Supporting Document – (i) Please review and categorize the responsibilities of visual inspections appropriately, instead of referring to them as "Other" manufacturing activities.
Answer/Response:
The operation “visual inspection” is formally classified as a manufacturing step and is applied to 100% of all filled prefilled syringes. Within the available options for manufacturing activities/role, it is categorized under “manufacturer of dosage form”.
Nonetheless, Bayer would like to point out that the purpose of this “manufacturing step” is not any kind of manipulation of the intermediate drug product, but only a visual check of every single prefilled syringes to ensure that any prefilled syringes with visible defects are rejected. In this respect it is similar to quality control testing which collects information about the product without altering it.
More than one site is used for this step in order to have some flexibility for this very time- and personnel-consuming activity. Due to the sensitivity of the protein and the resulting need of reduced time out of refrigeration (TOR), rapid processing is needed for biological product. This approach was accepted and has been unchanged since the initial NDA for Eylea solution for intravitreal injection in pre-filled syringe 40mg/ml, and we urge that this could be maintained.

doc_name: VV-RFI-004607 - CMC Response - NDA - Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL in prefilled syringe - HK
Question/Consideration:
(i) Please clarify how the data for real-time storage conditions in Table 4-1 to 4-4 can support the in-use stability. Should provide cycling studies/stress tests.
(ii) Please clarify how the TOR was determined.
(iii) Please clarify how to determine 24 hours despite the TOR proposed.
Answer/Response:
The applicant would like to highlight that the proposed allowable storage of the unopened blister outside of the refrigerator for up to 24 hours does not present an in-use scenario of the drug product. The drug product remains within its protective packaging and is not exposed to the environment as would be the case for multi-dose products or products that require constitution/dilution for which actual in-use stability studies are conducted. Resultantly, the storage of the unopened blister is rather similar to a short-term temperature excursion from the long-term storage conditions and is therefore also investigated with respective real-time data after maximal exposure to 25°C.
To define the maximum exposure of the drug product to up to 25°C an end-to-end Time Out of Refrigeration (TOR) concept for Aflibercept 114.3 mg/mL in prefilled syringe (PFS) was established. This concept covers all TOR occurring throughout the lifecycle of a batch of Aflibercept 114.3 mg/mL in PFS from the start of manufacture, over distribution until handling by healthcare professionals (HCP). The maximum total TOR defined for Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL in PFS was defined as 226.5 h, respectively 237.5 h for the extended sterilization batch (see CTD section (P.8.3.11-03).
Table 1 provides further details of the allocation of maximum allowable TOR for each step, along with the criteria applied to define the TOR for each stage. As indicated in the table, the TOR concept reserves 24 hours for handling by HCP. This forms the basis for the label claim: “Prior to usage, the unopened blister may be stored outside the refrigerator below 25 °C for up to 24 hours.”. 24 hours for HCP handling were defined based on requirements from several global markets and as established for the approved Aflibercept 40 mg/mL strength and the Aflibercept 114.3 mg/mL vial presentation.
The real-time storage data presented in Tables 4-1 to 4-4 of CTD section P.8.3.11-03 were sourced from Process Performance Qualification (PPQ) batches that were cycled at 25 °C and exceeding the defined maximum end-to-end TOR shown in Table 1. Consequently, the applicant has provided data demonstrating the stability of the product after being exposed to the maximum end-to-end TOR. Up to date, 18 months real-time stability data are available. The data are projected to meet the shelf-life specification limits after 24 months of storage.
keywords: Stability data; Shelf Life; Storage Condition; stability commitment; in-use stability

Question/Consideration: For the part, there are only a brief risk assessment and conclusion provided. Please see if there is further test result detail for the elemental impurity as there is conclusion only.
Answer/Response:
The risk assessment for elemental impurities and accordingly the P.5.5.01-01 which the applicant provided are based on studies to determine the amount of elemental impurities in the product. Two types of studies were executed.
Elemental impurities were tested with Inductively Coupled Plasma-Mass Spectrometry(ICP-MS) for water and simulated leachable extracts (Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL) as a part of the extractables studies to characterize product contact materials. PFS filling process components were extracted at 25 C for 24 hours. PFS components: plunger stopper, tip cap, syringe barrel, and bulk PFS (Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL), which have undergone only the manufacturing steps at the filling site Vetter Pharma, were extracted at 25 C for 48 h. All components characterized in these studies provided results for leachable elements in the ng/dose level and below the analytical evaluation threshold (AET), which were assessed as not critical in the elemental impurities safety assessment. The results of this study can be found in P.2.4.06-01.
Further there is an ongoing leachables stability study for the finished goods of Aflibercept 114.3 mg/mL in PFS. Currently leachable stability data for 3 batches of finished goods PFS at the initial time point and after 12 months of storage at 2 -8 C are available. Here for single elements results above their specific limit of quantitation were obtained. None of these elements belongs to ICH classes 1, 2A, 2B or 3. The results of all elements are well below the Safety Concern Threshold/Threshold of Toxicological Concern of 1.5 μg/day for genotoxic impurities.
Detailed results and discussion for elemental impurities, i.e. leachable elements, after real time storage at 2 – 8 C are presented in P.2.4.07-01.

Question/Consideration:
3.2.P.5.6 (section 7.2). The limits for the microbial control for alert and action should be below 
100 cfu/100 ml according to the guideline on the sterilization of the medicinal product, active 
substance, excipient and primary container, which states 100 CFU/100 mL (table 1, 
EMA/CHMP/CVMP/QWP/850374/2015). The alert limit should be lower than the action limit 
(100 cfu/100 mL). Please comment and update the limits accordingly.
Answer/Response:
We acknowledge the authority’s comment and providing here below the justifying answer in 
regards to the 3.2.P.5.6 (Section 7.2):-
For bioburden, an action limit and an internal action limit (defined as alert limit) is established 
at the production site Berlin for terminally sterilized aqueous solution. The internal action limit 
is 10 CFU/10 mL and corresponds to limit of 100 CFU/100 mL as outlined in 
EMA/CHMP/CVMP/QWP/850374/2015.   
The registered limit of 10 CFU/mL has been approved worldwide since 2008 and was 
established prior the implementation of EMA/CHMP/CVMP/QWP/850374/2015. A solid 
bioburden reduction or contamination control strategy is installed, including but not limited to 
incoming goods control, bioburden reduction filtration, equipment decontamination and 
defined holding times. The Iopromide solution itself was shown to not be susceptible to 
microbial growth.  
With the establishment of the EMA guideline in 2019, a historical review of bioburden data of 
terminally sterilized aqueous solution has been performed from 2019 to 2022 to evaluate the 
status and registered limits. The evaluation confirmed that the production process is under 
control. A  very low rate of microbial contamination was detected, showing no growth in the 
vast majority of cases and retrospectively complying with the limit value recommended by the 
EMA.  
Terminal sterilization of aqueous solution is performed  with a 12-log overkill sterilization 
process, which is regularly validated by biological indicators to ensure a SAL of 10-6 
(independent of the initial bioburden). Under the currently submitted bioburden limits of 10 
CFU/mL a SAL of 10-6 was always ensured.
“The current action limit of 10 CFU/mL is included in the dossiers submitted to health 
authorities and is registered worldwide”.
Time consuming filing of an extensive number of non-essential variations to health authorities 
should be avoided. However, to follow the recommendation of the EMA guideline, for all 
bioburden of terminally sterilized aqueous solution products, the existing internal action limit 
(alert limit) was reduced to 10 CFU/10 mL, which corresponds to 100 CFU/100 mL. If the 
internal action limit of 10 CFU/10 mL is exceeded, an investigation according to the local

deviation process is initiated, which includes a detailed root cause investigation and an 
evaluation of bioburden resistance.
keywords: Sterility Testing; Sterilization; Microbiological Attributes; Bioburden Control Strategy; risk assessment
