Question/Consideration:
Question 1
Tests of particle size, residual solvents, and related impurities in the batch analysis are 
inconsistent with the information in the CEP and EP, please explain.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1:
Please find below explanation for each item:
Particle size:
The particle size distribution is determined using a laser diffraction spectroscopic procedure,  
which is a standard pharmacopeial procedure. Standard requirements applied for hormonal  
drug substances are set as limits in the specification. With the specification of particle size, a  
safe content uniformity and dissolution is guaranteed even in low doses.  
 
Compared to the CEP from Newchem S.p.A., the specification includes additionally the  
evaluation of larger particles via optical microscopy and the specification limits for particle  
size analysis by laser diffraction is tighter. This is to make sure that the material from external 
manufacturing has the same particle size distribution as the known Bayer material. The  
particle size distribution is determined by the validated laser diffraction method also applied  
for the Bayer material and not by the method described on the CEP. The aim is to maintain 
the current approved and stricter particle size specification from Bayer material to ensure 
maintenance in the quality of the drug product. 
 
Residual solvents:
Methylene chloride, methanol, ethyl acetate and acetone are relevant solvents and therefore 
specified. A standard head-space gas chromatographic procedure is applied. All four residual 
solvents are specified according to the limits proposed by the ICH Q3C guideline on residual 
solvents.
Methylene chloride: Class 2 ICH limit not more than 600 ppm
Methanol: Class 2 ICH limit not more than 3000 ppm
Ethyl acetate: Class 3 ICH limit not more than 5000 ppm
Acetone: Class 3 ICH limit not more than 5000 ppm

In the CEP from Newchem, only the Class 2 solvents methylene chloride and methanol are 
listed with the limits stated in ICH Q3C guideline. The limits presented here also include the 
class 3 solvents to allow a better control of the process and the residual solvents present in the 
drug substance. The determination is carried out according to a validated standard inhouse 
head-space method and not by the method described in the CEP.

Related impurities: 
The limits for related substances of cyproterone acetate are determined based on the Ph. Eur. 
requirements described in the general chapter 5.10 Control of Impurities in substances for 
pharmaceutical use and in the ICH Q3A guideline for impurity testing. Please find more 
detailed information in the shared S.4.5.01 section (justification of specification).
The CEP from Newchem S.p.A. refers to the impurity specification according to the Ph.Eur. 
monograph. Therefore the impurity specification selected is even tighter in most cases. This is 
to make sure that the material from external manufacturing has the same impurity profile as 
the known Bayer material.
Source:  S.4.5.01 Justification of Specification and Skip Testing / Cyproterone acetate
micronized drug substance (#022982414; /unchanged)
keywords: justification of specification DS; related substances; residual solvents; test method; drug substance specification

which have no chemical source are magnesium stearate and lactose monohydrate.
The source of origin from the excipients magnesium stearate and lactose monohydrate of the

sourced from healthy animals in the same condition as milk collected for human consumption.

In accordance to the European guideline <Note for guidance on minimizing the risk of

products> (EMEA/410/01 in its current revision), the drug product can be regarded as safe

Please note that the lactose has bovine source because the raw material “milk” is coming from

performed by the Committee for Proprietary Medicinal Products (CPMP) and its Biotech-  
nology Working Party (BWP). In accordance with Public Statement EMEA/CPMP/571/02 of 
February 27 2002 the TSE risk is negligible if the calf rennet is produced in accordance with

Question/Consideration:
Question 1
Microbiology
1. We acknowledge the description of the manufacturing process and process controls as
well as the process validation information provided in Sections 3.2.P.3.3 and 3.2.P.3.5.
However, information concerning the depyrogenation of the proposed drug product vials
and bottles could not be located in the application. We note that none of the currently
provided Letters of Authorization (LoA/s) in section 1.4.1. of your submission refer to
depyrogenation information for the vials and bottles. Describe the depyrogenation
process for vials and bottles during routine production and provide the corresponding
validation studies, including study design, acceptance criteria, study results, and
endotoxin indicator (EI) information (i.e., manufacturer, expiry, challenge concentration
and results of spiked vials and controls) and requalification program. Provide three
successful consecutive heat distribution / heat penetration/ EI challenge runs for the
initial qualification and the most recent requalification data, if the initial qualification is
more than two years old. Alternatively, if this data is contained in a DMF, provide an LoA
providing access to the relevant information (e.g., document names, submission dates)
in the DMF. Reference is made to FDA’s 1994 Guidance document “Guidance for
Industry for the Submission Documentation for Sterilization Process Validation in
Applications for Human and Veterinary Drug Products.”
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1 ( 3.2.P.3.3, 3.2.P.3.5):
We acknowledge FDA’s review of sections 3.2.P.3.3 and 3.2.P.3.5 and the request for 
depyrogenation validation data of the proposed drug product vials and bottles. Gadoquatrane 
solution 0.4 mmol Gd/mL in vial or bottle is a terminally sterilized product, as described 
under “II. Information for terminal moist heat sterilization processes” in the referenced 
“Guidance for Industry for the Submission Documentation for Sterilization Process 
Validation in Applications for Human and Veterinary Drug Products” and information on the 
sterilization process is included in Module 3.

Bayer follows a holistic endotoxin control strategy based on USP <1228> that encompasses

Question/Consideration:
Question 1
In accordance with BPOM Regulation No. 23 Year 2022 regarding Standards 
and/or Requirement on Quality of Drug Product and Drug Material, please review 
the document of specification and analytical method of drug product and drug 
materials (active substances and excipients) used in this product in the form of a 
matrix of comparisons for each parameter so that it is clear:
• Are there any test parameters that are not carried out according to Indonesian 
Pharmacopoeia or BPOM regulation No. 23 Year 2022 along with the detailed 
justification.
• Are there differences in the test parameters against Indonesian Pharmacopoeia 
or BPOM regulation No. 23 Year 2022 along with the detailed justification
• If the monograph is not available in Indonesia Pharmacopoeia or BPOM 
Regulation No. 23 Year 2022, then which monograph is used as a reference, 
along with the detailed justification
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1:
For the Drug Product, Sodium gadoxetate solution 0.25 mol/L for parenteral use 
(PRIMOVIST) as well as for the employed drug materials (drug substance and 
excipients), Bayer has performed a detailed analysis on the availability and 
suitability of pharmacopeial monographs including the Indonesian Pharmacopeia. 
The following approach was followed:
• In case a monograph is available for a Sodium gadoxetate solution 0.25 mol/L 
for parenteral use (PRIMOVIST) component in the Indonesian Pharmacopeia, 
Bayer has prepared a matrix comparison between current implementation 
versus Indonesian Pharmacopoeia including a justification for the implemented 
procedure.
• In case a monograph is not available for a Sodium gadoxetate solution 0.25 
mol/L for parenteral use (PRIMOVIST) component in the Indonesian 
Pharmacopoeia / BPOM Regulation No. 23 Year 2022, but it is listed in 
established pharmacopoeia in other country (Ph.Eur., USP, JP), Bayer has 
prepared a matrix comparison between current implementation versus 
established pharmacopoeia (e.g., USP, Ph. Eur. and JP) including a justification.
• In case no monograph is available, Bayer provides a statement on the in-house 
testing.

1. Sodium gadoxetate solution 0.25 mol/L for parenteral use (PRIMOVIST), 
drug product
Sodium gadoxetate solution 0.25 mol/L for parenteral use (PRIMOVIST) itself is 
not monographed, neither in the Indonesian Pharmacopoeia (FI), nor in the 
European Pharmacopoeia (Ph.Eur.) or the United States Pharmacopoeia (USP). The

Question 1
Please clarify the scope of production activities of the active ingredient manufacturer's

ingredient.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1
As mentioned in P.1.02_IQMS-189833_2.0, Meglumine is used as a starting material. It is 
added to the reactor vessel during the manufacturing process and then it reacts with 
amidotriozoic acid to form the salt: meglumine amidotrizoate, which is the drug substance 
that appears in the final product. This also happens with Sodium, as well . Although we use 
Sodium Hydroxide as a starting material, in the final product, it is in the form of the salt 
(sodium amidotrizoate).
The GMP certificate of Justea S.A is related to Amidotrizoic acid only and the Drug 
substances formed during the manufacturing process i.e. meglumine amidotrizoate  and 
sodium amidotrizoate  do not come under scope of the GMP certificate.

Answer/Response:

These are the reagents used for the turbidimetric method: 
-LAL Reagent: Lyophilized Endosafe KTA LAL Reagent, contains buffered amebocyte lysate 
stabilized by monovalent and divalent cations. 
 
Reconstitution: Collect LAL powder into the bottom of the vial by tapping on a firm surface. 
Unseal and release the vacuum by slowly lifting the stopper, avoiding touch contamination. The 
small amount of LAL on the stopper is insignificant. Rehydrate with 5,2 ml of LAL Reagent 
Water or an Endosafe R reconstitution buffer by pipetting directly into the vial immediately 
before use. Remove and discard the stopper. Cover the vial with an endotoxin-free surface or 
the inner side of Parafilm when not in immediate use. Gently swirl until LAL dissolves into a 
colorless solution. Discard if the seal integrity is breached or if color or opacity is present after 
rehydration. 
 
Storage: Lyophilized LAL is relatively heat stable and should be stored at 2-25 ºC: avoid 
prolonged exposure to temperatures above 25 ºC. Rehydrated LAL ideally should be stored on 
a cold surface or in a refrigerator at 2-8 ºC during intermittent use, for up to 8 hours. Otherwise 
store LAL below minus 20 ºC for up to twenty eight days after reconstitution and freezing, LAL 
may only be frozen and thawed once.

confirm LAL reagent sensitivity, validate product test methods, and prepare inhibition controls 
(positive water and positive product controls). Refer to the Certificate of Analysis for each CSE

product.

potency of the is as 10,000 IU per vial of is, so that IU = 1 EU- The potency of this endotoxin 
standard in International (Endotoxin) Units, IU, has been designed as 11 IU/ng. 
Directions for use: Reconstitute the lyophilized material with 2.2 ml of LAL reagent grade 
water to obtain 50 EU/ml or 50 IU/ml. Vortex mix vigorously for at least 5 minutes after 
rehydration, and for at least 1 minute immediately prior to each use.

controlled room temperature or refrigerated as preferred. Diluted endotoxin should not be stored 
except under validated conditions.

(3) Provide data demonstrating that the absolute value of the correlation coefficient of
the calibration curve prepared with Solution C is 0.980 or higher, and explain

Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 3 (3):
Calibration curves were prepared by using the concentrations of Solution C and the reaction 
time. Table titled “INFORMACIÓN DE ESTÁNDARES Y CONTROLES” in the reports 
(Informe detallado del ensayo cinético) above show the information on the concentration of 
Solution C and the reaction time obtained from solution C as “Concentración Esperada” and 
“Tiempo de reacción (s)”, respectively. Also, The calibration curves prepared by using the 
results are presented in the reports. The absolute values of the correlation coefficients for each 
calibration curve prepared based on the results have been confirmed to be 0.980 or higher, as 
shown in the validation report Document No. IVM2025-001.01

In an endotoxin assay, the calibration curve is used to determine the concentration of 
endotoxins in a sample. The correlation coefficient of this curve indicates how well the data 
points fit a straight line. A correlation coefficient close to 1, such as 0,98 or higher, suggests 
that there is a strong linear relationship between the concentration of endotoxins and the 
response recorded by the assay. 
Here’s why a correlation coefficient above 0.98 is considered good for the analysis:
1. Accuracy and Reliability: A high correlation coefficient indicates that the assay is
accurately and reliably measuring endotoxin concentrations. This is crucial for ensuring 
that the results are precise and consistent with the actual endotoxin levels. 
2. Linearity: A curve with a high value confirms that the assay is linear across the range
of concentrations tested. This linearity is essential for quantifying unknown samples 
accurately. 
3. Quality Control: In quality control, a high correlation coefficient is a sign that the assay
is performing well and that the experimental conditions were well-controlled. It reduces 
the likelihood of errors and increases confidence in the results. 
Overall, a correlation coefficient above 0.98 in an endotoxin assay indicates that the analytical 
method is robust, reliable, and suitable for detecting and quantifying endotoxins in the samples 
being tested.

Question/Consideration:
(4) Provide data demonstrating that the measurement result for Solution D does not 
exceed the limit value of the blank test specified for the lysate reagent, or that it is below 
the detection limit of endotoxin.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 3 (4):
Table titled “INFORMACIÓN DE ESTÁNDARES Y CONTROLES” in the reports (Informe 
detallado del ensayo cinético) show the results of Solution D as “CTRL 1” and “CTRL 2”. 
The sensitivity of LAL reagent used for the testing is 0.005EU/mL (λ). The results of reaction 
time obtained from Solution D could not be determined, and the value calculated from the 
calibration curve (Valor nuevamente calculado) were evaluated to be <0.0050EU/mL.
In a turbidimetric endotoxin assay, negative control is a sample that is expected to contain no 
endotoxins. The purpose of the negative control is to confirm that the assay is not detecting 
endotoxins where there should be none, which helps to ensure the specificity and accuracy of 
the test.

When the negative control in a turbidimetric endotoxin assay results in a value below 0,0050 
EU/ml, it has several important implications:
1. Assay Sensitivity: A negative control value below 0.005 EU/mL indicates that the assay
is highly sensitive. It can detect very low levels of endotoxins, which is crucial for 
ensuring that even small contaminations are identified. 
2. Specificity: A low value for the negative control demonstrates that the assay is specific
to endotoxins and not giving false-positive results due to other substances. This 
specificity is vital for the reliability of the assay. 
3. Baseline Noise: The result suggests that the baseline noise of the assay is minimal. This
low level of background interference means that the assay can accurately measure low 
concentrations of endotoxins without being affected by random fluctuations or 
contaminants.

assay is being performed correctly and that the reagents and equipment are free from 
endotoxin contamination. This is important for maintaining the integrity of the assay 
results.

indicates that the test is performing well, with high sensitivity, specificity, and minimal baseline 
noise. This enhances the reliability and accuracy of the assay, ensuring that the detection of 
endotoxins in test samples is both precise and trustworthy.

Question/Consideration:
Question 1
For the Type IB BIId1z deletion of total impurity (TLC) test parameter from batch release 
specifications, they are requesting the proving documents that are below the limit of detection 
(LOD). (13 Nov 2025) And, because TR HA mentions that this will not be possible due to 
this test being a TLC test, it will be appropriate to wait after the approval of the other 
variations being submitted for REC 32843 which also includes the addition of “any individual 
impurity” to the shelf life specification and also switching from TLC method to LC 
method  for the impurity test. And, after these approvals, they mention that we can make a 
variation by submitting proving documents for the deletion of the impurity parameter from 
the batch release specifications. And the results for any individual impurity parameter must be 
added to the proving document.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1 ( CTD section):
The test procedure for impurities in Mirena IUS has been revised to include only 
levonorgestrel (LNG) related degradation products, not any more synthesis related impurities 
as the current test. This approach is in line with the EMA guideline CPMP/ICH/2738/99 (ICH 
Q3B). The guideline states: “impurities present in the drug substance need not be monitored 
or specified in the drug product specifications unless they are also degradation products”.   
This proposed new impurity test is removed from Release Specifications, i.e. it will be 
included in the Shelf-life testing only. To support the change, the acceptance limit for the sum 
of the degradation products is tightened from NMT 2.0% to NMT 1.0%. The potential known 
and unidentified LNG degradation products above 0.1% reporting threshold are included in 
the test results.   
Levonorgestrel is inherently stable. The long history of Mirena IUS has verified that LNG 
remains virtually unchanged in the product manufacture, and during the shelf-life. This is 
demonstrated by comparing results of five MIRENA IUS drug product stability batches with 
the results for corresponding drug substance batches in Justification of Specification (IQMS-
187354). The results for drug substance batches in accordance with the Ph. Eur. method 
indicate actual low amount of degradation products for Mirena IUS as the synthesis related 
impurities need not to be included in the results. This is shown to be true for the drug product 
batches listed, as the maximum result for the Sum of degradation products is only 0.1 %.     
The daily dose released from a Mirena IUS is ca. 20 μg. According to the EMA guideline 
CPMP/ICH/2738/99 the identification threshold for impurities in a drug product with a 
maximum daily dose of 1 mg is 1.0% or 5 μg Total Daily Intake (TDI), whichever is lower. 
The potential known and unidentified LNG degradation products above 0.1% reporting 
threshold are included in the specifications of Mirena. Calculated as daily intake an impurity 
at 0.1 % level in Mirena provides a daily intake of 0.02 μg only. The level of possible 
unspecified degradation products in Mirena are therefore far below the identification 
threshold of 5 μg TDI. Even the sum of all degradation products calculated as daily intake 
(1.0 % of 20 μg daily dose) is ca. 0.2 μg (TDI) only. Based on the above arguments the 
proposed limits for the impurity test are well justified.

Furthermore, stability data covering the whole Shelf-life (36 months) of Mirena is provided to 
the competent Health Authority with impurity tests results for three batches of Mirena. The 
impurity results verify clearly the good stability of Mirena, as even the Sum of impurities is at 
level 0.0 % at the last 36 M study point for all three batches.  
The 36 months’ stability data in report IQMS-263018 verifies that no degradation is observed 
until up to the end of Shelf-life of Mirena for these three batches. Therefore, deletion of 
Impurity testing from the release specification of Mirena is justified.

Question/Consideration:
Question 1
In the submitted CoA, the testing item, microbiological test and particle size (100% NMT 
15µm; 99% NMT 12.5µm; 95% NMT 10.0µm; 50% NMT 3.0µm; NMT 40% NMT 1.3µm) 
are not listed in European pharmacopeia, and not listed in CEP.
Please provide declaration letter from manufacturer to confirm that the testing items and 
related info (including testing methods & result) were submitted to EDQM in CEP cert 
application, but EDQM didn’t add those items to API testing spec.
If the letter cannot be provided, then the above-mentioned testing items are not applicable to 
this submission. The testing items must be removed from spec and updated CoA should be 
provided.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1:
Please be informed that the Certificate of Analysis shared in previous request are issued by 
Newchem. Bayer Certificate of analysis do not contain microbiological test.
We would like to explain the reasoning why Microbiological test and Particle size are not 
critical for quality and not mandatory to be included in CEP or Pharmacopoeia.
Regarding CEP:
Please kindly find enclosed the guideline “how to read CEP”, where it is explained that 
Microbial quality is an aspect not covered by CEP since the final use of the substance is not 
known. This parameter can be checked at drug product level.
For the Particle size test, it is also not mandatory to be included in the CEP. It can be included 
as subtitle as it is the case for Newchem’s CEP. In this case, the limits from the Certificate of 
Analysis includes both the limits from the CEP and also the limits from Bayer specification, 
since Bayer specification limits are tighter. In order to maintain the quality, safety and 
efficacy of the product and because the specifications are maintained, there is a quality 
internal agreement between the manufacturer and Bayer, thus the Certificate contains both 
limits.
Below a couple of snips from the guideline were this information is explained:

For European Monograph: Microbial test and particle size are not included because 
Cyproterone acetate is a drug substance with well-defined purity and crystalline 
characteristics. Microbial contamination risk is assessed during manufacturing of the dosage 
form, not at the raw API stage. The drug substance is a crystalline powder, typically 
processed under controlled conditions, so microbial testing is not considered critical at the 
monograph level.  Particle size is a performance attribute relevant to specific formulations 
(e.g., inhalation powders, suspensions). For cyproterone acetate tablets, particle size may 
influence dissolution, but this is controlled by the manufacturer through formulation 
development and validated methods, not by the API monograph.

Source:  How to read a CEP

Question/Consideration:
Question 2
Provide justification and technical support for the evaluation of the impact of the change on 
the process and on the quality, safety, and efficacy of the finished product, including data on 
the suitability of the container-closure system (e.g., leachables and extractables testing, 
permeability, light effect, humidity) demonstrating equivalent or superior protection 
compared to the current container-closure system for the presentations of a box with a Type I 
clear glass vial with a bromobutyl stopper of 7.5 mL and a Type II clear glass bottle with a 
bromobutyl stopper of 65 mL, considering that only the 30 mL Type I clear glass vial with a 
bromobutyl stopper presentation was submitted.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1 (CTD section):
We would like to provide the requested justification and supporting technical information 
regarding the suitability and protective performance of the container-closure systems for the 
7.5 mL Type I clear glass vial with bromobutyl stopper and the 65 mL Type II clear glass 
bottle with bromobutyl stopper, in comparison with the submitted 30 mL Type I clear glass 
vial presentation. 

1. Stopper Material and Closure System 
The introduction of a new stopper and crimp cap as an additional packaging option does not 
alter the container-closure system’s protective performance. 
Based on validated CCI data, material compliance (Type I/II glass and bromobutyl stoppers), 
and established extractables/leachables profiles, the packaging for the 7.5 mL Type I vial and 
65 mL Type II bottle provides equivalent protection to that of the submitted 30 mL Type I 
vial. 

2. Container Closure Integrity Demonstrates Equivalent Protection 
As documented in the TRD P.2.4.02_IQMS-248898_2.0 (Container Closure Integrity Test, 
Section 1.1), container-closure integrity (CCI) was validated using helium leak testing on 
various vial and bottle sizes:
• 2 mL Type I vial 
• 15 mL Type I vial 
• 50 mL Type II glass bottle 
The method applies USP <1207> helium mass spectrometry with a maximum allowable 
leakage limit (MALL) of 6 × 10⁻⁶ mbar·L/s. 
The TRD explicitly states:
• Results for 15 mL vials are representative for 10–30 mL vials, as the neck inner 
diameter is identical. 
→ This includes the 7.5 mL and 30 mL Type I vial presentations. 
• Results for 50 mL glass bottles are representative for 100–500 mL glass bottles, 
since the inner neck diameter is identical and tolerance variations are negligible. 
→ Therefore, the 65 mL Type II bottle is technically covered by the validated 50 mL 
bottle data. 
Based on this, the validated CCI studies scientifically cover the 7.5 mL Type I vial and 65 
mL Type II bottle presentations and confirm equivalent sealing performance. 

3. Leachables/Extractables, Permeability, and Environmental Protection 
Type I and Type II glass, as well as bromobutyl stoppers, are established components of the 
product’s primary packaging system. Historical data and material specifications show:
• Glass types (Type I and II) do not introduce organic leachables and have controlled 
inorganic extractables. 
• Bromobutyl stoppers have well-characterized extractables profiles, meeting Ph. Eur. 
3.2.9 requirements. 
• The packaging components are non-permeable and protect against moisture and gas 
ingress. 
• Both Type I and Type II glass provide complete protection from humidity and light 
(colorless glass is accepted for this product since the drug substance is not light-
sensitive). 
No new leachables/extractables risks are introduced, as no new material or supplier is being 
implemented. 

4. Impact on Product Quality, Safety, and Efficacy 
The proposed presentations introduce no change to:
• the drug product formulation, 
• the manufacturing process, 
• sterilization method, or 
The packaging systems are pharmacopeially compliant, validated, and technically equivalent. 
Therefore, there is no negative impact on:
• product quality, 
• safety, 
• efficacy, 
• or stability.

5. Conclusion 
The introduction of a new stopper and crimp cap as an additional packaging option does not 
alter the container-closure system’s protective performance. 
Based on validated CCI data, material compliance (Type I/II glass and bromobutyl stoppers), 
and established extractables/leachables profiles, the packaging for the 7.5 mL Type I vial and 
65 mL Type II bottle provides equivalent protection to that of the submitted 30 mL Type I 
vial.

Question/Consideration:
Question 3
Please provide the results of the natural stability study of the finished product prepared with 
the proposed change (change in packaging-closing system) that you have to date, from the 
batches submitted in the initial dossier, in order to support the required shelf life of the 
product. Please note that the product's shelf life will be granted based on the submitted 
stability results and in accordance with the decision tree for data evaluation for estimating the 
shelf life period of PFTs contained in Appendix 1 of Resolution No. 3157 of 2018.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1 (CTD section):
We would like to inform that in support of the requested shelf life, we would like to clarify 
the following: 
Natural (long-term) stability data for the finished product packaged with the proposed 
bromobutyl stopper are currently available up to 12 months the same is provided for your 
ready reference. The complete 48-month stability data will be available by February 2028, in 
accordance with the approved Post-Approval Stability Protocol and Stability Commitment 
(Module 3 sections P.8.1, P.8.2, and P.8.3). 
Although the full 48-month data set for the bromobutyl stopper is not yet finalized, we 
respectfully request the Health Authority to maintain the 48-month shelf life, based on the 
following scientific and regulatory justifications: 

1. Demonstrated equivalent or superior protection of the new bromobutyl stopper 
Extensive characterization studies, including:
• Extractables and leachables assessment, P.2.4.06_022984962 
• Container-Closure Integrity (CCI), P.2.4.02_022985167 
• Compatibility of Drug Product with Packaging Materials P.2.4.05_022985168 
• Justification of the Choice of the Container Closure System and the Container 
Materials, P.2.4.01_022985165 
All the characterization provided demonstrated that the bromobutyl stopper provides 
equivalent or superior protection compared to the currently registered chlorobutyl stopper. 
No interactions or adverse trends have been identified that would indicate an impact on 
quality, safety, or efficacy over long-term storage. 

2. Supportive 12-month natural stability data 
The 12-month long-term stability data available for the finished product with the bromobutyl 
stopper (P.8.3.01_IQMS-260415) remain well within specification and are fully aligned 
with the historical stability profile of batches packaged with the chlorobutyl stopper 
(approved for 48 months). 
These results provide strong early confirmation that the change in stopper composition does 
not alter degradation behavior or product stability. 

3. No changes to other critical parameters 
The following remain unchanged:
• Formulation 
• Manufacturing process 
• Type I/II glass container 
• Storage conditions 
The stopper composition is the only variable, and such changes are not expected to affect 
long-term stability for this type of parenteral formulation. 

4. Post-Approval Stability Commitment ensures full long-term verification 
In accordance with the Post-Approval Stability Protocol and Stability Commitment 
P.8.2.01_022988083, Bayer will:
• Continue the long-term stability study up to 48 months, 
• Submit periodic updates to the Health Authority as data become available.

This ensures robust ongoing verification of the product’s stability with the new stopper. 

Request to Maintain the 48-Month Shelf Life 
Given that:
• Bromobutyl rubber is scientifically and commercially recognized as a suitable and 
stable elastomer for long-term parenteral packaging, 
• Available 12-month natural stability data show no changes or trends of concern, and 
• Full 48-month data will be provided as committed, 
We respectfully request the Health Authority to maintain the 48-month shelf life for the 
product.

Answer/Response:
보완답변 1 (3.2.S.2.5):
A) Regeneron Ireland 의 원료의약품(FDS) 공정밸리데이션 중
- UF/DF 공정의 단백질 농도 기준 설정 타당성
제조 공정 개발 과정에서, 개발 및 특성화 연구와 과거 제조 경험을 기반으로 목표 FCP(Final Concentrated Pool) 단백질 농도에 대한 허용 가능한 제조 범위가 설정되었습니다. FCP 의 높은 단백질 농도는 sucrose 조정 및 제형 단위 작업을 통해 허용 가능한 수준으로 희석됩니다. FCP 단계에서 단백질 농도가 낮으면 제형화 중 과다 희석이 발생하여 잠재적으로 지정된 범위 미만의 원료의약품(FDS)이 발생할 수 있습니다. 상업 제조를 위해 확립된 범위(165-184 g/L)는 공정 일관성을 보장하기 위해 일상적인 제조 중에 충족해야 하는 주요하지 않은 공정 조건으로 간주됩니다.
일반적으로 생명공학 공정에서 한외여과/정용여과(ultrafiltration/diafiltration) 후 최종 농축 풀(FCP)은 실제 필요한 최소 농도보다 훨씬 높게 설정됩니다.
그런 다음 목표 FCP 단백질 농도 외에도 FCP 단백질 농도에 대한 하한 기준을 설정하고 CQA(Critical Quality Attribute)로 분류했습니다.
CQA(≥ 128.8g/L)는 생산된 물질이 추가 제품 희석 및 제제화 단계와 호환되는 농도를 갖도록 하는 데 필요한 최소 FCP 단백질 농도입니다. 추가 세부 정보는 아래 표 1 에 나와 있습니다.
한외여과/정용여과(UF/DF) 단위 작동 후 제제화 단계에서 sucrose 완충액, 첨가제 완충액 및 희석 완충액의 첨가로 인한 희석이 있습니다. 허용 기준(≥ 128.8 g/L)은 3 개의 완충액을 추가한 후 FDS 가 최종 출하 기준(103 - 126 g/L) 내에 있도록 FCP 단계에서 필요한 최소 농도로 설정되었습니다.

- 모든 배치의 UF/DF 공정의 TMP 기준 및 결과
UF/DF 공급 유량과 TMP 기준 및 결과는 아래를 참조하십시오.
로트 8337700061 의 허용 가능한 막횡단 압력(TMP) 및 공급 유량 한계 미만의 이탈은 분석법에서 의도하지 않은 보류 후 1 차 농축 단계를 다시 시작한 것에 기인하며, 배치 로트 8337700061 에 대한 고분자량 형성의 증가가 없었기 때문에 검증에 영향을 미치지 않았습니다. (S.2.5.01_022985518_01 point 2.1.4. Concentration and Diafiltration Process Step Performance 참조)
1 프로세싱 중 작업자가 실수로 바닥 저울을 밟아 중량 경보가 울리고 시스템이 일시적으로 멈췄습니다.

B) Regeneron Ireland 에서 수행한 원료의약품 중간체 hold time 검증자료(공정별 미생물학적,
물리화학적 안정성 평가 자료)
문서 S.2.5.01_022985518_01 section 3 Validation of Extended Hold Times 에서는, 화학 및 미생물 시험에 대해 발송 구역(Regeneron, USA, 공정 구역 PA2X)에서 수행된 기존의 공정 밸리데이션에 대한 참조가 이루어집니다. 화학적 안정성은 장비 및 용액에 따라 다르고 미생물학적 안정성은 장비에 따라 달라지지만, 화학적 안정성과 미생물 안정성은 모두 사이트에 독립적입니다. 동일한 홀드 백과 폐쇄 시스템이 사용됩니다. PA2X holding time 밸리데이션을 참조하기 위한 포인트별 근거는 표 3-2 에 나와 있습니다.
PA12 에서의 추가 holding time 밸리데이션은 UF/DF hold time 에 대해서만 수행되었습니다(섹션 3.1 Microbial Hold 참조). UF/DF 공정 중 풀 백은 미국 Regeneron PA2X 와 아일랜드 Regeneron PA12 간에 동일하지만, 제조 유연성을 위해 hold time 을 연장하기 위해 PPQ 동안 PA12 에서 microbial hold 를 검증했습니다.
따라서 전송 장치에서의 공정 밸리데이션으로서 이전에 제출된 문서인 S.2.5.01#022972866_02 section 4 Validation of Extended Hold Times 또한 참조하십시오.

doc_name: VV-RFI-004209 - CMC Response - REC:31184+REC_32903 - Eylea 8mg PFS - KR (Korean trans)
Question/Consideration:
보완요청 2
- 바이알과 프리필드시린지 출하시험 비교평가 시 기준설정 타당성
- 프리필드시린지에 대한 MFI 분석 결과 및 고찰
Answer/Response:
보완답변 2 (3.2.S.4.5; 3.2.P.2.2; 3.2.P.2.4; 3.2.P.5.6; 3.2.R.2):
Vial 및 PFS 의 출하 시험을 평가하여 기준의 설정근거
배치 출하 비교 한계를 계산하기 위해 신청자가 일반적으로 사용하는 통계 방법론은 95% 신뢰도/99% 커버리지 허용 오차 구간(TI)입니다. 이 방법론은 여기에 적용되지 않았는데, 이는 바이알 내 DP 와 PFS 내 DP 간의 comparability exercise 에 사용할 수 있는 것과 거의 동일한 과거 바이알 배치 세트를 사용하여 바이알 배치 출하 기준을 계산하는 데 동일한 방법론이 사용되었기 때문입니다. 바이알 내 DP 에 대한 기준 허용 한계 계산은 CTD 섹션 S.4.5.01-01 및 P.5.6.01-01 을 참조하십시오.
바이알 내 DP 와 PFS 내 DP 간의 comparability exercise 을 위해 3 개의 추가 바이알 배치, 즉 3 개의 바이알 비교기 배치만 사용할 수 있었습니다. 따라서 사용 가능한 바이알 배치의 최소/최대 범위를 comparability exercise 의 벤치마크로 사용했으며, 이는 95% 신뢰도/99% 커버리지 허용 오차 구간(TI)에 비해 더 엄격한 접근 방식입니다. 95% 신뢰도/ 99% TI 는 CTD 섹션 R.2.02-02 에 보고된 통계와 함께 표 2 에 제공됩니다. SE-UPLC 의 경우 통계에 소수 자릿수가 추가되었습니다. 모든 TI 는 각각의 최소/최대 범위보다 넓습니다. 따라서 PFS 의 결과를 과거 바이알의 최소 및 최대 값과 비교하는 것은 PFS 와 바이알의 comparability 를 평가하기 위해 정당화되는 것으로 간주됩니다.

PFS 에 대한 MFI 분석 결과 및 고찰
유리 시린지 배럴은 플런저 스토퍼의 움직임을 보장하기 위해 실리콘 오일로 윤활되고 시린지 팁은 텅스텐 형식 부품을 사용하여 제조되므로 두 구성 요소 모두에 대해 완제의약품의 품질에 미치는 영향을 철저히 평가했습니다.
첫 번째 연구에서는 Design of Experience 접근 방식을 사용하여 제품의 안정성을 분석하기 위해 Aflibercept 용액 114.3mg/mL 에 실리콘 오일과 텅스텐을 스파이크했습니다. 스파이크 농도는 시린지의 지정된 최대 실리콘 오일 함량의 10%, 100% 및 200%에 해당하며, 각각 시린지의 지정된 최대 텅스텐 함량에 해당합니다.
포괄적인 결과는 CTD 섹션 P.2.2.10-02 에 나와 있습니다. 전반적으로 5°C 에서 24 개월 보관하는 동안 물리적 외관, 투명도, 색상, pH, 단백질 농도 및 단백질 무결성에서 의미 있는 변화가 관찰되지 않았습니다. 또한, 현미경 검사로 측정된 보이지 않는 미립자의 의미 있는 증가도 관찰되지 않았습니다. 전반적으로 모든 기준 한계가 충족되었습니다.
이 데이터는 Aflibercept 용액 114.3 mg/mL 제형과 유리 실리콘 오일 및 텅스텐의 잠재적 잔류물과 호환성을 확인하고 Aflibercept 용액 114.3 mg/mL 와 용기 폐쇄 시스템의 호환성을 확인했습니다(CTD 섹션 P.2.2.10-02 참조).
두 번째 연구에서는 완제의약품 용액으로 잠재적인 실리콘 (오일)이 침출될 수 있는 전반적인 위험을 분석했습니다. Vetter 에서 충전된 기술 배치의 시린지는 실험실 조건 또는 상용 규모 장비에서 가해지는 다양한 응력(stress)을 받았습니다.
유도 결합 플라즈마 발광 분광법(ICP-OES) 및 유동 이미징 현미경(MFI)을 사용하여 잠재적인 실리콘 오일 전달과 관련하여 응력을 받은 시린지를 분석했습니다. MFI 소프트웨어는 실리콘 오일 방울/입자를 전용으로 계수하기 위해 필터를 적용하고 있었습니다.
MFI 및 ICP-OES 로 측정한 샘플은 압력 변화(외부 표면 멸균 과정뿐만 아니라 공기 운송 중 잠재적인 스토퍼 움직임을 시뮬레이션하기 위해)와 와류(vortex) 장치를 사용한 집중적인 진탕(shaking)을 가했습니다. 전반적으로 표 3 및 표 4 에 나타난 바와 같이, 스트레스를 받지 않은 대조군에 비해 유리 실리콘 오일 및 실리콘 오일 입자의 증가는 관찰되지 않았습니다.
테스트된 시나리오 및 분석 방법과 무관하게, 기술 배치에 대한 모든 데이터는 예상된 방법 및 샘플 변동성 범위에 속합니다.
또한, 시린지 배럴을 포함한 일차 포장 구성 요소로 추출물(extractable) 연구를 수행했습니다. 추출은 물과 50% 에탄올로 수행되었습니다. 분석은 LC-MS, GC-MS 및 HC-GC-MS 로 수행되었습니다. 이에 따라, 추출물 용매에서 1.5 ug/day 의 안전 우려 임계값을 초과하는 유기 화합물을 함유한 실리콘이 검출되지 않았습니다(CTD 섹션 P.2.4.06-01 참조).
추출물 결과는 3 개의 Aflibercept 용액 114.3 mg/mL PPQ 최종 패키징 배치에 대한 침출 안정성 연구에서 추가로 확인되었습니다. 12 개월 보관 후 결과를 확인할 수 있으며, AFL 114.3 mg/mL 용액의 보고된 임계값인 1.0 μg/mL 를 초과하는 농도에서 유기 침출물 화합물을 함유한 실리콘이 검출되지 않았습니다(CTD 섹션 P.2.4.07-01). 이 연구는 사용기한 24 개월이 끝날 때까지 계속됩니다.
전반적으로, 수행된 연구는 실리콘 및 텅스텐 입자와 관련하여 제품 품질 위험을 나타내지 않았으며 Aflibercept 용액 114.3 mg/mL 와 용기 마개 시스템의 호환성을 확인했습니다.

doc_name: VV-RFI-004209 - CMC Response - REC:31184+REC_32903 - Eylea 8mg PFS - KR (Korean trans)
Question/Consideration:
보완요청 3
1) 완제의약품 일차용기 관련
- 추출물 상세 결과
- 침출물 계획서, 시험조건 및 최신의 자료
2) 완제의약품 사용 중 안정성 타당성(필요시 사용기간을 고려한 사용 중 안정성 자료 제출)
Answer/Response:
보완답변 3 (3.2.P.2.4; 3.2.P.2.6; 3.2.P.8.3):
3.1)
추출물 연구의 자세한 결과가 제공되며 연구 디자인, 저장 조건 및 결과를 포함한 침출 물 연구 데이터가 각각 CTD 섹션 P.2.4.06-01 및 P.2.4.07-01 에 포함되었습니다.

3.2)
신청자는 (투여를 위해 준비된 PFS 로서) 25°C 에서 6 시간 시점과, PFS 내 Aflibercept 114.3 mg/mL 의 미개봉 블리스터로서 의료전문가(HCP)의 조작이 예약된 25°C 에서 24 시간 시점의 평가된 사용 중 안정성 간의 차이를 설명하고자 합니다.
Aflibercept 114.3 mg/mL PFS 의 제안된 라벨에는 다음과 같은 문구가 포함되어 있습니다: “사용 전 미개봉된 아일리아 8mg 의 블리스터팩은 24 시간까지 실온(25°C / 77°F)에서 보관할 수 있다. 신청자는 이 문구에 설명된 24 시간이 CTD 섹션 P.2.6.01-01 에 기술된 compatibility (“사용 중 안정성”) 연구를 참조하지 않는다는 점을 강조하고 싶습니다.
제안된 라벨 문구는 멸균 장벽이 손상되지 않은 미개봉 블리스터를 의미하며 섹션 P.8.3.11-04 에 설명된 전체 냉장 보관 시간(TOR) 평가를 기반으로 합니다. 이 전용 연구에서는 PFS 내 Aflibercept 114.3 mg/mL 의 최대 TOR 을 전체 공정 밸리데이션의 일부로 평가했습니다. PFS 내 Aflibercept 용액 114.3mg/mL 완제의약품(DP)의 총 TOR 은 충전, 라벨링, 조립, 블리스터링, 멸균 및 포장으로 구성된 end-to-end 제조 시간뿐만 아니라 완제품을 환자에게 유통 및 배송하는 시간을 포함합니다. PFS 내 Aflibercept 114.3 mg/mL 의 경우, 전체 TOR 이 정의 및 제어되며, 최대 TOR 에는 실온에서 사용하기 전에 미개봉 블리스터를 보관할 수 있도록 의료전문가(HCP)의 핸들링을 위해 24 시간의 예약이 포함되어 있습니다. 이 연구에 대해 현재 모든 이용 가능한 24M 안정성 결과는 사용기한 기준 내에 있습니다. 몇몇 소수의 데이터 포인트가 보완답변서 작성 시점에 보류중입니다.
또한, 분석 비교 프로그램의 결과가 PFS 제조 공정(멸균된 PFS 가 사용됨)이 바이알로 제조된 완제의약품과 분석적으로 유사한 Aflibercept 용액 114.3 mg/mL 완제의약품을 산출한다는 것을 입증하였기 때문에, 생성된 바이알 데이터는 25°C 에서 24 시간 동안 PFS 보관을 지원한다는 충분한 확신을 제공합니다.
전체 데이터는 개봉하지 않은 블리스터를 최대 24 시간 동안 실온에서 보관할 수 있다는 주장을 뒷받침합니다.

반면, 신청자는 완제의약품 용액과 주사 바늘의 호환성을 입증하는 데이터를 제공했습니다. 이 전용 "사용 중 안정성" 연구는 CTD 섹션 P.2.6.01-01 에 설명되어 있습니다. P.8.3.11-04 에 기술된 컨셉에 따라 최대 TOR 에 노출된 후, PFS 를 블리스터에서 꺼내고, 바늘을 부착하고, PFS 를 프라이밍하고, 25°C 에서 최대 6 시간 동안(주입 단계 전) 프라이밍된 상태로 유지했습니다. 그 후 DP 를 분석했습니다. 이 데이터는 25°C 에서 최대 6 시간 동안 DP 와 주사 바늘의 내부 내강(lumen)이 접촉하여 품질 손상이 없었으며 제품이 프라이밍된 주사기 단계에서 안정적임을 확인합니다. 이 연구는 적용하기 전에 투여 구성(administration configuration)과의 호환성을 확인하기 위한 것입니다. 데이터는 완제의약품에 대한 지식을 늘리기 위해 얻어졌으며 특정 사용 중 안정성 시간을 정의하도록 예상되지 않습니다.

Answer/Response:
보완답변 4 (3.2.P.3.5; 3.2.P.8.3):
기능적 성능은 현재까지 24 개월 동안 진행 중인 실시간 안정성 연구의 일환으로 성공적으로 테스트되었습니다. 결과는 CTD 섹션 P.8.3.11-02 에 나와 있습니다. 장기 보관 중 기능성 시험에 대한 모든 허용 기준이 충족되었습니다.
기능적 성능은 전체 제어 전략 내에서 공정 중 제어(IPC)로 평가됩니다. 이 테스트는 DP 공정 밸리데이션 중에 수행되었으며 상업적 제조 전반에 걸쳐 계속 유지될 것입니다.
기능성 시험은 ISO 2859-1 “Sampling procedures for inspection by attributes — Part 1: Sampling schemes indexed by acceptance quality limit (AQL) for lot-by-lot inspection”에 따라 수행되며, 이는 샘플 세트 검사를 기반으로 배치를 수락하기 위한 샘플링 계획 및 절차를 제공합니다. 이 표준은 구체적인 실제 결과나 값을 제공하지 않고 제품 배치가 지정된 품질 요구 사항을 충족하는지 여부를 결정하는 방법론을 간략하게 설명합니다.
ISO 2859-1 에 따른 평가 프로세스에는 제조 배치의 대표 샘플 크기 테스트와 사전 결정된 허용 기준에 대한 평가가 포함됩니다. 제조 배치의 적합 또는 거부는 특정 기준을 준수하거나 준수하지 않은 배치 특정 샘플 세트에서 발견된 샘플의 수를 기반으로 합니다. 테스트 결과는 P.3.5.01-01 과 같이 "pass" 또는 "complies"로 보고됩니다.

doc_name: VV-RFI-004209 - CMC Response - REC:31184+REC_32903 - Eylea 8mg PFS - KR (Korean trans)
Question/Consideration:
보완요청 5
A) 완제의약품의 냉장 및 상온 노출이 엔도톡신시험 결과에 미치는 영향(Low Endotoxin Recovery)에 대한 평가 자료
B) 불용성미립자 기준 설정 타당성
Answer/Response:
보완답변 5:
A)
냉장 및 실온에 노출된 후 내독소 검사 결과는 제형 원료 의약품(FDS)에 대해 사용할 수 있으며 CTD 섹션 S.4.3.01-02 에 제공됩니다. 결과는 냉장 조건 또는 실온에서 보관하는 경우 FDS 의 내독소 회수에 영향을 미치지 않는 것으로 나타났습니다.
FDS 는 완제의약품 용액과 동일한 조성을 가지고 있으며, 이에 따라 완제의약품 시험에서도 낮은 내독소 회수율(Low Endotoxin Recovery)이 발생하지 않는다고 가정할 수 있습니다.
LER 의 부재를 확인하기 위해 현재 Vetter Pharma 의 제조 및 시험 사이트에서 전용 연구가 진행되었습니다. 결과는 사전에 정의된 기준사항을 충족하였고, 최종 연구 보고서가 제공됩니다.

B)
Subvisible Particulate Matter Content 에 대한 기준은 Ph. Eur. chapter 2.9.19 의 필수적인 부분입니다. 하위 장 “Method 2. Microscopic particle count test”에 따르면, 평가 항에 “Test 2.B – 공칭 함량이 100mL 미만인 용기에 공급되는 injection 용액 또는 infusion 용액: 테스트된 단위에 존재하는 입자의 평균 수가 10 μm 이상의 용기 당 3000 개를 초과하지 않고 25 μm 이상의 용기당 300 개를 초과하지 않는 경우 준비물은 시험을 준수합니다." 10 μm 이상 입자에 대해 200 particles/mL 이하, 25 μm 이상 입자에 대해 20 particles/mL 이하로 제출된 보다 엄격한 기준은 Aflibercept 용액 40 mg/mL 프리필드시린지에 대해 승인된 기준과 조화를 이뤘습니다. 이러한 제안된 한계는 이미 주사 용액에 대해 Ph. Eur.에 따라 허용되는 한계에 비해 상당히 타이트하게 구성되며, Ph. Eur. 한계는 용기당 허용되는 입자를 나타내고 제안된 한계는 입자/mL 를 나타냅니다. 0.184 mL/PFS 의 목표 충전 부피를 기준으로 현재 제안된 입자/mL 의 허용 기준은 10 μm 이상의 입자에 대해 ~37 개 입자/용기, 25μm 이상의 입자에 대해 ~4 개 입자/용기에 해당하며, 따라서 Ph. Eur. 챕터 2.9.19 에 명시된 용기당 허용 기준과 비교할 때 ~81 의 인자 타이트닝을 구성합니다. 또한, 미립자 물질 함량의 경우 Aflibercept 용액 114.3 mg/mL 에 대해 현재 사용 가능한 데이터 세트는 너무 제한되어 더 엄격한 사양 한계를 도출할 수 없는 것으로 여겨집니다.
Subvisible particulate matter 결과는 정규 분포가 없는 것으로 알려져 있으므로 향후 결과의 범위를 예측하기 어렵습니다. 따라서 신청자는 10μm 이상 입자에 대해 200particles/mL 이하, 25μm 이상 입자에 대해 20 particles/mL 이하로 제안된 한계를 정당한 것으로 여깁니다.

Source:
Eylea_114.3 mg-mL_PFS_LER_Report_signed (new)

Question/Consideration: Potential residues of class 1 solvent (carbon tetrachloride) in an intermediate or in the final substance should be addressed since some originator solvents (e.g. chloroform and dichloromethane (methylene chloride)) have been used in the route of synthesis (refer to CPMP/QWP/450/03 Rev. 1, Annex I, B: Class 1 Solvents Present as an Impurity).
Answer/Response:
Below, a detailed purge factor calculation of carbon tetrachloride, a potential mutagenic impurity (PMI) in the starting material phenyl-oxodihydropyridine-carbothioamide of the manufacturing process of BAY 2927088 hydrate micronized drug substance, is described.
For the calculation of purge factors, reactivity, solubility and volatility of the impurities are identified as physicochemical parameters that influence the removal of the specific impurity in the manufacturing process. Under the given process conditions these parameters are assessed to define the purge factors for each individual operation. Basis of the determination of purge factors is provided in Table 2, as described by A. Teasdale et al.2

The total purge factor is obtained by multiplication of the purge factors of each operation and step. The concentration of the respective impurity before purging (concentration at start) is estimated in a conservative way. Purge ratios are calculated by division of the obtained total purge factors by the total purge factor required to ensure an acceptable level of the respective impurity in BAY 2927088 hydrate micronized drug substance, i.e. 1000 ppm = 0.10%, in line with ICH guideline S9. A purge ratio of at least 1000 is considered to provide “sufficient confidence that the level of the impurity in the drug substance will be below the acceptable limit such that no analytical testing is recommended for this impurity.”3

Carbon tetrachloride is a potential impurity in dichloromethane, which is employed as solvent in the first part of step B-2 of the synthesis of starting material phenyl-oxodihydropyridine-carbothioamide. Due to its high volatility (boiling point of 77 °C), carbon tetrachloride would effectively be purged during the drying procedure of isolated solid products in steps where higher-boiling solvents are utilized. Moreover, solvents of low or moderate polarity as utilized in steps 1 and B-2 (part 2) would additionally contribute to the purge of carbon tetrachloride during the isolation procedures of the solid products of those steps.

Source:  S.2.6.11_1.0 Manufacturing Process Development-Additional Information/ BAY2927088 hydrate micronized drug substance (purge factor calculation)(#IQMS _427463_1.0; new)

2 (a) A. Teasdale, S. Fenner, A. Ray, A. Ford, A. Phillips, Org. Process Res. Dev. 2010, 14, 943–945. (b) A. Teasdale, D. Elder, S.-J. Chang, S. Wang, R. Thompson, N. Benz, I.H. Sanchez Flores, Org. Process Res. Dev. 2013, 17, 221−230.
3 ICH M7(R2) Guideline on assessment and control of DNA reactive (mutagenic) impurities in pharmaceuticals to limit potential carcinogenic risk EMA/CHMP/ICH/83812/2013.

Question/Consideration: Skip testing to ensure capability of the analytical procedures to detect and measure the following residual solvents (n-Heptane, tert-Butyl alcohol, 2-Methyltetrahydrofuran, & methanol).
Answer/Response:
Organic solvents 2-Methyltetrahydrofuran, n-Heptane, and tert-Butyl alcohol are used to manufacture Pyridyl-methylammonium ethanesulfonate.
2-Methyltetrahydrofuran, n-Heptane and tert-Butyl alcohol are all below the limit of quantification (quantification limit is less than 10 percent of the ICH Q3C limit of 0.5% for n-Heptane / 2-Methyltetrahydrofuran and 0.35% for tert-Butyl alcohol) in the starting material Pyridyl-methylammonium ethanesulfonate.
Tert-Butyl alcohol is also used to manufacture starting material Phenyl-oxodihydropyridine-carbothioamideand and is specified according to ICH Q3C class 2 with a limit of 0.35% in this starting material.
Thus, carry-over into the drug substance does not need to be considered and therefore skip testing of the drug substance is not required.
Methanol is used in step 2a of BAY 2927088 purified intermediate. Methanol is observed in BAY 2927088 purified at levels < 0.03% in development and validation campaign batches.
Thus, methanol was never observed above ten percent of the ICH Q3C limit (class 2, limit of 3000 mg/kg) in batches of BAY 2927088 hydrate micronized drug substance. The risk of a contamination of BAY 2927088 hydrate micronized drug substance with methanol is therefore assessed to be very low, and the quality attribute residual methanol is not included in the specification of BAY 2927088 hydrate micronized drug substance. The analytical method employed for residual solvents is selective also for methanol, thus, in case methanol would be present in batches it would be detected and therefore no additional skip testing is required.

Source:   S.2.3.03_4.0 Justification of Starting Materials / BAY 2927088 hydrate micronized drug substance (IQMS_417984_4.0; amended)
S.2.4.01_1.0 Discussion and Control of Critical Steps / BAY 2927088 hydrate micronized drug substance (#IQMS_260925_1.0; unchanged)

Question/Consideration: For tables 4-5 and 4-6 of “P.2.4.07_022986601_01 Migration Studies.pdf”, please clarify how the concentration limit (e.g. from ICH Q3D(R2)) can be converted the same unit as to the tables for comparison.
Answer/Response:
The appendix 2 of ICH Q3D is listing permittable daily exposure (PDE) for elements of classes 1, 2A, 2B and 3 in µg/day (see table A.2.1 of ICH Q3D). The CTD section P.2.4.07-01 expresses the results obtained for elemental impurities in leachable studies as ng/mL (refer to tables 4-5 to 4-6 of the respective document).

To convert the concentration of ng/mL into µg/day, the maximum daily injection volume of Eylea 8mg PFS of 0.14 mL (bilateral treatment with 0.07 mL) must be considered, together with a conversion factor of 1000 between µg and ng.

Resultantly:
Y µg/day =
X ng/mL × 0.14 mL/day
1000
= 0,000140 × X ng/mL

And for conversion in the other direction:
Y ng/mL =
X µg/day × 1000
0.14 mL/day = 7142.857 × X µg/day

That means that the highest concentration found for an elemental impurity, being Aluminum concentration of 5711 ng/mL at the 12 months time point, converts into 0.80 µg/day.

On the other hand, the lowest PDE for elemental impurities in ICH Q3D Table A.2.1, being Cadmium at 2 µg/day, converts into 14285.71 ng/mL.

This means consequently that all results reported in P.2.4.07-01 are below the limits for elemental impurities given in ICH Q3D.

Source: P.2.4.07-01 Migration Studies / Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL in prefilled syringe for intravitreous injection (#022986601; unchanged)
keywords: ICHQ3D; elemental impurities; risk assessment; analytical procedures

doc_name: VV-RFI-005544 - CMC Response - Finerenone coated tablet 40 mg - 20260416
Question/Consideration:
Submit the rationale for not establishing control specifications for solvents and catalysts used in starting material synthesis.
Additional request:
Re-submission for N, N- Dimethylformamide is required with measured data showing <10% of AI (actual measured values).
Methanol is Class 2, so loss on drying cannot be used. Please submit data demonstrating detection at <10% of AI.
Answer/Response:
KOEI utilizes N, N-Dimethylformamide and methanol during the manufacturing of the starting material 4-Amino-5-methylpyridone (SM2). As part of supplier qualification risk assessment, monitoring data of selected batches have been evaluated showing that N, N-Dimethylformamide is consistently below 1/10 of the ICH limit (ICH Q3C option 1).
Methanol is controlled by means of the test item loss on drying with an acceptance criterium of max. 0.3%. This acceptance criterium is equivalent to the requirement of the ICH limit (ICH Q3C option 1) for methanol, especially when considering that N, N-Dimethylformamide and methanol are controlled together with water as by means of the test item loss on drying.
Please note that loss on drying included in the specification S.2.3.08 is used for the control of the starting material 4-Amino-5-methylpyridone. This control determination of the 4-Amino-5-methylpyridone is not used for the evaluation on the presence/non-presence of methanol in Finerenone micronized drug substance. Since methanol is used in the manufacturing process at a later stage (i.e. step 6: manufacturing of Finerenone crude), methanol is controlled by introduction of a specification limit in the already established specification of Finerenone crude by means of headspace gas chromatography using flame ionization detection, see S.2.4.03. Summarizing, with regard to the control of methanol it is concluded that the control strategy adopts the use of methanol adequately - based on the design of the manufacturing process and in compliance with the requirements of the guideline ICH Q3C.
Regarding catalysts: KOEI uses Pd/C during the synthesis of 4-Amino-5-methylpyridone. As part of supplier qualification risk assessment, monitoring data of selected batches have been evaluated showing that Pd is consistently below 0.3 ppm (mg/kg). Thus, residual amounts of Pd in the starting material 4-Amino-5-methylpyridone are far below the control limit of ICH guideline Q3D (R2), which is 10 mg/kg for oral drug product formulations.
Data on N, N-Dimethylformamide and Pd are presented in amended document S.2.3.12. The three batches presented in S.2.3.12 indicate that the content of N,N-Dimethylformamide is consistently below 0.009%. According to ICH guideline Q3C, the control limit of N,N-Dimethylformamide is 880 ppm or 0.088%. Thus, the 10% threshold of the ICH guideline equals 88 ppm or 0.009%. Therefore, the residual solvent N,N-Dimethylformamide is considered not to represent a risk with regard to carry over (from the starting material 4-Amino-5-methylpyridone from the supplier KOEI into the manufacturing process of Finerenone). In the terminology of the guideline ICH Q3C, these solvents are not likely to be present.
Please note that according to section 3.5 of the ICH Q3C guideline, pharmaceutical manufacturers have to provide information as following: “If solvents of Class 2 or Class 3 are present at greater than their Option 1 limits or 0.5%, respectively, they should be identified and quantified.” Thus, since N, N-Dimethylformamide is not likely to be present, it is neither required by the guideline to introduce a control limit for N, N-Dimethylformamide nor to provide quantitative data for the residual solvent N, N-Dimethylformamide below the reporting threshold of 10 % of the control limit.

doc_name: VV-RFI-005544 - CMC Response - Finerenone coated tablet 40 mg - 20260416
Question/Consideration: Among the data on the starting material manufacturers (Kingchem Life Science LLC and SAI Life Science Limited), submit the rationale for not establishing control specifications for solvents and catalysts used in starting material synthesis.
Answer/Response:
Kingchem Life Science LLC utilizes dichloroethane, tetrahydrofuran, dichloromethane, and isopropanol during the manufacturing of the starting material methoxy nitrile aldehyde (SM1).
Regarding tetrahydrofuran and isopropanol: Since these solvents are intentionally introduced and utilized as processing solvents in subsequent steps of the API synthesis (isopropanol in step 2 (ethyl-pyridinone intermediate), tetrahydrofuran in step 5 (rac-Amido-TH-naphthyridine intermediate), establishing separate control specifications for them in the starting material (SM1) is considered redundant. Comprehensive controls for these solvents are appropriately implemented and monitored at these later stages of the manufacturing process to ensure compliance in the final API.
Regarding dichloromethane and dichloroethane: As part of supplier qualification risk assessments, residual dichloromethane and dichloroethane have been detected in the starting material methoxy nitrile aldehyde (SM1) at levels already below the established ICH Q3C limits for residual solvents. Considering the subsequent 8-step synthesis process, which includes purification steps, a significant further depletion of these residual solvents is expected. Consequently, any potential impact from these solvents on the quality of the final API can be reliably precluded, and therefore, no additional specific control specifications for dichloromethane and dichloroethane are deemed necessary within the SM1 specification.
As dichloromethane is classified by ICH Q3C as a class II solvent, a risk assessment was performed to evaluate the necessity of setting a specification for dichloromethane in the starting material methoxy nitrile aldehyde supplied by Kingchem Life Science LLC.
The starting condition for the worst-case risk assessment was the hypothesis that dichloromethane is present in the starting material methoxy nitrile aldehyde at a concentration level of 3%, which would exceed the ICH Q3C limit by a factor of 50. In this case, the required depletion factor with regard to Finerenone micronized drug substance would be 50 in order to reach a concentration level of 600 mg/kg in Finerenone micronized drug substance. The depletion capacity of the manufacturing process of Finerenone micronized drug substance was evaluated to be greater than 9*1013. Thus, the ratio of the required depletion factor compared to the assessed depletion factor of the manufacturing process is at least 1012. In other words, even if dichloromethane would be present in the starting material methoxy nitrile aldehyde at 3%, it would be depleted to a concentration level of far below 0.00000003 mg/kg (3*10-8 mg/kg) by means of the design of the manufacturing process.
In chapter 8.1 of the ICH M7 guideline, the following is stated: “Option 4: Understand process parameters and impact on residual impurity levels (including fate and purge knowledge) with sufficient confidence that the level of the impurity in the drug substance will be below the acceptable limit such that no analytical testing is recommended for this impurity. (i.e., the impurity does not need to be listed on any specification).”
Based on the worst-case assessment described above, the residual solvent dichloromethane would be reduced to a concentration level far below the allowed concentration threshold of 600 mg/kg in Finerenone micronized drug substance even if an unrealistically high amount of dichloromethane (of 3 %) in the starting material methoxy nitrile aldehyde would be assumed. Thus, it is in line with ICH guideline M7 to control this impurity by means of the design of the manufacturing process in which methoxy nitrile aldehyde supplied by Kingchem Life Science LLC is used as a starting material
As dichloroethane is classified by ICH Q3C as a class I solvent, a risk assessment was performed to evaluate the necessity of setting a specification for dichloroethane in the starting material methoxy nitrile aldehyde supplied by Kingchem Life Science LLC.
The starting condition for the worst-case risk assessment was the hypothesis that dichloroethane is present in the starting material methoxy nitrile aldehyde at a concentration level of 3%, which would exceed the ICH Q3C limit by a factor of 6000. In this case, the required depletion factor with regard to Finerenone micronized drug substance would be 6000 in order to reach a concentration level of 5 mg/kg in Finerenone micronized drug substance. Therefore, the depletion capacity of the manufacturing process of Finerenone micronized drug substance was evaluated to be greater than 1*1013. Thus, the ratio of the required depletion factor compared to the assessed depletion factor of the manufacturing process is at least 109. In other words, even if dichloroethane were present in the starting material methoxy nitrile aldehyde at 3%, it would be depleted to a concentration level of far below 0.00003 mg/kg by means of the design of the manufacturing process.
In chapter 8.1 of the ICH M7 guideline, the following is stated: “Option 4: Understand process parameters and impact on residual impurity levels (including fate and purge knowledge) with sufficient confidence that the level of the impurity in the drug substance will be below the acceptable limit such that no analytical testing is recommended for this impurity. (i.e., the impurity does not need to be listed on any specification).”
Based on the worst-case assessment described above, the residual solvent dichloroethane would be reduced to a concentration level far below the allowed concentration threshold of 5 mg/kg in Finerenone micronized drug substance even if an unrealistically high amount of dichloroethane (of 3 %) in the starting material methoxy nitrile aldehyde would be assumed. Thus, it is in line with ICH guideline M7 to control this impurity by means of the design of the manufacturing process in which methoxy nitrile aldehyde supplied by Kingchem Life Science LLC is used as a starting material.
Regarding catalysts: Kingchem Life Science LLC uses copper bromide during the synthesis of methoxy nitrile aldehyde. As part of the supplier's qualification risk assessment, elemental screening was performed, and copper was detected far below 30% of the ICH limit in the starting material.
Data on dichloromethane and dichloroethane and Cu are presented in document S.2.3.12.

SAI Life Science Limited does not use any catalysts or metal reagents during the synthesis of methoxy nitrile aldehyde (SM1).
Regarding solvents: They utilize chlorobenzene, dimethylformamide, methyl isobutyl ketone, and n-heptane for manufacturing the starting material methoxy nitrile aldehyde (SM1).
Chlorobenzene and n-heptane are routinely controlled within the specification of methoxy nitrile aldehyde (SM1).
Regarding dimethylformamide and methyl isobutyl ketone: As part of supplier qualification risk assessments, residual dimethylformamide and methyl isobutyl ketone have been detected in the starting material methoxy nitrile aldehyde (SM1) at levels already below the established ICH Q3C limits for residual solvents. Due to further depletion of theses solvents during the subsequent synthesis steps, any potential impact on the Finerenone quality can be reliably precluded, and consequently, no specific control limits for dimethylformamide and methyl isobutyl ketone are considered necessary within the SM1 specification.
Data on dimethylformamide and methyl isobutyl ketone are presented in document S.2.3.12.
As dimethylformamide is classified by ICH Q3C as a class II solvent, a risk assessment was performed to evaluate the necessity of setting a specification for dimethylformamide in the starting material methoxy nitrile aldehyde supplied by SAI.
The starting condition for the worst-case risk assessment was the hypothesis that dimethylformamide is present in the starting material methoxy nitrile aldehyde at a concentration level of 3%, which would exceed the ICH Q3C limit by a factor of 34. In this case, the required depletion factor with regard to Finerenone micronized drug substance would be 34 in order to reach a concentration level of 880 mg/kg in Finerenone micronized drug substance. The depletion capacity of the manufacturing process of Finerenone micronized drug substance was evaluated to be greater than 1*107. Thus, the ratio of the required depletion factor compared to the assessed depletion factor of the manufacturing process is at least 105. In other words, even if dimethylformamide would be present in the starting material methoxy nitrile aldehyde at 3%, it would be depleted to a concentration level of far below 0.3 mg/kg by means of the design of the manufacturing process.
In chapter 8.1 of the ICH M7 guideline, the following is stated: “Option 4: Understand process parameters and impact on residual impurity levels (including fate and purge knowledge) with sufficient confidence that the level of the impurity in the drug substance will be below the acceptable limit such that no analytical testing is recommended for this impurity. (i.e., the impurity does not need to be listed on any specification).”
Based on the worst-case assessment described above, the residual solvent dimethylformamide would be reduced to a concentration level far below the allowed concentration threshold of 880 mg/kg in Finerenone micronized drug substance even if an unrealistically high amount of dimethylformamide (of 3 %) in the starting material methoxy nitrile aldehyde would be assumed. Thus, it is in line with ICH guideline M7 to control this impurity by means of the design of the manufacturing process in which methoxy nitrile aldehyde supplied by SAI is used as a starting material.

As methyl isobutyl ketone is classified by ICH Q3C as a class II solvent, a risk assessment was performed to evaluate the necessity of setting a specification for methyl isobutyl ketone in the starting material methoxy nitrile aldehyde supplied by SAI.
The starting condition for the worst-case risk assessment was the hypothesis that methyl isobutyl ketone is present in the starting material methoxy nitrile aldehyde at a concentration level of 3%, which would exceed the ICH Q3C limit by a factor of 6.7. In this case, the required depletion factor with regard to Finerenone micronized drug substance would be 6.7 in order to reach a concentration level of 4500 mg/kg in Finerenone micronized drug substance. The depletion capacity of the manufacturing process of Finerenone micronized drug substance was evaluated to be greater than 3*107. Thus, the ratio of the required depletion factor compared to the assessed depletion factor of the manufacturing process is at least 106. In other words, even if methyl isobutyl ketone would be present in the starting material methoxy nitrile aldehyde at 3%, it would be depleted to a concentration level of far below 0.03 mg/kg by means of the design of the manufacturing process.
In chapter 8.1 of the ICH M7 guideline, the following is stated: “Option 4: Understand process parameters and impact on residual impurity levels (including fate and purge knowledge) with sufficient confidence that the level of the impurity in the drug substance will be below the acceptable limit such that no analytical testing is recommended for this impurity. (i.e., the impurity does not need to be listed on any specification).”
Based on the worst-case assessment described above, the residual solvent methyl isobutyl ketone would be reduced to a concentration level far below the allowed concentration threshold of 4500 mg/kg in Finerenone micronized drug substance even if an unrealistically high amount of methyl isobutyl ketone (of 3 %) in the starting material methoxy nitrile aldehyde would be assumed. Thus, it is in line with ICH guideline M7 to control this impurity by means of the design of the manufacturing process in which methoxy nitrile aldehyde supplied by SAI is used as a starting material.

Question/Consideration:
Describe the manufacturing process in detail, including step-by-step operating conditions, process control items, and equipment used in the process.
Additional request:
In-process control (IPC) information for the compression (tableting) step is missing in 32P33 and needs to be added. Since IPC results for the compression process are included in 32P35.
Answer/Response:
The manufacturing process description has been amended, including step-by-step operating conditions and information on the respective equipment (please see P.3.3.01). The process control items are listed in the section 3.2.P.3.3.02 (please refer to P.3.3.02).
The 3.2.P.3.3. section includes the documents P.3.3.01 as well as P.3.3.02. In‑process control (IPC) information for the compression (tableting) step is integrated in the manufacturing flow chart of the document P.3.3.01 and in the document P.3.3.02, Table 2. The table in P.3.3.02 describes the in‑process controls applied during the compression step (e.g. uniformity of mass, breaking load, disintegration and friability), including the respective acceptance criteria and test procedures according to Ph. Eur./USP/JP.
The operating conditions of the tableting step are selected to ensure compliance with the IPC ranges given in P.3.3.02. This means that the compression force is among other things adjusted based on the resulting/achieved breaking load of the tablets. Granule properties, such as the particle size distribution, can lead to varying compression forces, which is the reason why no specific compression force is defined. The operational setting parameters of the tableting step are therefore a consequence of adhering to the given IPCs. The max. applicable compression force is 16 kN. This information was amended to document P.3.3.01.

Answer/Response:
The consistency of the manufacturing process is, among other items, controlled by a regular determination of the tablet weight throughout the whole tableting process. The limit for this IPC test is set in accordance with Ph. Eur. 2.9.5 uniformity of mass +/- 7.5% (90% of the tablets) and +/- 15% (100% of the tablets). This methodology is also in line with the Korean Pharmacopeia (KP X 1689 – 1693).
The acceptance criteria for the IPC uniformity of mass in section 3.2.P.3.5 (Process Validation) have been aligned with the criteria specified in section 3.2.P.3.3 (Process Controls) to ensure consistency throughout the dossier.

The appropriateness of this concept was proven during process validation (please refer to the adapted P.3.5.01). All predefined IPCs, additional tests and CQAs fulfilled the acceptance criteria. Particularly, the content uniformity test of the uncoated tablets during the tableting showed narrowly distributed results and very low variability. Consequently, based on the results of the process validation, it was demonstrated that the manufacturing process is well under control with the current IPC methodology.

Question/Consideration:
Question 1
It is recommended to correct the concentration of citrate stock solution under the reference 
solution preparation section in the submitted specification from "1mol/L" to "1000 ppm 
(5.29mol/L)", and specify the name of the component corresponding to this concentration. 
According to description in the analytical method of the dossier, this concentration 
corresponds to the concentration of citrate. Please verify this and clearly specify the source or 
preparation method of the stock solution in the submitted specification.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1:
The submitted concentration of citrate stock solution “1 mol/L” is a typo in the JX 
specification. The correct concentration is 1000 ppm (5.29 mol/L) and has been corrected 
accordingly in the JX specification.
In the source document Test Procedure P.5.2.01-11.0 the correct concentration of 1000 ppm 
(5.29 mol/L) for citrate stock solution is stated.
The pKa values of citrate are 6.40, 4.76, and 3.13. When the pH of the mobile phase is lower 
than the pKa values, citrate becomes protonated at the carboxyl groups, and the absorption at 
these groups depends on the protonation state. Since the pH of the mobile phase solution 
(14.6 mM phosphoric acid) is approximately 2, which is clearly lower than the lowest pKa 
value of citrate (3.13), the citrate molecules in the solution are fully protonated and exist in 
the mobile phase in the form of citrate (C₆H₅O₇³⁻). Therefore, when converting the 
concentration  of a 1000 ppm stock solution in the C₆H₅O₇³⁻ form (molecular weight 189.1 
g/mol) into molar concentration, the result is 5.29 mmol/L.

Currently, Radium chloride [²²³Ra] injection has two manufacturing sites worldwide, but only 
one site, Agilera, is registered for China. The testing method document P.5.2.01-11.0 is a 
globally applicable technical document covering all manufacturing sites. After confirmation 
with the Agilera site, it was verified that Agilera only uses trisodium citrate dihydrate salt to 
prepare the standard solution (1) and (2) and has never used a 1000 ppm citrate stock solution 
to prepare these two standard solutions. For the purpose of registration in China, since Agilera 
has not actually used the 1000 ppm citrate stock solution to prepare the standard solution (1) 
and (2), this preparation method should not be included in the Chinese submission standard. 
Therefore, this preparation method has now been deleted, and only the preparation method 
from the trisodium citrate dihydrate salt has been retained.

Question/Consideration:
Question 3
3.2.P.5.1 and 3.2.P.5.6: The acceptance criteria for the degradation products should be set according to ICH Q6A, taking into account the batch and stability results. We expect the acceptance criteria (maximum likely level) to be narrowed in accordance with the stability results (testosterone nmt 0.25%, Δ6-testosterone enanthate nmt 0.2%, total impurities nmt 0.5%).
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 3 ( CTD section):
We acknowledge Agency’s comments. The acceptance criteria for degradation products is reestablished in below table

Degradation Products
- Testosterone: Release ≤0.4%; Shelf life ≤0.4% (Health Authority proposal 0.25%; current ≤0.5%)
- Delta 6-testosterone enantate: Release ≤0.3%; Shelf life ≤0.3% (Health Authority proposal 0.2%; current ≤0.3%)
- Any other individual: Release ≤0.2%; Shelf life ≤0.2% (Health Authority proposal 0.2%; current ≤0.2%)
- Total: Release ≤1.0%; Shelf life ≤1.0% (Health Authority proposal 0.5%; current ≤2.0%)

The revised release and shelf life specifications are included in Module 3, section 3.3.P.5.1.

Justification for the proposed limits:
The limit for degradation products Testosterone is set to ≤ 0.4% and for Δ6-testosterone enantate is set to ≤ 0.3% for both release and shelf life specification, following the established limit of the monograph Testosterone enantate no. 1048 of Eur. Ph. Monograph. Although this limit is the same as for the impurities in the drug substance, the acceptance criterion is established by taking into account the acceptance criterion in the drug substance, the qualified level, stability studies data, and data from the drug product manufactured by the proposed commercial process. Therefore, an evaluation of the data from the drug product batches currently under stability studies and from the completed stability studies was performed, along with an assessment of the impurity limits of the active ingredient.
The specification limit of ≤ 0.2% for any unspecified degradation products ensures that any degradation product remains below the qualification threshold. According to the ICH guideline (Q3B) <Impurities in New Drug Products>, the identification and qualification threshold for degradation products is 0.2%.
The total limit is set based on historical data and is reflecting the individual acceptance criteria for Testosterone, Δ6-testosterone enantate and any other individual.
The above justification is included in the justification of specifications and the updated TRD is included in the Module 3, section 3.2.P.5.6.

Question/Consideration: The submitted Master Batch Record* states that the quantity of the material added may differ from that described in the approval application form for marketing authorization in Japan (J-AAF), depending on the content of GD-GLYDONIP. Since it seems different from what is stated in the approval application form (J-AAF), justify the difference. If the applicant considers that the approval application form (J-AAF) should be revised, respond as such to this query first as early as possible, regardless of the above-stated response deadline.
Answer/Response:
Regarding the neopentyltetramine hydrochloride input in step 4b of batch size 1 you pointed out, explanation is provided below about the description that the charge quantity may differ from that described in the AAF depending on the content of GD-GLYDONIP.
During the manufacturing development research phase, studies to optimize stoichiometry were performed based on the stoichiometry of neopentyltetramine hydrochloride (NPTA HCl) and GD-GLYDONIP. As a result, it was confirmed that if the content of GD-GLYDONIP is not less than 60%, a constant equivalent ratio with the amount of NPTA HCl does not affect the quality.
Under GMP operations, if the content of GD-GLYDONIP is below 78% in batch size 1, the amount of NPTA HCl can be adjusted during the manufacturing, and MBR specifies the NPTA HCl input corresponding to the content of GD-GLYDONIP indicated by IPC as follows:
1st Limit test: Content of GD-GLYDONIP: not less than 78%
NPTA HCl input 27.5 kg
If the content of GD-GLYDONIP is below 78%, a second limit test is performed on the batch:
2nd Limit test: Content of GD-GLYDONIP (HPLC): not less than 72%
NPTA HCl input 25.3 kg
If the content of GD-GLYDONIP is below 72%, a third, final limit test is performed on the batch:
3rd Limit test: Content of GD-GLYDONIP (HPLC): not less than 60%
NPTA HCl input 21.0 kg
Note that, in Step 4b of batch size 2, the operation is the same as batch size 1. Namely, if the content of GD-GLYDONIP is not less than 60%, a constant equivalent ratio with the amount of NPTA HCl is maintained. Thus, the NPTA HCl input can be adjusted depending on the content of GD-GLYDONIP as shown below. A supporting document describing the following adjustment is submitted as Attachment 1:
1st Limit test: Content of GD-GLYDONIP (HPLC): not less than 81%
NPTA HCl input 48.9 kg
If the content of GD-GLYDONIP is below 81%, a second limit test is performed on the batch:
2nd Limit test: Content of GD-GLYDONIP (HPLC): not less than 78%
NPTA HCl input 47.1 kg
If the content of GD-GLYDONIP is below 78%, a third limit test is performed on the batch:
3rd Limit test: Content of GD-GLYDONIP (HPLC): not less than 72%
NPTA HCl input 43.4 kg
If the content of GD-GLYDONIP is below 72%, a fourth, final limit test is performed on the batch:
4th Limit test: Content of GD-GLYDONIP (HPLC): not less than 60%
NPTA HCl input 36.1 kg
Based on the above, we consider it is appropriate to modify the AAF.

USP <61> or JP 4.05 (harmonized method). The test for specified microorganisms are 
described in detail in Ph. Eur. 2.6.13, USP <62> or JP 4.05 (harmonized method).
Procedure:
Weigh 10 g of the product into a tared container and document the weight. Add Buffered 
sodium chloride-peptone solution pH 7,0 to make 100 g and to get 1:10 dilution.
For TAMC-test add to parallel dishes 1 ml of the sample dilution 1:10. Add 15-20 ml of 
liquefied TSA agar (Casein soya bean digest agar) that has been cooled to +45°C. Incubate 
the plates at + 30°C - +35°C for 3-5 days (Pour-Plate Method of the Plate-Count method).
For TYMC-test add to parallel dishes 1 ml of the sample dilution 1:10. Add 15-20 ml of 
liquefied SAB agar (Sabouraud-dextose agar) that has been cooled to +45°C. Incubate the 
plates at + 20°C - +25°C for 5-7 days. (Pour-Plate Method of the Plate-Count method).
For the test for absence of Escherichia coli, shake and transfer 10 ml of 1:10 sample solution 
to 100 ml of Casein soya bean digest broth. Incubate at +30 - +35°C for 18-24 h. Shake and 
transfer 1 ml to 100 ml of MacConkey broth. Incubate at +42 - +44°C for 24-48 h. Subculture 
on a plate of MacConkey agar.  Incubate at +30 - +35°C for 18-72 h. Possible colonies are 
Gram-stained and if needed identified further.

Question/Consideration:
[Stability Report]:
(i).
Please explain the rationale for counting the initial real-time stability time point (i.e. t=0M) 
from bulk PFS instead of sterilized PFS.
(ii).
For stability data of lot (e.g. KT0KK7S), the stability starts from t=6M. Please clarify why 
there is no testing of product for Sterility (liquid DP) and Sterility (Syringe in Blister Tray).
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1 (3.2.P.8.1, 3.2.P.8.3):
(i).
Bayer defines the date of manufacturing of prefilled syringes as the time at which the bulk 
solution is filled into its final dosage form and container. Resultantly, the manufacturing date 
of Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL in prefilled syringe finished drug product is the filling 
date of the bulk solution into syringes (bulk PFS). The same approach is also registered and 
approved by EMA and in all other Bayer territories globally.
The filling date also marks the beginning of the shelf life of the drug product, meaning that 
the shelf life is already starting before the labeling, assembly, blistering and outer surface 
sterilization process (sterilized PFS). 
To cover the shelf life claim of the finished drug product, the stability studies are starting with 
the bulk PFS instead of the sterilized PFS and thus avoid having an offset of multiple months 
between shelf life start and stability study start.
This concept was established for the already approved Aflibercept solution 40 mg/mL in 
prefilled syringe and is now also applied to the new Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL 
strength.
(ii).
KT0KK7S is a sterilized PFS batch originating from the bulk PFS batch 31226. As explained 
in response to (i) the shelf life of the syringes already started with the manufacturing date of 
the bulk batch 31226. The earliest time point after batch 31226 was manufactured into the 
sterilized PFS batch KT0KK7S was the 6 month time point, meaning the syringes were 6 
months old at that time with only a part of that in sterilized PFS form. The same applies to the 
other sterilized PFS batches.
The stability testing of sterilized PFS batches (e.g., KT0KK7S) is conducted in accordance 
with the protocol given in P.8.1.01-06, requiring sterility testing only at T=0M (not available 
for sterilized PFS) and after 24 months and 36 months of storage. This is in accordance with 
ICH Q5C Quality of Biotechnological Products: Stability Testing of 
Biotechnological/Biological Products which states: “Sterility testing or alternatives (e.g., 
container/closure integrity testing) should be performed at a minimum initially and at the end 
of the proposed shelf-life.”
Results of sterility testing after 24 months are available for all sterilized PFS batches and are 
presented in P.8.3.01-07.
The same stability schedule and data is submitted and approved in all other Bayer territories 
where the Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL PFS is registered, including EU.

(#022984599; unchanged)

prefilled syringe for intravitreous injection (#022980339; unchanged)
