Question/Consideration:
Question 1:
Provide the source of the target gene, details of the optimization, design considerations, and main 
rationale.
Answer/Response:
Response:
The antibody intermediate, BAY 3547905, used in the manufacture of GPC3-TAC, 
BAY 3547926 injection, is based on a germlined and sequence optimized codrituzumab, an 
antibody that has shown signs of clinical efficacy in phase 1/ 2 studies.
The constant region of the murine antibody was exchanged against a human constant region. The 
variable light and heavy chain were humanized and germlined. Sequence Optimization included 
removal of four Lys residues in the Complementarity Determining Regions (CDR), being 
sensitive to unwanted chelator conjugation, as well as reduction of immunogenicity.
keywords: Elucidation of Structure and other Characteristics; Characterisation of Impurities; Formulation development; General Properties; manufacturing description

A CMV-8 kb ubiquitous chromatin opening element (UCOE) containing vector was in-licensed

Question/Consideration:
Question 1:
In R.2.02_022984027_01-comparability exercise, the residual DNA content in clinical batch is 
much higher than non-clinical batch, about 10 times higher. Please analyze the reasons and 
conduct a safety assessment.
Answer/Response:
Response:
The difference in residual DNA contents is based on the analytical method used for the testing of 
the non-clinical and clinical batch. The method was validated before measuring the clinical batch. 
This included the determination of the Limit of Quantitation (LOQ) for the method. The non-
clinical batch was analyzed using a non-validated method with a lower quantitation limit. There is 
no safety risk because the clinical batch is well below the specification limit of max. 50.0 ppb with 
a result of <5.9 ppb.
keywords: Comparative Batch Analysis; analytical method validation; LoQ; QC testing; batch data

Question/Consideration:
Question 1
Please clarify the following details:
1. It is noted from the Table of Summary of changes that the proposed change has been 
approved by EMA. However, based on the submitted EMA’s assessment report, the approved 
manufacturing sites for parametric release by EMA were Cardinal Health, US and Bayer AS, 
Norway instead of Agilera Pharma AS, Norway. Hence, please clarify if approval has been 
obtained from EMA or any HSA's reference agencies for the proposed change. If yes, please 
submit a copy of the approval letter(s) which should include details on the variations approved 
by the respective agencies.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1:
We, Bayer AG, herewith confirm that the parametric release variation has been approved by 
EMA for the manufacturing site Agilera Pharma AS, Norway. Our local Bayer subsidiary Bayer 
AS, Norway, is the final releasing site for Xofigo. Both sites are located in Norway.
During the variation procedure at EMA we were requested to provide the necessary GMP-
related proof for the employed contract manufacturer Agilera Pharma AS, Norway, from a 
competent GMP-inspection authority that no objection against the establishment of parametric 
release for this manufacturing site exists.
Back at that time, GMP compliance has been confirmed by Norwegian Medical Products 
Agency (NOMA) indirectly via a new issued manufacturing/import authorisation (MIA) for 
Agilera Pharma AS, Norway, listing parametric release explicitly as GMP compliant if 
regulatory bodies approved this procedure (see attachment). While this means that GMP 
compliance for Agilera Pharma AS, Norway, will legally only achieved after approval of this 
variation by EMA, we do comply with the requirement that parametric release activities have 
been properly audited and no objections have been found (see page 5, footnote to section 1.1.2.3 
in MIA Agilera Pharma AS). NOMA also clarified that updated GMP certificates were not 
issued but only in the future, despite positive audit of parametric release activities.
Together with the new MIA for Agilera Pharma AS (dated 22 January 2024) we provided the 
FDA approval letter (dated 26 September 2024) which states in general terms the approval for 
this US prior approval supplement for parametric release to EMA and received EMA approval 
(CHMP Opinion dated 12 December 2024). The US FDA approval comprises the approval of 
parametric release for both manufacturing sites, Cardinal Health, US and Agilera Pharma AS, 
Norway.
In the meantime, Agilera Pharma AS, Norway, was inspected by NOMA on 28 March 2025 
and issued a new GMP certificate (dated 17 June 2025) which includes parametric release for 
Xofigo (see footnote to section 1.1.2.3 in GMP Certificate Agilera Pharma AS).

Question/Consideration:
• Stability data (P.8):
o Based on proposal for having 36 months shelf life while the real time data is not
yet available, provide justification and analytical data, reference and quality data to 
support the justification
o Provide stability data 36 months with the current API source
Answer/Response:
We acknowledge the Agency’s comment requesting stability data and justification for the proposed 36-month shelf life. We have included a scientific justification letter along with the available analytical and quality documents to support the proposed 36-month shelf life in this submission. Based on the submitted documents—including Certificates of Analysis, batch analysis results, API and drug product stability data, and dissolution profiles—it is justified that the change in API source has no impact on the established shelf life of the product.

For the current API source (Bergkamen), the stability data supporting the 36-month shelf life are available and documented in TRD P.8.3.01_IQMS-190588_4.0, confirming that all quality parameters remain within specifications.

2. Stability Data for 36 Months with Current API Source
• Complete stability data for Diane drug product using Cyproterone acetate API from Bergkamen is available and demonstrates compliance with specifications for assay, degradation products, and dissolution up to 36 months.
• These data have been included in the Stability section of the dossier.
Source: P.8.3.01-04 Stability data / Cyproterone acetate + Ethinylestradiol sugar-coated tablet 2.0 mg + 35 µg (Diane 35)  (#190588; unchanged)

3. Extrapolation for New API Source (Newchem)
A new/alternative API supplier (NewChem) for Cyproterone acetate generated a stability study, according to the ICH-stability guideline. The corresponding ICH-stability report (IQMS-264244) contains the stability data of three finished drug product batches manufacturing with proposed API supplier. The accelerated data showed after 6 months of storage no discernable trend or any significant change for the stability indicating test items, like assay (mean) content, degradation products or drug dissolution. Therefore, a shelf-life prediction of real-time data can be given for max. 12 months, according to ICH-stability guideline Q1E. This supports a shelf-life prediction of the real time data (24 months) until the end of shelf-life (36-months).

The evaluation of the stability profile in the recently updated stability report showed no discernable trend until the 24-month test station for all stability indicating test parameters. Furthermore, assay (mean) content, dissolution, and the degradation profile of Cyproterone acetate (New Chem) are fully stable under the tested conditions which will result in a fulfilled shelf-life after 36 months of storage under climate IVb conditions.

For the API Ethinylestradiol a slight decrease in assay (mean) content corresponding with a slight increase of the main degradation product (6-keto-Ethinylestradiol) is monitored. All other stability indicating test items remain stable under the predefined storage conditions. For shelf-life prediction the statistical tool (SlimStat) is used.

The shelf-life prediction showed that both investigated stability indicating parameters will clearly fulfill the requirements of the shelf-life specification until shelf-life. Additionally, the data is comparable to the data of the former ICH-stability and confirms the defined shelf-life. The final stability report including the 36-months real time data will be updated at the end of 2026.

4. Commitment Letter
• We commit to providing complete 36-month stability data for Diane drug product manufactured with Cyproterone acetate API from Newchem by end of 2026.
• A signed commitment letter is attached for your reference.
keywords: Stability data; Shelf Life; Stability Summary and Conclusion; dissolution; assay and impurities

Question/Consideration:
Question 2
The COA for the Gadoquatrane RS indicates that, prior to use for quantitative determination, 
it must be equilibrated for at least 7 days at 40%–50% relative humidity.
Please confirm whether the water content and assay as is (Gadoquatrane) in the COA for 
were obtained after 7 days of equilibration.
In addition, please provide the solvent used when determining the water content of the 
Gadoquatrane RS by Karl Fischer coulometric titration..
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 2:
The water content and the assay as is for the Gadoquatrane reference standard were 
determined after 7 days of equilibration.

The determination of water content in the Gadoquatrane reference standard is conducted using 
coulometric Karl-Fischer titration, as outlined in S.4.2.01. The measurement system includes 
an oven where the solid sample is heated to 220°C. Water is transferred into the measurement 
cell via an inert gas flow, eliminating the need for a sample solvent. In the measurement cell, 
Hydranal Coulomat AG OVEN is utilized for coulometric titration.
keywords: CoAs; assay; analytical procedures; analytical test method DS; Validation of Analytical procedures

Question/Consideration:
Question 3
Apart from the requirement for certain reference standards to be equilibrated for 7 days before 
use, are there any other special precautions during the QC testing? Such as whether the 
autosampler tray needs to be temperature-controlled?  Whether reference standard solutions 
must be freshly prepared before use? If so, please provide instructions.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 3:
With respect to the drug product methods (Assay gadoquatrane / degradation products):
We recommend to use Waters, Screw Top Vials, 2 mL, e.g. 12x32 (P/N 186000307C) for 
determination of degradation products.
We recommend to use an Agilent 1290, Infinity II HPLC system.
Bayer uses a “Maximum Flow Gradient” setting of “5 mL/min2” for flow ramp up and flow 
ramp down (i.e. when the flow is switched between 0.4 mL/min and 0.8 mL/min and vice 
versa).
Autosampler / injector temperature is held at 23 +/-2 °C.
The gadoquatrane reference standard solution may be used for 4 days if stored at ambient 
conditions.
The sensitivity solution should be freshly diluted from the gadoquatrane reference standard 
solution on a working daily base.
Comparison solutions of the degradation products (i.e. Gd-GlyMe-DOTA, Glycine-Tris-Gd-
GlyMe-DOTA amide Isomer 2, Mono-Des-Gd-Gadoquatrane) are not routinely used. If 
required, they should be prepared and used freshly or prepared, aliquoted, stored at < -15°C 
and each aliquot should preferentially only be used once.
For calculation of the assay gadoquatrane based upon the weight of the solution, the density at 
20°C is required. Determine the density of Gadoquatrane solution 0.4 mmol Gd/mL for
injection at 20°C of the respective batch according to oscillating transducer method 
(Ph. Eur. 2.2.5) with at least four decimals.

Calcobutrol content:
The calcobutrol reference standard solution may be used for a maximum of six days, if stored 
at ambient conditions.
The sensitivity solution should be freshly prepared from the calcobutrol reference standard 
solution.
Determine the density of Gadoquatrane solution 0.4 mmol Gd/mL for injection at 20°C 
according to oscillating transducer method (Ph. Eur. 2.2.5) with at least four decimals.
keywords: QC testing; HPLC-method; assay and impurities; Degradation Products; Analytical Procedures

Question/Consideration:
Justify the choice of packaging and closure system for the active substance (Drospirenone 
micronized, Bayer)(3.2.S.6), in accordance with ICH requirements
Answer/Response:
Applicant acknowledges the Agency’s question and would like to inform that the drug  
dubstance Drospirenone is packed in  polyethylene (PE) bags as primary packaging. For 
technical reasons the substance may be filled in a polyethylene bag first which is then placed 
in a second polyethylene bag. The bags are then placed in a fiber drum as secondary packaging. 
For small quantities, the primary packaging may alternatively be placed in a press-in-lid 
container.
This container-closure system has been selected in accordance with ICH Q1A(R2), and Q7 to 
ensure adequate protection of the drug substance from environmental factors during storage and 
transportation. The PE liner provides an effective barrier, while the outer fiber drum provide 
mechanical protection. The polyethylene material is of pharmaceutical grade, and compliant 
with relevant pharmacopoeial requirements. Also, Stability studies have been conducted in 
accordance to  ICH Q1A(R2) confirming that the quality of the drug substance is maintained 
throughout its re-test period.

Question/Consideration:
Question 6 
 
Please revise the acceptance criteria in the CoAs for Hydrochloric acid, Ethanol 96%, Sodium 
chloride, Trometamol, and Water for injection to be explicit; replace “According to 
specification” with clear, detailed acceptance limits.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 6 ( CTD section):
We acknowledge the Agency’s comment and we would like to clarify the following:
For Hydrochloric acid 1N, we have provided the quality specification along with the 
corresponding test methods. Therefore, where the CoA states “according to specification,” this
is fully aligned with the approved in-house specification. All tests required by the in-house 
specification have been performed and meet the defined acceptance limits. The CoA language 
is therefore fully aligned with the approved specification.
For the remaining excipients, namely ethanol 96%, sodium chloride, trometamol, and water for 
injection, these are compendial excipients with established pharmacopoeial monographs. The 
submission already includes the applicable pharmacopoeial monographs that define the detailed 
test methods and acceptance criteria. Where the CoAs use the phrase “according to 
specification,” this indicates conformity to the applicable pharmacopoeial monograph 
referenced in the dossier.
The CoA therefore reflects compliance with the detailed, legally-recognized acceptance limits 
found in those monographs. Referencing a separate, clearly identified specification (inhouse or 
compendial monograph) rather than repeating full acceptance tables on every CoA is an 
accepted and routine practice in global pharmaceutical supply chains. No deficiencies have 
been raised regarding this aspect.
The CoA phrase “according to specification” is not ambiguous in this case because the 
referenced specifications (in-house for HCl 1N; pharmacopeial monographs for the compendial 
excipients) are included in the submission and contain the explicit acceptance limits and test 
methods.
Requiring revision of globally used, multi-market CoAs to list every individual acceptance limit 
is not necessary where the definitive specification is already part of the regulatory dossier and 
the batch test results demonstrate compliance.

found in those monographs. Referencing a separate, clearly identified specification (inhouse or 
compendial monograph) rather than repeating full acceptance tables on every CoA is an
accepted and routine practice in global pharmaceutical supply chains. No deficiencies have 
been raised regarding this aspect.

referenced specifications (in-house for HCl 1N; pharmacopeial monographs for the compendial 
excipients) are included in the submission and contain the explicit acceptance limits and test 
methods.
Requiring revision of globally used, multi-market CoAs to list every individual acceptance limit 
is not necessary where the definitive specification is already part of the regulatory dossier and

Question/Consideration:
Question 1
Provide the results of the Finished Product (FP) stability studies initiated in accordance with
the EMA Guidelines for Stability Studies for at least two pilot or industrial batches of FP
(batches sterilized at the proposed production site Sterigenics Belgium (Petit-Rechain,
Belgium) with satisfactory stability results for at least three months or more. (Section 3.2.R.8.
Stability).
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1 (P.8.3):
We would like to highlight that stability data are available for one Jaydess batch sterilized at
Sterigenics Belgium. Specifically, batch U11026, included in stability report P.8.3.01_IQMS-
174380_7.0 was sterilized at Sterigenics Belgium. Although the sterilization site is not
explicitly stated in the stability report, it is clearly documented in the corresponding Batch
Analysis P.5.4.01_IQMS-174192_1.0 of Jaydess.
Given this, we propose that the approval of Sterigenics Belgium as an alternative sterilization
site be supported using the available stability data for this batch. At present, there are no plans
to generate additional stability data for batches sterilized at Sterigenics, and we believe the
existing dataset is scientifically adequate.
Furthermore, stability report P.8.3.01_IQMS-205462_3.0 (Levonorgestrel intrauterine
delivery system 13.5 mg, ET03 sterilizer at Bayer Oy Turku) provides strong evidence that
the sterilization process does not impact product stability. During the qualification of the
ET03 sterilizer approximately seven years ago, it was demonstrated that the sterilization cycle
has no effect on the stability profile of the product. Importantly, the sterilization cycles used at
Turku and at Sterigenics are described as “substantially the same” (as referenced in section
P.3.3.01_IQMS-181188_5.0), confirming that the sterilization parameters are equivalent
across chambers.
Based on these data, we propose that Sterigenics Belgium be accepted as an alternative
sterilization site for Jaydess using the stability data available for the single Jaydess batch. The
product stability is not influenced by the sterilization chamber used, as the sterilization
processes are aligned and validated to the same performance criteria.
Additionally, Sterigenics is already approved as a sterilization site for Mirena in Ukraine.
Considering that all IUS products share highly similar design principles, materials, and
sterilization requirements, the existing approvals and stability data across the IUS portfolio
further reinforce that the sterilization process, regardless of chamber location, does not impact
product quality or stability. This cross-product consistency provides additional assurance that
the sterilization cycles used at Sterigenics are fully suitable for Jaydess.

Source:

Question/Consideration:
Question 12
Please justify why microbial limit testing was not performed on the excipients, in accordance

Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 12 ( CTD section):
While ICH Q6 provides general guidance on quality specifications, it also allows for a risk-
based approach to testing requirements. Given the low risk of microbial contamination in our 
excipients, we have determined that routine microbial limit testing is not necessary. This 
decision aligns with the principles of ICH Q6, which advocate for scientifically justified 
testing protocols based on risk assessment.

All excipients are sourced from qualified suppliers who adhere to Good Manufacturing 
Practices (GMP). These suppliers conduct rigorous quality control measures, including 
microbial testing, to ensure the excipients meet predefined specifications.
We conduct comprehensive microbial limit testing on the final drug product, which 
encompasses all excipients and the active pharmaceutical ingredient. This ensures that the 
final product meets the required microbial quality standards, thereby mitigating any potential 
risks associated with individual excipients. Since the final product testing is thorough and 
conclusive, additional testing of single excipients is redundant and unnecessary.

Question/Consideration:
Question 1
Please provide a comprehensive introduction to the continuous manufacturing process based
on the actual production of this product, and further explain the rationale for considering the
collection of dry granules, final blending, and coating of existing sub-lot/lot as part of a
continuous manufacturing process (noting the certain differences compared with continuous
manufacturing processes developed using the conventional RTD model). If necessary, provide
images and videos to facilitate understanding. Please explain how, in commercial production,
effective quality control of the entire sub-lots can be ensured and consistency among sub-lots
maintained, based on the overall batch release requirements.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 1 ( P.2, P.3):
1) Overall Introduction to the Continuous Manufacturing Process
As shown in the process flow diagram submitted in the application dossier, the complete
manufacturing process for sevabertinib Tablets consists of  two major parts. The first part is
performed in batch mode, involving thorough mixing and sieving of all raw materials and
excipients (except magnesium stearate) to obtain a homogeneous pre-blend. The second part
employs continuous manufacturing on the integrated ConsiGma® 25 production line,
including processes such as powder feeding, roller compaction granulation, post-blending,
tableting, and coating.
A schematic diagram of the continuous manufacturing process is shown below Figure 1. The
specific description for the CM process is as follows:
1. The pre-blended material is filled into loss in weight feeder (the top-left in Figure 1) of
the ConsiGma® 25 for continuous feeding. The throughput rate of the process is
approximately 12kg/h.
2. After feeding, the material is directly conveyed to the roller compactor. With set
parameters for specific compaction force and  gap width, dry granulation is performed.
3. The granules produced are automatically conveyed via tubes to a weighing hopper for
weighing. If the granule weight is within the target range(approximately 1.3 kg), it
enters the blending hopper. A predetermined mass of magnesium stearate is
automatically added from its dedicated hopper for final blending. Each 1.3 kg of final
blended material is defined as a post-blended sublot.
4. After the final blending process, sub-lot is conveyed to a buffer hopper. Any non-
conforming sub-lot is diverted at this point. All confirming material is conveyed to the
tablet press.
5. During tableting, conforming core tablets are conveyed via tubes to  buffer hoppers,
located directly above the pan coaters. Approximately 3 kg sublots of core tablets are
then conveyed via gravity to two parallel, series-connected pan coaters. During film
coating  a predetermined mass of coating suspension is sprayed on the tablets, forming
each coating sublot.
Figure 1 Schematic of the continuous manufacturing line.
For this continuous manufacturing process, the residence time distribution (RTD)
characterization is not necessary since there are no feeding and/or continuous blending
operations of individual components that would require detailed understanding of mixing
dynamics. The process utilizes a pre-blended material with established uniformity from batch
blending steps, rather than continuous feeding of individual components, eliminating the risk
of compositional variations. Both initial and post-blending are performed in controlled batch
mode, where blend uniformity is verified using traditional methods for the pre-blend and the
final blend quality by content uniformity of tablets.
Uniformity of the material has been consistently demonstrated through content uniformity
testing of all sub-lots across all manufactured batches, confirming that products meeting quality
requirements can be manufactured continuously, and RTD-based process characterization is
not required.

2) A justification about the quality consistency among sub-lots in PPQ batches
The continuous manufacturing process on the ConsiGma® line ensures effective quality control
of all sub‑lots through high‑frequency automated sampling (≥1 IPC test set per sub‑lot) during
tableting, continuous monitoring of process parameters, and full sub‑lot traceability. Deviating
sub‑lots can be uniquely identified and diverted, ensuring that only conforming material
contributes to the final batch. During clinical manufacturing campaigns and throughout
validation, each coating sub‑lot was fully tested (e.g. see P.2.3. Chapter 4.3. for primary stability
batches), confirming that all sub‑lots consistently met the specification. PPQ data further
demonstrated sub-lot quality and inter-batch consistency （see P.3.5.1）. Final batch release
requires both full sub‑lot‑level IPC compliance and batch‑level specification QC testing
compliance. Thus, full consistency among sub‑lots as well overall batch quality are ensured for
each batch.
keywords: Description of Manufacturing Process and Process Controls; in-process control; Process Validation and/or Evaluation; Batch Report; QC testing

Question/Consideration:
Question 2
Please describe the material diversion and traceability strategies for each continuous
manufacturing step, and comprehensively demonstrate how non-conforming samples are
effectively segregated. Please confirm whether PAT tools are used, if yes, please provide the
development and application of PAT tools along with relevant validation information. For the
tablet compression step, the production process description indicates the installation of an
automatic tablet inspection device to measure tablet mass uniformity and hardness online,
enabling automatic adjustment and diversion. Please specify the detection frequency and its
rationale for the online measurements, detailed standards for automatic adjustment and
diversion, as well as supporting study/validation data.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 2 ( P.3):
The control strategy of the ConsiGma 25 manufacturing line is designed to ensure final product
quality by monitoring the process parameters and automatically diverting any material that does
not meet pre-defined criteria. Traceability is maintained throughout the process using a “sublot”
principle.

Traceability via sublot principle:
Unit operations, that are intrinsically continuous processes, specifically the roller compaction
and tablet compression, are managed by creating discrete portions of material, hereinafter
referred to as "sublots." Sublots are generated based on a defined time or mass. Each sublot is
assigned a unique identification number by the ConsiGma 25 control system, allowing for
complete traceability as it moves to the next integrated unit operation. This system ensures that
a sublot cannot proceed unless all in-process controls and quality criteria for the current step
have been met. These criteria are defined in the product-specific recipe that governs the entire
manufacturing process.

Segregation of non-conforming material:
If a deviation from a defined criterion occurs, the entire affected sublot is diverted at a
designated diversion point. For the tableting process, individual non-conforming tablets are
diverted.
The primary diversion points are (see Figure 1):
• Post-blending sublot (after post-blending step)
The respective post-blending sublot is discarded before entering the tablet
press
• Individual tablets (directly at the tablet press) of uncoated tablets
The respective uncoated tablets are discarded before entering the coating
units
• Coating sublots (after the coating step)
The respective coating sublots are discarded and collected in separate
waste drums.
Examples for diversion triggers:
• Diversion point a):
A granule sublot, generated at the roller compactor, is diverted if its weight is too high
or low, if the lubricant was not added correctly, or if process parameters during roller
compaction (e.g. specific compaction force, gap width) or blending (e.g. blending
speed)) were outside their validated ranges.
• Diversion point b):
Individual tablets are diverted if the main compression force or the pre-compression
force displacement deviates from the target setpoint
• Diversion point c):
A coating sublot is flagged and diverted if upstream tablet testing shows non-
conforming results, or if coating process parameters (e.g., spray rate, inlet air
temperature/flow, drum speed) deviate from their validated ranges.

Application of Process Analytical Technology (PAT):
While no multivariate PAT tools (such as spectroscopic methods, e.g. NIR) are currently
implemented, the process control strategy relies on an online tablet multicheck for the tablet
compression step. It provides real-time data by direct mass and hardness measurement that is
used to monitor and control the process.
• The multicheck system was integrated into the manufacturing line to provide a high
degree of process assurance. It functions by automatically sampling and testing tablets
at a high frequency (20 tablets every 10 minutes). The data on mass uniformity and
hardness is fed back to the tablet press control system, enabling automatic adjustments
to the compression parameters (e.g., die fill depth) to maintain consistent tablet
quality. This immediate feedback loop ensures the process remains in a state of
control.
•
The functionality of the multicheck, including its accuracy, precision, and the
qualification of its integration in the manufacturing line, was part of the equipment
qualification activities and were validated during process performance qualification
(P.3.5.01).

Tablet Compression: Online Measurement, Adjustment, and Diversion
Sampling philosophy:
There are two different types of sampling strategies performed for uniformity of mass and
resistance to crushing of uncoated tablets.
An automated process of highly frequent automated sampling and testing is achieved by the
multicheck. The tablet multicheck samples and tests 20 individual tablets every 10 minutes.
To further safeguard the automated measurements, there is a manual process for measuring
the tablet hardness and tablet weights as at-line IPC on standard stand-alone test equipment at
the beginning, middle and end of each batch (and after possible manual adaptation of
parameters).The combination of both independent measurements, one for direct process
control and adjustment and one as traditional at-line IPC to demonstrate accordance with the
specification allows increased process reliability.

Sampling frequency:
The testing frequency of the multicheck was established based on the process dynamics of the
continuous coating system. A new sublot begins the coating process approximately every 15
minutes. By testing every 10 minutes, it is ensured that every single coating sublot is
evaluated at least once, and often twice, by the multicheck system during its transit and
processing. This frequency guarantees that any potential deviation is detected.

Standards for adjustments:
The standards for action are based on the results from the multicheck. If the measured average
tablet mass begins to drift towards the specification limits, the system automatically adjusts
the fill depth of the tablet press die to bring the mass back to the target. This control prevents
the production of out-of-specification tablets. In the case of drifting resistance to crushing
values, the main compression force is adapted accordingly.
If any tested tablet is measured to be out of specification for mass or resistance to crushing,
the system initiates the following sequence:
1. An alarm notifies the operator.
2. The control system flags all tablets produced between the last conforming
measurement and the next conforming measurement as "non-conforming."
3. Due to the process flow, these flagged tablets will be part of specific coating sublots.
After the coating process for each affected sublot is complete, the control system
automatically diverts the entire non-conforming sublot at diversion point (c).

Verification/ Validation:
The described process control was investigated extensively during manufacturing process
development and is presented in section 4.8 of P.2.3.01. In this study, the process dynamics of
continuous process were investigated. The functionality of the multicheck control loop was an
integral part of this study. In addition, the reliability of the control system was proven during
process performance qualification. The results are presented in P.3.5.01.
keywords: in-process control; Method Transfer; Process Validation and/or Evaluation; Description of Manufacturing Process and Process Controls; manufacturing equipment

process validation activities. Also, please describe the special considerations for process
validation in continuous manufacturing processes
Answer/Response:
Bayer's Reply to Question 3 (P. 2 P.3.5):
Based on equipment performance, product physicochemical properties, and prior DoE stage
studies (see dossier P.2.3.01 Process Development), it was determined that within the proposed
parameter ranges  a production throughput rate of approximately 12 kg/h can ensure continuous
production across the  process.
The drug product manufacturing process has been validated using three consecutive batches,
meeting general process validation requirements and aligning with the scientific and regulatory
principles described in ICH Q13.
The process parameters evaluated as critical process parameters during the process and product
development are sieve size (pre-blend sieving), specific compaction force (roller compaction),
gap width (roller compaction), and spray rate (coating).
As described in the  process description above, a pre-blend is manufactured prior to the
continuous production of tablets  in batch mode, where sieve size was validated as a critical
process parameter.
Granulation and tableting are performed in a continuous process. Based on prior process
development studies, the setting of specific compaction force and  gap width affects granulation
quality and are relevant  parameters for  the continuous production throughput rate. During the
three validation batches, validation was conducted using a constant throughput rate and process
parameters to ensure stability and controllability of the continuous process conditions.
The  spray rate during coating  affects tablet appearance and is a critical parameter for the
coating process. This parameter was validated.

process

As in continuous manufacturing, batch size is primarily defined by run time rather than
equipment capacity different batch sizes (20 ~ 60 kg) were manufactured by adjusting the total
run time while keeping the process settings/parameters unchanged. ICH Q13 clearly states that
batch definition in continuous manufacturing can be based on run time at a defined throughput
rate (mass flow rate), and batch size can also be defined as a range, e.g., by defining minimum
and maximum run times. Therefore, the continuous manufacturing system allows flexible batch
sizes without equipment changes. The selected batch size range (20 ~ 60 kg) aligns with
anticipated market demands.

During validation, extensive testing was performed, covering both the sub-lots and overall batch
level. Results confirmed consistent quality for all tablets produced under the validated
conditions.

Question/Consideration:
Pharmaceutical Development (3.2.P.2): please provide manufacturer's justiﬁcation regarding the requested method for dissolution according to Chapter 32P52 (0.6% Polysorbate 20) as discriminatory.
According to the tests presented as part of Chapter 32P22 and according to the proposed method development report, The method reveals discriminatory (change) only in relation to the particle size of the active ingredient and to a small extent for diﬀerent compression force in the process.
Answer/Response:
The EMA states in its Assessment Report that “The development of the dissolution method has been well described, and the use of a surfactant has been acceptably justified. It was shown that 0.1 % Tween 20 and 0.3 % Tween 20 did not achieve sink conditions. The discriminatory ability of the dissolution method has been shown.”
Finerenone is a poorly soluble drug substance in aqueous solution. This is demonstrated in S.1.3.01_022285635_01 (Finerenone micronized drug substance – General information) and P.5.3.21_IQMS-451745_2.0 (Finerenone coated tablet 40 mg – Method Development – Dissolution) documents.
The development of the dissolution test method is described in P.5.3.21_IQMS-451745_2.0.
In accordance with general requirements on dissolution testing, i.e. as described in USP <1092>, dissolution conditions should consider the solubility of the drug substance. To improve solubility, the addition of surfactant is allowed in order to achieve sink conditions.
In addition, the dissolution method should show discriminatory power concerning the most critical product attributes, as e.g. particle size, compression force, etc., that may affect the release of the drug substance and therefore the quality of the drug product.
During development of the dissolution test method the discriminatory power of the method was investigated for the following critical attributes:
• Influence of Particle Size Distribution of the Drug Substance (refer to Figure 1)
• Influence of Disintegrant (refer to Figure 2)
• Influence of Compression Force (refer to Figure 3)
• Influence of Accelerated Stability Testing (refer to Figure 4)
Overlays of all investigated critical product attributes examined in the context of determining the discriminatory properties of the dissolution method are shown below in Figure 1 to Figure 4.
Stress stability conditions do not show significant influence of the dissolution behavior that is in line with the results of stability testing for Finerenone coated tablet 40 mg.
Differences of compression force shows only a small influence on the dissolution behavior.
Moreover, it was demonstrated that the selected dissolution method shows good discriminatory power for the most critical attributes as particle size and the availability of disintegrant.

doc_name: VV-RFI-005704 - CMC Response_Finerenone coated tablet 40 mg_IL_28032026
Question/Consideration:
Validation of analytical methods (3.2.P.5.3) –
I. In the validation report for the Assay & Impurities method, no reference was found for forced degradation tests and within them, results for peak purity and mass balance to demonstrate the method as stability indicating. Reference was found to peak purity as part of the speciﬁcity on unstressed sol. Also, as part of the stability chapter, the results of Stress studies were presented under two conditions, hydrolysis and heating, in which no signiﬁcant degradation of the active substance/increase in degradation substances was found. Why didn’t you considered oxidation and direct light tested on the DP solution?
II. No comparative dissolution proﬁle was found between a 20 mg and 40 mg dose in a medium containing a concentration of 0.1% Tween 80.
In addition, are the characteristics for which the method was found to be discriminatory for a 20 mg dose (0.1% Tween 80) similar to the characteristics for which the method was found to be discriminatory for a 40mg dose (0.6% Tween 80), please explained and summarized.
Was the dissolution of a 40mg dose tested using a method containing only 0.1% Tween 80? If yes, please provide a dissolution proﬁle and a reference that shows compliance with the requested speciﬁcations, and reference to discriminatory characteristics.
If not available, please provide a justiﬁcation as to why it was not tested.
Answer/Response:
I. Although forced degradation studies are not explicitly required with regard to ICH guidelines, ICH Q1A (R2) recommends stress testing to help identifying likely degradation products which can in turn help establish the intrinsic stability of the molecule and validate the stability indicating power of the analytical procedures used. As thermal and hydrolytic stress conditions, as well as photolytic stability revealed a high stability of Finerenone (P.8.3.04_022987142_01 and P.8.3.05_022987143_01), i.e. only minor degradation was observed, additional chemical stress conditions were applied.
Samples of Finerenone micronized drug substance and Finerenone coated tablet 40 mg were subjected to extended stress tests (e.g. thermal, hydrolytic, photolytic and oxidative) as summarized in Table 1 in order to investigate the formation of potential degradation products and to demonstrate the assay and degradation products method is selective and accurate regarding potential degradation products.
The mass balance has been calculated as well (see Table 2 and Table 3) applying the following equation:
(Assay (post-stress) + Impurities (post stress))/ (Assay (pre-stress) + Impurities (pre-stress)) x 100 = Mass balance (%)
The additional chemical stress test conditions are well suited to obtain assay drop in the range from 5 to 15% and no lack of mass balance (< 95%) was observed, neither for the Finerenone micronized drug substance nor for Finerenone coated tablets 40 mg.
Thus, the methods were shown to be stability indicating and are suitable for determination of assay and degradation products.
Under all stress conditions, the peak purity of the finerenone in drug product was given (purity angel < purity threshold) (see purity plots Figure 5 - Figure 12).
The photostability of the drug substance in solution was investigated in the drug substance part 3.2.S (please refer to S.7.3.05_022475896_01).
The drug product solution for determination of degradation products is slightly sensitive to light. Therefore the sample solution has to be prepared freshly (see test procedure P.8.3.05_022987143_01).
Generally, the sensitivity to light of the drug product-solution (acetonitrile/water; 70:30) is not relevant in the context of the light stability of the drug product.
Source: P.8.3.04_01 Finerenone coated tablet 40 mg / Stability Data - Stress Tests (P.8.3.04_022987142_01, unchanged); P.8.3.05_01 Finerenone coated tablet 40 mg / Stability Data - Photostability (P.8.3.05_022987143_01, unchanged); P.5.2.01_1.0 Finerenone coated tablet 40 mg / Test Procedure (P.5.2.01_IQMS-397602_1.0, amended); S.7.3.05_01 Finerenone micronized drug substance / Stability Data - Photostability (S.7.3.05_022475896_01, unchanged)

II. In accordance with USP <1092>, the dissolution methods for finerenone-coated tablets at 20 mg and 40 mg were developed with the aim to ensure sink conditions for the drug substance and show sufficient discriminatory power regarding important critical attributes such as particle size, compression force, etc., to distinguish between acceptable and unacceptable batches.
Sink conditions are defined as the volume of dissolution medium which is at least greater than three times that is required to form a saturated solution of the drug substance.
During development of the dissolution methods, solubility data of the drug substance has shown that sink conditions for 20 mg Finerenone are only achieved, if 0.1% Tween 20 has been added to the dissolution medium acetate buffer pH 4.5. Whereas 0.6 % Tween 20 has to be added to the selected dissolution medium for Finerenone coated tablet 40 mg to achieve sink conditions.
In addition, the dissolution method of Finerenone 20 mg that uses a dissolution medium with 0.1% Tween 20 shows good discriminatory power to the most important critical process parameters: particle size of the drug substance and the amount of disintegrant (please refer to P.5.3.21_022302454_01 Finerenone coated tablet – Method Development – Dissolution)
The selected dissolution method of Finerenone 40 mg that uses a medium with 0.6% Tween 20 shows good discriminatory power for the particle size and the disintegrant as well (see P.5.3.21_IQMS-451745_2.0).
Therefore, the dissolution method of Finerenone 20 mg and the method of Finerenone 40 mg have comparable discriminatory properties.
Bayer performed dissolution testing in acetate buffer pH 4.5 + 0.1% Tween 20 with 6 items of Finerenone coated tablet 40 mg from the primary stability batch KM60385 and reports complete dissolution data in Table 6 and profiles in Figure 14 and Figure 15.
Although the dissolution profile of the investigated primary stability batch KM60385 obtained in acetate buffer pH 4.5 + 0.1% Tween 20 would possibly meet the specification limit in stage 2, the dissolution medium acetate buffer pH 4.5 + 0.6% Tween 20 has been chosen for release - and stability testing, as this method is found to show good discriminatory power in relation to critical formulation attributes and 3 fold sink conditions as required in USP<1092>.
This ensures that the dissolution method is able to reveal physical differences of the formulations and solubility of the drug substance does not become the limiting factor during dissolution testing.
In conclusion, Bayer shows that the selected dissolution medium acetate buffer pH 4.5 with addition of 0.6% Tween 20, provides acceptable sink conditions and has shown discriminatory power (see P.5.3.21, section 2.6) and robustness (see P.5.3.21, section 2). This also corresponds to the dissolution method of Finerenone coated tablet 20 mg.
Source: S.1.3.01_022285635_01, Finerenone micronized drug substance – General information (IQMS-231278 unchanged); P.5.3.21_IQMS-451745_2.0, Finerenone coated tablet 40 mg / Method Development – Dissolution (IQMS-451745, amended); P.5.3.21_022302454_01, Finerenone coated tablet / Method Development – Dissolution (IQMS-260469, unchanged)

Please provide the details of the Time Out of Refrigeration (TOR) and Temperature Excursion studies to confirm that the excursion condition does not impact batch quality over 36 months. Please refer to the guideline for Stability testing for prescription medicines (Sections 14.4.3 and 14.4.4).
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 2:
The current available data of TOR and temperature excursion (cycling) studies for Aflibercept solution 114.3 mg/mL in vial and PFS are provided in CTD sections P.8.3.11-2.0, P.8.3.11-6.0, P.8.3.04-02 and P.8.3.04-1.0. Those include respective results for up to 24 months of long-term storage, which are well within the shelf-life specification acceptance criteria. Only minor differences in relation to the shelf-life specification acceptance criteria were observed between studies subjected to additional cycling/ TOR and studies without additional stress for those quality attributes that are linked to the major degradation pathways of Aflibercept, i.e. aggregation as determined by SE-UPLC and isoaspartate content formation. The results are compiled in the tables below. Note that an additional decimal is provided for aggregation results to demonstrate that there is no significant difference between cycled/TOR product and non-cycled product. The impact of the additional stress through cycling conditions and additional TOR is also negligible compared to the range left up to the shelf-life specification acceptance criteria. It is therefore expected that the allowed temperature excursions and respective TOR times are also associated with no impact on product quality for a shelf-life of 36 months.
The TOR and cycling studies for the PFS are still ongoing and will be continued up to 36 months. The respective data is expected to be available in Q3 2026. Like for the vial presentation, it is expected that the allowed temperature excursions and respective TOR times are associated with no impact on product quality for a shelf-life of 36 months based on available data in the referenced CTD sections and as compiled below in Table 2. and Table 3.
The cycling study of the vial presentation ended after 24 months as the original study protocol did not foresee a test point after 36 months storage and the time point had already passed in October 2024. The applicant is conducting an additional study where three vial batches that are currently on long-term storage will be temperature cycled and tested after 36 months.
The data obtained in the vial cycling study indicate that an initial temperature cycling at the start of the shelf life does not accelerate the drug product degradation when compared to non-cycled drug product.
For isoaspartate, the offset between cycled and non-cycled drug product at T=0 was basically maintained until the 24 months timepoint, being up to 0.03 mol/mol higher for cycled product at T=0 and up to 0.02 mol/mol higher for cycled product at T=24. For SE-UPLC main peak purity, the gap between cycled and non-cycled drug product decreases along the shelf-life. While at T=0 the maximum observed gap is 1.2 %, at T=24 the gap is 0 %. Similar results are obtained for aggregates.
Therefore, the applicant is convinced that a cycling study with the temperature cycling taking place at the end of the shelf life is representative for any temperature excursions during the shelf life and the study design of the proposed 36M cycling study justified.
Respective data is expected to be available in Q3 2026.
The applicant commits to conduct the stability studies as indicated above and to provide the data of the studies to the health authority after their finalization.

to R. mucosa, that was found to be non proliferating, your growth study is not
comprehensive enough to eliminate the potential risk from any gram negative bacteria
that may be present at a clinical site. Additionally, the automated contrast injection
system study only shows that a one time use of the drug product and system without a
worst case microbial challenge by a specific operator and conditions does not lead to
product contamination. Similarly, your proposed study to test the sterility of the PBP over
24 hours within a laminar air flow environment would not provide a sufficient microbial
challenge for the same reasons.

supported by the microbiological hold time studies and update the drug product labeling,
accordingly.

The XRPD patterns of the XRPD moisture measurement sorption in the ranges of 1 to 20%

Figure 2: Overlay of XRPD pattern Sorption 80%, Sorption 1%, Hydrate 1 Mod. A and 
Mod. IV.

As the overlay of the XRPD shows, we must accept quality degradation in the respective 
patterns during the sorption measurements. The humidification duration for the XRPD 
sorption was 60 minutes, and the XRPD measurements were performed in reflection

texture effects, as can the changes in humidity. All these factors result in the observation that

tendency towards the crystal lattice of Hydrate 1 Mod. A at high humidity and towards the 
lattice of Mod. IV at very low humidity.

Question/Consideration:
Question 11
Section 3.2.P.4.1 should include controls on functionality-related characteristics of 
relevant excipients in line with their specific grade. Whether this is reassured by the 
drug product manufacturer by routine testing or solely relying on CoAs from the 
relevant excipient suppliers, it need not be specified in the regulatory dossier as it falls 
under GMP.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 11 (P.2; P.4):
The P.2.2.01 Pharmaceutical Development – Drug Product document (section 2.6) shows a 
comparison of two or more grades of four excipients (microcrystalline cellulose, lactose 
monohydrate, crospovidone, magnesium stearate). The purpose of this comparison was to 
determine whether one or more grades are not suitable for further process development. If a 
grade is not suitable, it follows that the physical-chemical parameter (e.g. particle size 
distribution) that sets it apart from the other grades must be critical. Any such parameter 
would require a control strategy, either via GMP procedures or as a regulatory requirement.
It was found that all grades tested are, in principle, suitable. Therefore, none of the parameters 
are critical and no controls are required. In other words, none of the grades tested had a 
characteristic that was relevant for its function in this product. For each excipient, one grade 
was then selected for further development.
Only one excipient (microcrystalline cellulose) was, however, found to have a potential effect, 
depending on the grade, on a critical quality attribute of the product (dissolution). Although 
all results were within specification, the rate of dissolution may be affected by the grade 
selected. The primary distinguishing feature of each grade is the particle size distribution 
(PSD). Therefore, even though the PSD of the excipient grade is not a critical parameter per 
se, it is indicated in the P.4.1.01 document (T.03.91_5.0 Quality Reference / Cellulose 
microcrystalline excipient) that PSD requires control, if applicable.
The specified ranges and test method for PSD are defined and justified by the qualified 
manufacturer and/or supplier. Bayer therefore controls, if applicable, the PSD of the 
microcrystalline cellulose for use in drug formulation. This case applies to Sevabertinib 10 
mg coated tablet.
The current PSD ranges for Avicel PH 101, set by the supplier are as follows:
d10 
14 – 30 µm
d50 
40 – 75 µm
d90 
77 – 156 µm

The PSD results (by laser diffraction) for the Avicel PH 101 batch that is referenced in the 
P.2.2.01 Pharmaceutical Development – Drug Product (no. BX07559) are within the above-
mentioned specification:
d10 
22 µm
d50 
63 µm
d90 
138 µm
Any change that is proposed by the supplier is evaluated via the established GMP change 
management procedure for any impact on a marketed product, including Sevabertinib 10 mg 
coated tablet.
The other three excipients did not yield a significant difference in dissolution behavior. As a 
result, no additional requirements or controls, beyond the compendial ones, are considered 
meaningful.

Question/Consideration:
Question 12
An increased frequency of in-process control testing should be adopted to effectively 
monitor the continuous manufacturing process, i.e. every 15 minutes. It should 
additionally be confirmed that testing will be completed following any period of 
downtime.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 12 (P.3; R.3):
Please be aware that the control strategy for the process is based on two independent systems. 
An automated process of highly frequent automated sampling and testing is achieved by a 
tablet multicheck (testing of 20 individual tablets every 10 minutes). The multicheck is 
directly connected to the tablet press, and the measured values allow automatic re-adjustments 
of the tablet press. This part of the control strategy therefore ensures a high degree of process 
reliability due to its immediate process monitoring and short reaction times associated with 
stable production parameters, so that tablets can be reliably produced in accordance with 
specifications. The limits of this automated testing are described in the summary of the 
production recipe (R.3.1.02 Batch Record Master).

To further safeguard the automated measurements, there is a manual process for measuring 
the tablets as at-line IPC on standard stand-alone test equipment at the beginning, middle and 
end of each batch (and after possible adaptation of parameters or downtimes). The 
combination of both independent measurements, one for direct process control (R.3.1.02 
Batch Record Master) and adjustment and one as traditional at-line IPC to demonstrate 
accordance with the specification (P.3.3.01 Manufacturing Process and Process Controls) 
allows increased process reliability.

Question/Consideration:
Question 14
An in-process control limit for friability of core tablets should be adopted.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 14 (P.3):
With respect to the production of tablets, Ph.Eur. states the following: „In the manufacture of 
tablets, measures are taken to ensure that they possess a suitable mechanical strength to avoid 
crumbling or breaking on handling or subsequent processing. This may be demonstrated using 
the tests described in general chapters 2.9.7. Friability of uncoated tablets and 2.9.8. 
Resistance to crushing of tablets.“
Ph. Eur. 2.9.7 states that “the measurement of tablet friability supplements other physical 
strength tests, such as tablet breaking force.”

Bayer maintains that the originally proposed control strategy, without a supplementary in-
process control for friability, remains scientifically justified. The originally proposed control 
strategy ensures that tablets complying with the established specifications, including release 
testing, are consistently safe and effective for patients. The scientific rationale was reviewed 
and accepted by both the FDA and Health Canada. It is also noted that while the harmonized 
USP/Ph.Eur. chapter describes friability testing as an additional method for assessing physical 
strength, it does not mandate its use as an in-process control.

In line with the argumentation provided above, batches manufactured subsequent to process 
validation, did not include an in-process control for friability.
Bayer acknowledges MHRA’s position and therefore commits to adopting the in-process 
control for the friability of core tablets for all future manufacturing batches intended for the 
UK market. At the same time Bayer respectfully requests that the MHRA accept the batches 
already produced post-process validation for release to the UK as these batches were 
produced under scientifically justified control strategy and are intended to supply the UK as 
well.

Given that the average weight of film-coated tablet is not controlled in the finished drug 
product specification, an in-process control for film-coating uptake should be adopted.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 15 (P.2; P.3; R.3):
We acknowledge the recommendation from MHRA to adopt an in-process control (IPC) for 
film-coating uptake, given that the average weight of the film-coated tablet is not included in 
the finished drug product specification. However, based on extensive process development 
within the Quality by Design (QbD) framework, we have established a comprehensive control 
strategy that ensures process consistency and product quality. We would like to provide 
scientific justification for why our existing control strategy provides robust control and why 
the addition of a formal IPC for coating weight gain would not add value.
The primary purpose of the film coating for BAY 2927088 (Sevabertinib) 10 mg coated tablet 
is cosmetic/ non-functional, i.e. to enable easier identification of tablets for the patients due to 
its red brown color. The effect of the materials and the process parameters on the appearance 
of coated tablets was evaluated within the QbD framework (ICH Q8), and an extensive risk 
analysis using FMEA was carried out and its summary is reported in the P.2.3.01 
Manufacturing Process Development section 2.3. 
The coating of the BAY 2927088 (Sevabertinib) 10 mg coated tablet has high opacity and 
achieves full color saturation at approx. 50 % of the target coating amount (i.e. at 1.4 mg of 
the final 2.8 mg target). This means that beyond this point, variations in the final coating 
amount have no notable effect on the tablet’s appearance, which is the coating’s primary 
function. Furthermore, the effect of coating amount on drug release was investigated. Even 
with a significant over-coating resulting in a tablet weight gain of 5.6 mg (double the target of 
2.8 mg), no impact on the dissolution profile was observed. Details are provided in the dossier 
(P.2.2.01 Pharmaceutical Development Drug Product, Section 2.5). Thus, within a range of 
50 - 200 % of the intended coating uptake, both appearance and dissolution requirements are 
met.
In addition, thorough process understanding and a multifaceted control strategy have been 
established to ensure effective process control and direct verification of product output.
Control of Tablet Cores: 
In-process controls are in place for the uncoated tablet cores including tablet core weight and 
resistance to crushing. This ensures consistency of the tablets entering the coating process.
Control of Process Parameters:  
The coating process is managed by a validated recipe (R.3.2.01 Batch Record Master 
(Recipe)) with tightly controlled and monitored process parameters, including:
• 
Coater load (1.5 – 3.0 kg) 
• 
Spray rate (40 – 50 g/min) (CPP) 
• 
Inlet air temperature (76 – 90°C) 
• 
Inlet air volume (195 – 255 m³/h) 
• 
Drum rotation speed (92 – 98 rpm)
These process parameters were all part of the DoE studies on a commercial scale. A violation 
of any of these ranges leads to a diversion of the respective sublot (as described in P.2.3.01 
Manufacturing Process Development, Section 4.1.3.1 and P.3.3.01 Manufacturing Process 
and Process Controls). 
The process parameters that could affect the amount of the deposited sprayed material on the 
tablets such as spray rate, air flow rate, inlet air temperature, drum speed and coater load are 
all controlled. The average film coat uptake and the intra coating amount variability were 
studied in detail also for this coater in the past (Sivanesapillai et al. A validation of discrete-
element model simulations for predicting tablet coating variability, International Journal of 
Pharmaceutics, Volume 642, 25 July 2023, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijpharm.2023.123109) 
and this was considered in the development of the control strategy.

Direct In-Process and Release Testing of the Appearance: 
The most relevant indicator of coating quality is the final appearance. This is controlled via:
• 
In-Process Control: Appearance testing is performed for each batch. 
• 
Release Testing: Appearance testing is a formal test on the release sample. This provides 
direct verification that the coating process has achieved its intended purpose.
During the process development, it has been investigated whether weight gain is an indicator 
of coated tablet appearance, but it turned out that weight gain is not a reliable or relevant 
indicator of quality for this specific process. Our data show that weight gain does not correlate 
with the quality attribute appearance, specifically the number of defects in the AQL testing 
(see. Figure 3) performed during process development (P.2.3.01 Manufacturing Process 
Development, Table 4-10). No correlation between the measured weight gain and the resulting 
appearance could be observed across a wide range of measured weight gains (50 – 130 % of 
target weight gain). Therefore, appearance testing is a more direct and more effective in-
process control.

An IPC for coating weight gain was never used during the production of clinical samples of 
BAY 2927088 (Sevabertinib) 10 mg coated tablet. For clinical supply, all produced coating 
sublots were intensively analyzed regarding outer appearance. None of the coating sublots 
were rejected because of appearance defects. The data are summarized in P.2.3.01 
Manufacturing Process Development, Table 4-4 (clinical supply), Table 4-10 (DoE studies). 
 
In conclusion, the control strategy for BAY 2927088 (Sevabertinib) 10 mg coated tablet was 
developed based on a scientific understanding of the product and process. The strategy relies 
on controlling the process parameters while verifying the most relevant quality attribute 
appearance directly. Given that the amount of film coating has been demonstrated to be a 
non-critical parameter and that weight gain is a poor indicator of the consistent performance 
of the coating process for this system, we maintain that our existing control strategy is robust 
and sufficient. We believe that adding an IPC for coating weight gain would not enhance 
process control, process consistency, or product quality assurance.

Question/Consideration:
Question 17
In order to assure future batches are representative of submission batches, the total impurities 
specification limit in the drug product should be tightened to 1.0%.
Answer/Response:
Bayer Response to Question 17 (P.5):
Bayer agrees to tighten the release and shelf-life specification (P.5.1.01, P.5.1.02) for sum of 
degradants in the drug product from max. 1.5% to max. 1.2%.
As explained in the P.5.6.01 Justification of Specification document, this limit combines the 
established specification for DS-Pyridone (max. 1.0%) with a single unspecified degradant 
(max. 0.2%).
It is acknowledged that the submission batches (primary stability and process validation) 
show results for sum of degradants that are consistently below 1.0% and typically show < 
0.1% for any unspecified degradant. Nevertheless, a further restriction to max. 1.0% is not 
warranted. It would contradict the toxicologically confirmed limit for DS-Pyridone, which is 
the main metabolite in vivo. The sum of degradation products must take into account the 
occurrence of at least one degradant, other than DS-Pyridone, at 0.1 – 0.2%. Applying a limit 
of max. 1.0% for the sum would effectively mean lowering the limit for DS-Pyridone to max. 
0.8%, meaning below that of the Drug Substance. Such a change is not considered meaningful 
for control over the quality of the Drug Product.
Based on this rationale, a limit of max. 1.2% for the sum of degradation products is 
considered the most stringent specification that can be appropriately justified.

Question/Consideration:
Question 1
1. Documents regarding the Drug Substance that comply with Article 7(2)(b) of the
regulation.
Answer/Response:
Question 1a.
a. Related Regulation: Article 7(2)(b)
Reason for Supplement: 3.2.S.1.3. General Characteristics and 3.2.S.3.1 
Structure and Other Characteristics
1) Submission of detailed results of structural analysis on the non-quantified
hydrate form of the drug substance is required.
2) Molecular formula and molecular weight should be presented based on the
hydrated form of the drug substance.
3) Solubility data for non-polar solvents have not been submitted.
4) XRPD detailed numerical data (2Θ) for verification of the drug substance has
not been submitted and insufficient explanation of results based on the 
hydrated state.
Supplement Requirement: Please submit additional materials regarding the general 
characteristics of the drug substance considering the above matters.

Bayer Response to Question 1a. ( S.3.1):
a.1)
The dose strength of the DP, which is critical for correct dosing of the drug, is based on the 
anhydrate form, specifying that each tablet contains 10 mg of sevabertinib. As the dose 
strength is independent of the number of water molecules (x) in the hydrate, and does not 
affect the labeled strength, a specification of (x) is not required from a safety and efficacy 
point of view. From scientific point of view, it is correct to keep the number of water 
molecules (x) unspecified in the molecular formula of the drug substance.
Although the number of water molecules (x) cannot be specified, the amount of water in the 
DS is ensured by the manufacturing process and is controlled by the DS specification (refer to 
Specification S.4.1.01). DS batches that do not comply with the specification will not be used 
to manufacture the drug product (DP).
The drug substance in its crystalline form, Hydrate 1 Mod. A, has been fully characterized by 
thermoanalytical, spectroscopic, and X-ray diffractometric data (see S 3.1.01 Structure 
Elucidation and other Characteristics). In addition, the special non-stoichiometric character 
of this hydrate was clearly demonstrated by an X-ray single-crystal structure based on one
single crystal. In the X-ray single-crystal analysis, it can be seen that the water molecules are 
randomly arranged between the layers of the active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) 
molecules.
In addition to the interactions between the API molecule and the water molecules, 
intermolecular hydrogen bonds also occur between the water molecules, which supports the 
nonstoichiometric, variable character of Hydrate 1 Mod. A.
These different types of intermolecular interactions explain why this crystal lattice can 
implement varying numbers of water molecules without the actual lattice structure changing. 
The correlation of XRPD data to the X-ray single-crystal structure was achieved by 
comparing the calculated X-ray powder diffraction pattern with the measured X-ray powder 
diffraction pattern of the various batches of Hydrate 1 Mod. A.
Based on the nonstoichiometric, variable character of Hydrate 1 Mod. A with an undefined 
ratio of sevabertinib to water, a value for (x) cannot be specified.
However, it may seem that based on the water content 1-4% specified for the drug substance, 
it is theoretically possible to calculate a number of water molecules (x) in the crystalline 
lattice. The theoretical value based on measured water content 1-4% is provided for 
information purposes only and corresponds approximately to x = 0.28 – 1.12. This calculated 
number of water molecules does not describe the actual water amount in the lattice structure 
of the drug substance and would not be a correct representation of the DS physical structure.
Water content (%) and the hydration number x represent fundamentally different concepts and 
physical dimensions. Water content determined by Karl Fischer titration is a mass‑based 
parameter (w/w%) that reflects the total amount of water present, including surface‑adsorbed 
water, channel/pore water, and lattice‑associated water. In contrast, the hydration number x is
a crystallographic concept describing the molar ratio (mol/mol) of structurally defined water 
molecules within the crystal lattice per mole of the drug substance.
As the lattice occupancy of water can vary with the environmental equilibrium state rather 
than remaining within a specification‑worthy interval, it is not only inappropriate to define a 
fixed hydration number x, but also scientifically unsound to provide a “range” for x.
To clarify once again, due to the nonstoichiometric, variable character of Hydrate 1 Mod. A 
varying amounts of water molecules can be included in the lattice structure of the drug 
substance, which go beyond the theoretically calculated range. Therefore, it is scientifically 
not correct to specify a number or a range for the amount of (x) water molecules in the 
molecular formula of the drug substance. Bayer kindly asks the Agency to accept an
undefined amount of water (x = variable, non-stoichiometric hydrate) in the Korean 
application form.

a.2)
It is well-known that two kinds of hydrate formation exist[1]:
Stoichiometric hydrates have a crystal lattice based on an exact water content with a well-
defined mole ratio of water molecules and given API molecule.
Non-stoichiometric hydrates have a continuously variable composition (due to the water 
content) within a certain range without any significant changes in crystalline structure.
Hydrate 1 Mod. A belongs to the second class described above and thus exhibits variability in 
water content. This must be described by the following structural formula:
C24H25ClN4O5 · x H2O
The variable molar fraction of water in the crystal lattice of hydrate 1 Mod. A makes it 
impossible to name a molar mass based on the hydrated form. The molecular weight can only 
be provided for the anhydrous form.
By using these criteria and based on the given definitions, Sevabertinib Hydrate (BAY 
2927088 hydrate) can be described as a non-stoichiometric hydrate, because its crystalline 
lattice is able to include variable numbers of water molecules without changes in the observed 
XRPD pattern and consequentially the crystalline structure. Water content in the drug 
substance will be controlled with the specification of 1.0 to 4.0 %.

a.3)
We have determined the requested solubility data of the solvents Tetrahydrofuran and 
Isopropyl acetate.
Solubility for Tetrahydrofuran was found to be 41.579 g/l (after 3 hours at 25°C).
Solubility for Isopropyl acetate was found to be 2.695 g/l (after 3 hours at 25°C).
This information is included in S.1.3.01 General Information - General Properties.

a.4)
Detailed numerical data (2Θ) of all technically relevant XRPD patterns of the different 
crystalline forms is provided in S.3.1.01 Structure Elucidation and other Characteristics / 
Additional Information on Polymorphism.
In RH XRPD experiments, the behavior of the crystalline lattice of Hydrate 1 Mod. A was 
examined under different humidity conditions (0 – 90% RH sorption and desorption in 10% 
steps) at a constant temperature of 25°C.
The RH XRPD results perfectly match the data from the DVS measurements, which gives us 
information on the change of water amount in and on the sample BXR9J78 (Hydrate 1 Mod. 
A).
Another technique for investigating the behavior of Hydrate 1 Mod. A upon loss of water are 
thermoanalytical methods. Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC) and 
Thermogravimetry (TGA) techniques were used.
In summary, all available data support the assignment of sevabertinib hydrate as a non-
stoichiometric hydrate.

e. Related Regulation: Article 7(2)(b)

Bayer Response to Question 1e. ( S.2; S.3; S.4):
e.1)
The control strategy for genotoxic impurities is in line with the ICH M7 guideline, which 
states that the Threshold of Toxicological Concern (TTC) concept is not directly applicable in 
the case of a drug substance and drug product intended for advanced cancer indications as 
defined in the scope of ICH S9, which is relevant for BAY 2927088 hydrate micronized drug 
substance. In this case, impurities are controlled at acceptable levels for non-mutagenic 
impurities. During development, the risk calculations of BAY 2927088 hydrate micronized 
drug substance were based on an acceptable limit of max. 0.10%, as this is the identification 
threshold for organic impurities in the ICH Q3A impurity guideline.
Mutagenic organic impurity 3-Chloro-2-methoxyaniline is analyzed in BAY 2927088 hydrate 
micronized drug substance (active substance) and in BAY 2927088 purified intermediate 
(step 2a) using HPLC method described in S.4.2.01 Test procedure.
The Batch data (S.2.4.05 Batch Analyses for Intermediates and S.4.4.01 Batch Analyses) show 
that “Any unspecified impurity” and therefore 3-Chloro-2-methoxyaniline was < 0.05 % in 
BAY 2927088 purified intermediate and BAY 2927088 hydrate micronized drug substance.

e.2)
A spiking experiment demonstrated that a quantity of 5.0% of 3-chloro-2-methoxyaniline 
added to step BAY 2927088 crude (2a) leads to a content of 3-chloro-2-methoxyaniline of 
0.06% in isolated BAY 2927088 crude. Adding 5.0% of 3-chloro-2-methoxyaniline to step 
BAY 2927088 purified (2b) leads to a content of 3-chloro-2-methoxyaniline of <0.05% in 
isolated BAY 2927088 purified. Thus, steps BAY 2927088 crude and purified combined 
render an overall purge factor of at least 8100 (cf. S.2.4.01 Discussion and Control of Critical 
Steps).
For the calculation of purge factors, reactivity, solubility and volatility of the impurities are 
identified as physicochemical parameters that influence the removal of the specific impurity 
in the manufacturing process.
The total purge factor is obtained by multiplication of the purge factors of each operation and 
step.
A purge ratio of at least 1000 is considered to provide “sufficient 
confidence that the level of the impurity in the drug substance will be below the acceptable 
limit such that no analytical testing is recommended for this impurity. [4]

Question/Consideration:
(1) Explain the manufacturing scale and container (e.g., name of production line) used for the
commercial manufacturing and process validation (PV) for each manufacturing step for 
the drug product of each formulation*.
Answer/Response:
First, we will explain the design of PV performed for this drug and the plan for future commercial 
production. Many of gadoquatrane drug products are marketed overseas only, and the combinations of batch 
size of bulk formulation and filled drug product are determined based on the predicted demand and supply 
in each country. A batch of bulk formulation is not usually assumed to be filled into only a single product 
item (e.g., 2-mL vials) or a single product category (e.g., syringes), but rather into drug products which vary 
in type of container and volume.
Therefore, in the PV for the production of bulk formulation, the minimum (33.822 kg) and the maximum 
(2818.5 kg) manufacturing scales were determined by considering and examining various potential scenarios 
of the commercial production, and a total of 9 batches of different sizes were manufactured within the range 
(Table 1 and Table 2). As shown inTable 2, since two types of formulation container are used depending on 
the batch size, PV was performed at the batch sizes assumed to be the minimum and maximum scales for 
each container. For all batches, free gadolinium content, calcobutrol content, bioburden, and endotoxin were 
tested as validation items in addition to the usual process control and quality control test items, and all met 
the acceptance criteria.

Mobile formulation container：移動式混合容器 
Stationary formulation container：固定式混合容器
PV of the filling step was performed using the filling line currently planned to be used for commercial 
production, and produced three batches of 2 mL vial each filled with a different bulk formulation batch (Table 
3), and a total of nine batches of syringe consisting of three batches each of different fill volumes, each of 
which were filled with a different bulk formulation batch (Table 4). Taking risks into consideration, the 
validation confirmed that stable filling operation can be performed continuously for more than one hour for 
each batch, demonstrating reproducibility and robustness of the step.
Table 3 Batches of vials manufactured in PV of the filling step

Note that the process is controlled with a safety factor determined based on the characteristics and control 
methods of microorganisms, and with the maximum processing time of 6 days from the start of filtration step 
(Step 4) to the completion of sterilization step (Step 6).
The minimum batch size for bulk formulation of 33.8 kg is quite small as it assumes the manufacturing of 
2 mL vials only, while the minimum batch size for bulk formulation for the manufacturing of other 
presentations is 281.85 kg. For the manufacturing of syringe presentations, the bulk formulation is produced 
within the range of 281.85 - 2818.5 kg and filled according to the type and required amount of the drug 
product required. When a group of products with relatively large volume is manufactured, the batch size of 
bulk formulation is larger, and assumed to be split into multiple batches to separately filling individual 
product items.
The same manufacturing scales and equipment as those used for PV are applied to the commercial 
manufacturing (Table 5).
